From Captain America wielding Mjolnir all the way to the the infamous leader finally saying "Avengers Assemble". I just feel like everything I wanted to happen, happened. All of the characters came together well and there was even a woman power moment to keep everyone happy, in my opinion I don't know what else could be added!In terms of the special effects it was definitely almost perfect and it helped set the scene. The only flaw that stood out to me was when the characters came through the portal from Titan, the green screen shot seemed to stand out like a sore thumb. Other than that, with all those characters and entities on screen at once that need to be computer generate I think it was incredibly well made and I really give a round of applause to everyone that worked on this movie. A special round of applause goes to the Russo brothers for making something so special and astonishing.I think this is definitely the best movie so far in the MCU, a movie that will be difficult to trump. Review Title: A fine ending to a fine series
Review: I haven't heard more people upset about spoilers since the Star Wars prequels, so please consider this sentence the spoiler space you very well may need if you don't want to learn more. Then again, I'm going to discuss the idea of this film more than the actual movie itself.Avengers: Endgame is the blockbuster of 2019. It's a juggernaut that has the biggest cast of any superhero film ever, wrapping up almost 12 years of storyline and multiple movies, all to answer the question that came up at the end of Avengers: Infinity War: after you kill half of everything, what happens next?There's been a lot of soapboxing and online hand wringing about this film. Plenty of people feel the need to show that they're above the paltry populace, happy to proclaim their intellectual superiority and state that comic book related films demand that adults remain stuck in the days of adolescence. Much like the issues of today's politics, I'm not going to change anyone's mind that feels that way. All that ends up is two people shouting their talking points and refusing to learn anything from one another. But my snide comment is this: can't you just leave well enough alone?This is a popcorn movie that appeals to the biggest audience ever. And that's fine. You can ignore it if you like - we've never lived in a time where there's more opportunity to enjoy the media that you want. Me, I ignore mumblecore, critic beloved films and Oscar-bait movies for the most part. And that is also fine.All that I know is that I've seen nearly every Marvel film with the same set of guys that I've seen movies with since I was 25 or so. Each movie is an event where we get the chance to grab a meal, catch up and enjoy one another's company in the midst of our exceedingly stressful and busy lives. If a movie can do that, it's already a success before you even watch one frame. Movies bring us together, a light on the cave wall where we can hear a fantastic tale that's bigger than us. That's what this movie is - modern mythology of larger than life heroes who are the best of all of us battling the worst villains possible.Spoiler warning part two - here's where I get into major plot points. You've been warned.More than the overall tale, I enjoyed the story beats here. Hawkeye becoming Ronin, enraged that evil survived the purge while his family did not. The main sacrifice of this film isn't Black Widow's, but his. He was the first person who saw her as more than a killing machine and gave her a chance at life. Now, she repays the favor, taking him from killing machine back to family man. However, he must sacrifice their friendship and the knowledge that her loss will always be in the background when measured against the perceived greater loss of Iron Man.But hey - I've always loved the background characters more than the heavy hitters.There are moments here that really portray what the three main Avengers have had to give up to protect us. Iron Man must lose the stability and family he never knew he needed. Captain America's longing for Agent Carter, trapped by a glass wall that may as well be decades and not inches thick. Thor's descent into depression as he realizes that he couldn't save the day. Their fates each show them finally achieving the final part of their hero's journey save Thor, who is fated to repeat his journey over and over throughout rebirth after rebirth, even after Ragnarok, the end of all things.Those small moments mean more than the big explosions and special effects throughout this film. Tony's quick hug with his unsuspecting father. Thor's moment with his mother, who sees right through his deceptions. Even Quill's way too brief reunion with Gamora. The heart behind each charcter is why we care. There are hundreds of superpowered characters on the screen. The fact that we know the minute motivations of more than one of them is a credit to this tale.I love that this film both wraps up and begins new stories at its close. Sam Wilson must become Captain America, finally receiving the approval and friendship of the Winter Soldier. Thor realizes that his role is to be an adventurer, not the king, and gives the ownership of Asgard to Valkyrie. Even Steve Rogers realizes that despite becoming a grief counselor and telling people to live the new life they've been given, when the opportunity arises to return to his life, it's one he should embrace.Speaking of Rogers, I haven't heard an audience start cheering in the theater for a long time. The fact that he's able to lift Mjolnir, Thor's hammer, was not lost on this audience. Before, he was able to budge it. Now, his journey has made him truly worthy to lead the forces against Thanos, even if he appears alone at the seeming conclusion of the final battle.I also like the synchronicity that the first words that kicked off the Marvel cinematic universe were Tony Stark saying, "I am Iron Man," which are also his last words. There's just something poetic about that.Hey look - I was happy that Crossbones got a few seconds of screentime. I'm that kind of geek. And if that fact upsets you, I'm never going to convince you that this is a good movie.

The movie is very, very, very wonderful, and the end is cooler when Iron Man killed Thanos, but Iron Man died, Captain America has grown old, Thor is no longer a graceful body, and the fighting girl has died, except that there is a transformation in the heroes and new generations will come.

Creators tried to balance heroes personal life and heroic life in both hands but along the way they switched the hands and dropped the balls towards the ending.Instead of trying to undo Thanos's snap,they undid everything that Infinity war was good at.To sum up Endgame = 2hrs Dwell in the Past + 1hr Fight for the Future.

Review:
You know what surprised me the most about this film? It's that it had some minor problems that - in any other film - would bug me out, but in this film, I honestly didn't care about them. The small issues here and there were overshadowed greatly by the sum brilliance of the film.
What issues? First of all, the inconsistent tones in some scenes. You would expect that a film carrying such a grim premise would not be providing as much humour as this film does. Captain America delivers a serious address to the Avengers only for Rocket and Antman to respond with humorous remarks. I recall some moments where a very serious scene transitioned into a humorous one that completely disrespected what the previous scene had tried to establish. But like I said, a minor issue, mostly because the humour was restricted to the first act of the film.
And that brings me to my second issue, the first act. The first act had some incredible moments. Thanos getting his head chopped off was COMPLETELY unexpected and made for a truly icon scene. But after that, it went downhill for a bit. The pacing slowed down to the point the film felt sluggish. I remember in the cinema feeling as if I was pushing against a blockade in a river, trying to push it away so the river could continue running its course. It did not help that most of the scenes in the first act were revealed in the trailer so you felt as if you were rewatching instead of experiencing something new.
What else? There probably are a few issues here and there that others will pick out, but that's all for me.
Did these issues ruin the film? ABSOLUTELY NOT. The film was incredible. It's leagues above any MCU film. I am usually quite critical of MCU films (rating most of them as B-rated action films) but this was a great film. The last two acts were so utterly brilliant that they outweighed the first act. The execution was excellent and a testimony to the skills of the Russo brothers, each character was given their own moment to shine and develop, the plot served up many plot twists that diverted expectations, and God damn it, was it emotional.
There is literally no way you can not watch this film. Even if you're not an MCU fan. Just watch Civil War and Infinity War (that's all you need to fill you in on what's happening in Endgame), and then just watch it. Do it. It will provide you with a cinematic experience like no other.P.S: Another minor issue I had was the scene where all the females united. I'm all for female representation, but it was so clearly forced that it added for a :/ moment during what was one of the best battle scenes I've ever witnessed in film.

Review Title: Completely meaningless, wasted and over the top action CGI set-pieces interspersed by boring and long-winded 'go-team!' techno-babble speak.
Review: The acting in these films consists of Downey Jr, talking fast and everyone standing around posing in their superhero costumes giving each other intense looks that includes the most long-winded 'techno-babble' dialouge that has ever been in any film. Also included is constant 'self-referencing' and supposed 'humour'. There is lots of 'banter' between each superhero as they 'hang out' and it is unbearablly cringey. They are sharing 'inside jokes' that only they actually get. As a viewer it makes me feel nervous like I'm at a party around people where I have no idea what they're talking about and I'm meant to be 'having fun'. Bit like my veiwing experience.The story is completely thread-bare in that it is so convoluted that is anyone really following along? I don't understand how anyone could get through one of Downy Jr's seventh thousand fast talking 'techno-babble' monolouge and still know what is going on. When I think about this film all I see is the 'go-team' sorrounding a table and the camera pans in on them as they look deadly serious and then deliver another vacuous line. No one cares about the characters, every 'sad' moment for me is just another scene that I feel completely indifferent about. I don't have any feelings for the relationships in the film. And then that terrible Music Motif will be cued again and we'll get another 10 minutes of close ups of all the 'superheroses' looking prepared. The whole 'go-team' stlye of the film is so stifling for an emotional and engaging film. It is like they can only pose in their costumes looking buff and say one liners to each other.I've never watched an action set-piece in a film before and actually thought 'god, when is this going to end'. It seems that the the more random things happening in each scene the better. And the more superheros and aliens and tribes and factions in the fight scene the better. The last scene of this film was completely ridiculous, it took them half an hour just to introduce every superhero in this 'fight'. And there was no climax for me , very similar to the ridiculous hodge podge mess in 'ready player one'. Is End game actually based on Comic material? Probably not because the writers wouldn't want to make or draw such a ridiculous looking scenario. It's was just a large mess on screen. I am one for appreciating impressive CGI, but somehow I never feel impressed by any CGI in any of these films. Something feels so 'off' about the way the action unfolds as well. Every film in this franchise just leaves me feeling exhausted from watching it. And all the 'tie-ins'/ cross-overs between each superhero and their own worlds is just so cheap and is just a blatant cash grab. Only adding to all this 'self reference' parody crap, that's meant to be funny and 'next-level'. And it's not like it's even stylish. It would be different if they they replaced the lack of being able to identify with characters with really stylish looking shots, but it's just bland.This film is a piece of hot garbage. Watch the OG spidermans, the first Iron Man or Ang Lee's Hulk for an actual Superhero film as they don't just have 10+ superheros delivering one liners and standing around looking important... and muscly.

Review Title: A worthy conclusion of a ten-year journey but no masterpiece
Review: Considering that the writers had so many opportunities to mess this up they did a marvelous job of holding all the strings to so many story arcs together and leading them to satisfying resolutions worthy of the characters we have come to love and respect in the MCU.Time travel always is a tricky business for a writing team and if you dig a little in this story you'll sure find the inevitable logical inconsistencies and paradoxes but they are handled well and don't distract from the storytelling. The emotions are injected just right and even though the final moment of triumph was to be expected they added enough plot twists and suspense to make an ultimate defeat at least plausible.Why then don't I think that this isn't the best work in the MCU? Well, one reason might be that they walk back the character development of the main villain Thanos. In Infinity War he was presented as a villain who at least had a clear and somewhat logical motivation for his actions and he had to sacrifice to attain his ultimate goal. The Thanos we see defeated at the hands of the Avengers is one-dimensional and megalomaniacal like a cookie cutter comic book villain and his defeat hinges on several "changes of heart" by key characters which seem implausible considering their stage of development in the "time line".All that being said, this movie leaves the MCU in an interesting state to go forward. I just fear that the movie will not stand the test of time very well.

Review Title: You went for Thanos, do not deny it!
Review: I have read a handful of reviews on here and not just the ones that highly rate the movie.The first thing I will say is I can see why the last Avengers has been split into two parts. I also think this is absolutely essential to consider before leaving your rating. It is my opinion that to truly enjoy this end to the MCU (for now) you need to carefully think about the film. Did you go to see the Avengers return to their former glory or did you go to see what was going to happen to Thanos? Ponder that question carefully!Without a shadow of a doubt the end of Infinity War is one of my favorite movie endings of any film released in the past 10 years. Who was sitting in the cinema expecting them to role the credits when the mad Titan had snapped his fingers and wiped out half of the Universe - did it come as a surprise to you? It shouldn't have, he told you he was going to do it and was way to overpowered to be stopped. Sometimes the "bad guys" are just too strong to be defeated by your favorite characters, sorry to disappoint! Cut to the first hour or Endgame, when Thanos gives his epic dialogue on the "garden" before Thor cuts his head off. Thanos was a no nonsense straight-talking super villain hell bent on his agenda. This is why he is one of the best written Villains of our time. We then find he is so good he even foils their time travel plan somewhat until the last 40 odd minutes of the film. I was truly on the edge of my seat wondering if he was going to do it again, when he got the stone again I honestly thought this was it and then of course Iron Man snaps him out of existence - which was indeed satisfying. You can see Thanos thinking calmly that "its over" he had failed, he then sat down and you could see his acceptance he has lost. "You have my respect Stark" - Thanos, Infinity War. He lived it out in his last few moments. Beaten and outsmarted.I went to this film because I wanted to see Thanos be beaten and I was not disappointed, he did not go down easy. I suspect a lot of us did the same. That is my review.

Review Title: One of the greatest movie of this decade
Review:
Outstanding movie, It best describes the final chapter that culminates Marvel Cinematic Universe's 21 iconic films into one. And that also describes the experience of watching your favourite superheroes come together for a singular goal, for one last time. Directors Anthony and Joe Russo ensure that the humongous build-up and the avalanche of expectations do not get the better of them. They deliver a largely wholesome product that is full of moments laced with action, emotion, comedy and drama. Writers Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely take you along, even if you haven't been following the franchise. They do an incredible job with the screenplay to balance emotions with visual spectacle. So if you're not a fan yet, chances are, you might become one after watching this instalment.
While the screen time for each character is not equal, their significance in the story is. And there are enough surprises in store, as far as their fates are concerned. 'Endgame' delivers quite well on the emotional quotient, bringing out superpowers and vulnerabilities of its cinematic demigods through their measured performances. From an upright Captain America (Chris Evans) to a stoic Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson) and from a straight-faced Captain Marvel (Brie Larson) delivering the punches to the reassuring presence of Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.), 'Endgame' has it all and a lot more. Thanks to the conviction in performances, you also might just find yourself rooting for the bad guy, Thanos (Josh Brolin) at some point. However, it's the comic collective of Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Hulk (Mark Ruffalo) and Ant Man (Paul Rudd) that ensures there are enough lighter moments in this otherwise heartfelt finale.
The action becomes progressively intense, but never overbearing. In fact, it remains relevant and true to the narrative, such that it weaves in enough opportunities for major plot twists that even the diehard fans may not see coming. The extensive CGI work adds to the visual appeal, even in 2D.
For the non-fans, the film's explanatory tone might come across as a speed breaker at times, but for the fans, the same invokes hope and excitement, leading to constant gasps and howls.
Overall, 'Avengers: Endgame' is a befitting tribute to the Cinematic Universe that has spawned larger-than-life superheroes and super fans. At three hours plus, 'Endgame' delivers on a lot of its hallmark promises, leaving its fans with a range of emotions and fond memories.

Why didn't Thor go for the head ? He does here.Also disappointing was Steve offering the shield to Wilson instead of Bucky.Stan Lee's cameo came and went so fast I didn't know it was him.All in all, for me, a anti-climatic end for the series, ending with a whimper instead of a bang. As far as the Marvel series goes, this isn't one of its best and that's sad for the last one.

Review Title: Requiem for a Shared Cinematic Universe
Review: As the culmination of 21 movies, "Avengers: Endgame" bears a hefty investment from audiences. To merely call this an "event movie" would be to overlook how much the Marvel Cinematic Universe has ingratiated itself into mass culture over the last 11 years. For better or worse, the filmmakers understand this. One consequence I'm not especially fond of is that much time is spent on send-offs for the retired superheroes. I don't even too much mind the bloated some-three-hours runtime, nor that I listened to a cinema full of sniffling during the movie's sappier moments, but I do think it detracts from any semblance of a self-contained artistic or narrative work that could stand on its own. And, sure, I enjoyed some of the comic relief injected to lighten that mood--even if there were a few too many jokes at the expense of Professor Hulk, or Ant-Man's stupidity, or Thor's newfound obesity (c'mon, "Cheez Wiz" running through his veins--really?). On the other hand, I am fond of the self-reflexive use of time travel, to, in effect, return to some of the cinematic highlights of prior entries in the MCU. Because that's what "Endgame" is about: it's a movie founded upon a past of 21 other movies.The scenes with Captain America interacting with his past in the 2012 "The Avengers," including a nifty reference to a scene from "Captain America: Winter Soldier" (2014) and of Thor reliving his memories of "Thor: The Dark World" (2013) are especially rewarding. It's a heritage we share with the movie and with the characters. Despite all of the humorous talk concerning the illogic of space-time-continuum fare such as the "Back to the Future" series, "Endgame," in one respect at least, follows the time-travel rules of "Back to the Future Part II" (1989). Both movies exploit time travel to relive highlights from and the success of prior movies--whether it's Marty McFly watching himself inventing rock-n-roll on stage from the first "Back to the Future" (1985) film or Cap fighting his younger and more naive self from the first Avengers assemblage.I enjoyed this part enough, upon initial viewing at least, for it to largely compensate for the faults in other parts. That the final battle almost seems anti-climactic, dark and, naturally, cluttered. Or that while several of the characters have well-defined arcs, others do not, despite having also survived the dust turning in "Infinity War" (2018). Bruce Banner's lack of development seems especially egregious, as he continues to serve as comedic relief, as well as for spouting science-y exposition, in his last two appearances, which stands as a disappointing departure from the centrality of this character from "Age of Ultron" (2015) to "Ragnarok" (2017). Likewise, Thanos, after dominating "Infinity War," is reduced back to a run-of-the-mill underdeveloped villain. More minor characters also seem short-changed, including Okoye, the raccoon and Rhodey. Even some of the previously-deceased, like Gamora, are better rounded-out in a shorter amount of time. Perhaps, worst of all is the use of Captain Marvel here as a deus-ex-machina Superman--conveniently flying in at the last moment to save a plot in need. Moreover, the scene where all of the female superheros happen to be in the same spot is such a eye-rolling and self-defeating piece of self-congratulating political correctness or pandering (besides, as if Danvers needs help getting through a battle zone--she just blew up a spaceship by flying through it, for crying out loud). A similar scene, if on a smaller scale, worked more organically in "Infinity War."But, I like the quieter moments, especially early on, which are something of a relieving contrast to the relentless momentum of "Infinity War." Perhaps, it's the appropriate send-off, too, for the characters who are well-developed here, including ("fridging" aside) Black Widow, Cap and Iron Man. The benefit of such fine acting talent, after all, isn't for their fighting skills; it's commendable that "Endgame" allows their characters some time to breath and reflect before moving on or saying goodbye.

The film opens with Clint Barton on his family farm about to have a picnic just before the Snap of Infinity War, and he's left alone as his family mysterious disappears into dust. Yes, it's as heartbreaking as it sounds. We cut to Stark and Nebula aboard the Milano after twenty-odd days in the void of space, hopeless and running out of essentials. Stark has practically given up when Captain Marvel appears and carries them back to Earth. The post-credits scene of Captain Marvel never actually features in Endgame, and I feel like it was ultimately something too important to leave to another movie (oh look, my first criticism). Chronologically Barton's family gets dusted, jump forward a couple of weeks when the Avengers have Fury's pager trying to work out who it's calling when Carol Danvers appears. Presumably they persuade her to back into space to try and find Tony. It's a crucial piece of the early puzzle to make sure everything flows, and it was left out. Redundant after Captain Marvel? Maybe, but it would've been nice anyway, just to keep Endgame complete.From here the Avengers fix up the Milano and fly off to confront Thanos, a now broken and frail man living peacefully off the land. In the first real subversion of expectations, he offers them no fight and he's promptly dealt with, less than half an hour into the movie's runtime. So where does Endgame go now that it's villain is dead with two and a half hours left to go?! The Quantum Realm of course! Don't worry I'm not going to give a running commentary of the whole film (because hopefully if you're reading this you've seen it already anyway), but with the infinity stones destroyed, they hatch a plan to go back in time, steal the stones before Thanos ever has them, and snap half the universe back into existence. Of course things go wrong along the way, people die, others are dragged into the mess, the plan has to be improvised, and it all culminates in a monumental battle comparative in scale to Return of the King.Now I'm going to get this off my chest now as it's what I'm most keen to talk about, and that's all the callbacks, references, and cameos. Oh my god the movie is full of them, and each one surprised me for a number of reasons. Once the Time Heist begins, we are of course thrust back to the events of a number of previous MCU films. We go back to the Battle of New York in Avengers, we go back to the beginning of Guardians of the Galaxy on Morag, and yes, we also revisit Thor 2. To avoid referencing these movies in these scenes would've been impossible, the but the opportunity is also used to drop in some other movies and events. The Ancient One from Doctor Strange appears, Jasper Sitwell, a SHIELD agent all the way up to Winter Soldier appears alongside Crossbones (as well as Cap standing in a crowded elevator with them all to boot), we see Starlord singing and dancing to himself on Morag, Thor has a tender reconnection with Frigga, Edwin Jarvis from the Agent Carter TV show marks the first crossover from TV to film, but the one that really surprised me was Alexander Pierce. Freaking Robert Redford came back for a cameo! Then there's all the additional cameos elsewhere, and alternate aliases too (like Hawkeye being Ronin, Banner and Hulk living together as Professor Hulk, and Pepper Potts finally taking up the mantle of Rescue)Seriously, this movie has possibly the craziest castlist ever assembled for a single film, and every single one of them slays it. The vast majority of them get stylised credits as well making for a special moment in lieu of an actual post-credits scene, with the original six Avengers literally signing off from the franchise. I admit, I choked up a bit at this point. Nothing made Endgame feel more final than those credits. So here's a little game, I'm going to list every actor I remember seeing, and you've got to pin them to a character. But also, this will display just how crazy this castlist is. Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Chris Hemsworth, Mark Ruffalo, Scarlett Johansson, Jeremy Renner, Samuel L Jackson, Brie Larson, Jon Favreau, Gwyneth Paltrow, Ty Simpkins, Cobie Smulders, Josh Brolin, Zoe Saldana, Karen Gillan, Chris Pratt, Bradley Cooper, Vin Diesel, Dave Bautista, Pom Klementieff, Sean Gunn, Evangeline Lilly, Paul Rudd, Michael Douglas, Michelle Pfeiffer, Benedict Cumberbatch, Benedict Wong, Tilda Swinton, Don Cheadle, Danai Gurira, Chadwick Boseman, Angela Bassett, Letitia Wright, Winston Duke, Tessa Thompson, Taika Waititi, Tom Hiddleston, Rene Russo, Elizabeth Olsen, Anthony Mackie, Sebastian Stan, Tom Holland, Marisa Tomei, William Hurt, Robert Redford, Frank Grillo, Hayley Atwell, James D'Arcy, John Slattery, Natalie Portman, Linda Cardellini, Ross Marquand, Callan Mulvey, Yvette Nicole Brown, Hiroyuki Sanada, and of course Stan Lee himself. For anyone counting, that's nearly twenty academy award nominees.All right, I think that's enough raving for a minute. Let's kick back for some ranting, because Endgame still wasn't perfect, not in my opinion. The biggest one for me (which is still comparatively a niggle) is how it contradicts itself on time travel. Time travel is a huge part of Endgame, and they explain it away nice and neatly, without risk of confusing things or retconning previous film entries. Going back and changing things doesn't affect the current timeline, the timeline of our characters, the timeline we've been following all along. Instead every change creates a new, separate timeline. There will be a timeline where Thor loses his hammer for a brief moment during the dark elves assault on Asgard, there will be a timeline where Loki escapes after the Battle of New York with the Tesseract, there will be a timeline where Thanos and his armies just up and disappeared around the events of Guardians of the Galaxy, there will be a timeline where Starlord doesn't find the Orb, there will be a timeline where Howard Stark got advice on how to be a father from a "stranger". But most crucially there will be a timeline where Cap and Peggy grow old together. A completely separate timeline. This is where Endgame breaks its own rules, as an old Cap appears just sitting on a bench nearby. For starters why did they decide to set up the time travel device in order to close the loops near some random old guy on a bench? But more importantly how is there an old Cap there when the timeline he went back to would have diverged from the current one? We didn't need a whole monologue about living his life and literally passing the torch over to Falcon. It was redundant, didn't make sense to the film's own logic, and in a way undercut the emotional punch of Cap's eventual fate right at the end of the film.It also creates problems, moreso than anyone else, for Spider-Man. Half the people on the planet are five years older. In adults this isn't quite as noticeable and life goes on, but for Peter he's just a teenager. Five years at that age is huge. Cassie Lang is now a teenager as well when she was just a kid during the snap. Half of Peter's friends will have grown-up and left school, gone to college, maybe even moved out, have jobs, and started paying bills. If Far From Home doesn't address this, we're going to have some problems. But that aside what are the odds all the major characters of Spider-Man were all snapped and will come back exactly as we expect them? That just feels way to convenient!Cap v Cap was amazing, as was the "I can do this all day" exchange between them. The constant references to Winter Soldier were amazing, what with Pierce and Crossbones back, as well recreating the elevator scene, Cap whispering hail Hydra (in reference to the comics), and of course Sam saying "On your left" to Cap as Doctor Strange opens a whole bunch of portals around him. Then there's Cap wielding Mjolnir after causing it to nudge in Age of Ultron. All things considered, Cap had an exceptional send-off in this movie. Tony had a lot of great things too. He got the family he wanted in Infinity War, he finally got Pepper to embrace the suits and become Rescue, he was sent off with his "heart", the mention of cheeseburgers made made me want to blubber like a baby, and even Harley from Iron Man 3 made a brief appearance! In fact Age of Ultron got a lot of nods as almost every single element of Tony's vision was met; the broken shield, the Chitauri worms, space, Black Widow's death.Thanos was great too. Early on you can see the toll the stones had taken on him. He was a shadow of his former self, basically succumbing to his fate. When we go back and meet younger Thanos at the height of his ambitions, he's so much more menacing. In a way he sort of reverts back to being a generic superhero villain who just seeks the end of the universe, but he's in full Mad Titan mode before Gamora's betrayal in Guardians of the Galaxy, and we've seen how capable he can be even without the stones in Infinity War. Now he has a double-bladed sword-glaive thing and it's awesome!Yeah, Endgame was pretty damn amazing. It was the perfect culmination of everything. It sent-off our original heroes with the most perfect endings, and gave each and every one of them a moment to shine, accommodated heaps of fan-service without getting schlocky, and gave the bittersweet conclusion we as fans needed. It took us in directions we never expected, no matter how rampant our theories and rumours became, no matter how hard the trolls of us tried to spoil it for everyone else. There's so much in this movie, but it never feels rushed, and it's three hour length never drags or feels too long. It's not a perfect movie for me, it never will be, and if I'm honest Infinity War is still my favourite film of the entire saga. But all-in-all I couldn't be happier. I give Avengers Endgame well-deserved and emotional 9/10. Godspeed!

After Avengers Infinity War, we waited for the Avengers Endgame. We wondered how the story would go on, how our heroes would turn back, what would be the end of Thanos. Many theories related to this have been put forward. Avengers Endgame was undoubtedly the most anticipated film of recent years. Normally, the higher the expectation, the higher the probability of disappointment. But this is not the case for Endgame. Whatever you're expecting, you find much more in the film. This means that the biggest concern about the film has disappeared.On the other hand, another comparison comes up. Is Endgame more successful than Infinity War? We can comfortably say it Avengers Infinity War is just the beginning of the story. Endgame was the finale of the story. So we shouldn't think of these two films as two separate stories. There is only one story divided into two parts.Avengers Endgame is, above all, a great homage to the ten-year history of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The story highlights the original Avengers team. Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow and Hawkeye are at the center of events. No character comes in front of them. Of course there are many characters that play an important role in the story outside the original Avengers team. Everyone's concern was that Captain Marvel, who was included in the Marvel world, overshadowed other heroes. We can say that this certainly did not happen. What is important in this struggle is not how strong you are, but how good you are. This comes to the fore in all areas. It gives good message about being a hero and a family.Of course, Avengers Endgame has some critical aspects. For example, is the three-hour period necessary in terms of the story? It can be discussed. The head of the story moves much slower than the rest. It also drags the heroes into an emotional predicament. Then the tempo is rising and the heavy scenes we are watching are getting more meaningful. The last 45 minutes of the movie is fully action packed. But the last 45 minutes goes so fast that you don't even realize it. Action and battle scenes are really successful. There is not even a slight distress about visual effects. There are also slight logic errors in the film, but in general the story is so successful that these details become meaningless and insignificant after a certain point.Lastly, Avengers Endgame doesn't have a movie end scene. Because after the film's final, there is no need for another scene. The Marvel legend Stan Lee appears with a small stage. But this is the last surprise scene in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Moreover, there is no clue about Marvel's future. This makes us wonder more about Spider-Man: Far from Home. 10/10.

Review Title: A strong climax to 11 years of build up
Review: Avengers: Endgame was a fantastic movie that paid off 11 years of set up. It has so much that the fans always wanted to see and also managed to surprise a few times. It had humor and heart in all the right places. An excellent send off for some of the characters we've grown to love over the years. If you'd told me that a movie like this could be possible back in 2008 when Iron Man was released I'd have thought you were insane.Apologies for the short review but I'd have to see it again before doing a deep dive. In the meantime all I can say is 10/10. Worth the wait!

"Endgame embodies a satisfying conclusion to an eleven-year-old franchise, it is exceptionally deepened when concentrating on determined characters such as Steve Rogers, Tony Stark and Hawkeye. Still, it is under the weather in some features, for example, regarding action scenes and some baffling-undeveloped subplots"It has passed nearly seven years since I went to the cinema to watch The Avengers with some classmates to celebrate my friend's birthday, the end result was purely adrenaline-charged. If someone had asked about living the same sensations at the fullest the following decade with the MCU, my immediate response would have been an instant "nope" because I never ever distinguished a franchise which lasted more than a decade in the history of the seventh art. Today, if I had the chance, I would ratify my answer. Endgame does embody a satisfying conclusion to an eleven-year-old franchise, the finest news is that it surpassed almost every single Marvel movie to the point it joined, in my opinion, the top10 list of the best MCU flicks to date. Mainly for three main reasons: I) An Emotional Farewell: Marvel has produced to date more than twenty movies which had a strong bond between each one, the continuity presented, the fun cameos and the mutual action pieces are melted in one single movie whose name is Endgame, probably it becomes the last movie you will ever meet your favourite characters. II) The Characters Development: Over the years, within each superhero solo movie, we came across with own personalities from each member of the Avengers. Yet, in the fourth Avengers instalment, the feelings run high because it represents a unique encounter with the most beloved people in their lives (like Tony with Howard, Steve with Peggy, Thor with Frigga) and it turns out to be some of the most heart-warming scenes of all the MCU. III) The Epic Final: After fighting the almighty-badass-titan Thanos, the Avengers assembled once more. The fact they are willing to fight in spite of not having all of their members and the probability of winning the match out of fourteen million possibilities makes it special because in this case, they are willing, as well, to sacrifice their particular lives. The final battle is stunning not only for its remarkable visual effects but the action pieces and the ensemble of all the superheroes, making it some of the greatest ones from all the saga, as outstanding as the one in Civil War, Infinity War and a couple more.Nevertheless, it displays some faults which can infuriate some viewers. To begin with, there is the under the weather action scenes and some underdeveloped subplots, take the example of Loki with the Tesseract, the moment where Thor goes back with his hammer (WTF happened then in The Dark World?), Cap vs Cap (amusing but confusing) and many more examples. I know it brings back some Back to the Future essence but it just keeps driving us up to the wall. In addition, the only memorable fight was the final one and the brief but impressive Stark-Cap-Thor vs Thanos, then for the first time I can assure the formula exchange brand-new genres because the movie exhibited drama rather than action spectacle.Apart from that, just spot the closest cinema possible and behold this superhero masterpiece. (83/100)

Review Title: This movie is my least favorite Marvel movie to date.
Review: I wanted this movie to be good, no great. But it just wasn't. Plot holes galore, needless scenes, and terrible pacing riddle this movie like buckshot. I so wanted this movie to be good that I went back to see it again. And as I sit here with my Captain America t shirt still on from the night before, I feel the need to vent some honest nerd rage.First and foremost, time travel is the biggest, dumbest McGuffin (a tool you use to forward the plot) ever. For one thing it's tricky, you don't want paradoxes and you to mess with the time stream continuem. But they did. The movie opens with Thanos, who is at this point the most powerful, knowledgeable person in exsistence. So he destroys the stones so no one can undo what he's done. Well, if you had all the infinity stones you would be aware of multiple timelines and universes and destroying the gems in this timeline is utterly futile. And while we are taking about Thanos, he is way more one dimensional and dumbed down than he was in "Infinity War".Secondly, time travel!! Captain America goes back and encounters his past self. Past Cap says that it's Loki but when their shields collide, Past Cap should realize something is afoot. If it was Loki, the illusion should have shattered, yet both shields rebound after impact and fall into the abyss. When did Future Cap get his shield back and if he didn't, wouldn't we have a Past Cap moving forward with 2 shields. Again, time travel is a tricky thing.Thirdly, didn't Doctor Strange have the time stone the entire time?! He could have went back and changed any number of possibilities. I suppose by oath he was barred from using it even if it meant saving half the universe.I'm going to stop counting at this point.But hey, don't give the gauntlet to the only god you have on the team because he's been drinking for five years. No give it to Robert Downy Jr. because he's tired of being Iron Man and that makes sense. Also, how many times do you need to snap the gauntlet?! One to bring everyone back and another to dust Thanos? Why couldn't have been one snap? (Answer: contract negotiations)Did the Hulk smash anything other than keys on a keyboard?And finally, no after credit anything????? I mean, if you count your average comic book fan, at matinee prices we spent on average $220 just to see this in theatres, not including dvds, blu rays, and other merch. The very least you could've done was a thank you for watching or in the infamous words of Stan Lee "Nuff said".

Review Title: Okay, but does not stick to original source material.
Review: First, go on Amazon and get an old copy of Infinite War that came out originally in the 1990's and read it. You will be hit in the face hard that the original comic book is a far cry from what was dragged up on the screen. The original comic was far more cosmic, having many metaphysical characters in it. With Thantos not just being able to snap his fingers to win. While the movie was good and entertaining although slow to start, it was good once is got moving, kept up the roller coaster ride well. But my main problem with Marvel is that they have sold out so completely to Hollywood not thinking of their original fans at all. They have so hugely abandoned the original mythos of the comics books for a complete re-write of the Marvel Universe. Also, the Fantastic Four and the X-Men who were in the original story line were cut out completely on the movie re-make. Just is not the Marvel that I have in my comic collection. Could have been so much better.

First, let me say I've been an MCU fan since the beginning, so this review is from that standpoint.To everyone bashing the use of time travel: So what? The writers deliver a twist in the first 5 minutes of the movie when Thanos reveals that he destroyed the stones and then loses is head. Soooo...where else did anyone think the movie could go other than time travel? To the writers' credit, they used time travel differently than most other time travel movies that I've seen. They're not trying to undo the snap or make it so it never happened. They're just trying to get the tools they need to fix it. So if you're at the movie because of time travel, I suggest you watch it again and really pay attention, particularly when Hulk explains what they're doing. Plus, the writers didn't only use time travel to achieve an objective, but also gave us some nice character development and resolution on the way.I'm also seeing a lot of people complaining about the first act and that the whole movie is too slow. Well, maybe, but there's a reason for that. The MCU has been trying to show audiences that there are consequences to our heroes' actions/failures (Civil War, anyone?). The movie picks up 5 years after half of everything was dusted. The writers and directors took the time needed to show what the world was like now and show that the characters really haven't moved on from the Snap. They didn't want us to just see it. They wanted us to feel it. Personally, I did.A lot of reviews are saying this movie doesn't make sense if you're not a MCU fan. Um...duh? No point addressing it beyond that. Go watch the rest of the movies.I've also seen people say that Thanos is different and not as relatable in Endgame as he is in Infinity War. Again, this is on purpose, and after watching the commentary, it makes sense. Thanos in IW is more of a philosopher, 2014 Thanos that we see in Endgame is a butcher. He's not supposed to be likable.A note about Fat Thor: at first, I didn't like that he didn't transform back into the fit, muscly Thor we expect. But the more I think about it, the more I appreciate it. There's plenty of explanations out there about it, so I won't explain it all here, but it can give you something to think about. It's actually really great character development.Do I think the movie is perfect? No. Captain Marvel is a cool character, but I felt that she was used as a fix-all when the writers ran into a roadblock. Her finding Tony and bringing him back to earth was fine, but then she was conveniently absent until the end of the movie when they needed a good way to destroy Thanos' ship. And then after all of that, she still couldn't offer much of a challenge to Thanos himself. That was pretty weak and inconsistent writing. Also, I've nothing against strong female characters or the "feminist movement" (which I don't think really applies here but that's what everyone else who doesn't like it says), but the scene that highlights all the female characters felt a little forced.Endgame strips down the 22-movie saga and focuses on the original team. We see our favorite characters come full circle and find the resolution they deserve. It is sometimes heartbreaking (Iron Man and Widow), sometimes satisfying (Cap), and sometimes in unexpected ways (Hulk and Fat Thor). It nearly perfectly wraps up the Infinity Saga while still leaving the door open for more stories. I haven't seen Spider-Man: Far From Home yet but I'm excited to see where the MCU and various Disney+ series go from here. 9/10

Warning - SpoilersOverall, Endgame is a good but not great superhero movie. Marvel did something I never thought possible, they made a boring movie. I understand it is difficult to maintain continuity over 20+ movies and introduce new characters and plots along the way and Marvel has done a phenomenal job with the MCU. This culminated in the excellent Infinity War which I loved and have watched 5 or 6 times now. What made IW great was the energy they were able to maintain while weaving together different characters and stories. It was funny, emotional, and had lots of great action.Here are some things I liked about Endgame:
Tony's ending seemed like a fitting conclusion for this phase. He essentially started the MCU way back in 2008 and his sendoff here was a nice tribute to his character. I didn't feel like he needed to die and thought he would serve as a father figure and guide for Peter Parker in future Spiderman movies but can see how Marvel went in this direction.Captain America living but altering his past seemed like a choice he would make given how he seemed to have no place in the present or future. He lived in the past and was a relic of a bygone era. The ending was a bit schmaltzy but I liked him passing on the shield to Sam. One issue, so Cap can suddenly wield Mjolnir and summon lightning?What I didn't like:Runtime and pacing! Ok, so they wanted to make a 3 hour movie, fine, I love Return of the King and all. If you do that, you have to keep the energy up! I felt like Marvel didn't know what to do with the characters that survived the snap. Without most of the Guardians, Black Panther, Dr. Strange, Spidey, etc., the focus was on minor characters like Black Widow, Hawkeye, and Nebula. Did we really need to see Hawkeye mope around for 180 minutes?? Strange move for Marvel to snap most of the newer (and funnier!) heroes and not bring them back until the last 30 minutes of the movie. These seemed more like cameo appearances to me. It produced a lot of forced comedy which no one in my theater laughed at. I even missed Ebony Maw and the CoT who really fleshed out the bad guys in IW. Without these interactions which made IW so great, the movie dragged!Thor and Hulk. It's an absolute disgrace to turn Thor into a Jim Carrey impersonation of Jim Morrison for most of this movie. I chuckled when he is introduced but the joke became old fast. He is one of the best developed characters in Ragnarok and IW because he has so much emotional baggage regarding Thanos and they ruined him here. In the first 120 minutes he makes no contribution to the plot, as if he is just a drunk frat boy hung over in the corner. Professor Hulk was okay but they could have spent at least 10 minutes of the first 2 hours showing us how he made that balance happen. Wouldn't that have been cool?? We are first introduced to him in a diner dabbing for some kids taking selfies, pretty lame.Time travel and hand waving. Okay so time travel is how they figure out how to defeat Thanos and undo the snap. I'll suspend belief a bit on how it works but did Tony really figure it out after running a few models in his basement in 1 day?? I won't even get into the altered timelines and whether or not you change the future by changing the past!Thanos was written so well in IW, he had a clear plan and was shown as a sometimes conflicted villain. Here he just decides to destroy everything because the survivors couldn't let go of the past 5 years later. No discussion of balance, just a one note villain.Captain Marvel. So we have an all-powerful being who can pretty much rip through any opponent or ship but she basically says I'll see you in 2 hours instead of helping out with the time travel stuff?Not showing everyone coming back when Hulk reversed the snap. Marvel missed a huge opportunity to show Black Panther, Spidey, etc. coming back into existence!! Where were they when it happened? What year was it? To have a 3 hour movie but not include this is baffling! It would have been a huge emotional moment to show their reactions and their reunions with those that survived. They all just come walking out of portals at the same time to conveniently battle Thanos in the end. But hey, we got to see some birds come back so there's that.Overall, I expected much more content in a 3 hour movie. Review Title: A true gem of the mcu and a satisfying end to a decade of Marvel movies.
Review: Wow...now that's how you wrap up a long running series! I did actually enjoy Infinity War a tiny bit more just because it was generally more of a nonstop ride and had a slightly more coherent narrative as it built up to its cliffhanger ending, whereas this was kind of all over the place, but in a good way! Infinity War, or part one as it really was because these two movies go together so amazingly well, was better in terms of action and was more conventionally 'fun', but this is definitely a deeper and more emotionally and thematically rich movie and it certainly made an impact on me, by the end I sure felt I'd been through the cinematic wringer! At the beginning I was quite taken back by how they unceremoniously lop off a very weakened Thanos' head and the screen abruptly cut to five years later. The movie slows itself way down and spends a hefty amount of time setting up how broken the characters are as it languishes in the faded world that the dreaded snap left behind, and I won't lie that part of it did begin to drag for me, but it was still a much needed slow start, because it serves the purpose of just carrying on where things last left off and making you feel for the scattered heroes more as they gradually mobilise and begin to formulate a very tenacious plan of action to set things right, and when the lost heroes do return from oblivion near the end it felt very earned. It was so brilliant how the quantum realm time hopping Infinity Stone hunt doubled as a way of tying up some very longstanding plot threads and character arcs. I think what they did with Captain America was beautiful, with him doing something for himself for once instead of the greater good and having the happy ending he deserved in the time where he truly belonged. Cap always seemed a bit like a man out of time and it was touching to see him get to go home at last... I also liked the scene where the comically chunky, but no less heroic where it counted Thor got to share a few words with his mother, I thought her death in Dark World was sad and I'm pretty sure I'm one of the few out there who actually thought that particular movie was pretty good! The best reunion though for me would have to be when Tony Stark finally shared a scene with his estranged and late father, albeit a much younger version of him, and although he might not have known who Tony really was, they had such an easy chemistry together that you did believe them as father and son and that moment did offer a little closure for Tony as a character, and I loved that scene. Robert Downey gave it his all and while seeing his character die was really sad he did sacrifice himself to save the whole world and maybe even the universe, there's surely no grander a way to go out than that! His character was certainly the most iconic Avenger and probably a main factor of what got this franchise off the ground and turned it into what it became in the first place, so it was only right that the final defeat of Thanos should have belonged to him. They saved the really huge fantastical fight sequence till last, but man did they make up for it, such an incredible battle, good god was I in awe!!! The stakes were effectively higher because after seeing that his grand plan for the galaxy didn't really change anything for the better as well as his own death, Thanos had a far worse plan in store once he had his hands on the stones and was more malevolent and determined than ever before to destroy the Avengers, so it did kind of make sense how he was harder to defeat in armed combat with a giant sword against all three of the main Avengers champions than he was when armed with the gauntlet! The big, purple and bald tyrant just would not go down and there were numerous awesome moments to take in, among the best being Scarlet Witch's reckoning where she breaks his blade in two with her powers and almost tears him limb from limb until he cheats and orders an aerial bombardment in order to get away, and I loved when he took out that overpowered wench Captain Marvel with one Power Stone-powered punch, because she was just as tacked-on and off-putting as she was in her stupid lame movie! I also liked the clever role-reversal in the subplot with the reformed Nebula convincing the younger Gamora to turn to the side of good like she once had done with her, but unfortunately being unable to reach her more fanatical former self... So this was terrific, I'm so glad that I was able to get onboard with these movies that involved and expanded upon each other and slowly build up to this incredible closing chapter, I don't speak for everyone of course, and I'll happily check out whatever's next for the mcu, but as far as this movie goes, the whole endeavour feels like it's run its course now, and I doubt very much that they'll ever be able to equal it, much less top it. Infinity War and Endgame were the big one, and I loved them, wonderful conclusion, what a blast, what a Marvel! X

Review Title: The Most epic conclusion in the history of film.
Review:
There were so many intriguing concepts that I picked up while watching this masterpiece. The Russo brothers and writers Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely really outdid themselves with this adrenaline-rushed film.A couple things I must establish of course
The first thing would be Hulk's arc. Professor Hulk was a great idea, even though it was predicted long ago, we get as Banner says "the best of both worlds" and I understand people will and have already said or made complaints about how Hulk/banner didn't do much in the film, yet he was the one to wear the gauntlet, if anyone else put it on even for a second, they would've perished, whereas for Banner, it only damaged his arm.As for things that went into making this film, there is literally so much detail that went into producing this movie. Some examples being 'Harley' portrayed by Ty Simpkins from way back in 2013 during Ironman's final solo film debut, making an appearance during the funeral scene for simply showing his respects for a father figure like Tony Stark(Robert Downey Jr.). Every time travel scene as well was perfect and exactly the way it was back in The first avengers film, thor's sequel, etc. They managed to callback every actor that was in the original scenes.The story arcs:
Steve Rogers'(Chris Evans) arc was by far my favorite. "God's righteous man, pretending you could live without a war" as quoted by Ultron(James Spader) in Avengers: Age of Ultron(2015). His reunion with Peggy(Hayley Atwell) in the end was so beautiful and long awaited, after all that Cap has done for his country and comrades, he really deserved something as simple as that dance with her as he promised at the end of "The first Avenger"(2011) before he went into the ice. Cap wielding Mjolnir was my all time dream as many as other fans', you'd never think that Cap would actually wield Thor's mighty hammer but he DID and man did everyone in my theatre go crazy.And Thor being fat is the most understandable plot point that lots of people fail to understand or try to hate on. He lost countless loved ones, half of his people, and most of all screwed up by decapitating Thanos thinking that it'd fix something but it didn't, it was only a matter of time before he fell off the deep end and hit rock bottom after all that happened.Tony Stark's death was the most saddening thing in the film. Stark has always been getting negative feedback from everyone, saying things like he isn't hero, he's narcissistic, only fights for himself, or even as quoted by a naive Steve Rogers in the first Avengers film "Not the guy to make the sacrifice play, to lay on a wire and the let the other guy crawl over you". Or as an evil Wanda Maximoff(Elizabeth Olsen) forsaw in "Age of Ultron" where Stark was the only surviving Avenger and that he didn't do enough, yet he snapped his fingers to save trillions and was venerated as he deserved it.All of the fan service and call backs were perfect and I wouldn't say unnecessary or overdone. The scene in which all of the dusted and remaining heroes return, was THE biggest most immense scene in the history of cinema, I can happily tell my children in the future "Yeah, the biggest event in Cinematic history, I was there and I witnessed something truly special that will never happen again." The callback to "The Winter Soldier"(2014) was perfect when Falcon quoted "On your left", *CHILLS* as the portal opened and the score began. Don't even get me started on the OST, Alan Silvestri was tasked with one of THE hardest jobs that factored into this film and he nailed it, he hammered that sh** hard. Not only did he construct the most epic soundtrack ever but he at the same time was able to invoke a sense of different types of pathos in multiple tracks. From hopeful, empowering, and epic in his song "Portals", to something that venerates Rdj's character like "The Real Hero". Or even something that admits a feel of tribute and legacy in "Main on End" during the end credits, in which there were 6 Original Avengers being honored amongst the fans, writers, everyone who was in support of this film. 6 signatures with the iconic original melody of the Avengers theme song rolling as we see Jeremy Renner's "Hawkeye", Scarlet Johansson's "Black Widow", Chris Hemsworth's "Thor", Mark Ruffalo's "Hulk"/"Bruce Banner", Chris Evans' "Captain America", & Robert Downey Jr's "Ironman".The intensity this film emits is truly satisfying and a film like this deserves even more credit and recognition. It's not some overhyped comicbook film that fails to please the fans, it is one of the most satisfying conclusive films to a 22-film saga, which has never been done.One flaw that I could not bare to ignore after watching a couple times was the final battle, the lead-up was perfect, the intensity was perfect, we get a perfect bone-chilling scene of all our heroes lined up to fight the biggest battle in film then they all run up and... its horrible. Its literally just the heroes running up and slaughtering a CGI army, there were no nail-biting climactic fights. And another thing is that we never see someone physically best thanos in a fight. One thing Infinity War did better than Endgame(And I hate to compare two films from the same saga and franchise) was the fight scene between Stark and Thanos on Titan, Thanos even had 4 stones and got wiped pretty good by the nanotech armor. If anything, they should have done a similar scene because the only instance in which we really see Thanos get bested was between him and Cap Marvel(briefly) and between him and Scarlett Witch as well. But it only lasted like 30 seconds. I wanted to see a rematch between him and banner or Stark, Thor, Cap, at least one of those four! Not a 10-15 second scene of Cap, thor, and Cap Marvel trying to hold him down until stark takes the stones out. Stark was nerfed as well as Thor. Captain Marvel was straight shoe-horned in as well, she only a got a few good licks in and that was it. Although that was just the climax, it could've been so much better, the wasted potential.

Review Title: Amazing but it trumps any need for more films
Review: While it wasn't my number one favorite of the year, "Endgame" is still definitely on my top ten list of this year (for now...) I found the film to be an extremely satisfying and immensely entertaining super epic that made "Infinity War" look like a puppet show.With all this said, I will briefly give the highs and the lows of the film:Highs: It perfectly wraps up the storyline that's been building up for 11 years to a fitting (and tear jerking) ending. All the Avengers come back in an awesome final battle that we've all been waiting for. The time travel sequences are super fun and they add a good layer of needed humor to the sad plot. The acting was incredible and the characters were used perfectly in their roles. Overall, it was easy to say that I wasn't bored at all.Lows: There, of course, is so much going on at once. Understandably, it'd be hard to do it in any other way than the way they already did, but it's honestly just a ton going on at once and it becomes pretty ridiculous. I've recently heard people complain that the new "Hellboy" and how ridiculously over stuffed and busy it was, but once they hear about Avengers they flock together like a bunch of monkeys because they're biased. Hulk's appearance and the fact that he could talk was very weird looking and didn't feel right. Just seeing this big green Mark Ruffalo face talking in Mark Ruffalo's voice just looked and sounded so unusual that it was kind of hard to take seriously. Last complaint, the movie was really good, it was, but why on earth is Disney making more Marvel movies at this point? Or at the very least, any more Marvel movies involving the same characters. Like, Endgame wrapped everything up so perfectly that it kinda trumps the need to make more films involving those characters. Can we just get some more new movies about characters we've never seen before (Moon Knight, anyone?) or just maybe have filmmakers adapt superhero movies that aren't from Marvel or DC (Dark Horse and Image need love too!)Just a little food for thought.

While most of the movie was amazing, I have one bad criticism for it, which has knocked it down a point. The 'girl power' scene at the point where Spider Man says to Captain Marvel 'I don't know how you're going to get through all of that.' And she's joined by every possible female character. The scene was completely forced. They might as well have waved a flag and yelled, "Look, girls are fighting in this battle! Yay girl power!" It totally broke the third wall, reminded me I was watching a movie, and brought politics into something I went to watch for fun. There's no need to point out that there are indeed girls fighting in the battle. If they're strong role models we'll remember they're there. If not, how does this help further the story-line? Marvel is known and loved for its strong female leads. It doesn't need to be pointed out that they're awesome, we know it. Look at Electra, Jessica Jones, Medusa, The Phoenix, Rogue. All amazing characters, it doesn't matter what gender they are. There it is, the problem I have with this scene was that it was about 'girl power'. It undermined what the rest of the movie was about. The story wasn't about whether or not the people fighting were males or females, it was about good people doing what's right, against all odds. Except for those few moments the film, where it was more about 'strong women' than 'good people' fighting to save humanity.
Here's a quote for you: "Any man who must say 'I am the king' is no true king at all." ~Lord Tywin Lannister GOT. I get the quotes about men but let's put it this way. Any woman who has to tell the world 'I'm a strong female role model.' is no true role model at all." If you need to force the message in our face that your female leads are strong, then they were never really that strong to begin with. Don't pander to the audience to try to push an agenda, stay true to the message of the original story. Your strong role models won't need special scenes just for them to make sure everyone knows who they are, it will be made evident through their actions and characters. It doesn't matter if a person is male or female, what makes them a good role model has nothing to do with gender. 'Hero's are made by the path they choose, not the powers they are graced with.'
The rest of the movie was amazing, even though they ended up with a Captain America from an alternate reality- he couldn't have gone back to their past, because by doing what they did they changed the past, splitting the time line and creating an alternate reality, which Captain America would have ended up in if he went back to the past. Yay, theoretical physics! Anyway, special effects, acting, puns, the entire rest of the movie was totally up to par. Amazing! A beautifully crafted film, aside from that one little blemish, it was a job well done.

OK so I always struggle with time travel as a plot device. Mostly because I consider it to be lazy in terms of the story writing ... don't like how the ending went? ... we'll go back in time and undo it! It's LAZY.And when I saw Endgame in the theaters I LOVED the beginning and they kill Thanos and I'm thinking "ok he destroyed the stones ... how are they going to undo this?" and then they go "TIME TRAVEL" and my heart just sank. So the first time through I missed a LOT due to being bummed out. And I walked out of the theater with a disgruntled smirk.However ... the second time, I had a chance to pause and rewind when Dr Hulk explains the time travel rules and, to my surprise, they actually do make sense.
Which made me far less irritated when he explained why they couldn't just go back and kill baby Thanos. And with that part making better sense I was able to pay more attention to the other bits that bothered me the first time and upon second viewing I realized that they actually did a pretty decent job of telling the story and nearly everything lined up.I still have bones to pick ... for instance, it was purely coincidence that Nat and Hawkeye went to Vormir? Cuz if Nebula and Rodi had gone then they would've been screwed. Seriously nobody knew the trick to getting the soul stone but they sent nearly the only pair that could make it work? Just dumb luck? OK ... fine. And I don't understand why the 4 had to land on Morag and then split up ... but ok. And then Captain America going back in time wouldn't have messed up his own timeline but he would've messed with Peggy's. Wouldn't that mean he would end up on a different trajectory? So he wouldn't have ended up on that bench at the end?See this is the problem with time travel.And I was disappointed by some missed opportunities. What I loved about Infinity War was the mash-ups of the different worlds, the characters meeting and collaborating. And with the exception of Nebula there weren't really that many mash-ups. I would've loved more Okoye ... even some Okoye would've been nice. She was relegated to 1 scene and then the end ... bummer. I would've loved a lot more Rocket. I think it would've been better if they'd left Shuri alive and had her contribute to the science since that part of Infinity War was awesome. And more Captain Marvel of course though I know why they did what they did with her ...All of that being said, the final battle is one of the greatest things I've ever watched. I loved it both times and wanted to watch it again immediately after finishing which means I'll likely watch this film several more times.Endgame is a wonderful conclusion to an outstanding film series ... the most epic ever attempted. And while it's not perfect it's still very well done.

Review Title: A good Avengers ending but not a good movie
Review: Pretty much all the 10/10 ratings have said it's a great ending to the epic story that has been going since 2008 or so and I agree.Ending a story doesn't mean a movie should be able to ignore storytelling techniques, explanations and other things just to make you sad at the end.There is another review that said the movie was good but when you think about it it gets worse, and I felt this way too.Here are issues I had:Scott Lang getting out of quantum realm felt like a cop out (Time jump between Scott driving from San Fran to New York was unexplained (not a major issue but just made later problems more obvious)Time travel idea was semi-ok but then Captain America appeared at the end in same timeline: thought they couldn't be in same timeline, and wasn't explained that he travelled again later (if that's what he did)Thanos was completely O.P. despite not having infinity gauntletCaptain Marvel would have won in about 2 seconds but flew off somewhere and only appeared again at the endScarlet Witch would have won in about 2 seconds as well but apparently Thanos is more powerful without the gauntlet (artillery from ship was a realistic way to save him though so fair enough)Captain America's use of mjolnir seemed like a convenient cop out as well - Jackson etc. didn't get as much time because they are great actors.In the end, wasn't even that sad Tony died because he had just been lost in among all the characters and I've been keeping up, saw Iron Man 1 in cinemas when it came out.

I loved this movie, it beautifully encapsulated all the movies that helped build to this point, and rewarded the ones who became fully immersed by the infinity saga.
Tony's interaction and accusation of Steve after returning to earth, removing his chest piece and telling him to hide is absolutely fantastic acting.
Scarlets performance and character arc was amazing as she selflessly saves the universe and will go down as one of the strongest female protagonists on screen.
The Timeheist scenes are a great call back and I appreciate the time they took to explain the logistics of time travel and the effect on the existing and alternative timelines created.
The final fight sequence was amazing, and was a reward to see all these stories and heroes tied together for the battle. Beautifully shot and masterfully choreographed (for most scenes) to keep the action rolling; Ending with an amazing finished to each main characters arc. A terrific movie and a justified end.My only gripe of the movie is the corny all female fight sequence. If properly executed it would have been a perfect callback to the world black widow has opened for the women of the MCU. However, all women stopping in battle and lining up was completely immersion breaking. Review:
Some thoughts I had whole watching this:1. Given the importance of their mission, and considering they only had one shot to get it right, wouldn't it have been better to wait a bit for Thor to get back in shape after 5 years of total inactivity? You know, just on the off chance would need the God of Thunder in all his glory?
(Speaking of, I find it interesting that they didn't include Fat Thor on the poster)2. Wouldn't it have been smarter to tell Carol Danvers/Captain Marvel about their plan to go back in time, and then wait for her to maybe tag along too? Just in case her help would prove valuable in defeating Thanos?3. Tony being such a genius and all, who pretty much solved the time travel equation in one night, couldn't he have made some more Pym Particles so they'd have more than one chance to make the future right again?4. Am I the only one who thought that Tony's sacrifice, while heroic and noble, was also somewhat preventable? He had the gauntlet with the stones, why didn't he just fly away with and let someone else snap their fingers, someone who was not just a regular human with no superpowers? Like Hulk, who had done it once already. Or Thor, who absorbed the energy of a star in the previous Avengers movie and lived to tell the tale. Or Captain Marvel, who also absorbed copious amounts of alien energy and was pretty fine afterwards. He had the stones and he could make his suit fly, what would Thanos have done, who was now probably afraid of him because of the potential power afforded him by the infinity stones?5. Speaking of sacrifices, Natasha's was foreseeable from the moment it was decided she and Clint/Hawkeye would go after the Soul Stone. They all knew, or should have known from Nebula at the very least, that the Soul Stone requires a sacrifice, so shouldn't they have discussed it before? The way she and Clint fought over who gets to sacrifice themselves, they risked both of them dying and no one actually getting the stone.6. How did past!Nebula manage to bring Thanos and Gamora from the past to the future? How did they all have enough Pym Particles? I thought they only had one particle for each of them, so where did Nebula manage to find a spare to give to Thanos and Gamora?7. What was Pepper Potts even doing in the fight? Aside from the plot needing her there so she could witness Tony's final moments? Oh, wait.8. How do the stones even work, anyway? You snap your fingers, you can kill half of a whole planet's population. You snap your fingers, you can also bring back all the people who had been vanished previously? How did they even know they COULD bring everyone back? How did they know they wouldn't just cut the population in half once again?9. I'm curious, what does everyone who's been snapped think about the whole experience? Did they feel anything in those 5 years?And many more, but for now this is it. Personally I think I liked Infinity War better, but oh well.

I had lost my interest in Marvel films a long time ago, but I kept watching them, hoping that one day another good one like 'Iron Man' (2008) or 'Guardians of the Galaxy' (2014) would be released. When they announced the two-part final Avenger movies, I had high hopes: there was much potential there... only a pity that the makers completely blew there chances of winning me (and many others I'm sure) back; especially with this one.The first half of this film was just plain stupidly boring. When watching Marvel movies I expect farfetched plots, lots of action and some underbelly that moves the characters and the story. But this underbelly changed the characters themselves. Thor, Iron Man, the bloody Hulk! Why? Superhero-movies aren't supposed to have character development in this way, and surely not development that feels to be written by people that have no idea how real people change.
Besides that, the characters for an hour and a half just walk and talk... in an action movie. WALK AND TALK! What's up with that? Where is the action? Where is the excitement? Why do they all act as if their personal struggles are of any interest to us, the audience? Marvel has already made sure we don't really care for the characters in their previous films, so don't pretend like we do.The second half of the film was better: there was some action and the way the makers incorporated the previous films into this was very well done and amusing. The plot finally kicks off and although most of it was quite predictable, it was better.
But the only part of the movie that I truly enjoyed and (well, maybe) loved, was the final battle. THAT'S what we want to see: all the Avengers fighting side by side, kicking ass, jumping, swinging and being EPIC. This was also where the score by Alan Silvestry stood out and it gave me goose bumps (gotta love that main theme).
The ending was stupid again though. Dr. Strange told everyone that there was only ONE possible outcome in - what? - a trillion; I honestly don't remember. But when that one in a trillion happened, I could not help but think "truly? THAT is the one? What a f..... waste." And then Tony died... I guess it was sad, but please, I could smell that coming from miles away.The music is okay; Silvestry can do better, but didn't. I do blame the directors and the producers for that actually. The special effects are absolutely astonishing! Nothing to say against that! Whoever worked on that: you can be proud of yourself, because the CGI rocks! Acting ranges from mediocre to bad. Overhyped, overly advertised, more bore than actual good filmmaking.One thing is a given: I am not watching any new Marvel movies ever. I won't grant them the money to continue with their follies. The superhero-genre is as good as dead - has been dying for quite some time actually - and nothing they attempt will bring it back. Deal with it and start making some new movies. And perhaps in a dozen or so years superhero-films will be brought back, starting a thing we'll probably call the 'neosuperheromovie'.

Review Title: Great Final battle with all the avengers

What is important in this struggle is not how strong you are, but how good you are. This comes to the fore in all areas. Then the tempo is rising and the heavy scenes we are watching are getting more meaningful. The last 45 minutes of the movie is fully action packed.
