There are also slight logic errors in the film, but in general the story is so successful that these details become meaningless and insignificant after a certain point.Lastly, Avengers Endgame doesn't have a movie end scene. Because after the film's final, there is no need for another scene. The Marvel legend Stan Lee appears with a small stage. But this is the last surprise scene in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Review Title: Emotional Drama with Illogically carried away storyline
Review:

What's most important for me is the storyline of the movie and the absolute justification of the story portrayed. Maybe that's why it went from "great+5" to "disappointing-6" by the end of the movie.**SPOILERS**The story had the most simple and obvious start to the story with Captain Marvel bringing Tony Stark and Nebula to Earth. And they rushed in showing that....... The rescue went on so quickly that it couldn't create a sense of excitement and suspense of how Tony Stark reaches Earth after being stranded mid-space..... Thus wasting all the hype created by the first Endgame Trailer.Then, just like that, they went to get Thanos at another planet and Thor finally goes for the Head...... Done...... Accepted...... And that's the end of Captain Marvel's hype created at the end of Infinity War and in Captain Marvel.Now, Avengers are broken and living quietly trying to recover from the losses...... Done...... Agreed...... Too much to take....... But why make Thor a Santa Clause.....? That was the most rated character to take on Thanos one on one........ But he was used as a Comedian in the whole movie, Drunk and Fat. Stormbreaker for opening Beer Bottles..??? Hilarious and Disappointing.Coming to Hulk, or Professor Hulk........ Good character..... And equally powerful to take on Thanos.......but he was buried all the time under the debris....... That's where the character got wasted. No proper use of an important character.Clint and Natasha....... Ok......
Went on Vormir...... One sacrifices life to get the stone...... Ok...... Accepted....... That was the only thing Black Widow had to do in movie...... Atleast they used Clint Barton in a proper way this time.Scott Lang all of a sudden becomes a science genius who talks about Time Travel and Quantum Physics. And seriously....... A mouse rescues Antman from Quantum Realm...??No words for Thanos, Steve Rogers and Tony Stark because these three were the only ones who got proper screen time and focus.But Time Travel and Timelines...? They hell lot messed it up despite saying they'll restore it after everything is over. Cmon..., Thanos and his Army came from past to the present and Died. That means New York, Ultron, Civil War, Infinity War and all of it....... That must not happen at all....... And how did they restore the Tesseract and Sceptre after using the Stones, to put it back in the past........And it seems there were two Steve Rogers all this time, since the present one went back and stayed. Again.... Sentimental touch......And why create an emotional drama by killing Tony Stark....... The character on which the whole MCU is dependent........ Could have easily retired him to a quiet life in the woods........The final Battle is the only thing that looked worthwhile with the exceptions of lesser Thor and Hulk vs Thanos....... And now out of nowhere Captain Marvel comes back to take some credits and lead the girls gang of MCU........Dr. Strange gets special appearanceIts just an entertainer for the MCU Fans....... But if you try finding logic in the storyline....... I think you'll be just as confused as I was after watching the movie. Go for it to complete the MCU journey and 3D Action Experience. Review Title: Endgame: The textbook definition of payoff
Review: I have been following the MCU since 2008 when I was 9 years old. I still remember the first time I watched the trailer for the first Iron Man movie starring Robert Downey Jr. and I BEGGED to my knees to my parents to go see it. After I left the theater with my dad I just remember never shutting up about it. I just adored it. 9-year-old me didn't know that Iron Man was just the beginning of something bigger that was to come.Over the last 11 years, we saw the release of 22 movies (Excluding Far From Home even though it is technically the last movie of this phase). 22 Marvel movies consisting of origin stories, trilogy's, crossovers, and more. Over hundreds of actors in a brilliant family-woven cast. Thousands of crew members and over 1000 minutes of screen time over the course of all the movies. Breaking box-office records everywhere. Each one told a new story that was unique, new, and fun. Even though there were a few misses here and there, you could always feel like the story was building to something new. Kevin Feige and the Russo brothers knew how much this 11 year journey was to people like me, and it really showed in this film.First, I'll get my negatives out first, because all MCU movies have some negatives. Some have more than others. I really despised what they did with Hulk and Thor. 'Fat-Thor' was funny at first, but then he became really insufferable to watch. Hulk was bizzare and they really didn't do right by his character. The Hulk I saw in 'The Avengers' wasn't here, and this interwoven Banner/Hulk didn't do it for me. I'd say the time travel plan sounded dumb at first, but Tony and Steve's time travel scenes were great to watch because it was nice seeing them revisit earlier established scenes. I think that Natasha's death was beautiful, but no funeral? She is one of the most deserving members of the team and deserves that honor. Also, I'm disappointed that they didn't really tie up Steve and Bucky's relationship. I don't have a problem with Steve going back to the past, living his life with Peggy, and giving his shield to Sam. But, they could've concluded Steve and Bucky's friendship arc way better, cause after all those two have been through together, you'd think we'd have a nice scene between them. Also, there were moments of complete and utter cringe in this movie. Like please, don't drag fortnite into this. That all woman shot in the final battle was very forced and cringy to watch. No problem with feminism in film or TV, but it shouldn't be too forced. And that is what it was. Rhodey was kinda awkwards and out of place in this movie. So was Captain Marvel. But that's it for the complaints.Alan Silvestri and his scores man. Music was spot on all the way throughout. I will never forget the iconic Avengers theme and the way it was incorporated was just...can someone give him an Oscar? Please.I'm gonna keep some of the scenes as my wallpaper because the cinematography was absolutely gorgeous. The most pleasing effect and settings I've seen in my life.Fan service is so much more satisfying to watch. For all the people who say fan service is a bad thing- In this context, it's amazing.Hilarious moments like 'America's a--" (Thank god for Paul Rudd) and the Captain America "Hail Hydra" moment in the elevator (Russo's literally waved a middle finger to the comics, and it was beautiful and funny). Strangling baby Thanos. Ha! And the odd test aging of Scott Lang was great. Comedy was on point.Then came the satisfying parts. I love Natasha Romanoff so much. She is one of the best female characters in the MCU next to Scarlet Witch. So watching her sacrifice herself was very fulfilling to everything she has been built up to be. She sacrificed herself for the Avengers, which she considers family. That was the best way she could've possibly gone. Bummer she wasn't in the final fight, but it felt right. The fight between the Avengers trinity (Iron Man, Thor, and Captain America) and Thanos was divine. These 3 fighting off a mad titan like Thanos together was worth it. Seeing Cap wield Mjolnir was just satisfying to the T. Always knew he was worthy, this movie cemented it. Look, I waited a full decade to watch all of these stories, characters, and plot intertwine into one moment that I will never ever let go of. The moment all of our dusted heroes return, and Captain America with his shield and Mjolnir saying, "Avengers......Assemble." I just, I couldn't take it. I literally got out of my seat in the theater like everyone else and cheered my a-- off while holding off the tears. This movie was like a reward. A reward for the decade long investment. I am not ashamed to say I left the theater nearly weeping like a baby when Tony Stark died. This man literally started everything. He kickstarted this universe to the top. I hate to be that person, but Marvel has now definitivly crushed DC. Tony was one of my favorites, so watching him die felt like watching a part of me dying as well. It even hurt worse because the second they introduced his adorable daughter, I just knew in my heart that something bad happens to Tony. 10/10 best way to end his arc. Sacrificing himself for the good of humanity.That funeral scene was expertly shot, and whoever held the camera there deserves an award. And then, finally giving Cap the chance to have that dance with Peggy made me so happy. You don't know how much I wanted Cap and Peggy to have a reunion so they can finally have that dance that Cap promised her way back in his first movie. That was the best way you could've ended it.Even the end credits was nothing short of a masterpiece.I started nearly bawling when the original 6 avengers started signing off one by one in the credits. I am genuinely proud of this cast. All of them have risen to better things, and lord. When RDJ signed off, that was it for me and my theater. A standing ovation and the screen went black.This era of MCU movies is over. That 9 year old me is grateful to have been able to have experienced this journey. This incredible journey. I am looking forward to the future, but it won't feel the same without Iron Man and Captain America. But it's time for the new age of Avengers.To the cast and crew- I love you 3000!Final rating- 9.1/10

Review Title: Could have felt so right if only the characters in the sacrificial pairs were switched...
Review: Steve's character has always been about self-sacrifice, from the very first movie, from his very first heroic moment that led to his becoming Captain America. His whole life is defined by doing the right thing, fighting, and saving (and sacrificing if he has to in the process of saving). Don't get me wrong: I love him and I want him to get his happy ending. But the way it is done, it just feels wrong for the character. How did we get from the Steve of all previous movies, basically, to the Steve of the end of Endgame? He went back to Peggy and had a happy and peaceful life, stayed out of all major world events and injustices for 70 years. How is that the Captain America we know and love?! There is a major development arc missing from his storyline; the same way there was a major development arc missing to expalin how he finally got worthy of Mijolnir... As a whole, Steve's character was rather flat in Endgame. What did he learn? How did he change and grow? It's not that characters have to change and evolve in every episode of a series, but such development was strongly implied when it comes to Steve Rogers in Endgame, although we never see it on the screen. The whole episode starts with Tony's accusations--so that scene was just about Tony?? What was Steve's response?--and ends with his getting worthy... how? Hmmm, how did a storyline giving my favorite MCU character all he supposedly wanted leave me so empty and unmoved? I hope the Russo brothers will get to write the jumping-between-timelines explanation they have mentioned and explain what actually happened there...Tony... After everything he's done for the world... After the glimpse we got into a happy retired family-man life for him... he deserved better. He had a plan, a family. He could have been happy without being a superhero from now on. Why couldn't he get that peace and happiness? He had grown enough over the course of the movies to finally be ready for it. I hope they'll bring him back.Alternatively, they could have let Steve sacrifice (go back in time and take Tony's place, for example) and Tony live happily with his family... It would have been painful, dramatic, and in character. I don't buy the whole Tony-was-incapable-of-self-sacrifice "character development" argument, when he risked his life over and over again to save the world. Last time he did was in Infinity War when he was so disappointed Dr. Strange didn't let Thanos kill him.Same with Natasha and Clint. What was the point of Nat sacrifing? If Clint had died, it would have been seen as character development and would have probably led to Natasha's further character development. Natasha's death didn't contribute to anyone's development. It was just a plot device. Therefore, just bring her back, too, and be done with character deaths in Endgame--it's a dumb trope, anyway...

The first time I watched this movie, I was really annoyed by it and even disappointed, it didn't live up to MY expectations but after a second and a third or so watch, it gets better and even picked up some tiny details that I missed the first I watched it. I still have some problems with it tho;
The hulk was a little disappointing, we don't see him at all in Infinity War and they are almost building to this big event where we will finally meet the Hulk and maybe even get a rematch with Thanos but unfortunately, we didn't get any of it, instead we get Hulk, now Professor Hulk in a diner in a such an anticlimactic way. would have loved to have watched how he became Professor Hulk.
I loved Thor, I know it's not how we are used to seeing him but once you consider his story arc, dude's been through a lot; loses his brother, father, mother, hammer, home, half of his people, sister, eye and even his hair haha. It kinda make sense why he just locked himself away. The humor in Ragnorak kinda ease the pain Thor's going through, so he's chubby now....... but still a badass.
I'm still in the air about Cap staying in the past, I like that he finally found happiness but don't like how he just up and left.
I was not a fan of the whole women's moment in the final battle, it was kinda forced truth be told. Most of them had no previous connection whatsoever, not even an exchange of dialogue, so to see them like that all of a sudden, was very cringey. Moreover, Captain Marvel doesn't need help, she's the only character that could get through the army alone without breaking a sweat, would have preferred to see Shuri or Hope have the Gauntlet and then everyone back them up.
The end battle was chaotic and hard to follow, The CGI while it's excellent, it was overused in the sequences, and some character interaction wasn't that necessary.
The screentime is not balanced at all, there's too many scenes with the original Avengers and the first half of the movie is basically just talking, and the comedy ran its course a little bit.
I've got a mixed feeling about the time travel, but then there's not way it's going to be that there won't be a plot hole, time travel is complicated so I'm okay with how it played out here.Thanos is a bit one-dimensional and rougher than the Thanos we saw in Infinity War but he's still memorable as ever, his lines are still chilling. All thanks to Josh Brolin for bringing this wonderfully likable villain to life, no one could have done a better job.
There were really emotional moments like Black Widow sacrificing herself for the greater good, Ironman's selfless sacrifice, Thor with his mother, Tony and Peter hugging, Steve and Peggy finally getting that dance, Those scenes were really moving.And some funny moments; like Scott's age transformation when testing the time machine, Thor saying "you take the little one" to Cap, Thor and Quill's "who's in charge" scene, and almost all scenes with Thor and Antman and Quill......and rocket!Cool moments like Cap picking Mjnoir and fighting with Thanos with it, Captain Marvel's arrival during the battle, Cap saying "Avengers assemble", The trio fight with Thanos, and all the dusted Avengers coming through the portal etc
All in all, The direction is good, CGI is brilliant of course, acting's better than ever, score is evacotive.I personally prefer Infinity War to this, but I think it's a pretty satisfying conclusion to this incredible franchise, okay maybe not the franchise conclusion yet but it still tidied up the story arc of many characters and the Gauntlet/infinity Stones storyline nicely.

Review Title: It was actually pretty good and enjoyable. But that's it.
Review:
The film was overall pretty well shot, but there were some things that made me frown upon.
In the first scene, where Clint loses his family, there is an hand-held shot, presumably, so that we can get the confusing and panic feeling that Barton felt. However, at the end of the scene, we go back to the wide shot used in the start of the scene, kind of dropping what the hand-held shot built up.
Some similar situations were reoccurring throughout the film. Situations where the camera seemed confused, giving different and ambiguous impressions about given scenes.The battle scene seemed utterly full of grandeur and splendor. It's sense of unity against Thano's tyranny was beautifully constructed to match moving pictures. One of the best CGI I have ever seen. From the tracking-shots following the glove to the shifting perspective each participant in the battle had, I had the feeling I was just enough inside the battle, while retaining the idea that I was only observing, having the conscience to judge the struggle of each and every character.As for the whole picture affair, I'd say Endgame deserves a good 8/10.
The plot and story, however, didn't feel as good.
First things first, it's something that has affected marvel for the past films. The disturbing likeness of some characters.
I feel like since "Guardians of the galaxy" and "Deadpool", Marvel has adopted the comedy side to super-heroes, as it has been something audiences have enjoyed. And although some characters already had it within their construction (Tony Stark, Peter Quill), some characters didn't.
I always remembered Thor as a character who was serious and traditional, behaving almost like a medieval prince. But since Ragnarok, he feels like a goofball.
I feel like this is not shared by many, but it is something that has bugged me.
Going afoot from here, I also don't feel very comfortable around how Hulk evolved. I always felt like Bruce was a genuinely nice guy, balancing his intelligence and awkwardness. And now he feels like an all-feel-good vegan millennial trying his best at his new job.
It feels like a sudden try to connect with younger generations, bringing odd behaviors through the wrong characters.Following, there is the issue with all the "time-travel" burp plot.
It all seemed so random, so out of focus and reasoning. I think I understood what went on. But during the film it all looked like it was justified by a "just because".But a lot of characters just feel rushed and messy. The feel like they lack traits of their own. A significant portion of the plot feels saturated and out of goals. Throughout the middle of the movie I found myself disconnected from it all.In the end, I'd say the plot and story goes for a 6/10.Balancing the two, I'd say the film's fine for a 7/10.

Review Title: The journey ends with the best of the best
Review: OH MY GOD ARE THERE SPOILERS IN THIS REVIEW. IF YOU HAVE NOT SEEN THE MOVIE YET, DO NOT READ THIS REVIEW.Also, I'm baaaaack! Sorry I was absent for quite a while. Also, this review is extremely late; I was planning on making an Endgame review for quite a while, but now I'm doing it! YAY!!!!So this is it. This is the big one. The ultimate conclusion. Avengers: Endgame. TONS AND TONS of hype was built up for this movie, and it's probably the biggest movie of all time even. But with all that said, is it any good? You better believe it. This might actually be the greatest superhero movie of all time, even better than Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, Logan, and The Dark Knight. If you can top The Dark Knight, then you're an extremely powerful sorcerer.What's the story? After the devastating events of Avengers: Infinity War (2018), the universe is in ruins. With the help of remaining allies, the Avengers assemble once more in order to reverse Thanos's actions and restore balance to the universe.Alright. What am I supposed to say about this movie that hasn't been said by literally everyone yet? Well, let's talk about the fight scene first: I think it is the greatest moment in cinema history. Now, I know what you're all thinking: "REALLY? THAT'S THE GREATEST MOMENT IN CINEMA HISTORY? WHAT KIND OF LOW STANDARDS DO YOU HAVE?" Well, I am an ENORMOUS fan of the MCU, and I'm not a master critic, so please bear with me! I feel like that scene is just sooooooo amazing because we see all of the Avengers together and trying to destroy Thanos and his army, and it's just so beautiful. Once Cap whispers "assemble", everything is just so amazing- actually, saying it's amazing is an understatement. Almost EVERY character from the Marvel Cinematic Universe is in it, and they're just doing what they do best: being awesome and murdering everything. Even the Thanos snap victims walk through a bunch of portals and arrive, and when I saw it opening morning (yeah, I managed to get tickets for OPENING DAY), the audience went WILD. What accompanies this mind-blowing fight is the insanely heroic and powerful score by Alan Silvestri (my favorite film composer of all time) that REALLY emphasizes how big it is, but that's not all! The end of this scene made me CRY. Yeah, a lot of movies don't make me cry, but this one DOES. So after Tony Stark snaps his fingers on the new Infinity Gauntlet and delivers his instant classic line, "I am Iron Man", he dies. The reason why this scene is so emotionally affective is not only the buildup to the scene, but the fact that Tony Stark was the man who started it all. Don't argue Carol Danvers because it took her 21 movies to actually be in the MCU. The funeral didn't help either. But anyways, another really sad scene in the movie is the Soul Stone Sacrifice scene where Black Widow/Natasha Romanoff dies as well. This wasn't as affective as the Tony Stark death scene, but it was still emotionally powerful because the buildup was, once again, properly dramatic. You can tell Clint didn't want her to die, and they kept fighting until Natasha finally decided to sacrifice herself. "It was supposed to be me," Clint says in a future scene of the movie. The only actual flaw in the movie is that it feels kinda slow-paced, but that was probably the intention of the film to make it more serious and dramatic compared to most of the other MCU movies. The real hero of the movie, however, is the rat that saved Ant-Man from the Quantum Realm. The rat deserves all of the attention. I also like how they went back in time to get all of the Infinity Stones and added their more comical spin on the previous MCU movies (that is, until the Soul Stone scene). One more thing I'd like to mention is that Captain America/Steve Rogers goes back in time at the end of the movie to restore the Infinity Stones, but ends up old in the future and gives Falcon his shield, proving that Falcon is gonna be the next Captain America!!!! Meanwhile, Steve decided to go back in time to be with Peggy Carter (he found her in an earlier time-travel scene), and I feel like that's the ultimate part of emotion in the movie. Just... the ending is awesome and so is the rest of the movie!!!!!In conclusion, Avengers: Endgame is a fantastic movie filled with tons and tons of answers after what happened in Avengers: Infinity War and even more really engaging things that make it really good as a standalone movie. If you like Marvel, you'll LOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOVE this movie!!!!!! The ending is so mind-blowing and the rest of the movie is really good, and that FINAL BATTLE!!!! Even the TITLE CARD emphasizes how awesome the movie is by playing a powerful and heroic version of the Avengers theme. One more thing: you know how I said The Dark Knight was my favorite movie of all time? Well, now it's this. Avengers: Endgame. TOO MUCH YES. I can't wait for Phase 4 of the MCU!!!! Right up there with The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King and Harry Potter & The Deathly Hallows: Part 2 as just some of the BEST franchise endings ever.Funny thing: I went this ENTIRE review without mentioning Stan Lee's final cameo. Personally, it's not one of his BEST cameos, but it's still a funny cameo. God, I miss Stan Lee... he was awesome. Things are never gonna be the same without his cameos...

SPOILER WARNING!!!!going into this movie I was expecting it to be a good film, but I was blown away. I will be going to see it a second time sometime in the next week.From the trailers and teasers they released before the films release, I thought that there could be some early fight back against Thanos, but to see him decapitated was a complete shock. I didn't believe for one minute that this would be the last we saw of him though, and I was right. But the way that they re introduced him was a huge shock. The contrast from how Thanos was portrayed in Infinity War to Endgame was huge. We didn't need much if any Thanos screen time apart from major plot points and we didn't get any. Infinity War was Thanos' film, Endgame belongs to the heroes. And they didn't fail to deliver.They plot of the film was laid on pretty early, after the (I know I'm over using this word, I really could use a Thesaurus) shocking 5 year time jump which I never saw a jump of that length of time coming. They split into teams with one objective: go back in time to gather the infinity stones for themselves. And boy was that a fun part of this film. Seeing different angles, and behind the scenes as such moments from previous movies was the best way they could mark a film 10 years in the making: re visit previous films. Although many predicted this would happen, it was still incredible to see them actually do it. The reappearance of many known characters was great. From seeing The Ancient One, Rumlow, Loki again in New York, to seeing Jane Foster and Thor's Mother again on Asgard, it was brilliant.When Hawkeye and Black Widow arrived on Vormir to find the Soul Stone, I think everyone in the cinema knew what they needed to do, but didn't want to believe it. When the who will it be scene was playing out with each hero trying to sacrifice themselves, even when they wanted to make you think this is the end for the Black Widow, I was thinking 'no way will they kill her off, Hawkeye's time is up'. Well I couldn't of been more wrong, could I? She managed to sacrifice herself and that was the first of many occasions during this film my jaw was open in (yes I know, gimme a break) shock.After all the stones had been recovered by our heroes, they returned to Avengers HQ to build a glove and bring back their friends using the same snap Thanos did to get rid of them in the first place. Snap complete, and Laura Barton was on hand with her phone to reveal that they were back. 2014 Nebula, who played a really big role in this film, had already done her job in creating a window for her Father to enter through. Que 2014 Thanos' (honestly the amount of times my phone has written Thanks rather than Thanos is killing me) explosive entrance, in which I genuinely thought Ant-Man was a gonner, and the stage was set for the final FINAL shockdown. I MEAN SHOWDOWN. SHOOWWDOWN.All of our dusted heroes reappearing was probably my favourite moment from this 3 hour spectacle. Seeing the gathering of everyone we know, even Pepper in an iron suit for crying out loud, and Thanos never stood a chance. And by the way, the reunion of Peter Parker and Tony Stark was the scene that made me the most emotional. After a big final battle, featuring a brilliant team up of all the MCUs female heroes, it was down to the one and only Tony Stark to snap his own Infinity Gauntlet and get rid of Thanos for good. This was it. This was how that 1 chance in 14,000,605 outcomes had to happen. Tony Stark sacrificing himself to save the universe. And what made this even more special? The "I am Iron Man" quote that would be the last words to come from Tony Stark (well, a living Tony Stark at least). Cue the tears in the cinema, and my god did some people cry. There were people physically sobbing so loudly I struggled to here what was being said after. Yes, seriously. As big a death as this was, I think deep down a lot of people saw this one coming.After the snap, we see Tony's funeral where the camera pans through everyone there, including the kid from Iron Man 3 for some weird reason I still don't understand. And seeing Tony's daughter telling Happy she wants a cheeseburger was another brilliant throwback to where the MCU all started in Iron Man. Then comes the time for the reality stones to be put back where they belong in time. And who better to achieve this than Captain America. And what a way for Steve Rogers to go. He decided to stay in the past and live out his live the way he was intended. He finally got that dance with Peggy Carter, and lives to a ripe old age where we see him just seconds after he left the present. He chats with Sam Wilson and hands him the Captain America shield with Bucky looking on. For me, the perfect way to end Steve Rogers' story. And seeing Thor joining the Guardians of the Galaxy has got me SUPER excited.Overall this was by far my favourite MCU movie to date. It was brilliant. I laughed, I cheered and of course I cried. The perfect way to end 10 years worth of movies. 3 of the original 6 avengers are gone, but the future of the MCU is looking bright, and super duper exciting. I know there's a LOT I've missed out, but my fingers are hurting so this is all your getting. I can't wait to watch this again. It really was the Endgame.

This was a great movie, but I wasn't as satisfied as a lot of other people who gave this movie a perfect 10 and I definitely found some problems with this movie which took away from the experience.Things I liked:
All the fanservice. Seeing so many familiar faces and locations from the MCU was great.The unexpectedness of the events of the movie, given that they kill Thanos in the beginning and the 5 year time-jump that follows.How the movie handles both emotional depth and humor.There were a lot of great memorable individual scenes (Tony talking with his dad, Hawkeye and Black Widow's struggle to get the soul stone, the plan to get the Tesseract failing the first time, Cap saying "Hail Hydra" and "Avengers Assemble", Cap using Mjolnir, Tony's "I am Iron Man", etc.).All of the main characters got some important moments (Hawkeye and Ant-Man deserved them).The final battle and the scene where all Avengers show up was just fantastic.Tony and Cap got great send-off's.Things I did not like:
Thor. I get why he is this way, from both a narrative standpoint and because he would overpower Thanos if they did not go this route, but he's just a joke throughout the movie while he was one of my favourites in IW. He just wasn't satisfying here, but since this is not his last movie it is not a big problem.Hulk. I liked his fusion with Banner but he doesn't do any fighting at all. Where is his well-deserved rematch with Thanos? I really feel like he is underused in the MCU.The whole time-travel plotline leaves some plotholes, like how Captain America ended up in the same timeline as where he started in the ending of the movie and how Thanos, Gamora and his Black Order teleported to the future without having any Pym particles. If you can transport objects like Thanos' ship with multiple people inside through time, could the main crew not have done that when they split up to save up on Pym particles? Some of the plotholes can be resolved if you assume other things, but the fact that you have to do this, that these plotholes where never explained or addressed at all is already a problem.Thanos. This is by far the biggest problem of the movie for me. The 2014 Thanos is way more one-dimensional than the Thanos from IW. They spend an entire movie developing him just to throw that all away, and it lessens the impact of the final fight sequence (as glorious as it is) and makes it feel a little anticlimactic.The main conflict of the movie (bringing everyone from the snap back to life) is resolved right before the climax of the movie, making the actual climax and the plotline of 2014 Thanos going to the future feel slightly out of left field, again lessening the impact of the final fight and Tony's sacrifice.Some of these negatives are definitely nitpicks, but they did impact my enjoyment of the movie and I felt IW was the better movie. This was still a great watch overall though and I would recommend it to fans of the MCU.8/10 for me.

Review Title: Good movie but Russo brothers made a stupid mistake that has spoilt the ending.
Review:
What I have to admit and praise is the fact that this movie is really unpredictable.Everyone was thinking that the whole 3-hour-long plot will be focused on killing Thanos. And after 30 minutes you have him decapitated and you're thinking "So
now what?".That was the 1st Act's master move. You could empathize with the heroes who had their revenge and still nothing has changed. You could feel the void they feel. And you kept wondering what they are going to do now.So the 1st act was about grief and void.In the 2nd Act they start working with the time-machine. This part is very entertaining and nice. Although at first I felt it might be a little bit too complicated I think it's a very nice move to wrap up the whole story. You could see how the heroes has changed since then and feel some nostalgia.So the 2nd act is about memories, wrapping up the story and fun.And then comes the 3rd act - the final battle with Thanos and his army. And here's where Russo brothers made a stupid mistake. And as a consequence lost all the tension.What's the mistake about?In superheroes movies one of the most important thing is the characters' power level. You know that Black Widow is strong, Captain America is stronger, Hulk is even stronger and Thanos is even stronger than all of them combined. You have the hierarchy.It's very important since watching a fight between Black Widow and Thanos wouldn't give any suspense at all. You know their power levels, you know that Thanos is much stronger so you know the outcome of their fight. It's predictable.There are options to improve someone's power level. Iron Man gets better suits, Captain Marvel gets rid of the device that controls her, Thor gets a new axe and so on.What's exciting about Superhero movies is the fact that their Villains also gets stronger. In the 1st part they fought Loki. In the 2nd they fought Ultron. In the 3rd they fought Infinity-Gauntlet Thanos. And in the 4th...They fight Thanos and his army. More or less the same fight that they had in Wakanda. But there's one important difference. Thanos doesn't have the Infinity Gauntlet. So Endgame Thanos is much weaker than Infinity War Thanos. How much weaker? Maybe 2 maybe 5 maybe 10 times.Why it's that important?At the end of the Infinity War Thor arrives to Wakanda with Stormbreaker. He almost single-handedly destroys the whole Thanos' army, ships included. Then he wins with Infinity Gauntlet Thanos. Which means Infinity War's Thor is the most powerful creature in the Universe.He 'should've gone for the head' and he lets Thanos snap his fingers but the point has been made.Stormbreaker Thor > Infinity Gauntlet ThanosSo the Russo brothers went for making Thor weaker which was funny move. And it could be okay if they took into account that Endgame Thanos doesn't have the Gauntlet.So let's come back to the Endgame last fight.On the superheroes side:
You have out-of-shape but still Mjolnir-worthy Thor.
You have Captain Marvel.
You have Scarlett Witch.
You have Captain America with Mjolnir.
You have Dr Strange.And you have handful of other superheroes. And Wakanda's army.On the Villain's side:
You have Thanos without Infinity Gauntlet (like 2-5-10 times weaker than the one with a Gauntlet).
You have his disciples.
You have his army.It doesn't make sense on a Power Level dimension.As Thor has already defeated all the Villain's side with much stronger Thanos now it's obvious that they're going to win. Maybe he's out of shape and he lost like 50% of his power. But still he's stronger than the whole Villain's side combined.And he has Captain Marvel, Scarlett Witch, Captain America, Dr Stranger and all the other guys to help.So it's like watching Thanos vs. Black Widow. No tension at all.And that's why the last Act has been spoilt by a stupid mistake. Sorry to see that as I really wanted the most epic battle of the 22-movie series. What I had was a very predictable fight that has been somehow saved by an unpredictable ending with Tony Stark dying.What alternatives could we have?Just top of mind:1) Thanos gets the Gauntlet but doesn't snap his fingers. Due to the pride he decides to face the Avengers using the Infinity Stones like a badass.It would be a really entertaining fight with Thanos changing time, moving to portals, using power stone etc. Killing some of the heroes would also add more emotions to that.And we can really see what the whole series was about - the Stones. Stones which makes you superior to any superhero.Especially if we take into account the fact that Thanos is supersmart. He may not win with the Stormbreaker Thor but he can definitely outsmart him and the other Avengers in a fight.Apart from the one Avenger. Tony Stark. So the whole ending would be a 'who is smarter' battle between him and Tony Stark. And then Stark somehow gets the Gauntlet and snaps the fingers.2) Thanos gets the Gauntlet and gives the Avengers the tough choice.He throws a big rock on New York City (to wrap the story up). And now the Avengers have to decide - do we fight with Thanos or do we help innocent people survive?So they are about to go help the New Yorkers but Dr Strange stops them. He says "You can't go. We have only one chance. And we have to do it together. Whatever it takes.".How much better it would be? A lot. Even better than the Infinity War which I consider the best action-movie ever made.

Review Title: Film is inconsistent throughout its three acts, but is rewarding by the end
Review: The first act of this movie is a mixed bag. It tried to be very serious and emotional but they crack jokes like half the people on earth didn't just die. It leads to a very inconsistent mood, and it isn't helped by the fact that this first act is super boring and uneventful. They wasted a lot of time in the beginning just standing around talking about nothing, being sad and cracking jokes that didn't fit the vibe of the scene, but they skipped right over the whole time travel part. What a disappointing ending after a decade of films!I went into the film desperate to like it, and while it had a few twists and funny moments I was under impressed.The film starts on a ominous note, Captain Marvel flying through space to rescue Tony on his ship. Despite the ship being out of power, the food and air reserves used up, and being several lightyears from Earth, Captain Marvel 'carries' the ship back to Earth where Tony is alive and healed.So after Thanos has destroyed half the universes population he travels to 'The Garden' where the Avengers, or what remains of them, go to find him living in a shack; he was surprisingly easily defeated despite being so strong (even without the stones)
After they discover he's destroyed the stones and Thor murders him, they go about thier lives.Five years later it's interesting to see how they're doing; it's funny that Tony has escaped to the country and raised a family with Pepper (which he jokingly said he would do during Age of Ultron after seeing Clint's house)
I did like what Clint had become, a bit dark but really cool, I still says he's my favourite and deserves his own film.
I hate what happened to Thor, although it is understandable. Its interesting to see they made a New Asgard (but how did Meek, Valkyrie and Corg survive Thanos at the start of Infinity Wars?)I thought it was clever how they brought Ant-Man back, using the rat in the car impound after it was seemingly abandoned.Now here's where it really fell apart for me. Inspired by Ant-Mans story of the quantum realm, Tony and Bruce turn the quantum drive van into a time machine to test thier time travelling theory, and once its working they then suddenly gain a working time travel portal inside the Avengers headquarters?
But rather than going back to stop Thanos from using the stones they decide to split up to steal the stones from the past.Maybe they're right not to go back to stop him destroying half the universe because that would mean joining forces with thier previous selves during the battle in Wakanda, but what about intervening during the days between that event and Thanos destroying the stones?It is clever if they had to re-enact scene from previous films to fit with the story, but I felt this was only done to highlight that the stones have played a role in most of the previous film, which everyone knows anyway!?And going to events in the past let characters interact with people in the past that are gone; Thor spoke to his mother, Tony spoke to his father, Steve saw Peggy and many former Shield/Hydra agents then got to impersonate and fight himself, Banner got to speak to 'The Ancient One'.To sum up
Thor and Rocket went for the Reality stone/Aether during the events of Thor, the Dark World.Ant-Man, Steve and Tony went for the Mind and Space stones during the events of Avengers Assemble.
And when thier attempt for the Space stone failed Steve and Tony went to the army base where Steve was first trained in Captain America the First Avenger (although I think this will set some time after the film)Banner went for the Time stone, tagging along with Ant-Man, Steve and Tony during the events of Avengers Assemble.Clint and Natasha went for the Soul stone, technically this wasn't in any film until Thanos went to Vormir in Infinity Wars.It seemed rather presumptive here that Clint and Natasha both thought they were what the other loved most - Red Skull said that only sacrificing what you loved most would give the Soul stone, I knew they were friends but they were what each other love most? Natasha won the race to kill herself and Clint got the stone, presumably this is because he's already lost his family (everything he loved) but it is still very presumptive of Natasha.
If Cint had died what would happen? Last I heard Natasha loved Banner who is alive (more or less)(I would have liked to see Steve go for the Soul stone to encounter Red Skull)Rhody and Nebula went for the Power stone during the events of Guardians of the Galaxy.
I thought it was a very weak story how Thanos was able to see the future Nebula through the past Nebula, I realise she is the same person but how can they be that connected. As Rhody returns to his time they disable and capture Nebula.
It was clever that the past Nebula took her time travel gear to impersonate her future self.With all six stones together Banner uses thier own gauntlet (how did they get that? The last one had to be made by the Dwarfs on Nidavellir?) and everyone who is destroyed by the stone comes back - except Gamora and Natasha (as they were sacrificed to the Soul stone to aquire it I had thought they'd come back too?)When the past Thanos was then brought to the future by the past Nebula it began as a good fight scene - I thought giving Thor his new hammer/axe Stormbreaker stifled him in Infinity Wars, but now they had stolen Mjolnir from the past and he had both!
Then even more incredulously Steve was able to wield Mjolnir (he was 'unworthy' of Mjolnir during Age of Ultron. Since then he has become a rogue agent and is considered a criminal yet this made his worthy? Now there's a bad message to send out)
Steve even uses Mjolnir to summon lightning, I thought that was Thors power? Mjolnir is just a tool to focus that power!! Odin said so!!As before however thier combined efforts are no match for Thanos and he summons his army to destroy them. Then comes the cheesy heroic moment as a portal opens and Black Panther walks out from Wakanda, with Sam flying past and all those who were 'destroyed' there.
From another portal Dr Strange then emerges from Titan with the others who were destroyed there.
Suddenly hundreds more portals open as the Wakandan army emerges, and an army of sorcerers lead by Wong, and an army of Asgardians lead by Corg and Meek (followed by Valkyrie riding a Pagasus)
To complete the medley Ant-Man suddenly breaks through the wreckage as a giant to bring Banner, Rocket and Rhody to the fight (by his own admission Ant-Man cannot sustain that size for long, and has to rest afterwards so how does he stay like that?)Honestly I wouldn't be surprised to see a Ravenger army lead by Stallone!!The huge battle then commences with Clint, and Spider-Man trying to get the Gauntlet with the stones away. I would have liked to see Wasp do more in the fight.As Thanos orders his ship to fire down on the battleground, hitting his own men and the Avengers, Captain Marvel arrives and destroys the ship by crashing through it several times.
I am relieved that this is her first appearance in a while as she says she's been off world as every other planet is also dealing with thier loss after Thaos destroyed everything.As I said in my review of Captain Marvel film, she's almost boring to watch as she has no weaknesses and would make the others seem redundant.As Thanos manages to get the gauntlet with the stones the Avengers attack him with the same outcome as before.
In what I thought would be Thanos' downfall he was surprising able to fight off Captain Marvel (so she DOES have a weakness) then Tony switches out the gauntlet with the stones with Thanos' old broken gauntlet.
Clicking his own fingers Tony uses the stones to destroy Thanos and his army, except that it kills him too.After Tony's funeral and everyone has gone back to their normal lives (Thor meanwhile leaves with the Guardians of the Galaxy and makes Valkrie the Queen of New Asgard), Banner tasks Steve with returning the stone to thier place in history where they got them (because 'The Ancient One' said there would be consequences if he didn't)
Something that later occurred to me, the Space and Mind Stones (when they took them in the past) were inside Loki's staff and in the Tesseract which both had to be broken to obtain the Stones. So how did Steve return them?After returning the Stones Steve doesn't come back, instead an old man sitting on a bench nearby (who must have been there all the time?) reveals he is Steve and that he stayed in the past to live out his life as if he had not been frozen.
He then gives the Captain America shield to Sam and it cuts to a scene of him in the past with Peggy.Not the ending expected, and bit overly complicated. But as Tony, Steve and Natasha are gone will there be a new team in the future? And will Thor and Banner return?

Like most of the MCU, this film hits its highs. Snappy dialogue, likable characters, has some heart, laughs aplenty, huge cast, pop-culture references galore. You go see it and you enjoy yourself. But by the time you make it from your theater seat to your car, it's already started wearing off. This is much of my gripe with MCU films as a whole and much of my gripe with Endgame.I enjoyed the film. Like I said, fun. In the way that eating cotton candy is fun but leads to stomach pain minutes after you're done. Endgame suffers from too much fan-service at best and at worst is flat-out dumb and doesn't make sense.The Highs:
There's real heart here. The scenes with fathers and daughters got me in the feels. The Hawkeye opening with his family was really well-done. The Tony Stark daughter stuff was nice. I appreciated the opening third for giving in to the dark ending of the last film. I loved Fat Thor. And I thought the ending, though expected, was well executed.The Lows:
The middle chapter is a mess. I mean, a real mess. The time-traveling plot is so nonsensical that at one point they literally start rattling off other time-travel movies that don't make sense to excuse themselves. One of the lovable things about the MCU is it doesn't take itself too seriously, but this feels like a bridge too far. It literally doesn't make sense that they can change somethings and not others, and it's convoluted and it involves battery packs.The CGI overload gets tiresome. There are entire scenes where no one real is even on screen. You have giant purple Josh Brolin with a scrotum chin talking to blue lady with a mix of 6'8" Voldemort at Power Forward. I like some of this, but over-reliance on it feels too artificial and video-game like.The film tries to fit way too much in, such as the dark Hawkeye plotline that is referred to but mostly happens offscreen until one 2-minute fight. We didn't need to see that.While the device of literally traveling back through previous movies has a nostalgic touch, is that the best way to really wrap up the story? Or should we blaze a new trail here?Overall, the whole snap felt contrived, knowing that all the characters would come back and that the only one who would die were Cap and Iron Man, largely because the actors' contracts are up. We talked at the office about this going in and said Iron Man would die and Cap would likely go back to the '40s. So where's the surprising storytelling here?This is fun, entertaining popcorn fare, but it has zero depth and nothing truly fresh to offer.If you're reading this in the 2020s you probably agree this film doesn't hold up at all.Or you've gotten your hands on one of those magic Duracells.

Huge spoilers.Except for Doctor Who, I hate time travel. That is mostly because too many stories use it to undo things, which is fraught with peril both to the characters and to the writing. Paradoxes are inevitable. So, one of my biggest complaints consistently about Marvel is that the writers don't stick to their own rules, or any rules. Magical things happen and there is no explanation or cost.In this movie, the heroes spend a fair amount of screen time and angst explaining that you can't change the past. It is explained as if to say that ultimately it can't be done. This was by no means a small point in the story. So what does the story do? It changes things. Not the least of which is Captain America. And more to the point of the story, Thanos' history completely changes. (And how did he get that huge ship with thousands upon thousands of creatures through time?) Gamora's history also changes. And Nebula faces off with herself - that doesn't change time? In the present the three changed things and then none of them were there to do the things they did in the past, so the present should never happen. I hate time travel.Also, there are at least three major love stories set up in Infinity War. The threads continue, at least to some extent, in this movie. And at least two of them crash and burn. While that is not necessarily a writing flaw, it doesn't make me happy. Of the three, I'm not even counting Jane. Why did her love story disappear?So why did I really enjoy this movie? For one thing, the final conflict was awesome even if it was completely over the top. Another reason is that for 2 hours or more, there was a story with multiple threads. There was acting. There was humor. (I often think that Marvel humor is trite because they mix humor and tragedy with so little boundry, but in this movie, the humor was quicker and I don't know why, just better.) I loved big Hulk and fat Thor among other things.Other nitpicks: My first thought when the team lined up to go back in time, lamenting there was only one chance each, was - why don't you go grab some more formulas from Hank first? I think the writers masked this problem a little anyway given they had to save some for returning the stones later. Turns out I was right, but they just hadn't thought of getting it from Hank, YET.I didn't think the movie made it clear why Gamora didn't stick around for Quill. It was there, but you really have to think about it. My friend and I discussed it afterward and I didn't figure it out for a day. (She disappeared with Thanos when Stark snapped his fingers because she came through time to get there. And lest you say that explains my earlier complaint about her and Thanos changing their history, this still doesn't cover it because they still changed things before they poofed.Others have complained about Captain Marvel's inconsistencies and disappearence. She tries to explain that there are other problems in the universe. But as one Avenger responds as she disappears, the mess left by Thanos is the biggest problem and it affects the whole universe. Clearly, her more timely help would have made things far less uncertain. (And that's why the writers had to banish her for much of the movie - drama. It's a reason, just not one that justifies the way it's written.)So basically, my conclusion is - give me a fun, exciting story with good action and graphics (and some romance helps) and I might ignore the plot holes.

Review: The remaining Avengers must figure out a way to bring back their vanquished allies to destroy Thanos.A finely produced Marvel film, directors Anthony Russo and Joe Russo deliver on the mammoth task of concluding this phase of the MCU. End Game is packed with emotion, thrills and a number great action scenes. There's some interesting ideas - a washed up Thor, a vengeful Hawkeye, Gamora's 'return', Hulk's Bannerisms, fighting duplicates, revisiting past films, forgotten characters and much more.Russo's instalment is no doubt entertaining but after the credits roll and tears are shed for two of your favourite characters (many more, if you like root for the bad guys) 'fridge logic' creeps in.Christopher Markus, Stephen McFeely and other writers grapple with time travel concept and shrug it off, wiping their hands of their responsibilities seemingly walking away by throwing in some one-liners and diagrams. Maybe they threw the time kitchen sink in by design so that fans will debate for many years. And that's the major issue with End Game, it doesn't work within its own logic with the writers moving their own goal posts. Sadly, even Doctors Strange's 1 in 14 million outcome is flawed. It's difficult enough to do films based solely on time travel, like Back to the Future, Timecrimes, Predestination to name a few and End Game just doesn't wrap it up neatly. You really do have to leave you brain at the door to buy into it.Overall, a great film, with hard hitting emotional closure moments but unfortunately they've left it to 14 million fan theories to tie up the lose ends and as just you make sense of it - annoyingly it throws up another paradox issue or question.

Plot; The remaining Avengers attempt to reverse the result of Thanos' victory and restore the universe to its previous state.If building to the crescendo is tough, satisfyingly hitting that final note is, well, really tough. Thankfully the masterminds and powers that be in the MCU are up to the task. There have been bumps along the way leading to this point. Not every film in the MCU has been a classic, or frankly even good (Thor 2, Iron Man 3). But when it counts, Marvel delivers, and here it delivers in spades.Clocking in a shade under 3 hrs., Endgame never the less breezes by despite having significantly less action than any previous Avengers movie (@ least in ratio to its runtime). That's because by this point we're invested in story and character and the focus here is wisely there. Oh believe me there's action, but it's all the more satisfying because of the carefully crafted stakes. By this point the trick isn't finding emotional purchase. We come into the theater w/that already. The real trick is earning it, and Endgame does just that. Well done, everyone.

Review Title: Call it Marvel's last stand. Avengers: Endgame is an awesome finale to the Infinity Saga
Review:
Has the Marvel Cinematic Universe surpassed Star Wars when it comes to cultural icons? I would make the argument. I see more people wearing shirts of the Marvel heroes, kids are playing with the toys, adults still read the comics, and have several theme park attractions (at both Disney and Universal!). Even when it comes to content, Marvel has made more movies then Star Wars (compare Star Wars to its nine and the MCU's 23). The other piece of magic it has that no money could ever buy is its staying power. A lot like how Star Wars will continue to be introduced to new generations, the same will go for the MCU.Marvel also gave us one of the most talked about movies of last year, Avengers: Endgame. Most people I know, even my parents who don't watch superhero movies, were blown away with how much was thrown at them with action humor, and a shockingly bleak ending with half of life being erased and the villain winning. So how was Disney going to top it off in the next part? It's safe the say the Russo brothers did a phenomenal job showing where to go next in Avengers: Endgame. Is it perfect? For the most part.After Iron Man and Nebula are brought back to Earth by Captain Marvel, the surviving Avengers manage to track Thanos to try and undo the snap. Though they kill him, they also see that the stones were destroyed with the snap, thus making the snap permanent. Five years passes as the Earth and the rest of the universe cope with half of life gone. Some have moved on while others haven't. Iron Man has settled down with a family, Wakanda is without a king, many of the cosmic characters like Rocket Raccoon and Captain Marvel are dealing with the problems of space, Thor has become a fat drunk, Bruce Banner and Hulk have merged, and Captain America continues to cope with the fact he's more alone then ever.An new way to fix things comes in the answer of Scott Lang/Ant-Man who reveals that even though he was stuck in the quantum realm for five years, it only felt like five minutes to him. Seeing that time works and manipulates different at that level, the avengers convince Stark to help build a machine to shrink everyone. The goal is to split into teams and get the stones before Thanos does. It's a time heist to restore life and maybe get a second shot at defeating Thanos.Without revealing too much, Avengers: Endgame delivered more then I anticipated. This brings the infinity saga to a proper close that was started in Iron Man. Is it flawless? I wouldn't say that. But let's get to the good stuff first.The story and tone of the movie is great. This is a true epic that despite running over three hours, it doesn't feel like it. They could have added another half hour, but I probably wouldn't notice. Yes, there are a lot of slow burn moments like when the characters go through their struggles of lost friends, time travel, and fights, but all of it feels earned. I give credit to the script for still having some of the best "tongue-in-cheek" jokes in the series, and putting them in the story that's the most dramatic and somber.Like in Infinity War, the action is phenomenal. In fact, I don't even want to give it away, but with how the final act is set, it is a moment of movie magic that'll be remembered as much as the Death Star run in Star Wars and the ring being destroyed in Lord of the Rings. Every hero gets their shot and each one feels epic.
If the movie is flawed, its with the pacing. I don't mind a time jump, but not everything feels like an impact as the movie thinks it does. For example, when we see the Hulk, even though the effect is funny, I would have liked to have seen how he got there. Same thing for Hawkeye, Iron Man, and the cosmic characters. This is an instance where an extended cut would be welcome. Things flows better once the time heist plot starts and keeps it for the majority of the movie.I'll give nine infinity gauntlet comics out of ten. This is the moment where the orchestra plays it's big number. This is level eight of the Super Mario Bros. This is an awesome finale to a story that I don't know how Marvel and Disney are going to top this...nor do I think they ever will. If you haven't seen Infinity War yet, be sure to do before watching this. Endgame serves as a nice bookend to the series and I think everyone will be happy with this.

Review Title: My son and I watched a big part of our childhoods come to a satisfying conclusion.
Review: The MCU was something we shared from its start with Iron Man back when he was 8. He loved the Sam Raimi (sp?) Spider-Man movies as well, so you can imagine how excited he was when he heard about that character's reboot. I am so thankful to Marvel. They gave my son an epic story of heroism, friendship, sacrifice, and purpose. I got to revisit my childhood on the big screen in a way I never dreamed possible.

'Avengers: Endgame' continues from its previous instalment 'Avengers: Infinity War', where a chain of catastrophic events destroyed half the universe. The remaining Avengers now come together for one final time to reverse the actions of the evil Thanos and restore the order of the universe. But will they succeed?
Overwhelming. It best describes the final chapter that culminates Marvel Cinematic Universe's 21 iconic films into one. And that also describes the experience of watching your favourite superheroes come together for a singular goal, for one last time. Directors Anthony and Joe Russo ensure that the humongous build-up and the avalanche of expectations do not get the better of them. They deliver a largely wholesome product that is full of moments laced with action, emotion, comedy and drama. Writers Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely take you along, even if you haven't been following the franchise. They do an incredible job with the screenplay to balance emotions with visual spectacle. So if you're not a fan yet, chances are, you might become one after watching this instalment.While the screen time for each character is not equal, their significance in the story is. And there are enough surprises in store, as far as their fates are concerned. 'Endgame' delivers quite well on the emotional quotient, bringing out superpowers and vulnerabilities of its cinematic demigods through their measured performances. From an upright Captain America (Chris Evans) to a stoic Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson) and from a straight-faced Captain Marvel (Brie Larson) delivering the punches to the reassuring presence of Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.), 'Endgame' has it all and a lot more. Thanks to the conviction in performances, you also might just find yourself rooting for the bad guy, Thanos (Josh Brolin) at some point. However, it's the comic collective of Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Hulk (Mark Ruffalo) and Ant Man (Paul Rudd) that ensures there are enough lighter moments in this otherwise heartfelt finale.
The action becomes progressively intense, but never overbearing. In fact, it remains relevant and true to the narrative, such that it weaves in enough opportunities for major plot twists that even the diehard fans may not see coming. The extensive CGI work adds to the visual appeal, even in 2D.
For the non-fans, the film's explanatory tone might come across as a speed breaker at times, but for the fans, the same invokes hope and excitement, leading to constant gasps and howls.
Overall, 'Avengers: Endgame' is a befitting tribute to the Cinematic Universe that has spawned larger-than-life superheroes and super fans. At three hours plus, 'Endgame' delivers on a lot of its hallmark promises, leaving its fans with a range of emotions and fond memories.

Avengers: Endgame
2019
Dir: Anthony and Joe Russo
Runtime: 3 hr and 1 min
Rated: PG:13
WARNING: SPOILERS AHEAD
Synopsis: After the devastating events of "Avengers: Infinity War" the universe is in ruins. With the help of remaining allies, the Avengers band together once more to undo Thanos' actions and restore order to the universe.
Last year I wrote a pretty crummy review for Infinity War and I'm going to make up for it by doing this one the proper way. First and foremost let me say that this is truly a cinematic event, such an incredible way to bring all of these characters together for a finale that is the Infinity Saga. I really don't believe that something as grand as the MCU can be achieved after this nor do I believe that this can happen on this scale again. And I'm not even just saying this as a fan of the MCU but as a whole, the 11 years and 22 films, this was an amazing way to end the journey. So much thought was put into this storyline from day one, when Nick Fury was at Tony Stark's home and told him he's become apart of a bigger universe. This film was made for the fans with elements that the MCU is known for as well as pieces that are taken straight from the comics. But because of that it will cause some that have not been following the MCU or do not know any of the comic book history of these character won't have as much of an appreciation of the film.
Prior to the film being released the Russo brothers wanted to state that Infinity War is its own film. It's Thanos' story and they wanted that to be a complete story. The Avengers fought and Thanos won. So they wanted to make that separation that Endgame was going to be it's own film as well. They confirm this well with making the difference between Infinity War not being a "cliff hanger". It's portrayed so that Endgame starts it's own storyline with Infinity War being actually concluded within probably the first 30 mins of the film. Then the film continues to create a new story, its own plot line, and the characters are set up to execute their plan to save the universe. To sum it up you have the original six avengers along with Rhodey, Nebula, Ant-Man, and Rocket all still trying to put themselves back together after the events of Infinity War.
With a runtime of 3 hours I can say that the pacing of the film is pretty good. The film certainly could have been shorter but they would just be cutting out the emotional parts of the film. While in the first act of the film may seem a bit drawn out if you peel back the "curtain" of the MCU you see that what they were trying to portray was depression and loss. The first act of the film is spent exploring how each of these chcaracters are dealing with their failure. With the stakes being so high in Infinity War for our heroes to lose it's something they cannot live with. From Cap holding grief meetings about the ones that vanished in the decimation to Natasha having a small group of Avengers still trying to do good in the world. Before the second act is in motion there is a bit of prelude to the second act. While the rest of the Avengers have pretty much lost everything Tony Stark has gained and leading up the stakes for him are as high as they've ever been. The second act is like a walk down memory lane of the MCU. While time travel plays a pivotal part in the story its used to build up the finale. You get to see some great revisited scenes from the earlier MCU films. At first it seems like all is going according to plan when a rock is thrown into the plan which causes Cap and Ironman to adjust accordingly which gives a great almost tribute to the past of the two characters. Oh and speaking of time travel in the beginning of the second act the rules of time travel for this film are explained. So just know ahead of time that it does not follow the standard rules of cinema time travel. The third act of the film is the grand finale and it acts as a finale to the story arc of the Infinity saga. We get our showdown we've been waiting for along with the perfect send off for some of the core characters that couldn't have been done better. Considering most of the film is CGI it looks really really good. There is a scene toward the end where the CGI looks a bit choppy even on IMAX I saw it but if your not looking for it you won't notice it. The casting and characters are all on point with everyone playing the roles they've been playing for years now along with most of these actors being veterans in their own right. I've read a few articles already with talks of RDJ getting a nomination for the Oscars which I could see happening and would be amazing. Most of the time the only time these films win or get nominated it's for music or VFX. I really think RDJ could get a nomination for his role as Ironman in this. I would recommend this for anyone that's a fan of the franchise or the comics. Very small kids maybe not so much considering it's so long and the story is a little intricate. Absolutely a theater watch and I really feel bad for anyone that didn't get to experience this opening night.
5/5 Easily. I've only talked to a few people that didn't like the film but as I said before those are usually the ones that either haven't read the comics or haven't been keeping up with the MCU films. It's really remarkable that we live in a time where technology has caught up with my childhood dreams of seeing these characters on screen. Seeing Cap pick up that damn hammer and say "Avengers assemble" it was like seeing something I've wanted out of these films all along but didn't know it until it actually happened. This film isn't really to be seen and broken down as a film on its own but as an ending to an era that has been built up for the last 11 years.

Review Title: A Near Perfect Conclusion to the Previous Movies
Review: For a movie that was to address the bleak consequences of Thanos' snap in Infinity War, I was surprised by how much I laughed during the movie. But, it strikes a good balance, keeping humor in appropriate moments and amounts to keep you from spiraling into a deep depression. On top of that, the humor does help you experience the painful scenes more intensely, because you can't know pain without pleasure, and vice versa.One complaint I do have about the movie is that Tony Stark figured out time travel a bit too quickly. It was overly convenient, but considering the movie is 3 hours long, it's hard to build up that up and pay it off well, when you have so much more plot to get to.This movie really rewards you for watching all of the previous movies, and even makes one of the worst movies of the MCU, Thor: The Dark World, a prominent part of the movie, which I appreciate, because that could easily be left behind in the dust, but decided to include it and make it "belong to the family," so to speak. There are many pay-offs that have been teased and make you wonder, "How on earth did they remember that, and pay off that tiny little thing from 10 years ago?!?" However, this could never work as a standalone movie, as my father-in-law experienced watching the movie with my wife and I. He had never seen a Marvel movie before and jumped right into this one, and at the end said that he didn't like it.Avengers: Endgame wraps up the Infinity Saga nicely, while leaving some threads untied to continue the story for years to come.

Review Title: 2019's Greatest Movie Ever!! Everything is unforgettable
Review:
I've just seen Avengers: Endgame (2019) and it was the greatest moment I've ever experienced. If you read this review, first I had to warn you that there would be spoilers. I laughed and cried and sometimes I cheered for unusual and things I wanted to happen.
The acting was way better than last time in Avengers: Infinity War (2018). I really am impressed, especially Robert Downey Jr. and Chris Evans, they're the best!
The actions and fight scenes were the most EPIC. The scenes were mostly unforgettable. I could remember a lot after watching it for the first time. Every character were there (except Vision, Black Widow (cuz she's dead) and maybe M'Baku (I haven't seen him). There were portals everywhere and the final battle was a lot better than I had expected. Here are my top 10 best scenes of the movie:
1. "Portals" or "Avengers Assemble"
2. Iron-Man's Death and Funeral
3. Cap Wields Mjolnir
4. Banner mixed brains and brawns together into Professor Hulk
5. Cap passes the Shield to Sam Wilson to be the next Captain America
7. Black Widow's sacrifice
8. Thor chops off Thanos' head
9. Thor joins the Guardians of the Galaxy
10. Cap, Iron-Man and Thor vs Thanos
Some scenes were hilarious like Thor changed into an overweight man and ate junk food, drank beer and played Fortnite with Korg. Some were emotional when Iron-Man died and his funeral was attended by lots of people and Black Widow sacrificed for the soul stone. The lines were really iconic to me like "I am inevitable" by Thanos and Iron-Man's last words before he snapped his fingers "And I...am...Iron-Man". It was hilarious but then it got emotional that his mortal body couldn't hold the infinity stones and he died. I was crying so bad. The next sad thing I saw was that Steve Rogers retired being Captain America but I was glad that The Cap generation passed on to someone else and it was Falcon (Sam Wilson).
The sountrack was marvelous, better than in Infinity War. Alan Silvestri did an excellent job, especially "Portals", I liked that one most. The Marvel Studios intro wasn't how I expected it to be. It was a little unsuitable
The movie's 3 hours and 1 minute was well-used. No scenes were useless or unnecessary at all. The ending was moving but perfect and someday, I wanted to watch this again and again. I just hope it would deserve 2020's Oscars's Best Picture, Best VFX, Best Original Score, Best Costumes and more. Avengers: Endgame is the greatest movie of 2019 and perhaps one of the best of the 2010s and maybe of all time. The movie deserved a 9.9 from me out of 10

Review Title: Beautiful ending to an amazing story in which we took part for the last 10 years.
Review: It's amazing how I do not feel sad that this franchise finally came to an end, I guess I am satisfied with the way it ended, maybe it was the only right way..I was surprised that not many characters actually died in the movie, apart from Black Widow and Iron Man, Gamora is alive and well, that was confirmed by the directors and Loki obviously is going to alternate his future with him running with the tesseract. Captain America had the best possible ending, altho I expected that Barnes will be the next Captain America, since he is also a super soldier, but later on I found out that Sam was the one in the comics also, so no hard feelings. The first half an hour were average to say at least, but you can't expect action all the time in a 3 hour movie. The ending battle was breathtaking and it was worth it all the wait. Pepper's costume made by Stark was out of this world, I would really wish a stand alone film featuring Pepper continuing the legacy of our beloved Iron Man.

Now here we are at the Endgame. Iron Man said it in Age of Ultron. Dr. Strange in Infinity War. Currently it's the second highest-grossing film of all time, relegating Titanic to third place, and is only $400M away from overtaking Avatar. And it deserves to be right up there, because all three prompted the world to get off of their records and go to the cinema to be a part of a mini cultural movement. I remember when the first Avengers movie was announced, I counted down the days until it was finally shown. Going back further, I remember when I was kid my mom would buy me comic books, most of which were X-men titles but an Avenger one would slip through once in a while. So I really don't like Iron Man because he's too steely, Cap was boring, Black Widow was here then gone, Hawkeye was too arrogant, Hulk was just green and Thor piqued my interest. But when I got a copy of Avengers West Coast, Scarlet Witch mesmerized me and Vision (all white version) got me sold. I mean a witch in love with a robot in the 90s? As an introvert teen trying to find his way in life, these are the people that accompanied me in the tiny corners of a place I'd run and hide to.It's one thing to read about them, it's another to see them alive and moving on the big screen. Or half of them alive anyway. Endgame continues on after the snap, with those left behind trying to continue on after the loss they suffered. If there's one thing negative I can say about the movie, is that the first hour showing the impact of the loss didn't resonate with me. Maybe because I knew beforehand those gone will be brought back and I just have to go through the motions to get to it. Maybe my opinion will change as I watch it again in the future.Now on to the good parts:Final warning, detailed spoilers ahead...1) Captain America wielding Mjolnir (collective gasp from the audience)
2) That shot when Thanos's army was approaching and only Captain America was left standing with a broken shield
3) "On your left..."
4) Pepper Potts as Rescue
5) Avengers!....Assemble.
6) Ant man punching an alien ship
7) Spider-man and Iron Man hug. Remember in Homecoming Peter thought they were going to hug and Tony said we're not there yet? They're there now.
8) Passing of the gauntlet from Hawkeye to Captain Marvel
9) Scarlet Witch. The only other Avenger who could've killed Thanos if he didn't get help.
10) Captain Marvel's entry...and short hair...and destroying Thanos's warship single handedly.
11) All female Avengers rescuing Peter. People are divided about this, some saying it felt forced, that it was a little hypocritical but me, I'm here for it.
12) Captain Marvel's one on one with Thanos, that head but and Thanos needing an Infinity Stone to fend her off.
13) Steve coming back to pass on the shield to Sam.What comes next though? How do they top something as big as this? Well there are so many other story lines in the comic book they can translate into the big screen. The actors? Tom, Chad, Benedict and Brie are more than capable of soldiering on. There's also the TV series set for Loki, Bucky and Sam, and Scarlet Witch and Vision. Let's also not forget that Disney now hold the rights to X-Men. So my prediction of still talking about the MCU well way into my 50s is starting to become possible. We might've gotten Endgame, but it seems the game has just begun.
