Over 20 films and over 10 years leading up to this, the wait is finally over, all the questions have been answered.......sort of. Go to be honest even though, I am personally not a fan of the MCU or any other comic book films these days, I was in awe of what I was watching in certain moments. However this film is a bit of a rollercoaster to say the least, there is a lot to process so forgive me if I forget something.Just like with "Infinity War" the Russo Brothers deserve a lot of praise for the directing and story telling in this film. It has everything you could want from a film like this and especially if your a die hard fan of the franchise. Action packed, solid story, emotional punch but most importantly damn entertaining. Amazing from there standpoint what an achievement..........wonder what they will do next??As I have preluded to I am not a fan of the MCU or of the genre anymore, about 8-10 years ago I was a die hard fan but now couldn't care less........become less and less interesting. I am a victim of over saturation of comic book films. Therefore I probably in the minority when I say that this film has many positives and more importantly negatives as well. These are just my personal favourite moments or moments I hated......yes hated!!!PositivesThe cast throughout is fantastic across the board in what they are given to do, Im not gonna list them all go google them yourself. However there are a couple of standout performances and story lines/moments that were really breathtaking. Chris Evans just knocked it out of the park.....well he has done since 2011 but its even more impressive in this film. Just spectacular, has some fantastic scenes throughout showing a huge range in the character we've grown to love and route for. His ending is fantastic I couldn't have thought of a better way for Steve Rogers to exit the MCU just perfection.The other two standout performances are Paul Rudd and Brie Larson, again just own the screen when they are on it. Ant-Man is strange character for me because I thought his solo films were ok but not much more, felt he was much better suited in a team up film. That feeling is even more justified in this film, the character was used perfectly and Paul Rudd was fantastic, made his story interesting and pulled it in new directions. On the other hand I was really shocked in how much I liked Captain Marvel early in the year, but man did nothing prepare me for her film stealing performance. Its only a couple of moments here and there but wow just wow.NegativesSorry the fun is over, no film is perfect there are quite a few problems with this film, I almost ended up not like the film because of them. Firstly and the biggest elephant in the room...Thor/MCU Humour. What on earth were the Russo's thinking, from a character standpoint this is the only thing they got wrong......and they got it badly wrong. Its is so cringeworthy I cant bare to think... for me it just doesn't work. Its another example of the that dreaded MCU humour that I simply don't find funny, its not the first MCU film and it won't be the last with this problem.....over reliance on humour.The other two big problems are the pacing and the runtime of the film. Firstly the pacing is all over the place, for 1/3 of the film is slowly paced, which I have no problem, but its 180 degrees opposite of rest of the film. The last 1/3 is just going at hyper-speed. I have scrolled through the reviews for this movie and been gently and mildly amused at how opinions about this film yo-yo much the same as this cinematic presentation. I could detail a whole laundry list of things I enjoyed about this movie, but I have observed that other reviewers have done this extensively and so I want to concentrate on personal impressions at this time. Later on, we can talk about scientific howlers concerning Time Travel and relativistic physics and quantum mechanics.First of all, I am a member of the group who grew up with and lived through the Marvel Age of Comics. I fully understand and remember vividly how this all started and now where it has finally arrived. I understand with absolute clarity and certainty how Darth Vader is actually an extrapolation of Doctor Doom and in the end a recapitulation of his origin story. This being true no matter what George Lucas says about the benefits he derived from his mentor Joe Campbell, which is also evidently beyond dispute.I remember idly considering while collecting DC comics how I wished there was a style of comic book writing and illustration that was more dramatic, structured around greater conflict and a bit more virile and witty. That was when I discovered Marvel Comics. I felt like life was giving me what I was dreaming about. Following the chronology and evolution of the Marvel Experience has simply affirmed and strengthened my conviction that what you imagine can actually come true.AVENGERS: ENDGAME is everything a bunch of scrappy ghetto kids cracked wise about and exulted over between games of lob baseball. This while hearing some neighborhood child from across the street tell us that our mother just said we should come home now that it was getting dark. We who started out with this experience are simply amazed and delighted with how far and wide this phenomena has expanded. We remember the cheesy fan buttons and the little red vinyl records for the Merry Marvel Marching Society and Stan's Soapbox. I remember how, reading about Doctor Strange and his redemption from his own arrogance, as well as Prince Namor: The Submariner finding his way back to his long lost Kingdom, helped fuel and catalyze my own desire to be a writer. I also remember the Pandora's Box I opened up when I first assayed to learn How To Draw Comics The Marvel Way. Through it all, Stan Lee kept promoting and building with others what is now a vast public relations machine and went on to the Great Beyond having conferred to us a profound legacy in Literature and Art along with Jack Kirby and an immense cadre of other artists and writers.I finally can say this while now in my advanced age; being willing to admit after taking Ann Wilkinson's class in Child Literature at Wayne State University that almost any good children's book is usually superior in thematic content to your average comic book. The fact that I can now say this without anyone having to wrestle me to the floor, strikes me as a major turning point in my own maturation.I watched AVENGERS: ENDGAME and felt a significant chapter of my life coming successfully to a close. The baroque ranging in Time and Space between screams and witty asides was everything I dreamed the Marvel experience could be in my youth and then some. Even the speculation of Captain America about what life would be like simply married to Sharon Carter as an ordinary Joe seemed oddly fitting in this wacky universe where anything can happen and you can hear the Mighty Thor burping over his beer belly from too much ale.I also found myself reflecting on Rob Bryanton and his ideas in IMAGINING THE TENTH DIMENSION: A NEW WAY OF THINKING ABOUT TIME AND SPACE as I was watching this movie. This is the spirit of the best of Juvenile Science Fiction. That it lightly touches on ideas and themes that can be explored more deeply later in a salutary way and lead to greater growth and development.When we came to the rousing finale, I felt that my conviction that life can be what you imagine it to be was finally successfully rewarded and my faith in this belief irrefutably validated.The Marvel Universe has landed, and so can yours, too.Deal with it.

This is an amazing film. I love almost every aspect of this film. As a Marvel fan, I can definitely say that Avengers: Endgame is a love letter to the fans and provides a satisfying emotional conclusion. Let's get some negatives out of the way. Everything up until the Time Heist drags on and starts to get boring. I know that they need to set everything up for the 2nd and 3rd acts of the film but I wish they had done it better. The 2nd and 3rd acts of this film make up for this though. I also didn't like the explanation for the their time travel. The film basically states that anything the characters do in the past doesn't affect the future which makes no sense at all. I know that this is their own rule but it just makes no sense at all. Why would changing the past not affect the future at all. That would mean that Nebula would have disappeared when she killed her past self. The one other problem is that some of the jokes didn't work. The positives far outweigh the negatives though. The cast does an outstanding job especially all of the main Avengers. I loved watching them together with War Machine, Nebula, and Rocket. All the supporting characters also did an amazing job. The plot can get confusing sometimes but generally, it's understandable. The tone remains consistent throughout the film. It's sometimes funny when it needs to be funny and it's serious when it needs to be serious. The cinematography was fine. It wasn't anything special. The visual effects for this film are amazing though. The armies look mostly real and Thanos looks great as always. There is a lot of emotional weight to this film which kinda surprised me. I was expecting Hawkeye to die but I was generally surprised and sad when they killed off Black Widow. I was really sad when they killed Iron Man. I knew they were but I didn't know how they would kill him. It was incredibly satisfying to hear Iron Man say "I am Iron Man" one last time. His death is sad but satisfying. The funeral scene at the end of the film was so awesome and brought back some characters we haven't seen for a long time. The action in this film is probably the best in the MCU. The climactic battle at the end is in my opinion the best action scene in all of cinema. Captain America wielding Mjolnir was so awesome to watch. Personally, I loved the ending for Captain America. He got to live the life he never lived. Overall, Avengers: Endgame is a satisfying conclusion to the first 22 films in the MCU while boosting a very strong cast, some amazing action, and an immensely satisfying conclusion. I give Avengers: Endgame a 9.5/10.

Review Title: Great movie, but not the best...
Review: In my opinion, Infinity War is the best Marvel movie, not this one. I enjoyed the long runtime, as this is the last avengers movie, however they did not take advantage of that. The movie took a very long time to get going and they rushed all of the action into the end. All the characters that were brought back had almost no screen time because they all had to share it in about 40 minutes.The main thing that I didn't like was that the movie was immature. The jokes were great, as they always are in a marvel movie but maybe this time they went a little overboard. This was supposed to be the conclusion of a decade of movies but it was overshadowed by some of the immature jokes. The one I hated the most was that Thor was fat for the whole movie. It was funny at first but I feel like they could have made him fit again at the part where he summons the lightning and his armor at the end. Also I didn't like how Bruce was the Hulk the whole movie. Like Thor, he should not have been like that for the entire movie.The relationship between Hawkeye and black widow was great and the Budapest line was a nice touch, as the movie can't full circle. Black widow's death however was brushed over in way and once again overshadowed by Tony's death.Another big problem is that the ending didn't make a lot of sense. After everyone was snapped back to life, they were put in a world that had turned into a wasteland after five years, where everyone had aged but they didn't. How is it that Peter just goes back to school the next day as if nothing had happened? Not only should half of his class mates be 5 years older, but the school would most likely not even function, as all the governments of the world collapsed.Finally, during this movie we saw the immense power that the infinity stones have all together. If they were used to wipe out half of all life, bring them back, then wipe out Thanos's army, then can't they also bring back Tony and Nat?In conclusion, I enjoyed watching this movie very much. I just feel like the movie was more serious and dark, like Infinity War was. Putting all these points aside, I would definitely recommend this movie to people and would watch it again myself.

I want to start this review off by saying that I am the farthest thing from an MCU fanboy. Try as I might, I've never loved these movies to the level that I always felt that I should as a diehard Marvel comics fan. That's not to say that there haven't been some genuinely great films in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but there have been just as many misses as hits for me and I have yet to see one fully live up to the boundless potential of the rich source material. I didn't even like Infinity War, or the original Avengers for that matter. I say all of this so that when I make the claim that Avengers: Endgame may be the best superhero film of all time, you know I'm coming from a place of sincerity and not bias. I've waited 11 years to feel this way about an MCU film and now that I do, it feels incredible.Endgame's use of humor is easily the best of any film in the MCU. That's not to say it's just the funniest (Though it most likely is the funniest MCU film as well), but the humor actually services the story and the characters here in a way that's been largely unrealized outside of Gunn's Guardians films. Moments like Thor becoming a lazy, unsubstantial Xbox Live troll or Hulk becoming a mild-mannered, affably dorky goofball don't exist merely for memes and throwaway gags, they're genuine pushes to flesh out and develop these characters, showing how these diverse personalities each react to the tragedy of failure and deep personal loss in their own ways. We laugh at their hijinks the same way we can look back at our own tragic experiences with darker, reflective comedy. The humor is deceptively smarter than it was in previous MCU films and it services the story rather than having the story serve the humor, throwing childish things aside while still honoring the spirit that these films are known for. One of the biggest reasons why Infinity War didn't work for me was because the inconsistent humor clashed so heavily with the emotional stakes of the film. Here, however, the humor compliments the stakes instead.Speaking of, the emotional power of Endgame is leagues above its contemporaries in the MCU. Characters genuinely have so much to lose here, so much to put at stake just to see their friends and loved ones alive and well again. Difficult choices have to be made here with tremendous consequences. The film feels grounded and human in a way that so many superhero films, particularly MCU films, seem to forget. It's these heroes willingness to sacrifice so much, and the film's strict adherence to establishing the enormous depth of their gambles, that makes them so heroic, and in turn makes this possibly the best superhero film to date. Heroes are not tested by their victories, but by their failures and their ability to rise above and grow from them. Captain America, Thor, Iron Man, Black Widow and Hawkeye are forced to give nothing less than everything for the very hope of a better tomorrow and they don't all make it back unscathed. Some don't make it back at all, and their sacrifices are very much ultimate. Avengers: Endgame is about as inspiring and uplifting a superhero film as the genre's finest and fully captures what makes its comic book paragons so beloved by readers across the glove.Endgame's characterization of Thanos is vastly improved this time around as well. Thanos' refusal to accept the possibility of failure, even in an alternate timeline, and his abandonment of an ethical highground upon the mere possibility of defeat not only creates a fascinating parallel with The Avengers, it completely shatters the argument of Thanos as a sympathetic figure with noble ends. He's a child wielding power he lacks both the respect and the fortitude for, a sore loser who can't see past his own narrow, close minded vision. The Russo brothers clearly predicted the misguided internet following that Thanos and his absurd ideology would gather and Thanos' characterization in Endgame represents a thorough dismantling of his unearned positive reputation.The direction here is absolutely top notch. The choreography, editing and camera work behind the action scenes is absolutely outstanding; from the tracking shot of Ronin taking out Yakuza in Japan to the epic, apocalyptically scaled final battle with Thanos himself. Avengers: Endgame doesn't just feel epic and exhilarating, it absolutely earns those emotions. It feels like a massive scale event and a filmmaking experience in a way that I never thought possible for this franchise, while still never losing sight of the more human and grounded journeys of our heroes. Even minor side characters from previous films such as Black Widow, Hawkeye and Nebula have genuinely strong arcs here; Black Widow redeeming her brutal past once and for all through the love of her friends, Hawkeye learning to respect Black Widow enough to come to terms with her tragic decisions and Nebula finding her place in the universe beyond being the pet of Thanos. That Endgame is able to take these seemingly insignificant characters and give them genuinely nuanced and three-dimensional arcs while also further developing the main Avengers cast that have been around for nearly a decade now is a true testament to just how much of a marvel (no pun intended) it is from a storytelling perspective.I can't believe I'm saying this, but believe the hype with Avengers: Endgame. It is everything I could have ever wanted it to be and so much more. It fixes problems not just with Infinity War, not just with previous MCU films like the Avengers films and Doctor Strange, but even with the comics it's based on. You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll cheer and, best of all, the film will have earned it.

Review Title: An epic end to a decade of fantastic movies.
Review: There has never been any kind of cinematic event like it and there may never be one again, but Endgame is the kind of superheroic fanservice most people have only dreamed of.

I personally believe 2019's "Avengers: Endgame" is unduly revered. The movie is definitely a grandiose phenomenon and a monumental crossover of comics superheroes unlike ever precedented in live-action. But that doesn't mean that it's story structure is weaved strong, because it certainly is broken and a muddled mess in areas; I'll mention some aspects soon. And surely box office success does not denote that a movie is a product of quality, so anyone using that as an argument is ridiculous. Consider the financial profit of fast-food chains that are a detriment to health. People are sometimes easy; flash the lights on a hawker, crowds will be enticed into the carnival tent. Or Moths to a flame, if you prefer that analogy instead.Before my criticism, one must undoubtedly admit the climactic final act of "Avengers: Endgame" is unequaled by any movie in the superhero genre. When the resurrected allied heroes burst forth from a sky spattered array of magic portals to confront an epic battle, it was an exhilarating and gratifying culmination of over ten years of build. It was overflowing with tension and audience eagerness; sensing that as I watched it in the theatre. It's an undeniable thing. Unfortunately though, the movie's runtime is a purposelessly long, frustratingly boring, and uneventful slog to get there. Irritating. So much time wasted. And there were so many plot elements that were stupid and faulty. To save length, I will list some glaring ones:Hawkeye brought a baseball mitt back through the time portal, so that obviously means the Avengers could have brought back through innumerable vials of Pym particles to not have a finite supply for time travel. At least enough to not be worried of making any mistakes.Killing Thanos near the opening of the movie, also dissolved the characterization of Thanos for the climactic third act. There was no emotional satisfaction of Thanos when defeated. Why? Because the Thanos of the past has no relationship to the Avengers or awareness of what he did to them or who they are, so the confrontation and retribution of the protagonists to the antagonist is emotionally hollowed. The tension plug was pulled. The characters have then no interrelation to each other anymore and their arcs are not entwined to the same emotionally meaningful degree as before. In other words, when Thanos was decapitated early, that too killed his character and reverted him to a state of a bland villain mentally unaware to the story's contextual conflict.Black Widow and Hawkeye brawling in contest to obtain the soul stone was incredibly senseless. Sacrificing something you love was established as the stipulation to obtain the stone - so brawling to kill theirselves would not earn the stone for the other because suicide is self-inflicted! Hawkeye only earned the stone because he released Black Widow's arm to fall to her death, so the whole contest of suicide was pointless. The emotional tension attempted to be made in the scene is not that; it's ridiculous.Past Nebula during a scene robotically connects and manipulates the time portal machine to conjure past Thanos through the portal. What!? Then the Avengers allied version of Nebula could've bypassed the need for Pym particles and the whole plot dilemma and procurement of Pym particles was a colossal waste of time! Why have it in the plot then?Those are the most glaring that come to my mind, but there's plenty more. "Avengers: Endgame" is a mess. And the convoluted concept of narrative timelines and time-travel in general of such stories muddle any possibility of the movie making sense; there will always be questions and alternative decisions thought of by the audience. It's just backing oneself into a corner really. This movie is not deserving of the reverence it's received; the stuff I mentioned is obvious and indisputable. Aside from the culminating epic third act ensemble battle of characters, there's no merit to this movie. Please read the multi-issue comic book series this movie was derived from; it's far superior with its storytelling, has better content this movie cut, and has a broader cast of Marvel characters and concepts not limited by what is and isn't in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

In 2008, I was intrigued with what Marvel was planning out after seeing the first Iron Man and its post-credit scene explaining of a wider universe. Now to the present time with the MCU's latest installment Avengers: Endgame - all the heroes and allies we've come to know culminating from 22 MCU movies - leads to an end of a magnificent saga. I did not expect it to be so engaging and downright fun! Joe and Anthony Russo did a splendid job setting up this climactic film. Stars Robert Downey Jr, Mark Ruffalo, Chris Hemsworth, Chris Evans, Jeremy Renner, and Scarlett Johansson gave it their all with performances that made their characters as humorous, clever, or just plain deep. What a run alongside the additional familiar faces in this all-star cast. No words can express how much I enjoyed out of this 3-hour spectacle.Three weeks have passed since Infinity War. The Mad Titan Thanos (Josh Brolin) has successfully decimated half the Earth's population with a single snap and the surviving Avengers along with their few remaining allies must find their resolve by setting things right.My curiosity and adrenaline kept growing with each pivotal scene playing out to either interesting cameo appearances to a shock of disbelief and dismay that I even yelped loudly when the final stand commenced. Music composer Alan Silvestri (who has done many other hit cinematic projects in the past) provided an enthralling score that accompanies and compliments the most tragic and triumphant moments of the film. Not to mention the right balance of drama and humor that felt like a roller coaster ride that toyed with my emotions. There were a few people at my local theater that quietly wept as the final act played out and that really caught my attention other than just the huge action scenes onscreen alone. The fate and great sacrifice of Tony Stark in particular, was a nail biter for me since Downey Jr's performance felt so believable as a nearly decrepit who's been through so much trauma. Saddens me The Stan Lee, nor Jack Kirby didn't live to see this spectacle that they and their associates drew and wrote on pages of paper many decades ago, but I have to say their legacies live on as these characters have cemented themselves as living and breathing entities in the world of film.I now see what both critics and audiences alike meant about how brilliant this movie can make anyone laugh, cry, or simply stay engaged. Easter eggs and cameos are also fun to find, especially if it foreshadows potential new heroes yet to be shown. Sure, this movie is not meant for everybody who are likely not into the genre, let alone comics in general. Likewise, I'll admit some scenes did feel somewhat confusing in terms of how the story builds, namely the use of time travel as a plot device was a bit difficult to follow when the rules are applied differently here compared to other past films that used it extensively. Though what matters to me is I was not at all disappointed of the end result spanning 11 years in the making.I applaud them all. Well done, well done.

I am a big MCU Fan, and watched each and every of them. Infinity Wars is 9/10, if not 10/10 ....Leaving the cinema, my immediate comparison was Skyfall v Spectre. I was also very disappointed about Spectre .... but this time, my feelings were more mixed.The good parts of the Endgame are many, of course, if you are a die hard MCU Fan. Eg, "hail Hydra", Peggy Carter, the jokes and fun (kind of resembling Regarnok but the latter is better), the recap of the different historical MCU movie scenes in the pretext of tracing the different stones. MCU Fans would love them, and so do I. It brings back a lot of fond memories I have had in the past 11 years and this is great for a finale.However, plot inconsistencies and illogical science aka time travel/Cap staying in the past etc just made me mad. The quantum realm can be better used to develop a much better, exciting plots without having too many inconsistencies and messes. The conversation between the Ancient One and Banner was so vague (ok, they can say that's a mix of science and myth and magic, fine ....) and if the Russo Brothers thought this can "rationalise" the whole inconsistent plots, they are undermining our intelligence. This is not an under 12 movie.The complete demolition of Hulk and Thor are disastrous. I guess they try to plot Thor into a funny and cartoon like character possibly to prepare for the GOTG3 ? But if not,, this is a complete disaster. Hulk doesn't get a revenge he deserves.There is a funeral for Iron Man, but how about Romanofff ? Romanoff also deserves some better treatment in the movie.Transponding Thanos' spacecraft from the past to the present is also totally unbelievable and defying logic. More elaboration as to what Nebula has done is needed. The past Gamora stocked in the future ? Are they really plotting for GOTG3 ??Another disappointing scene is Captain Marvel was beaten by Thanos without the stones - ok the last blast was because Thanos used the Power Stone, but otherwise it seems Thanos' power was too strong without the stones. This was not explained even at the Infinity War - as Thanos was already having the Power Stone (by destroying Xander) when they destroyed Thor and Loki at the opening scene. Last time at Titan the crew without Captain Marvel almost got Thanos (but for Star Lord), but this time with Thor and his new power, with Iron Man, Cap and Cap Marvel they were completely dismantled ! In the last fight scene which was quite messy (the opening was hilarious but that's all), Cap Marvel was blasted by the Power Stone but she's Cap Marvel .... since then she disappeared until the funeral ! That's why Iron Man was dead ....So many logic defying plots that I originally gave this 5/10 but the additional score was a compliment of a finale and an ending of an era. The movie nicely sums up what we have experienced in the last 11 years but I do expect something out of the box, something terrific, something more logical. MCU this time does not live up to my expectations !

Review Title: The End of a Great Journey
Review: Avengers: Endgame had quite a few tasks to pull off. It had to be the culmination of 21 MCU movies, it had to finish up several character arcs, it needed to deliver on what Infinity War set up, and it still had to be a good movie. It succeeded in these regards. Endgame is a thrill ride, delivering a fast-paced story, and an extremely emotional finale to one of the most ambitious franchises in movie history. Oh, and it also had to make a ton of money. Mission accomplished. Anyway, it's impossible to talk about Endgame without the spoilers, so this is a spoiler-filled review.The thing with Endgame is that it's not a movie that stands on its own. In order to appreciate Endgame to its fullest, you needed be there at least for most of the time. This is a movie primarily for fans. But it's not like it's off-limits to non-fans. It's possible to appreciate this movie as a casual fan who's only seen a few MCU movies, but it won't have the same impact as on someone who's been here every step of the way.After Thanos destroys the Infinity Stones and is beheaded by Thor, the Avengers must go back in time to retrieve the stones to bring them to the present. The time travel aspect is rather confusing, but then again, time travel across the board is confusing. The idea is that you can't change the present or future, you can only change the past. It's quite something. As far as I know, Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban is the only movie to have time travel that makes sense. With the time travel, we get a trip down memory lane, as we see several events from the MCU unfold again, although from different angles. We get the Avengers arresting Loki, Star-Lord looking for the Power Stone, and the elevator scene from Winter Soldier recreated, although with their own twists. We also see some old friends, like the Ancient One and Frigga. All of this leads to one giant final conclusion, a grand, epic-scale battle between Thanos and his army and the completely assembled Avengers. The final battle is beyond epic and is undoubtedly the best action scene in any superhero movie, ever. This is where the epic moments happen; Cap lifts Mjolnir and says "Avengers, assemble," much to the joy of audiences everywhere. Some may complain that it's fanservice, but it's not. It's the natural progression of the story that they've been telling since 2012. They teased Cap with Mjolnir in Age of Ultron, and the moment was worth the wait. And with the constant addition of new heroes, having them come together for the final battle was the optimal way to cap off 21 movies.As far as the spoilers go, there are several. The big one, of course, is the death of Tony Stark. He dies using the stones to take down Thanos. Having watched this character develop since 2008, going from a cocky billionaire to the guy who'll do anything for his family and planet, it was sad to see him go, but at least he died heroically. And in this movie, Tony's arc is interesting because he found happiness, even after the snap. By coming back to the battle, he gives up everything he gained in those 5 years and makes his sacrifice at the end all the more selfless. Plus, everyone thought Cap was going to be the one to die. Speaking of Cap, there's what happened to him. He stays in the past to live with Peggy Carter. Given everything Cap went through over the years, it was a well-deserved victory, and a happy way to end the movie. It's a very bittersweet ending, kind of like Lord of the Rings. On one hand, Thanos is defeated, Cap got to live a happy life, but on the other, Tony Stark is dead and this grand story we've been following for so long is over. It's very emotional, especially for those of us who have been here for years. One spoiler that's kind of odd was Black Widow dying. On one hand, someone had to die at Vormir, as they can't not get the Soul Stone. On the other hand, it felt forced. At least we see how upset Hawkeye and the other Avengers are, so they at least recognize her sacrifice. And, of course, she did sacrifice herself to save the universe, which is, obviously, heroic. But since the movie moves at a rapid pace, it does feel rather rushed.Another aspect of this movie is how it finishes a 22-movie arc, that started way back in 2008. With that in mind, it's the end of an era, but it doesn't jump right in to the next. People were speculating about how things would be after Endgame, but we hardly know. People said Captain Marvel would be leading the Avengers. We don't know. It respects the old characters and doesn't shove them aside for the sake of the new ones. Heck, you're probably fine watching Endgame if you haven't seen Captain Marvel yet. That's not to say it ignores the new characters. The Captain Marvel vs Thanos fight is pretty cool. That leads to another aspect: no one in this movie feels useless. In Civil War, for instance, they could have reached that outcome without Spidey or Ant-Man. Here, everyone plays a part, and every snap survivor did something that led to the conclusion.With that in mind, this movie marks the beginning of a new phase in the MCU, and a new chapter for our heroes. Of course, Iron Man died, Black Widow died, and Cap is old now, as established, but Thor's arc is interesting. He does fall on hard times, but he does come back. Because he's Thor. He rises above his giving up phase and rediscovers himself. Oh, but shame on them for the Fortnite joke. That was disgraceful. Having Thor join the Guardians of the Galaxy was an interesting twist, but I'm not sure where that'll end up. I also have no idea what'll happen with Valkyrie and the Asgardians in Norway. But at least it leaves us interested. It doesn't jump right in to Phase 4. The other character with a shift is Thanos. There are two Thanos's. The one that dies 20 minutes into the movie, and 2014 Thanos. He shifts from balancing the universe to starting the universe over, which isn't as interesting as before, but it definitely raises the stakes. Nebula also has quite the interesting arc. While she doesn't undo the snap in this version, having both versions of her, one seeking Thanos' approval and the other to kill him, is an interesting contrast.Despite the impressive runtime, it doesn't feel that long. Heck, this movie is longer than Fellowship of the Ring, but doesn't feel any longer than Infinity War. This is, of course, due to how fast the movie moves, juggling the post-snap world, all 3 time travel quests, Thanos, and everything else. Most impressively, it's never boring. It's a bit of a slow start, but when it picks up, it really picks up. It starts showing where everyone is post-snap, which it couldn't not have. It doesn't dig too much in, but we see Cap leading group-therapy, an abandoned MLB stadium, and a memorial to the snap victims, which was a neat touch as that would undoubtedly get built like that if it were to happen in real life.Avengers: Endgame is a thrilling, epic, emotional conclusion to the Infinity Saga. It's been fun to follow the story of the Infinity Stones for all these years, and it is sad to see this story end. But, as the tagline says, part of the journey is the end.

11 years, and still going strong, MARVEL and Disney were very much banking on audiences reacting well to to the big and very expensive climax to the Infinity Saga. And since this film became extremely close to toppling Avatar as the highest grossing film of all time, I think it's safe to say that Avengers: Endgame did so and much more.With over half the cast brutally turned to ash at the end of the equally incredible Infinity War, writers, Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely did a superb job of wrapping up the loose ends left by Infinity War, while also wrapped up many open ended points from many other aspects of the past 22 movies. While many studios continue to try and often fail at an extensive movie universe, MARVEL has very rarely fumbled in this monstrous achievement. Despite a couple of duds, (looking at you, Incredible Hulk and Thor 2) the MCU has gone down with universal praise from fans, critics and general audiences goers alike.Nevertheless, while it's very easy to proclaim Endgame as being perfect upon first viewing, (I was admittedly guilty of that) it does have a couple of problems that can hold it back. The biggest being the inconsistent and had to understand concept of time travel. Markus and McFeely seemingly have a juxtaposing explanation compared to that of directors, Joe and Anthony Russo. Personally, I've merged both explanations, which has made re-watching the film just as enjoyable as it was at the midnight release.Additionally, some moments can be questionable, in particular one big crowd pleasing moment between the female heroes, coming together to support Captain Marvel. (Brie Larson) Ultimately, there was clear evidence that Larson's character didn't need the support. And while the moment is brilliant to watch and definitely deserves the inevitable applause it receives, the moment would be even better had Captain Marvel not been the one needing support. A very good example of what I mean can be seen in the video below.But despite some small hiccups, the majority of this narrative holds up brilliantly, and still holds up as a sublime book end for that part of the MCU's history. And while technically, Jon Watt's Spider-Man: Far From Home is the final Phase 3 film, and is technically the last film in this saga, Endgame is the big book end for the majority of it's cast, and is a tremendous and emotional send off for many of our beloved heroes.As we've come to expect from MARVEL, the production values for Endgame are off the scale, with tremendous special effects, which blends in so many elements and characters, while still appearing cohesive and a beautiful spectacle. Cinematography by Trent Opaloch was beautifully frame, full of dazzling colours at the right moments, thankfully avoiding the drab and darkly lit cinematography seen in Captain Marvel earlier in the year. Additionally, with the time travelling aspect to the narrative, Opaloch's cinematography also pays respect to the work of MCU cinematographers from past installments. Since the film was shot entirely in IMAX alongside Infinity War, some may find the standard cinemascope version (the most common version shown) to feel boxed in at times, or not framed as well. And while this can be noticeable, it doesn't hinder the film much, since everything you need to see is perfectly visible, with the IMAX versions also bringing extra detail on a larger scale. It's films like this that deserve to be shown and seen on the big-screen.Throughout the MCU's run, many aspects have improved. And the biggest improvement Endgame demonstrates is the sublime music by legendary composer, Alan Silvestri. After years of bland and unimaginative music, Silvestri really gets to be creative with this tremendous collection of music. His use of Jazz during the heist adds a unique tone to those moments, and the many inclusions of his empowering Avengers theme keeps the excitement coming. If MARVEL keeps giving composers the freedom to embrace their creativity, I look forward to continue seeing more work like this.Obviously, after 11 years of story-telling, it's hard to please everyone with what you put out, and for those audience members that somehow haven't seen Endgame or any previous MCU installment, I do highly recommend taking the journey as many fans and general audiences have done. Start at the beginning, and follow the journey. Because after completing the entire Infinity Saga (including Far From Home) I can safely say that Endgame left me dazzled, shocked, but ultimately satisfied. And even with my minor problems, it's easy to look past, and just be entertained by this thrilling adventure. What else is there to say but... Avengers Assemble!SCORES
Story 4/5
Characters 5/5
Production 4.5/5
Acting 5/5
Music 5/5Overall - 4.7/5

It has been 11 years since the debut of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The surprise hit and excellent movie, Iron Man, paved way for one of if not the best movie franchises ever conceived. It has been a total of 21 films (some better than others but all consistently good) with many great characters, plot twists and turns. Now, to see it finally come to an end with Avengers Endgame was exciting.Avengers Endgame is directed by the now famous Russo Brothers. This duo were the ones responsible for the brilliant Captain America The Winter Soldier and Civil War as well the previous Avengers movie, Infinite War. They have done a great job with each movie and have done an incredible job of bringing and end to the MCU as we know it with Endgame.Endgame first takes place in the near future with the Avengers all demoralised after their brutal loss to Thanos. Their loss results in not just the loss of 50% of the civilised universe, but every animal that lives in it. The result is an empty self destructive Earth full of people struggling to deal with the immense loss that each and every person has suffered. Because of this pain, the Avengers decide to take the fight to Thanos and the result amounts to nothing, just more loss. After an extended period of time, we see that each hero has been struggling to deal with the loss in their own way, they come together to follow through a plan to undo what has happened. The result is an interesting ambitious story, one that I will not spoil here.I will say that the plan the Avengers sets in motion is quite different for the MCU and was very ambitious for a film of this magnitude. It handles the subject very differently from others out there and can be a bit hard to follow for some. Either way, it leads to a lot of great action set pieces and many call backs to previous films. We see a lot of great characters return, it should make fans of the MCU very happy.In terms of acting, this is about as good as it can be. Chris Hemsworth's Thor is still emotionally destroyed after the events of Ragnarok and he does a great job of portraying it. Chris Evans is great as the always plucky Captain America and Robert Downey Jr. without a doubt sets the bar incredibly high. He has moments in this film which I would consider his best work, period. No questions asked. He delivers like no other in Endgame and his acting will no doubt pluck at those heart strings. The biggest surprise of the lot is Jeremy Brenner as Clint (Hawkeye). Not only does he go from supporting character up to a heavy lead role, he absolutely delivers. His story arc is one of the more entertaining and darkest. He's a great actor with a great character, one that deserved to shine so bright after all these years.There's a lot of humour in the film. Those that liked the humour in Thor Ragnarok will be very happy here. It helps keep the tone of the film from being too bleak and depressing. There are moments in the film which are just laugh out loud funny. There are others which are quite subtle, like the infamous "Deep Fried Kebab" sign in Infinite War, which was good fun. Be prepared for a lot of swear words, if that is something you don't like or don't want your kids hearing. Obviously with the frustrations of the hero's, they bark out some naughty words as most adults do. It's otherwise fairly suitable for kids and certainly a film that would have blown my mind as a little one.For such a brilliant film its not quite a 10/10 film. I didn't like the way Captain Marvel was used in the film. She just appears in the movie without an introduction or explanation. She literally just turns up looking smug and it amounts to very little. She's there ten minutes tops at the start and then doesn't show up until the end. It takes a little focus off of the original team, who this movie should be and isOverall, I do think this is better than Avengers Infinite War and is definitely a good two part movie, it's definitely one of the greatest superhero movies ever made. I loved every so much of it and it really didn't feel like 3 hours. The movie had its deep emotional moments, it had its laugh out funny moments and had so many great action scenes. This is a superb film. Both directors deserve a lot of credit for pulling off a project of this magnitude with such success and is mightly impressive. If you've enjoyable any of the previous MCU films, you'll likely enjoy this.

Review Title: As the capstone of the MCU it succeeds, however.....
Review: The more I think about the plot holes, character arcs, and use of time travel the less I actually enjoy it.Avengers: Endgame is the capstone movie and conclusion of 10 years of Marvel movies as envisioned by Kevin Feige. While Infinity War successfully brought together almost all of the Marvel movie characters onto the big screen - Endgame focuses on the original core Avengers which gives it a more intimate and character-driven feel but less epic than Infinity War.This more intimate feel lets the first act of the movie, which focuses on the aftermath of the snap, shine better than the middle and climax in my opinion. We find our heroes living their lives and doing their best (or not, we'll talk more about that in a bit) to assuage their pain and move on: Captain America holds counseling sessions with survivors, Tony Stark has a young daughter who he loves dearly, and Thor, well, let's just say you may have heard a few nasty words from him on Xbox Live. He's also fat now. Lazy. Probably not worthy anymore. And I have to say his arc in this film is what brought the movie down for me. In Infinity War and previous movies, he's had to overcome his own arrogance, some red stuff, family drama and taking a supernova to the chest. While I understand failing to take out Thanos and letting half of all life get extinguished would get you down in the dumps - the beer-swilling, Xbox-playing, shutin seemed like a gag that went on way too long. I absolutely hated Thor's arc in this movie. Which brings me to Hulk, or should I say Professor Hulk now. Somehow, in the 5-years between them finding (and killing) Thanos, Bruce Banner somehow figured out how to merge his personality and the Hulk's into basically a big green mishmash of Hulk and Banner resulting in an almost-Hulk with the personality of Dr. Banner. Again, gimmicky at first and useful to move some of the plotpoints along (the reverse snap) but ultimately wasted as Hulk never had a chance to redeem himself, even slightly, against Thanos. Thor and Hulk were my biggest two problems with the movie.The second act of the movie finds the Avengers going on a quest to obtain the Infinity stones by engaging in a "Time Heist". Yes, there is time travel in this movie which if you don't pay attention and/or haven't watched the previous Avengers movies may end up confusing you. Albeit, it was a very cool ode to the previous movies in the Avengers' saga. Ultimately, it just was not coherent enough, for me anyway. Oh and we had better thank that rat the accidentally walked over the buttons and reactivated the quantum tunnel in AntMan's van. Way too convenient for my tastes.In the final act of the movie, the Avengers do manage to get all the Infinity Stones and reverse the snap. But it was not without cost and of course, not without some splinter in their plans. A mighty big splinter. "Bad" Nebula replaced "good" Nebula and let "past" Thanos travel through the time portal thus threatening all the work they did to get the Infinity Stones. However, this isn't the Thanos we remember from Infinity War, this Thanos has been reduced to a two-bit villain who now just wants to snap everything away and start over; still formidable mind you, but with none of the depth of Infinity Thanos. Quite disappointing. I know this movie wasn't his but it would have helped to feel like the Avengers' plans could have been spoiled if he had been a more threatening villain. But he wasn't and also took the movie down for me.I know it sounds like I'm dumping all over this movie but the moments that shined? They really stood out. Good ol' Cap weilding Mjolnir; Iron Man snapping away Thanos and his army; the end battle scene and Tony's funeral, which was really touching. But that's about it.All in all, I did enjoy the movie but in no way did it live up to the hype for me.

Review Title: Three moments made "Avengers: Endgame" terrific but not a masterpiece
Review: Most fans expected that "Avengers: Endgame" will resort to time travel to make everything right. It is the same idea of "X-Men: Days of Future Past".Three moments made "Avengers: Endgame" terrific but not a masterpiece, the 1st one is killing Thanos by Thor at the beginning, 2nd one is the sacrifice of Black Widow, and the last one is the death of Iron Man, actually these three unexpected moments shocked all Avengers fans.I have also some negative comments starting with the purpose of Captain Marvel in Endgame!! Actually the only role for her is saving Iron man from a lonely death in space!! The other thing is the final battle, in my humble opinion, it was chaotic as same as White Walker battle in Game of Thrones, also the time travel was a bit hasty and unconvinced, especially in the way of retrieving the infinity stones.Anyway, "Avengers: Endgame" is the final movie in the Avengers series, and its ending is a good way to say goodbye.

Review Title: Beautiful, epic, poetic; a gift to the fans
Review: This was it, the conclusion of the infinity saga, the past 22 films, and setting up the future for a new generation of the mcu. This film really did give fans what they wanted, and the way the movies ties EVERYTHING together from all the movies was beautiful. I've seen a lot of other reviews saying how the time travel and Thor stuff were problems but honestly I understand it completely. Thor lost everything, his brother, best friend, mother, father, Asgard, everything. On top of that he failed to stop thanos in infinity war, and his guilt carries on in this film. A lot of people hated the direction Thor went in this movie, and I wasn't a fan either, but I understand why. As for the time travel, it does create a lot of plot holes, but nonetheless the movie was touching and brought the mcu full circle. The last battle where EVERYONE came through to fight thanos and his army was beautiful. The art behind this scene was amazing. It showed the mcu as a whole and what it really is, and then tony, the one who started it all, also ended it all and made the ultimate heroic sacrifice so the marvel cinematic universe would live on. It's poetic how this movie ends, it really does conclude the last chapter of the mcu, and it sets up the new one beautifully. Iron man being the one to save the universe was touching and perfect. Of course this move was flawed, but it definitely did justice to fans and the mcu. I'm exited for what's in store next.

Review Title: There is only one end, and everything before it is just progress (c)
Review: Exactly a year has passed since the mighty titan Thanos made a fatal click, mercilessly spraying half of the living beings in the universe. Then this bold and unexpected ending shocked many, forcing them to wait for the final round with even greater trepidation. What kind of theories were not built by fans about the upcoming sequel - one is crazier than the other, but everyone agreed that it would be something grandiose, epoch-making, claiming to be another box office record. And now the painfully familiar hype is repeated, cinemas are bursting with hungry crowds and circuses, and those who have already had a chance to see this product, are ecstatic about what they saw. Or is it still not abiding?.."Infinity War", without exaggeration, brought the comic genre to a new level. It turned out that even in a story stuffed to the brim with fantastic creatures and superheroes, there may be a place for notes of drama, a colorful villain with a clear motivation, moderately pretentious speeches and, most importantly, the best character interaction in the history of the comic book adaptation. As a result, we are no longer just a humorous blockbuster with an armful of special effects, but a pretty serious movie that causes genuine emotions, and sometimes even dumb admiration. Long before the premiere, the Russo brothers said that the upcoming "Finale" and the "Infinity War" preceding it, in fact, are one big film divided into two parts a la "The Lord of the Rings". However, if "The Return of the King" organically fit into the canvas, becoming the best film of the trilogy, then "Avengers: Finale", alas, completely lost to its predecessor, spoiling everything that allowed "Infinity War" to break out of its genre and win praise from people far from the world of comics.The film begins very promisingly. Against the background of the prevailing gloom and general hopelessness, the heroes try to somehow fix the situation, but in the end they only experience bitter disappointment. Everyone copes with this in different ways: Tony Stark, who miraculously escaped from the space desert, settles in the forest with his wife, Captain America runs a therapeutic circle, Thor turns into an alcoholic and a glutton, and Hawkeye, who lost his family, like Yagami Light, punishes criminals in different parts of the planet. Dr. Benner uses the allotted time to establish contact with his green neighbor, and only the Black Widow, being a professional to the core, coordinates the actions of the remaining superheroes, including the Warrior, the orphaned raccoon and Captain Marvel, who joined them. It would seem that such an oppressive atmosphere was supposed to bring the necessary drama, but in the end the viewer feels only a deleterious delay for an entertaining movie. The move does not work properly, as general despondency and mass depression are diluted by an endless stream of humor. Of course, jokes-jokes have long become a well-known feature of Marvel films, and it would be madness to abandon them, but scenes with tombstones and crying people a priori will never get along with scenes where we are shown a fat Thor and the Hulk riding a truck to cheerful music. The artificiality of what is happening is evident in almost every frame, and the viewer simply cannot feel all the pain of losses together with the heroes. As a result, the drama ceases to be a drama, and the absence of any action at the initial stage makes the film bland and ordinary at all. The balance in the narrative that Infinity War could boast of was completely lost. If there for the first hour we could observe the Hulk's fight with Thanos, the scuffle of the titan's retinue with the defenders of the Earth and the harsh exit of the Cap, which were proportionally interspersed with meaningful conversations, then the "Finale" cannot boast of anything like this. The drama does not work, there is no action, and before us is almost a product that claims to be the reference picture of the genre.To some extent, it turns out to be cured of the disease in the second third of the film, when Ant-Man comes to the forefront with his grandiose plan. Here, references to popular paintings of the past, which amuse much better than silly jokes, have come in very handy. Well, the plan itself, in general, did not come as a surprise, because for anyone who is familiar with the fantastic crafts of famous directors, such an idea will be a priority. Scenario-wise, this move is logical and correct, since the Russo brothers kill not even two, but three birds with one stone: they link all the films of the series together, which looks reasonable and justified, play on nostalgic feelings and, in fact, move the plot in the right direction. However, there are problems with the implementation again. The authors of the film do not offer any clear rules, and in some places this excursion into the past looks like a saddle on a cow. There is no need to worry about the heroes, because their actions in the past do not affect events in the future in any way. It is a pity that the screenwriters were too lazy to complicate the plot layers with any creative ideas, leaving the viewer alone with their questions, which, upon closer examination, multiply exponentially. The only advantage is the opportunity to look at the Avengers through the eyes of Marty McFly with the help of a number of augmented and expanded scenes. Creative, fresh and cheerful.Thanos' exit. The third phase of the film is by far the coolest and most epic. The mighty titan turned out to be an intelligent and respectable opponent. Appearing in front of an impoverished squad of avengers in his shining armor, he cut the ribbon with a huge two-handed sword and opened the way for unrestrained computer action. Thus, the authors seemed to apologize for the "stagnation era" reigning in the first half of the film. The unfolding battle is filled with references to comics, blood, pain and fear for the fate of the defenders of the Earth. The culmination was the clash of the united forces of good with the legions of Chitauri and the entire retinue of the enraged Thanos. It looks really epic. It is no exaggeration to say that since the Battle of Minas Tirith, cinema has not seen such an impressive on-screen battle.The entire Marvel movie series is filled with contradictions. Over the long ten years, studio bosses have revealed 22 paintings to the world, among which there were both recognized masterpieces and frankly passing tapes. And this epic ended on an equally contradictory note. On the one hand, the "Finale" competently summed up the events of past paintings, put everything in its place with a sin in half and was even able to delight with an epic battle at the end. But on the other hand, the final part was supposed to be the crown of creation, the best picture of the series, which, alas, did not become. After all, from the point of view of plot construction, character interaction, drama and action, the "Finale" lost not only to the "Infinity War", but also to the first "Avengers", who were inferior to it only in terms of scale. An attempt to sit on three chairs at once did not lead to anything good, and the fear of moving away from the template and introducing something new eventually deprived the long-awaited film product of due originality, turning it into an ordinary pop gum.

For me this movie was like one of those meals where you were really enjoying it at the time, but then you ate too much and began to feel queasy and bloated, and later regretted having eaten so much and vow never to eat so much again.All the usual stylistic ingredients are present and skillfully executed, but by the end it is apparent that bad decisions have made which have undermined the very fabric of the MCU you previously knew and loved.Tony Stark - "I just need you to know my priorities. Bring back everyone we lost, hopefully. Keep what I found, definitely..."Screenwriters Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely decided that Tony Stark's death was inevitable... as a "(move) to selflessness". They felt that his death was earned after granting him "the perfect retirement life," adding, "That's the life he's been striving for... They got married, they had a kid, it was great. It's a good death. It doesn't feel like a tragedy. It feels like a heroic, finished life."Really? Maybe ask his daughter how she feels about that when she grows up, not to mention everyone else, who were condemned to endure the 5 years of suffering and loss, and then live with the trauma of those experiences forever after, all so that one person, Tony Stark, can preserve his child and the happy times he had with Pepper.Tony's feelings are very human, but not very heroic. On a personal level the trade off looks fine, Stark allowed to keep his 5 years of happy memories before risking his life to restore the Universe. However, looking at the bigger picture, it becomes monumentally "selfish" rather than "selfless".Steve Rogers - "I thought, after everything that's happened -- maybe I should try out some of that life Tony always told me to get."Sam Wilson - "Only thing bumming me out is now I live in a world without Captain America."Exactly, Captain America trades in his life as a hero for that of an ordinary person, and all those good deeds he did and all the people he saved as a hero in that version of his life are therefore not saved and all those villains he foiled are allowed to have their evil way and America is probably being run by Hydra.Again a very human desire but not a very heroic outcome when you examine the big picture and the type of person Steve Rogers was designed to be just would not do that. Even mixed up teenager Peter Parker knows that "with great power there must also come great responsibility" so there is no way Cap would abandon his. I'm not against characters developing and learning for their experiences and the situations they encounter during the telling of their story, but in the end they need to remain true to the essence of what their character represents.Of course we know there are 14,000,605 plus alternative futures, or multiverses, or whatever, which may contain happy Tony Starks and Steve Rogers', but in that case, why bother to try and change this particular one? But lets not go down the time travel rabbit hole just yetSmart Hulk - "Eighteen months in the Gamma Lab. I put the brains and the brawn together. And now look at me. Best of both worlds."Or the worst of all possible Worlds?Hulk without his raw overpowering emotion is no longer the HulkUltimately what is the point of difference for a Hulk who is fully in control of himself?Thor - It's time to be who I am, rather than who I'm supposed to be."Any Thor who has doubts about who he is and his place in the World is just not Thor. His arrogance has been the well spring of the humour in his stories and was the reason he was sent to Earth in the first place. Thor, if not literally a "God", is a member of a royal family that leads a race of super-powerful beings. Alexander the Great or Julius Caesar or Napoleon did not abandon their destiny and neither would Thor, because that is the type of hero he was designed to be.And finally we come to the rabbit hole that is time travel. Specifically time travel as the last refuge of failed writing, or the easy way out for lazy writing. When the authors have painted themselves into a corner from which there is not sensible way out.Unless the story is specifically centered around exploring the concept and implications of time travel, or is a comedy, I believe it is a subject that should be avoided, because it is too complex for anyone with a brain smaller than Stephen Hawking to cope with reconciling the ramifications (which includes 99.9% of all movie script writers). All the paradoxical problems that arise as a result of it can easily pull the rug out from under not only the current movie but those that went before.And so here we are with a selfish Tony Stark who deliberately condemned everyone in the Universe to 5 years of torture as the price for his own personal piece of mind, a Captain America who abandons everything he ever stood for, a Hulk who no longer the Hulk (instead a big green Ben Grimm with Reed Richards brains) and a Thor who doesn't really know who he is...Inferius!

Honestly, this has to be one of the best marvel movies I've ever seen, but although I feel like the plot could've done better and they really didn't have to kill off my boy Iron Man like that but anyways the movie was great and will always be a hall of fame banger.

Review Title: Not what I expected, but what I needed!!
Review:
The end of an era... Avengers: Endgame is directed by the Russo brothers and written by Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely. Starring Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Mark Ruffalo, Chris Hemsworth, Scarlett Johansson, Jeremy Renner, Josh Brolin and all the cast of the previous MCU movies.After what Thanos did in Avengers: Infinity War, the Avengers gathering for one last time together to face the biggest threat of all time again, but this time, they're getting the help they needed last time... The epic conclusion of 3 phases of the MCU is here... So let's talk about it!If u read my review of Avengers: Infinity War so u know that this is my favorite movie of the MCU, and it still is.. unfortunately, why? Because I wanted this one to be the best of the MCU, but it's not.. let's go in depth about it, but don't worry, this one will have no spoilers.The MCU always had those delightful superheros and overpowered supervillains, with there first look at Thanos at the end of The Avengers, and I couldn't wait to see the Avengers vs Thanos, untill we got it in Infinity War, and I had my issues with it.. so I had to wait for the Endgame to see a rematch.. but more epic, u know!Let's start with the pros cause this one has plenty of them! Avengers: Endgame is so charming and humorous, even more than I actually expected.. even more than I needed! The humor sometimes felt there, and sometimes it did not... It also has one of the best performances so far, I won't be surprised if Robert Downey Jr. was nominated for an Oscar, because he gave us his best in this movie.The movie is 3 hours 2 min long, so it's a little risky, because the movie doesn't have to offer during the entire duration of this movie and that's a con, I know.. but the director and the cast knew how to make this movie catching from the moment it began to the moment it ended.. seriously, guys u won't feel like it's 3 hours long, yeah some scenes were so unnecessary, they just added time to the movie.. but still it's fun to see them this long one last time!The action sequences r not as much as Infinity War.. but I saw that coming from the trailer, because it had no fighting scenes, or anything.. it has some, but like Infinity War. But it has that one epic final fight that we all wanted to see, it's so epic that we couldn't just stop screaming during the entire fight! Right there, that epic scene overcome the Wakanda fight scene.. but didn't overcome the Titan fight scene, which contain the Avengers vs Thanos. We'll get to that point in the spoiler review.The movie also has those very emotional scenes, that will touch everyone's heart, even more than Infinity War... Way way more than Infinity War.At the beginning of the movie, u feel like this movie is gonna be the fastest movie ever, but I didn't feel like, cause I knew the way the movie is gonna go after then, and it took more time to do even that! The first act was so slow and dramatic, I love how they showed us the way these superheros feel like after their biggest failure, because it's their fault, and they know it, regret it and feel it for the first time. The second act is where things started to happen, again slowly, but still entertaining! The third act is all what we wanted to see, an hour of insanity!I said some cons, but my biggest one is an spoiler, but of them actually, so I will just hint some, and then I will talk about them in depth in my spoiler review.My biggest issue with this movie is that they really made a very powerful character a joke, it has its reasons but I didn't like it. Also the final fight didn't last for so long as I really wanted it to be, with the same issue that I had with Infinity War!Overall Avengers: Endgame is a great superhero movie and an amazing conclusion to this amazing era, but it's not perfect, no matter how hard I really wanted it to be!
I'm gonna give Avengers: Endgame and A-!Alright guys, thank u as always for reading my review, the spoiler review is coming up, along with Shazam! review... And as always, if u like it, u can click on my name up above and read my old reviews and the upcoming reviews!

Review Title: As Silly As "Ant-Man and the Wasp", But Better, and More Memorable
Review: When I said Endgame was silly, I was referring to the science part. Yeah I know it's what people would call "Pseudo-Science" and the movie caught in a science-fiction genre, but still, bringing time travel theme (or rather, as Scott Lang put it, "Time Heist") to a movie, even if it's a sci-fi one, possess a great risk of making the movie a little bit (or maybe much) nonsensical that still got me thinking in my confusion up until now, like "wait, how's that happened?" "If this happened, shouldn't that never had happened?" "How can compressing yourself into a thing smaller than an atom so can get you travel back to the past?" and so on, and so on.Maybe if I'm not a science (and science fiction) enthusiast, who enjoys reading and finding out things like black holes, wormholes (Einstein-Rosen bridge), the Big Bang, Neutron Stars, etc I would have enjoyed the movie more. So I decided to do a different thing: make it as sensible as possible. And you know what I got from that? A decent superhero movie. A lot of people says it's great, the greatest superhero movie even, but I'm sorry, to me it's just good. And that's enough. it's boring at first up until the third act, in which the most intense action scene takes place, it has memorable, jaw-dropping, heart-pumping, touching, heart-warming, tear-jerking scenes along the way until the credit finally rolls at almost the third hour of the entire duration of the movie.I think Endgame is kind of a movie that I will actually enjoy several days after I watched it by re-watching some of the cool scenes form the leaked footage in Youtube (yeah they're literally everywhere in that video-sharing platform, that's how crazy the fans are). And I need to admit, maybe I miss some of the things that made people enjoy it far more than I did. I dunno, maybe I'm gonna watch it again on the theater, something that I have never did before for any movie, no matter how great it is.

Review Title: Good ending to a good series
Review: I haven't heard more people upset about spoilers since the Star Wars prequels, so please consider this sentence the spoiler space you very well may need if you don't want to learn more. Then again, I'm going to discuss the idea of this film more than the actual movie itself.Avengers: Endgame is the blockbuster of 2019. It's a juggernaut that has the biggest cast of any superhero film ever, wrapping up almost 12 years of storyline and multiple movies, all to answer the question that came up at the end of Avengers: Infinity War: after you kill half of everything, what happens next?There's been a lot of soapboxing and online hand wringing about this film. Plenty of people feel the need to show that they're above the paltry populace, happy to proclaim their intellectual superiority and state that comic book related films demand that adults remain stuck in the days of adolescence. Much like the issues of today's politics, I'm not going to change anyone's mind that feels that way. All that ends up is two people shouting their talking points and refusing to learn anything from one another. But my snide comment is this: can't you just leave well enough alone?This is a popcorn movie that appeals to the biggest audience ever. And that's fine. You can ignore it if you like - we've never lived in a time where there's more opportunity to enjoy the media that you want. Me, I ignore mumblecore, critic beloved films and Oscar-bait movies for the most part. And that is also fine.All that I know is that I've seen nearly every Marvel film with the same set of guys that I've seen movies with since I was 25 or so. Each movie is an event where we get the chance to grab a meal, catch up and enjoy one another's company in the midst of our exceedingly stressful and busy lives. If a movie can do that, it's already a success before you even watch one frame. Movies bring us together, a light on the cave wall where we can hear a fantastic tale that's bigger than us. That's what this movie is - modern mythology of larger than life heroes who are the best of all of us battling the worst villains possible.Spoiler warning part two - here's where I get into major plot points. You've been warned.More than the overall tale, I enjoyed the story beats here. Hawkeye becoming Ronin, enraged that evil survived the purge while his family did not. The main sacrifice of this film isn't Black Widow's, but his. He was the first person who saw her as more than a killing machine and gave her a chance at life. Now, she repays the favor, taking him from killing machine back to family man. However, he must sacrifice their friendship and the knowledge that her loss will always be in the background when measured against the perceived greater loss of Iron Man.

Review Title: Avengers: Endgame = Epically satisfying Balance of kinetic Cosmic conflagration with heartrending reflection & closure to MCU's 1st Decade.....
Review:
Avengers Endgame attains a valedictory level of closure (and even provides a bit of heartrending reflection/ quiet celebration) to end the first chapter of mighty "Marvel Cinematic Universe" ushered in with the wildly successful 'Iron Man' first released nearly 11 years ago circa 2008. Most cinematic 'Marvels' released to theaters within the past decade have proved mega-entertaining and usually 'spot-on' in terms of bringing to life those heroes from hallowed comic-book pages (first envisioned by Stan Lee, Jack Kirby, Roy Thomas, John Buscema, Jim Starlin, et al). With regard to Epic ensembles and Galactic-spanning, mind-blowing action, and sheer kinetic energy (infused with ample does of inter-personal humor and suspense) it has really been the 'Avengers' (and related Captain America tie-ins by the brilliant Russo brothers team) that has established Marvel as the ultimate Cinematic brand that most always satisfies beyond measure and gives audiences much more than pure entertainment. Thru the Russo Bros. direction (along with Joss Whedon before - and James Gunn in the cosmic-future), Marvel's ensemble Avengers & Cap films (along with Guardians of course, which in many ways feels like a futuristic/ anarchistic extension of Avengers) have created a genuine modernized Mythology that feels like it will endure for near Eternity (or at least as long as the complete duration/ lifespan of an average Celestial-Titan),
**possible spoilers**
Avengers Endgame literally brings it all home and amply rewards the loyal Marvel Cinematic viewers that stuck it out for the last decade.
It is true there seems to be something for everyone here (i,e, scenes that will most definitely indelibly and emotionally impact fans of each member of the 'original' Avengers ensemble). A few of the final resolutions were a bit unexpected - but make more sense upon hindsight.
This movie runs nearly 3 hours but moves briskly (as though you spent only a fraction of that time in the proverbial 'quantum realm time machine'). The penultimate battle with Thanos is about as good-Epic as IMAX gets! (and all heroes get their chance to shine on screen - in the final attempt to wallop Thanos and his galactic-army)
The over-arching Story is solid and surprisingly maintains an inner-logic/ consistency throughout (although you do need to have seen the two earlier Russo Bros. Cap films especially 'Civil-War' and the first Guardians of the Galaxy, along with Infinity-War of course for this Story to really coalesce (and familiarity with the Infinity-Gauntlet comic series from the very early 1990's certainly doesn't hurt!).
Even the quietly reflective epilog like ending works surprisingly well, giving audiences the feeling of spending a few intimate moments with these beleaguered heroes (and human counterparts) who gambled it all and triumphed (but also sacrificed much).... and deserve the chance to get on with 'normal' lives (at least until the next overpowered Galactic tyrant sets foot on our pale blue Earth with malevolent intentions!)
