Review Title: A truly epic conclusion... (Spoilers Warnings are stated throughout)
Review:
'Avengers: Endgame'... easily one of the biggest, most-hyped, grandest and monumental movies ever made. The epic culmination to one of, if not- the biggest movie franchises ever, spanning over ten years of work. The hype for this movie was unbelievable. Even bigger than that of 'Infinity War'. People shouting spoilers everywhere came along with that, of course, but that didn't change the hype. I had the whole movie spoiled for me (yep.) and I still went and watched it with the same hype. How did I find it?There is, as expected, a LOT to say:I was annoyed. But not in a bad way. I loved it. So why am I annoyed? Because of the little flaws that made this movie short of one of the best movies ever made. But I'll start with the good things:This movie really felt like a conclusion to 22 other movies. The scale is epic and not only does it complete the colossal story like it should, but it also complete's all the character's arcs in the best ways possible. It doesn't just feel like a money-making standalone film, but it goes and solves many problems across multiple films. That includes story problems, character problems, plot-holes and more. Every arc, every layer and every line is so seamlessly intertwined and concluded that it all wraps up so delightfully, and the fact that it goes beyond just solving the stories not only reaches our huge expectations, but defies them and surpasses them.And even still, along with the gargantuan load it already carries, Endgame manages to carefully and skilfully weave it in with real, hart felt emotional depth. Now, I'm not just saying this as a Marvel fanboy, but this film was truly an emotional roller coaster. It truly delivers sentiment. To prove that I'm not just saying this as a fan- many found Infinity War emotional. Was it? Well, it had it's emotional moments every now and then, but it was very much hidden under the action. I'm not saying that as a problem, but it didn't feel quite as powerful as it should have been on the emotional aspect. The action aspect, certainly, but the dramatic side- not so much. This film, on the other hand was powerful on both aspects. It delivers great action along with emotional depth. This movie makes you feel happy, sad, angry, mesmerised, supportive, hopeful and more. A true emotional roller-coaster, filled with laughs and cries alike. Just like in Infinity War, where each character had a chance to shine in terms of action, this film gives each character a chance to shine in terms of action and emotion, raising goosebumps and making everyone scream in awe as it should, making this what might just be my favourite MCU movie yet.So, the story's magnificent and the impact is great. Oh, and the visuals, as usual, are great. So what are the flaws of this movie?Apart from the lack of storytelling through the camera, a problem which Marvel has always had, there were other things too, but they are hard to get into without some very minor 'kind-of' spoilers, so skip to the conclusion if you want to avoid them:MINOR SPOILERS: Thor in this movie, is basically a character played for laughs. He suffers from PTSD, but his reaction to it feels very silly, and is basically there to make fat jokes, drunk jokes, etc. That would have been fine if he used the rest of the movie to redeem himself, and although he does gain hope, he is still an alcoholic, and is still a target for 'fat' jokes. This makes his emotional scenes in the movie lack depth, and it doesn't feel as satisfying as it should have. Another small problem: Hulk. Hulk's character arc was perfect, but it was again, unsatisfying, as his arc completed in the beginning of the film, and there is no real Hulk action. Had this been done at the end of the film, however, it would have been perfect. Maybe this was to cut down on the already lengthy run time of over three hours, but if they're already going for an epic scope and a conclusion to over twenty films, even a four hour movie would have been fine by me. There's one more thing that isn't really a flaw, but I feel like it needs addressing. The time-travel part of the movie often has plot holes and the movie feels like it's constantly, desperately trying ot write itself out of them by making it's own rules. However, I wouldn't lower the rating for this, as I always think that it doesn't matter if a movie has plot holes as long as it still makes a good story out of it, which in this case- it did.There is one more thing which isn't really a flaw at all but just another something I feel that needs addressing. MAJOR SPOILER though:MAJOR SPOILERS: Like I said just now, this is not a flaw and one of the best scenes in the whole movie (probably one of the two most sad- for me at least) is Black Widow's death. Now- it's not the fact that this character died that is a flaw, obviously, but the fact that at the end, when practically EVERYONE was in the huge battle scene, she was the only one not there. It's not a problem, but I would have just loved to see just one massive fight where everyone took part, and the fact that she was the only one that wasn't there, as she died, was just so unsatisfying. I would have just loved to see just one massive fight where everyone took part, but it won't happen. Not a flaw, but I just wanted to put that out there.CONCLUSION:
'Avengers: Endgame' is definitely flawed, but it does almost everything and more a truly epic conclusion sure to deliver a goose-bump-raising, emotionally-powerful and hugely entertaining finale that delivers justice to it's ever-growing franchise.

Review Title: The perfect culmination of 10 years of brilliance
Review: One of the biggest box office hits in history, Avengers: Endgame, marks the end of the first big era of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. It is a conclusion, but also a new beginning to the MCU. Looking at the film from every angle, it is a very good movie, although there are a few questionable views of morality presented, such as the lack of moral qualms with regard to killing, even when not completely necessary. This is present in most MCU films in some capacity. For the most part though, the heroes of the film have pretty good moral compasses, and they try not to cross any lines. It is important to be aware of the attitudes being put forth in the film. The Russo brothers (the directors of the film) slip in a couple of agenda-pushing elements in the film. One of these was a scene towards the beginning of the film, where one of the Russo brothers actually cameos as the first openly gay character in the MCU. Another moment is in a major scene, where all the female heroes band together on the battlefield to show the strength of the specifically female characters, as if strong femininity was a new concept. Both of these moments contributed very little to the film itself, they were simply put there clearly to push a liberal agenda, which is a typical Hollywood move. This film puts a great emphasis on the dignity of the human person, as the heroes fight against Thanos, who wants to wipe out half of all life in the universe in order to save resources and "save" life as a whole. The heroes recognize, however, that the possible threat due to growing populations in the universe does not make the dignity of the individual person invalid. This truth is fought for by all the heroes in this film. Everything the heroes do in this film is to try to save every single life Thanos tried to take. As is true with most of the Russo brothers' work, this movie is brilliantly made, creating many fan service moments, having an extremely interesting plot that keeps the viewer engaged throughout the entirety of the three-hour film, and leaving no plot-holes, thinking of every angle. They even went above making an engaging movie. They made it inspiring, as two of the main characters, Iron Man and Black Widow, make the ultimate sacrifice for the greater good. Captain America is also very inspiring in the film, as he is willing to fight till his last breath to save half the universe. The film also manages to be relevant to human experience, even with all the superheroes and aliens flying around. The viewer can relate to the characters and the decisions they make in the film. Overall, Endgame is an incredible movie, more than worthy of the ten years of fabulous films before it.

Review Title: Amazing character development, even in reverse!
Review: The Thanos we see in the beginning of the movie, the new-age super villain who thinks he is in the right, unlike the classic "just evil without a purpose" trope, gets replaced with a younger Thanos at the end, who is ruthless, arrogant and overconfident.That's good though! It doesn't destroy or deconstruct Thanos as a character. The character development of the original Thanos feeds right into the whole reversal of his development.The young Thanos was showing psychopathic tendencies, since he hadn't yet faced his own personal ultimate sacrifice. He had not yet fought to obtain the infinity stones. He never had the character development the old Thanos experienced. Never had to push Gamora to get the soul stone. It just landed on his lap.Having not faced such burdens, and poisoned by the illusion of "assured victory", he acted just as his character at that stage would have.Same with Nebula; none of the events had happened that would change her forever. Not having been exposed to the true love Gamora offered her, she never went over the tipping point; not even after seeing the future Nebula."What did it cost? Everything" is the punchline of Infinity War.Not for the young Thanos. Not for the young Nebula. None of the essential scars on their souls that would tip them to wherever existed when they traveled through the time portal.Also, Ironman, the true godfather of the MCU, got the sendoff that he deserved. It was a good decision to give the final snap to Ironman.And the Captain America send-off was so sweet, it was the perfect scene to end it all. A dance in peace with the one you love.Amazingly well done movie, with some small plot holes and minor disapointments here and there.

Avengers: Endgame is a 2019 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics superhero team the Avengers. Produced by Marvel Studios and distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures, it is the direct sequel to Avengers: Infinity War (2018) and the 22nd film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

We've gotten to know and love these characters through over 20 films over ten years, a fitting ending to the Infinity Saga was of course an extremely difficult task. But the Russo brothers (Joe & Anthony) deliver, once again, a glorious Marvel movie.After Infinity War, which at the time was the biggest cross-over event in film history, Marvel was on top of everything from the box office to the standards of Comic films. Marvel has excelled at every turn this past decade, Endgame HAD to do and be a lot of things. It had to break all the records Infinity War just broke, and please fans just as thoroughly.Not only does Endgame feel unique from all that's come before it, it also hones in on what made Marvel great to begin with: it's characters. Endgame's pivotal move was to make this movie extremely Narrative AND Character driven. It didn't bank too hard on its action set pieces or its witty comedy, but they did those exceedingly well too. Endgame had a heart.We took a stroll down memory lane, it feels like, through some of the best moments through MCU history. Time travel was bound to be a big part at some point in this universe. Marvel (and comic books in general) is no stranger to time travel, parallel dimensions, and alternate timelines; Endgame's excellent use of this narrative shows that Marvel isn't afraid to make bold choices.Endgame is a PERFECT follow up to the jaw-dropping Infinity War. They take all of our characters, especially our original set of Avengers, and bring them to some very interesting places, literally and figuratively.I cheered with joy, I bit my lip in anticipation, I sighed, I laughed, I cried; I love this whole saga with my whole heart. Endgame matches the expectations and surpasses them.It's easily a 10/10

Review Title: Incredibly Epic! and The End of an Era!
Review:
SPOILER ALERT!
IF YOU HAVEN"T WATCH IT, DO YOURSELF A FAVOR, DON'T READ REVIEWS YET, GO WATCH IT FIRST. OTHERWISE, YOU WILL GET SPOILED.
Everything has an explanation.If you didn't do a marathon watching the 21 marvel movies before Endgame (or at least 12 of the essential movies), you will probably end adding a negative review about Endgame.1st: Why Captain America was able to use Thor's hammer? (And some say: "the cap used even better than Thor, how?"). OK, here is why.You have to go back to Thor's and Captain America's movies. Back in Thor (2011), Thor committed an act of war that put the lives of millions of people on risk, so he demonstrated not to be worthy, so Odin exiled Thor, removing his rights to use the hammer. Odin said "Whosoever holds this hammer, if he be worthy, shall possess the power of Thor". In the same movie, Thor tried to pick up the hammer, and he wasn't able to do it because he was not worthy. The keyword here is "Worthy". At the end of the movie, when Thor sacrificed his life to save the world, then he demonstrated to be worthy, and then the hammer came back to him. Then, going back to Captain America's movies, from the very beginning, when Steve Rogers was not a superhero yet, in several occasions, he demonstrated to be worthy, including that moment on which he jumped over a pomegranate to save the lives of people that were just bullying him. In fact, he was chosen to become a super soldier, because of was worthy to become super powerful (did you watch Captain America the First Avenger?) if not, you won't understand anything about the cap. The movies after that, he also continues to give his life for others, putting himself on risk to save the world (even before having any power).Remember that fun scene in Age of Ultron on Thor is making fun of everybody because nobody can pick up the hammer? But when Captain America tried, Thor gets surprised because when Captain America make his try, the hammer moves, but then cap is so humble that look at Thor and then doesn't pick it up, maybe he was not fully worthy at that moment yet?. If you look back in the comics, the cap picked up the hammer a couple of times.2nd: Why Captain America took the hammer with him at the end of the movie when going back in time to return the infinity stones? This is not revealed in Endgame, but he was definitively returning everything back, maybe the Hammer was one of those things, so it won't mess Thor's timelines. Thor needed that hammer in the past, that's a reason.3rd: Why Captain America was able to use the StormBreaker? The StormBreaker doesn't has the magic from Odin. So anybody with enough strength can use it. Is not the hammer that has the magic from Odin.4th: Why Captain America appears as an old man, at the end of the movie? C'mon guys! You don't know this? Really? Again, watch Captain America: The First Avenger (2011), and also watch Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014), and you will find all answers. He had a pending dance with the love of his life, the woman with who he wanted to get old together. Remember in the Winter Soldier, he said to her (on her deathbed) "we still have a pending dance". That's why the movie ends with that dance! And c'mon! He deserves a life too! That's why he just appears as an old man in front of the lake, because he used the time travel to have a life and get old with his woman! Jesus! C'mon! Please tell me that you get it.5th: Why Captain Marvel doesn't really stick around to show off all her infinite power to just defeat Thanos? The simple answer is, because you guys hate her!!! If Marvel gives the main role to Captain Marvel, most of the Marvel fans will get pissed! C'mon tell if I am right or wrong?About the Timeline Mess-up: Yes, I understand, time travel in so many stories, it brings new time lines, and this leaves some unanswered questions. Now let's look at the future. Did you see the new Spider-man trailer? Nick Fury calls Spider-man to resolve a mess with the new timelines. In fact, he ask "why you didn't call Captain Marvel", they answer "She is not available". The real answer is "She is not that popular, the fan base hate her, that's why we called you, Spider-man". Also after Tony Stark death, which movie you think is more profitable? Either a Spider-man movie or Pepper's movie, right? But people won't really like Pepper as they already like Spider-man. So who is the go-to person now? Spider-man. And the probe of this is that he sets a new record in trailer views. Everybody wants to know what's next! That's why Spider-man is the man now. He was Iron man's pupil, and he still wears the suit made by Iron Man. So Spider-man is at the same time new Iron-man? And he is going to resolve some of the mess-up caused by the time travel? Well let me tell you, this is much better than having almost all superheroes dead.Do you guys really thing the planning for a movie with a budget of $356,000,000 (estimated), is just about a few guys just sitting and inventing random stories without analyzing? Nope. That's a lot of people thinking and challenging each other when a new idea comes out. Almost everything in this movie makes sense and is referenced from prior movies. And anything that doesn't makes sense yet, will makes sense in the future, in the next movies.My only concern in this movie is who dies. I still don't accept it. I can accept black widow death because she has a contract for a prequel, so we are going to watch much more about her. But Ironman! C'mon! Why him? You lost black widow, and we are losing the cap, and Ironman too? Marvel you sacrifice too much. We can still enjoy the movie without so many sacrifices. That's my only concern. Yes, I am still sad about who died. But I have to accept it. Let me tell you, if all the good guys always survive, and all the bad guys always die, in every single movie you watch, then what's the point? You will know the end already! But Marvel is giving us stories that keeps us thrilled because we cannot predict it (unless you have been spoiled of course). These are movies in where anything can happens, as they says "whatever it takes". But hey, I am still sad. Sad! Very Sad! Why him? This is the only reason why I would hate Marvel.Well, in overall, Avengers: Endgame, is the end of an era, and it is the most epic ending you couldn't even imagine.It took them more than a decade to make this movie. All of those 21 prior movies point to this one, and this on point back to the prior movies too. You may be surprised of finding also some references from the comics.Some of my favorite parts are the references to all the 21's prior movies to this one. But this is also a double-edged sword, because it is good for people that really remember those movies, but bad for those that are not fans, didn't watch the prior movies, and don't know what is going on.Another good mention about Endgame and all Marvel movies is that they are bordering the lines between science and science fiction. Marvel Studios prides itself on scientific continuity throughout its many movies, and this movie really made it in that direction. They give a drama story and origin to each super hero, and they also explain their powers and how these characters obtained these powers. Most of the story is actually based on scientific theories (the quantum physics), and how far a civilization can go if some of these theories are exploded. So can we become super heroes and travel back in time? Hey, I haven't say that. But if you are a science enthusiast, you will love how Marvel does it with science fiction.Marvel make us become children again by the time we sit to watch their movies.Everything in this movie is above and beyond amazing, in combination with the full sequel (as I mentioned above). The story and screenplay, the art direction, the acting, sound mixing, visual effects, engineering effects, music, cinematography, costume design (as always), action, drama, comedy, film editing, everything. No negative critics. Would it earn or be nominated to an Oscar? Well, I think Avengers in overall has the potential to add another category to the Oscars: 'Best Sequel'. Yeah! Why not? As I said, if you judge this movie itself without watching the entire 22 avenger's movies, it won't be a fair judgement! Period. Oscar's committee, please take that in mind.Would I watch it again! Yes, I'm going back to the movie theater, to watch it a couple of times more. And then when it gets released in Blu-Ray, I will watch it again about 4 times more. For real, it is fun to watch!

Review Title: Nice tour with feels and jokes
Review: Avengers Endgame is a competent movie, which felt like the closing of a circle. It starts with the loss and how it's dealt with, and continues as a journey to past Marvel movies. It's fun as that, giving a nice glimpse to what happened after the end of the first Avengers movie, letting Thor meet his mother and Iron Man his father, and so on, all with the typical Marvel sense of homour. My son of course liked that Thor and his pals were playing Fortnite.It doesn't have the desperation of Infinity War, which made it so strong for me, or even many other superhero movies where there's an enemy to be defeated. At this level, I feel that it's weaker than many previous movies. A lot of the movie shows off alternate versions of past movies or extensions of them, which, while somewhat boring plot-wise, is a treat for fans. I did enjoy all of it, but still, at this level the movie felt more like a homage to previous movies and a way to provide closure than a movie of it own.I won't go into too much further detail, but I'll discuss one small part that felt off to me, because I felt it weakened the ending, and that was Captain Marvel. Even at the end of her own movie (which was pretty good), it was clear to me that she became so overpowered that'd she'd be hard to write into anything. Endgame proved it. She was kept out of the game for most of the movie (obviously because she's overpowered), then arrived at the end flying unharmed through a barrage of missiles and plowing through a spaceship. Then she took the Infinity Gauntlet from Spiderman.And then things went south. Spiderman asked her how she'd get through the battlefield and then all the female heroes stopped the battle to pose and say they'd help her. Come on, this woman just flew through a starship like it wasn't there. She could probably destroy Thanos' entire army in a matter of minutes. And she needs help? And she loses to Thanos in a few seconds only to give Iron Man his chance to die? I think the writers would have done better to simply keep her out. A Deus Ex Machina is a bad plot device. One which fails for 'reasons' is even worse.

Review Title: The Ending We Needed, but never wanted!
Review:
Yes this review contains spoilers and theories, as well as my review on this epic film!So for starters, I saw the film on Sunday during it's opening weekend and I wanted to stay on social media and refused to click any link about Endgame as I did not want any spoilers, but after seeing it, all I want to do it talk about it, share idea and theories, and quote some of the best one liners in cinematic history.So, yes I gave this film a 10/10 and I would rate it higher if given the possibility. The story was amazing, and the trailer even though it told us about the Quantum Realm and that was going to be the focus of the film; the Russo brothers added many twists and definitely unforseen endings to our beloved superheroes.The one thing everybody was bashing the movie for was the end credits, or lack there of... However, Marvel end credits usually have been added as little last minute jokes and laughs, or leading into the next film. However, this film marks the end of Phase 3, so there is nothing to lead into and the film was over 3 hours long, so do you really need a little 15 second segment showing the group eating Shawarma?One ending that wasn't addressed and makes sense with the announcement of it's release on Disney+ was the disappearance of Loki after Tony, Steve, and Bruce travel back to 2012 to retrieve the Tesseract. However, after the foiled attempt, Loki manages to escape with the Tesseract. However, the group travels further in time to retrieve the Tesseract from the facility where Captain America was created. So my question is, if they retrieved the Tesseract earlier than 2012, does that mean the one Loki has is gone? Or did it create a ripple in the timeline as the Ancient One explained to Professor Hulk. I guess we will have to wait for that theory when Loki gets his show when Disney+ premieres.And finally, the end credits didn't have any videos but there was an audio snippet of what sounded like metal clashing on metal, almost like a forge or blacksmithing. So, many people are speculating that this is Iron Man making his Mach.1 suit in the cave. Kind of like a statement, ending where it began.But my theory is it's Eitri... The Giant Dwarf of Nidavellir. I believe it is him forging a weapon which would lead us into GotG: vol.3, which is why Marvel was so set of getting James Gunn back to direct as he had the plot and the story already wrote before his firing and while Endgame was being produced. At the end of GotG: vol.2 we get introduced to Adam Warlock, who, James Gunn, said wouldn't appear in Endgame, but his presence will be known in the MCU... Next major villian perhaps? Could he be forcing Eitri to make him a weapon more powerful than the Infinity Gauntlet? Perhaps not to harness all the stones, but perhaps to harness just one (Soul Stone, which he aquires in the comics after obtaining the Infinity Gauntlet) but make it even more powerful? The soul stone was barely used in Infinity War and Endgame, but it's considered the most powerful stone, so creating a villian that showcased such power might bring the Orange gem justice.That's my review and my theories.

Review Title: A film like no other, and my favourite
Review: Yes, I know it's blasphemy for some people, but after so much build-up and so much hype; Endgame met every expectation I had and exceeded them, which I can say was not an easy feat. The story was brilliant, as many people have said, it was not as tightly-woven as Infinity War's, but that doesn't detract much from the experience. The three hours flew by, and I had a grin on my face at every turn. The jokes landed fine and the emotional moments were, well, emotional. It is a very hard task to beat Infinity War, yet Endgame did it for me.This movie does indeed have a lot of fan service, but that is absolutely not a negative for me, especially since some of it was fantastic to see play out. My favourite part, like most, was The Avengers' Assembly. The music was brilliant throughout the film, and here the crescendo and the triumphance of the Avengers theme by Alan SIlvestri could not be matched. Thus follows the best action scene in the film and in my opinion, the best in the MCU. It was great and mind-blowing to see.Of course, the ensuing battle eventually results in Tony Stark's final "I am Iron Man" and a snap to end Thanos and his army. The man who started it all is gone. The movie did excellently with the character reactions from Rhodey, Peter and Pepper and their acting, along with Robert Downey Junior's, was phenomenal. The funeral and credits were suitably heart-breaking and were crafted expertly. The Russos did a great job at making it seem jubilant and melancholy at the same time. The end of an era. There is so much to talk about that I did not get to, but I commented on the best bits, and you most likely have seen it by now and can make a judgement for yourself. I will definitely continue seeing the MCU's next entries until the day I die or the day they stop and I am not going to avoid the future instalments because this Infinity Saga is over. I will instead look forward to what the future of the MCU holds, as I doubt it will ever get uninteresting. We will have to wait and see. Go watch this movie, even if you aren't a Marvel fan (as they have no doubt seen it multiple times already like I have), it is worth your time as it is a once in a lifetime experience and no way near a disappointment.

Review Title: A Fitting End to an Amazing Saga
Review: The grand finale of the Avengers' saga, which began over ten years ago with "Iron Man," comes to its epic conclusion. Just like the first Avengers movie featured every Marvel character that had had a movie at the time, Marvel's entire cinematic pantheon is involved in this battle, making for one hell of an extensive cast list. With exactly half of those characters being dead at the opening of this chapter (see Infinity War), the survivors find themselves in a desperate state. They've never dealt with defeat on this scale before, and though they do rally and make one more attempt defeat Thanos and restore what was lost, they find that there truly is no coming back from this one. Their defeat is total, and their losses are quite permanent. Over the next few years, they do their best to accept this and move on. A hero thought lost returns unexpectedly, however, bringing with him a chance to turn things around.Every character has their moment to shine.For characters whose sagas ended with this movie, adequate time is allotted to bring their stories to a fitting, satisfying close. Tony completes his transformation from selfish billionaire to selfless hero, making the sacrifice play that Cap once said he never could have made. Steve keeps the promise he made to Peggy decades ago, before he made his own sacrifice play. None of it feels rushed or abrupt.The attention to detail that is paid to each of the unprecedented number of characters should serve as an example for future epics on this scale. Classic lines from earlier movies are reprised, reinforcing the sense of continuity that has been so important in making these characters as beloved as they are, and in maintaining the integrity of the shared universe that they inhabit.The only negative I could think of is the death of Black Widow. Thanos sacrificing his daughter to get the Soul Stone made sense. Not only was he dedicated to his task, moving forward in his quest with the courage of his convictions, he was also the bad guy. Heartless acts like killing one's own daughter to obtain ultimate power become villains like he. The heroes, self-sacrificing individuals they may be, should have been able to find a way to get the Soul Stone without having to murder a loved one.

Review Title: A tribute to the Marvel Cinematic Universe
Review:
As "Avengers: Endgame" comes to a close, so does 10 years of marvelous movie-telling. To criticize it would be objective, and as it cumulate 21 movies before it, being unemotionally objective brings it no fairness.*** Beware, SPOILERS ahead ***Throughout the runtime of the movie, not only do the Avengers travel thru time, but so do we. To relive our childhood sensations when we were first introduced to these characters is a scripting masterpiece. Though the heroes were on an explicit mission to retrieve the Infinity stones before Thanos, the scriptwriters and directors successfully accomplished theirs by sending us back with the heroes to witness them one last time, to finally bid them farewell.STORY/PLOT: Rumors always had it that time travel must be part of the equation to undo the Snap. Nonetheless, the various theories were off point. The evolution of the script was beautifully crafted: they lost, they wanted to revert things, but they failed again. They tried to move on, but were they able to? None of them was able to, "not us". As we see the heroes on their respective journey, each had an encounter that was heartbreaking: Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) looking at Peggy after so many years, Tony Stark (Robert Downey Jr) talking to his father again, the Ancient One talking about Dr. Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch), Bruce Banner (Mark Ruffalo) finding purpose for his Hulk transformation, and Natasha Romanoff (Scarlett Johansson) finally paying her debt to Clint Barton (Jeremy Renner). These events truly sum up the relationships and sacrifices our heroes went thru, and recapitulate their separate stories across the decade. And as these conclude, they funnel into one last battle, together, for an overdue reward we longed for.CHARACTERS: At this point after 21 movies, the actors "are" the characters.Tony Stark/Iron Man has finally fulfilled his legacy. His conclusion deserves the utmost respect and no denying I heard people sob in the theater. You can rest now Mr. Stark, your watch has ended.Steve Rogers/Captain America has finally yielded Mjölnir and unlocked his ultimate power, finally becoming worthy. The most satisfying scene was seeing him finally finding happiness. He has persistently put everyone first and now, 80+ years later, he got the dance he so longed for.Thor's depiction in this movie was conflicting. Though he remained lovable, we are not accustomed to him with such a physique. I do not deny I hoped that somewhere in the plot, he would be the ultimate version of himself as Tony, Steve, Natasha, and Clint were.Natasha Romanoff/Black Widow: Her love for Clint was sufficiently seen with their encounter. Her demise was aching, but heroic nonetheless. A true personification of friendship, affection, and sacrifice.Bruce Banner/Hulk: Since "Thor: Ragnarok", I have disliked the evolution of the Hulk. Though his depiction in Avengers 1 and 2 was that of a Professor, a man of Science, his character's development to an unconfident, "cool", and bossed around person is unsatisfying. Following Nat's death however, we slightly see a glimpse of the anger that once composed and fueled him.Clint Barton/Hawkeye is the human of the team. His drive was true and the pain hope adds to impossible situations was beautifully depicted in his journey.The role of Captain Marvel (Brie Larson) in this movie was acceptable. She did not seem overpowered and her distinction from the rest of team was correctly depicted. Nonetheless, as we look to the future, she brings no nostalgia to our original six.CONCLUSION:
In my review of "Avengers: Infinity War" almost exactly one year ago, I concluded stating: "in Avengers 4, the Avengers must go back to their phase 1 roots and....Assemble." As I contemplate the events of "Endgame", this small sentence, though simple, plain and not explicitly revealing, was a prophecy. The Avengers went back - literally -, each found their roots (Tony his father, Steve Peggy, Natasha Clint), and after this was achieved, Assembled.*** END of SPOILERS ***As the credits rolled, emotionally and spiritually, we bow down in respect to such a finale. Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow, and Hawkeye: thank you for that decade of Marvel.

Review Title: A satisfying culmination of 22 movies and 10 years of a superhero franchise!
Review:
Avengers: Endgame is culmination of 22 movies which is something not many movie franchise can brag about but this also means that Endgame had a huge responsibility to carry on its shoulder. It had to bring closure to multiple character arc, ignite the fire for new ones to come and also deliver a coherent and meaningful story at the same time. There were a few snags but Russo brothers were mostly able to deliver on each of those expectation and gave us a cinematic extravaganza that will go down history as one of the most significant Hollywood event to take place in recent times.
This movie is a love letter to past 10 years of MCU from including multitude of past movie references to including its many type of signature humor, action scenes and shooting styles.
This movie had almost all the main cast from its previous 22 movies and each of one them gave their best in terms of acting especially the main avengers, this was one the best performance we have seen from Scarlett Johansson, Robert Downey Junior, Chris Evans, Paul Rudd and Jeremy Renner . I liked some of the direction choices made by Russo brothers and disliked the others, In a movie populated with so many characters they were able to do the balancing act just right, the emotional scene had impact and the humor scene made me laugh and most (not all) main character got the screen time they needed. Iron-Man and Ant-Man are really the highlights they bring in a lot a humanising elements to the movie.By the end the director were able to tell a story with a satisfying end to many of the superheroes arc who have inspired young and adults alike for the past 10 years and gave way to new superheroes to inspire next generation of kids.
There are consequences of having such large scale movie and it showed like there were lot of character development that happened behind the camera -
Hulk and Bruce Banner were never comfortable in each other skin and this is a theme going on since Avengers 1 but now we jumped directly to the conclusion which I think will leave Hulk fans a little disappointed
A lot of panic and menace which may happen after half the population disappears was never shown through a civilian perspective which would have given a more emotional gravitas to the situation.
Captain Marvel's character felt like it was shoehorned in the movie. Her main reason was to save Stark but how she found him remains a mystery.
Thanos was a very sophisticated villain in Infinity War whereas here he was just another big bad arrogant villain.
Compared to Infinity War this movie lacked a sense of forward motion, after killing Thanos and retrieving all the stones the rest of the people and avengers were avenged, their job was done and plot complete. The final battle felt like it was there because movie was lacking a big action set piece.
The final battle was great because of the characters present in them, seeing all of them in action was a sight to behold but there was no sense of scale(just compare it to Wakanda battle from Infinity War).The cinematography was also good in parts like the Ant-Man scene where he was searching if his daughter was alive was well shot and the frantic camera movement showed his angst as well but then the Captain America vs Captain America fight scene was very poorly shot with so many cuts that it was hard to follow their fight, Otherwise the CGI and most of the scene looked very beautiful.
The soundtrack is probably the best one yet.
This movie had to deliver on a lot of promises and initially I felt that few cons could have been neglected when scale of the movie is this big but seeing how Infinity War released just a year ago did delivered on a lot of similar promises in a shorter run time, I think this is a good movie which definitely could have done better but ultimately what matters is that it was able to give satisfying end to an era of superhero which are an inspiration to younger generation.

They put in mediocore 'sad music' in scenes that didn't need music at all. A lot of times when you want the audience to pay attention to the script and what people are saying in emotional moments music isn't needed. It can sometimes only take away from the feelings that you are ment to feel in that scene. And that is actually one of my biggest problems with this movie. THERE WAS NO IMPACT. This movie played it sooo save even after 28 other movies. They only killed Tony and Black Widow. Ofcourse Iron Man's death was expected and therefor less impactful. I do have to give credit to the execution though, i thought it was very well done and they did Iron Man a lot of justice in this movie. I loved that and i also hoped to see that.But lets get back to the impact problem. In Many Marvel movies we expected people to die. The Avengers (possibility), Age of Ultron (Only Quicksilver what is again cheating because it made no impact again), Civil War (this could have been a masterpiece if there were bigger consequences) etc. But every time we were like: 'ah its ok we understand because we know Thanos is coming and he is going to truly destroy everything' Then Infinity War arrived. One of the best Marvel movies by far, but again no impact. Cause killing people with the snap and not even main character is just weak. We all know Spider-Man and Black Panther are coming back because they have there own solo films coming up. Marvel has just been a victim of the Disney effect and its keeping them down from even more potential imo. Now i know some simple fans will read this and be like: 'what is he talking about it had massive impact a lot of people died!' but no guys, just no. Logan is a good example of a movie with real consequences. Every decision they make have a reaction. When they decide to help the family on the road and after that stay with them, they feel good and have a real family moment that they hadn't had in years. But at the same time that decision made that family a target and they eventually even get slaughterd by X-24. Also Logan decides to sacrifice himself for the new generation of mutants. He goes to the woods to fight an whole elite squad + X-24 eventhough he knows it will be his death, and eventually he does. In Endgame, the Avengers have to fight the biggest threat that the MCU has to offer, but does that really show at the end of the day? The awnser to that question is NO. They brought back every character that they killed in Infinity War (also Loki), exept for Vision. In Endgame they only really kill Iron Man, and therefor only show respect tot that character. 'but black widow died!' Nobody cares that black widow died. She was just as underdevelopt as the plot of Justice League, so don't hate on DC for reasons that are just as bad for some characters with Marvel.So consequences make it more realistic, and when a movie is more realistic its more reletable and it makes you even more invested in the characters, and therefore elevating the whole movie. Now that is why impact is so important. WE HAVE FOLLOWED THESE CHARACTERS FOR 10 YEARS. This movie is even called Endgame, like common. Imo at least Cap should have died too. Him sacrificing himself for the world, that is Captain America to the core of his characters and true fans know this. I swear i would have cried like a baby if that would have happend, but no. Disney ofcourse wants to please the children because they make them money, but it is a disrespect to the art of the content. Also i want to note that Thanos didn't even come close to the threat he was in Infinity War. I would have prefered to see a end fight with only the main Marvel characters but not a whole army, and them just taking on Thanos with the Infinity Glove (maybe missing one stone) so that you would be in constant fear of characters dying and really rooting for them. Instead they gave us a lesser and full CGI version of a LOTR battle with random beasts and armies that you will forget about in the next year.There i said it.People please try to be critical and not just accept everything that gets thrown at you.conclusion: It had beautiful little moments like Tony's reunion with is father and Tony's story overall carried this movie. But it was definitly not on the level that Infinity War was. therefor i give it a 7

Review Title: Stan Lee Would Not Have Made These Errors! Disney Strikes again!
Review:
So before i start let me just say not all of Endgame is bad, a 3 hour runtime in a movie with these characters will always have it's good moments. So many are shouting from the rooftops how amazing this movie is, well i'm happy for them that they walked away with a smile on their face, after all in this day & age, we all need one of those, although i don't think that in that last 15 minutes of Endgame their was that much to be joyous about but hey each to their own. Anyway so Disney not content with dismantling Star Wars to a point where it is no longer recognisable from the Classic original trilogy & turning it into what can only be described as one of the biggest cinematic betrayals of it's loyal fanbase, they now have moved on & along with the Russo's & their writers have managed to disassemble 11 years of great movies & resign them to the 'Oh No, it's Crisis on Infinite Earth's all over again' pile. Endgame despite all it's promise it's so unrecognisable from it's predesessor 'infinity war' that one might be forgiven for thinking that movie was made by an entirely different team of people. Not only have they pretty much trashed most of that film with the stupidity of this one, they have also gone back & made so much of their previous cinematic universe irrelevant. Who Green Lit this? did someone just say 'Oh well as long as these great actors get a good send off, no one will notice' & to an extent that seems to be happening. What a wonderful crazy mixed up world we live in. Let's have a look at some of these problems shall we, because many people are & just ignoring them or trying to fit events to suit their viewpoints (Hollywood Reporter, i'm looking at you!)
1. Firstly because actors want to move on, should beloved characters be killed off? i wonder what Stan Lee would have made of the blatant disregard for Tony Stark & Black Widow, yes theirs a case for saying that Tony's story was done but compare his screen time to his history in comics, a few movies versus hundreds & hundreds of comics, storylines, villains, dramas. Is a super-heroe's time ever done. We are in a world with a talking Raccoon so don't give me that we need some realism argument. And Black Widow was just ridiculous, thanks for the warning Nebula? although she may not have known what you needed to do to obtain the stone but now Natascha is Dead will anyone care about her own movie? Girl Power.
2. Captain America & Hulk are now snowflakes. Jeesh! Their is no excuse for what they did to Cap at the end of this film, I Love Chris Evans & he has been perfect in this role & did not deserve this (insert swear word). This non-sensical & weird way to ditch this character was so appalling that words are lost on me. For a start Captain's work is never done, he never thinks of himself, he wouldn't for a second lay down his shield, go back in time erase another person's life so he can fit into it & then sit back & let the wars go on & not get involved. It betrays everything that they built this character up as. Also some of the time travel logic (if you wanna call it that, comes in to play here) if what The Ancient One briefly explained is true & now multiple time lines exist, it would not be possible for Cap to appear in the 2023 timeline at the end. And giving his Shield to Falcon & not his greatest friend Bucky, again not what i would call logic in the scheme of whats come before. Falcon is .. Well Falcon. Bucky is trying to find his identity, surely Steve passing his mantle on to his best friend who sorely needs a new purpose would have been where the money was on.
3. Tony Stark can make an infinity Gauntlet in a mere day? & can use all the stones without getting decimated? if Infinity War taught us anything it' that their is only 1 place & 1 man that can make such a thing, but i guess it would have meant bringing Dinklage back & extending the runtime further to make any bit of sense to this part of the story. So let's have Tony do it, He's smart, no one will notice? will they? after all he figures out time travel in the space of 5 minutes by moving his hands really fast & saying Eureka!! This is a total betrayal to their own movie so the Russo's must have just shrugged their shoulders & let it play out. Ridiculous & insulting.
4. Everyone who didn't get incinerated by Thanos should be 5 Years older now. So are we to assume that In the next Spider-Man movie all of the relevant friends, family etc of Peter Parker were zapped so that's why no one has aged. We will have to wait & see with this one, but judging by the trailer, yes, even though the chances are slim, everyone that's important to Peter's life got zapped. Again possible but ridiculous!
5. Time Travel in general is a bad idea in films unless you have a chalk board like doc brown & lay it all out for those to see. Except in this movie, the entire logic of Hulk's explanation is stupid to the point of holding up a big sign & saying 'Our Audience doesn't care anyway' but the truth is, we do, we have always cared about these films, a little too much, why do you think i'm ranting now, i'm super angry that you constructed such a beautiful tapestry of movies, intelligent, exciting, silly, yes but still logical so to throw logic out the window & stick your middle finger up to all that's come before is criminal. If you are doing Multiple Time Lines, one of them is going to be destroyed by Thanos becuase your returning the stones from where they came, do these guys only care about the people in their time line. Now you have created these time lines, you are stuck with them (Crisis On Infinite Earths anyone?) bad idea!
6. Captain America using Thor's hammer.... what were you thinking? yes, that was a nod to 'Age of Ultron' good one we get it but seriously, it looked wrong, felt stupid & i'm telling you now, way to go to upset Comic Book Fans. Good work!
7. Thanos, you made him such a rich, deep, intelligent character in 'Infinity War' yet here you deconstruct him down to just a generic bland 'i'm going to kill all of you' villain. such a shame but hey worked well for that killer ending battle right? jeesh!!i could go on & on but my sadness is telling me to quit, no one will care at the moment, fans are swept up in the hype train. My own train of thought on this is that people will start to see all the problems on subsequent viewings. Sadly this is not what we signed up for in 2008, Marvel have let their characters down to give their actors a nice goodbye, something the great Stan Lee never did at his time at Marvel. It's ok to mess up from time to time, but don't do it at the expense of these great comics & don't treat your audience like fools, it will come back to bite you. Star Wars is feeling that now & although Marvel is not done i feel that the new batch of characters you are working with are not strong enough to keep the core fans happy. Give the next movies to Taiki or Gunn & you might do ok otherwise, start using that time machine to go back & sort out all the errors on this one & maybe you will find your own redemption.

Review Title: A Symphony of Action, Feels and Story
Review: The build up to the grand finale of this 22 film long story arc is slow, and is part of the reason that the 3 hour runtime is a thing. However the runtime proves useful for the story because if they had just done the first 2 hours in a matter of minutes, the film would feel as if it was rushed and possibly could've ruined it. That being said I feel like it could've had a bit more excitement than what it had but the story got a pass because the characters got the exposition and closure with other characters that they needed and that couldn't have been excused with the runtime under 3 hours long.One of my favorite parts in the film was the fight between Hawkeye/ Ronin vs Black Widow where they were fighting over who would sacrifice themselves so the other would get the Soul Stone. Jeremy Renner and Scarlet Johansson played their parts to a T and it provided one of the most emotional parts in the film.The last hour was probably my favorite in the MCU by far. The fact that we finally see Cap lift Mjilnoir and use it to the best of his ability plus using his shield to take on the Mad Titan one on one was amazing. Tony's sacrifice in the end was one of the saddest moments in cinema I've seen, especially since I've grown up with the MCU and got to see the end having watched the vast majority of the Infinity Saga. The closings of all our favorite characters was pure and blissful emotion that mad me sad to see it ending, but happy that the ends were what we as fans and them as characters both deserved.After the masterpiece that was Endgame, I am very much excited for the next story arc of the MCU and hope that it is even better than the Infinity Saga.

Avengers: Endgame will make some people angry. There's no question about that; unlike Infinity War, which, let's be honest, if you don't like the movie then I have several questions, but if you hate Endgame, I can't really blame you. The choices made by the writers and directors, let's just say their questionable at worst.When the movie is good, it's great. Amazing, even. You get great references and fun nods to if you were paying attention in previous movies. The humor (When they aren't fat jokes) is surprisingly clever and even dark, especially for the first act where Thor is all mopey and everyone's sad and moody. All the characters bar a few (We'll get to that later) had a proper send off and have perfect arcs when the movie ended. Iron Man's death was perfect, though I would have liked it better if Thanos directly killed him, I kinda hoped Steve would die, but you know: What can you do? Also I felt like the whole 40's dance with Peggy was too fast:; I would have liked to see him return and then they party, enjoy the booming 50s and drink and all that. Hawkeye was amazing in this film; he pretty much stopped being useless for one movie. Widow was also great, though the fight to the death scene...I don't know I just didn't feel it. Ant-Man was surprisingly awesome and Paul Rudd's acting when he reunites with an older Cassie is just beautiful. Rhodey finally gets something to do, Rocket is also fun......but Thor OH GOD. Ok, I'm perfectly fine with Thor being fat; it's at least understandable and relatable. But the fat jokes were just too much and they stopped being funny after 5 minutes. But, at the very least he had his moment in IW and obviously he's not gone for good because GOTG 3 is still a thing. What did bother me was hulk, who unlike Thor, was a complete joke in both films. What happened? Did the writers just give up? We didn't even get Hulk fighting Thanos in the final fight scene! Thanos is actually was OK with despite him not being as great as IW Thanos, but it's OK since this Thanos isn't a battle-scarred general who's lost everything overnight. Captain Marvel shows up to look cool, act cocky, get a haircut and then we never see her again. Thank God. Other negatives I have with the film is the entire second act. It was fun and cool to return to the previous films, but it stretched on a little too long. The first act should have been long; getting to know a post-snap world and how everyone's getting by. I don't care about Time Travel laws, but the entire second act still felt too long. However, the final act was still epic and mindblowing. Some characters like Wanda had their spotlight to 1v1 Thanos, but it wasn't enough. Drax didn't get a hit in, Hulk didn't get one, Bucky and Steve didn't even say a word to each other in that fight, and of course, that A-Force scene. Why?Final word: The movie isn't perfect, but it's very enjoyable. If you like the MCU, chances are you will like this movie too, but if you hate botched character finales and time travel, you'll hate this one. None of the time travel makes any sense at all. Review Title: A justifying end to over a decade long storytelling
Review: The slow pace in the beginning can surely be overlooked considering what's in stock during the second half of the movie. Although I'm not a vehement Marvel fan, it's apposite to say this movie a befitting end to the Thanos saga. Respect to Russo brothers for being able to pull off an onerous task of concluding the tapestry MCU has created over the decade.These movies are basically an end to 21 movies. So, the payoffs were huge. I loved that Captain used Mjolnir. Thor was most ridiculous for me in both Infinity War and Endgame. The tone of the character doesn't work somehow after Ragnarok, either he's cracking joke after Thanos kills Asgardians and Loki or he's being a self-pitying alcoholic post the snap. Captain Marvel does what she was introduced to do in this universe, she pops up where it is convenient to the plot. The fact that her character had less screen time was apposite to me considering her underwhelming origin movie. The surprising character was Clint. Even though his screen time in previous movies is less, the transformation of an uber agent after losing everything to become a ruthless killer in search of solace/purpose is intriguing. Ronan kind of reminded me of John Wick. But when Clint is given hope to undo what's done by the mad titan, you can see the compassionate and kind side of him; the scene between him and Agent Romanoff is heart-warming and poignant at the same time. The humane nature explored in Clint's character made is supremely engaging. I wanted more screen time for Doctor Strange so that I can hear more about his one in fourteen million possibilities. Professor Hulk was a fun character. And Iron Man sacrificing himself was an audacious move for the writers. I was reminded of a dialogue by Kylo Ren in The Last Jedi when he says to Ray, "Let the past die.Kill it, if you have to." This movie is more rewarding to the MCU fans. It is a love letter to the original Avengers. The makers have done everything which was warranted to close this chapter spanning a decade.

Review Title: The Culmination of Film's Most Incredible Universe
Review:
While Endgame is not necessary the greatest movie ever, what it accomplishes Is arguably the greatest feat ever pulled in film. To take the plots from 21 different movies and combine them into one three hour slot in a way that makes sense is incredible. Almost every single hero from the movies, no matter how minor, is included, and Marvel somehow manages to further develop the characters of almost every hero, which, again, is a mammoth feat for a three hour film. There is a clear path each character was on since the cinematic universe began, and they stay on their path through the end of this movie.As far as this movie by itself goes, it has the typical humor of a Marvel movie that may not please everyone, but it is not reliant on that humor and certainly has stretches where it allows tension to build without any comic relief. While some people may be displeased about the use of time travel in this film, it is much better than the easier alternative, which would have essentially been another battle with Thanos for the movie, resulting in little character development. Through the time travel, characters can explore their past and continue to develop through meaningful interactions with their past selves. For those people who dislike how un-scientific time travel seems, this is a super hero movie, not a documentary. It isn't supposed to be based on science. After they arrive back to the present, the battle scene begins. As all of the resurrected heroes arrive at the scene, viewers will get goosebumps. There is no better way Marvel could have demonstrated what they accomplished than having everyone together at once, battling evil. It is truly one of the most awe-inspiring scenes in film history.
There was only one real issue with the movie, which happens when all of the female heroes teamed up to protect the Infinity Stones. While this obviously carries a good message, it feels much too forced and comes across as an effort for political correctness rather than actually sending a message. The abilities of all the female superheroes on their own already carry that message in a much more natural way.
Overall, it is best to just step back and look at what Marvel has accomplished over the last 10+ years, and how they managed to pulpit off successfully. Just look at what DC is trying to do with its own universe right now to see how this can all go so wrong very easily. Marvel has managed to create a universe larger than any other film series ever (including Star Wars), filled with twists and turns and built to continue in the future (there are, after all, thousands of superheroes in this universe). While it certainly is not in the taste of film critics, this movie deserves to win awards because there will not be another film for a very long time that tells a story anywhere near the magnitude that this one does.

Sloppy in my opinion. When they suggested bringing the stones back to when they took them this made sense to me (even though Banners/sorceresses explanation sucked. "the stones are time?" shouldn't matter if you take an infinity stone or a rock, you have to bring it back before anyone notices if you want to avoid changing timelines)Other things that annoyed me: I expected 3 hours of movie because they must have so much story to tell, but the beginning and the end were heavily padded with uninteresting stuff.
Everybody was kind of OP sometimes and then weak at other times because I guess this is a team and they did not want anyone stick out as unimportant or too powerful.The movie is too "funny". This was kind of supposed to be a desperate situation yet every scene had to end with a joke and often the jokes were not worth ruining the mood of the scene. We get it Thor is fat now, how absurd!
Which brings me to the next point: the emotional pulling. Apparently a lot of people like it but this movies can not make me cry. Especially because it's always pretty arbitrary who dies and not some inevitable cosmic destiny, so I feel just played by the movie makers. A good death should seem inevitable (They had to kill him to make this work!). None of the deaths in this movie worked this way. In fact they literally played with the viewer by making you guess who is gonna die. Tony sacrificing himself bringing back or saving Spider Man for example would have felt meaningful to me. They did not need to make the gauntlet kill somebody, they made it work this way because they wanted to kill Tony. It just disappoints me sometimes because it seems like movie making 101 to me.On top of that you get the normal comic book nonsense I guess you can not be mad about at this point: Tony figuring out time travel within an afternoon, Nonsensical tech and the fact that you literally need to snap your fingers to make the stones work (who designed that thing this way?), people with spears fighting space ships, space ships bombing an armored compound to rubble but literally missing every living person and the time machine van, Bucky looking like he's on a bender with his band shooting a dang old machine gun at armored super aliens...I also kind of disliked the smart hulk. I would like to review it without spoilers, but I know I won't be able to... So here is my list:Liked:
* Hulk. Like all others, except Captain America, this original avenger has a very good growth arc. He is the embodiment of the inner division so many of us feel (wonder if this was the inspiration for the character - to give the inner rage, inner "i just want to smash things", which most of us so often have to suppress of keep deeply hidden due to our social role, mask). This Hulk is the result of inner peace that is so hard to find - just be a friend to yourself. The scene where current Hulk tries to be the Smash-all-things Hulk is very funny because it stresses the big inner differences between them. Just like the remark: "I wear shirts now". It uses very well the point in timespace when clothes became a symbol of "being civilised".* Black Widow and Hawkeye. These two have one of the best friendships on screen of all times. The love they have for each other could be easily felt in their every scene over the various films. I already saw some complains from a very bias group about he fate of Black Widow, but I assume that they are the kind of people where personal agenda wins over the character consistency. Back Widow has only one family - Hawkeye's family. She was the only one (except Fury, but he knew because of work) who knew about Hawkeye's family. They even named their kid after her, so you know that they each considers one another very closer. Closer than anyone else. And they will do everything for one another. Their main scene showed that very well too. There is no way Black Widow would have let her sister in law and her nephews and nieces live without a father. Their friendship is the goal how friendships between man and a woman should be portrayed. And we for sure don't have them enough on the screen.* Iron Man Tony Stark. His story is so symbolic in this one. Everything started with him and ended with him. His unwillingness to go and leave the family he has and the guilt he felt after Peter Parker turned to dust in his arms. Everything was great. Such a turn around from the playboy we first saw to a two women man. Plus, I doubt there is anyone else who is so much Tony Stark in real life as Robert Downey Jr. You will be missed as Tony Stark.* Captain Marvel. As expected, she didn't have a lot of screen time, but came to the final fight. Was she the key in defeating Thanos (or, more precisely, helping Tony to do it)? Debatable. But the visual effects around her are always very nice. I liked that she (and, sort of, was) the key character. This film wasn't about her or any other new character. This was all about the original 6 and including her would have taken that away.* Captain America. For me he is the most boring character. He is already fully developed in his first film and afterwards he doesn't change. On one hand, it is very nice to see such an unbendable morale and code, on the other hand it's a bit boring. His story end though rases for me a lot of questions that have to do with time travel paradox.* Thor. Nailed it!
Dislike:
* No Fury and Carol Danvers scenes. Seriously. Their first meeting after Fury was brought back should have been epic. Especially if Hill was by the side and has Fury something like: "Nick, what just happened?". The eye Carol should have given to Fury, the remark about "everybody calls me Fury". I also doubt that he would have held up his comments about her hair and her - about his eye. Such a wonderful opportunity missed.

Review Title: Overall, not bad but not as good as the hype.
Review: I have waited some time to do a review on this title so that I could see the market response to the film in addition to having seen it the movie on its opening day. I am happy I let the dust settle on this so I could be level-handed in how I appraised this film. Overall, the film is 'good' but has significant problems throughout. It does not disappoint, I am sure (and given it has already made almost 2 billion globally at the time I write this review). Still, I caution those going into the film with HIGH expectations - like I did. For those that are very detail-oriented, I'd have to say... you'll be disappointed to some degree but will not consider the film a waste of time and money to see. I'll break it down with positives and negatives. The positives are many. First, there seems to be solid continuity between part 1 and part 2. I was happy to see this. I can envision putting these two films together and it would not miss a step or skip a beat. Second, the acting was, as expected, around the same quality we've come to expect from those that have a history of acting in the Avengers and Avengers-related franchises. The special effects, as always, were superb. Now, for the negatives. First, it seems that putting Captain Marvel in there is basically forced and uncomfortable. This character did not belong. Second, this piece does too much social justice warrior messaging. We have Captain America's shield going to Falcon? Since no super capabilities is a part of his physical build, how does he replace a super-human like Captain America? You have a string of female heroes in the battle scene that all the sudden find themselves 'together' to fend off Thanos and company while transporting the glove with the infinity stones. "Oh, don't worry, we'll take it from here, fellas". And some stupid message that is guiding Thor is to be who he is and not what he is supposed to be (these were words from his mother as well). So, he gives up his kingship to Valkyrie? What? Yes, Valkyrie, "you'll be a good queen." And, lastly, holy smokes, this whole dimension of time aspects where you can go back and make changes with no consequences just cannot seem to be logically dealt with in any way. If it was true, why would the stones need to be returned? If it is false, then so many decisions change and likely problems result from the time rifts. In either case, the storyline was poorly written on this aspect and destroys the underlining mission right on up to wonderboy, Captain America, who did not move on from his old flame, staying with her after returning the stones to their original places (thereby interfering with a husband-to-be and children that she had). Irresponsible to significant degree that morally cannot be justified. And let's not even discuss how all these humans are able to hold infinity stones now, okay? The rest, see for yourself. Yes, it is worth seeing but if you try to make sense of it, you're setting yourself up for disappointment. Still worth some good, nonsensical fun.

Avengers Endgame: ReviewBlockbusters like this only come once in a generation. After the epic Infinity War Marvel opted for a more melancholy film. One where the heroes we had connected to lost.The Characters:
Our characters are broken. Destroyed by their failures from the previous film and trying to cope with what happened. Each heroes coping mechanism is different and fallows the characterization all ready established in the other films. Building off what was already established in previous films.
For me Hawkeye is one of the best characters in the film. His ark is set up from scene one. He starts and what he believes as someone who is unredeemable. Then gets a shot at redemption and thinks he will sacrifices himself for the crimes he committed. Instead it was Natasha who ends up sacrificing herself. Now with this new found purpose to live and keep going. This is helped through Jermy Renners acting. His acting throughout helps create as strong emotional core of the film.Acting:
Similar to Infinity War the acting is top notch. Standouts are Karen Gillian as Nebula and Robert Downy Jr. as Iron Man. All the acting is great, from the comedic Thor, to the understated Black Widow who is trying to redeem herself in this new world.Direction:
Joe and Anthony Ruso had there work cut out for them. They directed the film exquisitely creating iconic shots and emotionally impacting moments. The film can do dramatic and make it interesting to look at and watch. The action as well is amazing and similar to the massive battles from Lord Of The Rings.Writing and Story:
If you spent at least 5 minutes on the internet after infinity war you probably saw someone's theory. Every theory out there was wrong but not better than the film we got (something that The Last Jedi suffered from in some peoples opinion).
The smart snappy comedy that the MCU is known for is throughout and helps make the films not all a depressing movie that isn't entertaining.
The writing also do great at subverting audience expectations. Going in a direction that wasn't expected. This is shown perfectly in the first few minutes. Everyone expects the heroes to use the stones and bring all the dead hero's back. Instead the heroes have to wait to get there redemption.Ending A Franchise:
Ending a series in a satisfying and fulfilling ending is hard. But when done right is magical. Look at Return Of The King the film was the end of the LOTR series in a satisfying way. Endgame does this to giving an ending to the story of Tony Stark and Steve Rodgers in a satisfying and conclusive ending. Bring the ending that no one expected and didn't feel rushed.Conclusion:
The film is a blockbuster of the highest caliber. One of both emotion and action bringing everything together in a satisfying conclusive way.Final Score:
11/10

Review Title: The peak of Avengers and the end of an era.
Review: Fans of Marvel have been waiting to see this movie for a year but in reality we've waited to see this movie since the first Marvel movie in 2008 because this movie is the culmination of 11 years of the Marvel and Avengers as we've grown to know and love.Infinity War set a high standard for me and it was really hard to imagine that this movie would surpass that and to be honest I am not really sure if it does or doesn't. I've seen the movie a couple of hours ago and everything is still very fresh and trust me, there is a lot to take in. Nevertheless I feel that the movie is excellent and really well done.A big worry for me was that due to Captain Marvel being extremely OP she would swoop in at the end and destroy everyone, saving the day and being a super superhero. Thankfully that did not happen, although at one point I got big scared when she started smashing everyone. The Russo brothers introduced her to the Avengers really well, she was there for about 15 minutes of screen time and was really a background character which was a very smart thing to do because the last thing you want to do is shove a character down fans throats, especially a new one who has not yet been established, in the long run it will do well for Brie Larson and Captain Marvel.Hawkeye was missing from the Infinity War movie so in Endgame he got a big part, showing how much of a badass he truly is. He has had some crucial scenes in this movie and was one of the main characters which he deserves it since he was a part of the Marvel team for a very long time. He did a great job here and the fans will only grow to like him even more.Black Widow death was a bit of a shock to me. She was one of the characters I was adamant would survive because she has a movie coming out next year. Boy, was I wrong. She was there since the beginning and a big part of Avengers, in the end she sacrificed herself for the greater good. She wouldn't let Hawkeye sacrifice himself because he has a family and kids who need him and she always felt that the only family she has ever had was Avengers and she would do anything and everything for the greater good of that family. An honorable exit for an alumn of this franchise. She will be missed.Thanos is one of the best villains we have seen and ever will see. Thor decapitated him 15 minutes into the movie but we all knew from the trailer that he would come back and wreak havoc on the Avengers one more time. And he does. Even without Infinity Stones he proves just how incredibly strong he is, battling Iron Man, Captain America and Thor successfully. In the end he fails and gets erased from the existence but his actions will always scar the Avengers in many ways.The big death of the movie is of course Iron Man. He is the OG, the one who started it and the one who carried it for very, very long. Robert Downey Jr. will forever be Iron Man and every time you utter those words or mention Iron Man, you will immediately be linked to RDJ's face. He was the one to take the stones from Thanos and "snap" everything back to good, in the end he couldn't survive that and sacrificed himself for the Avengers. He is a staple of this franchise and it will be very hard to imagine another Avengers movie without him.Captain America survives this movie but Steve Rogers is not longer Captain America. He travels through time to return the Infinity Stones but doesn't come back when expected, instead he comes back as a old man who lived his life with his love Peggy Carter, growing old and happy. At the end he gives the shield to Falcon so that he becomes the next Captain and takes his place.There's not many things I didn't like in this movie but that part is definitely a hit and a miss for me. After all this time and all those movies dedicated to Bucky Barnes (Winter Soldier, Civil War), lifelong friendship and build up for him to assume the role of Captain after Steve Rogers, they went with Falcon instead? That just makes no sense to me. I know that Sam Wilson becomes Captain America, as well as Bucky Barnes in the comics but there was little to no build up for us to even treat Sam Wilson as anything more than a sidekick, that's all he ever was and now all of a sudden he assumes the role of one of the biggest superheroes instead of Bucky Barnes. It pissed me off and was definitely a wrong decision by Disney and Marvel.Overall the movie is excellent and definitely doesn't let fans down, it's a spectacle and an emotional experience that deserves to be spoken with the same praise as Infinity War.The future for Marvel and Avengers is very unknown after Endgame, so far we know next to nothing but after Spiderman and Phase 3 ends hopefully we will get some more information.This is definitely the end of an era and in my opinion the peak of Avengers. This is the best it will probably ever get and we should treasure these movies and these experiences for very long time.
