Review Title: Liked it, with some rather major reservations
Review:
I liked it, but I did experience some disappointment.******BEWARE: SPOILERS FOLLOW******I know few, if any, in fiction have come up with any concrete rules for time travel but this film doesn't even try to define any rules; it only mentions the rules of a bunch of other movies about time travel had that, while they didn't make much sense, were at least there. This wasn't a case of using the Time Stone to go back in time, and selectively undo bad things, this was using quantum pseudo-physics where there logically should have been some sort of a ripple effect.
Maybe this was all explained and I just failed to grasp it but let me try to list all of the times where messing with the time-space continuum are simply ignored. The movie acts as if the only bad thing that could have happened (and did happen) was for Thanos to be alerted to the Avengers' goal of finding the stones and traveling to the future to get the stones. But, logically, a lot of other things probably should, or should not, have happened, maybe some of them bad. This movie doesn't even raise the question:
1. Loki steals the Tesseract in 2012, after a flubbed attempt by present-day (that is five years into the future) Stark, Rogers and Lang to retrieve it. Shouldn't this have caused a ripple in the time-space continuum? No, I guess not. Also, does this happen before or after Thor and Rocket go to Asgard 2013 to retrieve the Reality Stone and pass Loki's cell on the way. I'm honestly just asking.
2. Or does Stark and Rogers going back to 1970 and taking the Tesseract from that point prevent whatever Loki was supposed to have done with the Tesseract in 2012 from happening? If so, wouldn't it also have prevented other things from happening? For instance, Captain Marvel?
3. In 2013 Thor calls Mjolnir to him after talking to his soon-to-be-slain) mother. Um...uh...er...yeah... Forgive me for asking the obvious but wouldn't this leave the Thor of 2013 rather in the lurch and changed the course of events in *The Dark World*?
4. Shouldn't present-day Nebula killing her past self have ended her life too? No? Does time not work like that either, then? Okay, sure, whatever. Have it your way then, movie.
5. Shouldn't 2014-Thanos being snapped out of existence have undone all the people he killed, including Heimdall, Loki, Gamora and Vision?
6. I'm not sure what Cap did after dancing with Peggy Carter. Did he never get frozen? Did he just live his life normally with Peggy?
7. Not really a time-space thing, but more of a movie (il)logic thing, but just like in *Captain Marvel*, we have a situation where a kid doesn't age after five or more years. In *Captain Marvel,* it was Monica Rambeau, not aging after six years. In this movie it was Ned who, after five years, is still in high school for some reason. On the flip side, we have a kid, Scott Lang's daughter Cassie, who was probably no older than ten in *Ant-Man and the Wasp* magically aged to what looks like seventeen or eighteen after five years. Maybe 2018 Cassie is supposed to be eleven in AMATW and sixteen in EG.
A few points not related to time travel:
* It was interesting to see a kinder, gentler Hulk, who is really just Banner in a nerfed Hulk body, but we were deprived of seeing the Hulk unleashed (we did get a bit of that with the 2012 Hulk). The anticipated fight between Hulk and, well, anybody, never materialized. The only story reason he is in a Hulk body at all is so he can survive snapping his fingers wearing a stoned Infinity Gauntlet. Also, once again, it looked like Thanos got the lion's share of the CGI budget. Banner-Hulk looked okay, just not as convincing as he might have.
* Didn't care to see Thor slapped around like a rag doll by Thanos. Thor really fared no better than Captain America and might even have done worse. Isn't Thor supposed to be far stronger and more durable than Cap? This brings to mind *Avengers: Age of Ultron*, where Cap holds his own against the titular villain while Thor needs Vision to stop Ultron beating on him. I'm as big a fan of Cap as anyone, but come on, stop making Thor into such a piker, Marvel Studios. Also, I can appreciate humor as well as anyone, but maybe stop making Thor into such a clown?
* I know they wanted to save Stark's best moment for last - and it was a truly epic movie moment - but it strikes me a bit odd that he could manage to give Thanos something of a fight after having a friggin' moon thrown at him in *Infinity War*, then get quickly knocked out in *Endgame* early in the fight while wearing a fully powered suit. On a related note, it's never really explained why Thanos is so tough. In the comics it is, but in the movies, not so much, if at all.
I liked pretty much everything else (one particular thing I liked was that Captain Marvel didn't save the day, as I feared she might). If I ever watch again, I'll try to think about the rules of time travel as much as the filmmakers did, which is to say, not at all.
(a2a)

Review Title: The missing resolution to the Thanos Problem
Review: Warning: Spoilers ahead!I have two major criticisms about Avengers Endgame that I call the "Thanos Problem". These are:1) In Infinity War, a very serious question was asked: what should be done about overpopulation and the increasing fight for limited resources? Thanos's answer was to wipe out half of all sentient life. It is very easy to see on how many different levels this answer is flawed. In this movie, Avengers Endgame, the heroes had their own opportunity, after acquiring all the infinity stones again to address this problem in a more constructive way. It was possible for them to literally do ANYTHING they wanted to make the world a better place. With just a snap of their fingers, they could have eradicated poverty and diseases, yet they did nothing with this power. Even if that is too much, they still could have started to change the world for the better, before for example the stones would power down, and show us how much good they did. It could have been so uplifting. But no, they need to bring the stones back right away where each of them belonged.2) My other major criticism is about the character of Thanos. In Infinity War, we saw a unique villain, who had emotions and was a much more complex villain than what we usually get. In this film, Endgame, we don't see the emotional side of Thanos at all, he is reverted back to the usual one-dimensional villain. They could have explored the human side of his character a bit more for example his relationship with his daughter. If they really wanted to bring back a dead character, why not bring back Gamora, which would allow this rediscovery of Thanos's human side to evolve? She could have been teleported out before dying by the mysterious force that required a sacrifice for exchange of the Soul Stone. Then, linking up with the Avengers, they could have devised a plan to find Thanos, and convince him that what he did to the world was wrong. This could have been done by exploiting his love for his daughter, and making him see that he took away the daughters and sons of so many, who all suffer, just as he did when he lost Gamora. After realizing this, he would correct his thinking and restore everyone thus providing a substantial character development to him and give him the proper ending he deserved (as opposed to being beheaded by Thor while unarmed).The humor and visual effects are excellent, but I was expecting more from the story and buildup of the previous film.

Review Title: a love letter to the fans
Review: I never thought that a comic book movie could make me cry, and Avengers: Endgame made me cry... several times. I was a little skeptical at first at the fact the movie was over three hours long, and that they couldn't tell what needed to be told without it feeing rushed, but I was so wrong. Avengers: Endgame is the perfect ending to a beloved story that has lasted over ten years, it makes all the right choices and ticks all the boxes. For the first time in a while a movie surprised me not only once but 10 times, for once twists actually feel like a twist, they're not predictable as most movies are now-a-days. The casts performances made these once cheesy and quirky comic book characters feel like more human, showing some of the finest and convincing acting ever put to screen. The movies serious moments are jaw-dropping, but that still doesn't mean that theres no humour, in fact Endgame nearly has as much comedy in it as guardians of the galaxy. I loved the second act simply because it was cool and interesting to see past MCU movies from a different perspective. then the climax happens, and theres more 'war' in the climax than there is in the whole of 'infinity war', The climax has some of the most stunning action sequences in movie history. Robert Downey Jr was the perfect choice to kill of, simply because the person who started it all, should be the one to end it, his final words "I am Iron Man" really got me crying, but it didn't make me cry as much as the very last scene, with captain America finally getting his dance with Peggy Carter, something that we've all been wanting for eight years since Captain America: the first Avenger. With that being said, Avengers: Endgame is an emotional and bitter sweet way to end the saga that has come close to all our hearts, it's a wild ride through everything we've been through over this long decade, with it's phenomenal performances, beautiful script, stunning effects, suspenseful action, brilliant script and top quality cinematography; Avengers: Endgame will go down in history as the final piece of the puzzle to the most beloved franchise of all time, its perfection amongst the millions of movies that have been made, it will be remembered until the end of days as a cinematic masterpiece.

As a casual fan of the MCU (watched most movies, read no comics) it didn't have such an impact on me but it was an enjoyable ride all the same. I was worried at the beginning that the three hours would drag (some scenes were padded, shall we say) but it was no difficulty. Though there was surprisingly little action, it kept my attention throughout. I did find myself getting lost occasionally with all the references to previous movies that I simply couldn't remember well enough.A scene I found particularly effective was the opening with Hawkeye's family. I thought it did well to remind us where we left off without retreading the same ground as before.I found one plot point particularly confusing. I thought Thanos had to sacrifice the thing most dear to him who was coincidentally beside him in the previous movie yet here it seemed like the soul stone just requires whoever happens to be standing next to you. I've got to say the image of the dead body was my favourite though, absolutely stunning.As for humour, some felt misplaced and fell flat but there were a few hilarious moments for sure. Thor is essentially comic relief which may not please some but I enjoyed almost all of his scenes. I just think Chris Hemsworth is such a pro at his delivery.Overall it was a tremendous effort to try to wrap up so many stories in a satisfying way. For most I imagine it will be successful, I just felt it tied too neat a bow on everything. I've got to say I wanted a higher body count, further showing my morbid taste. I had no significant attachment to the characters so my eyes remained completely dry as we progressed through the farewells which rival LOTR for length if not emotion. It was still a very enjoyable ride. I would say Infinity War was more thrilling but Endgame was more polished. Definitely worth a watch.

Review Title: Super-sized, roller coaster of fantastical fun
Review:
I was recently introduced to the Marvel Cinematic Universe by my wife, who is a long time fan of superhero film and TV. Apart from the occasional Batman movie, superheroes never really interested me, but I am now a convert.
Taking the MCU in the context in which it is intended, as fun and family orientated entertainment, you can allow yourself to become immersed in its brilliance.
Endgame ties up the Avengers franchise perfectly, with three hours of excellent action and character interaction.
The movies starts with Deadeye/Clint Barton losing his entire family. A story line taken from the characters origin story. It is a very emotional piece of cinematography to start the movie and creates a human connection with Deadeye (played by Jeremy Renner) in his pain and eventual mission to bring his family back. Thanos is dispatched early in the film with a swift strike of Thor's axe-hammer. The movie then delves into a series of time travel events to try and undo the devastation Thanos brought to planet Earth. Of course, surprise surprise, our heroes are successful, after an incredible final battle which involves every hero of the MCU coming together. It is a wonderful sight to behold. But alas, what has been foreshadowed throughout the franchise, finally came to pass. The passing of Tony Stark. A sad moment for all Iron Man and Avengers fans, for sure. An epic money spinner? Yes of course. But nobody can deny it's value for money to entertainment ratio. Possibly the greatest super hero movie ever made and it will take something truly special to take that crown.

This review contains spoilers for Avengers: Endgame and Infinity WarWe are in the endgame now...Is there anything left to say about a movie over two billion dollars and has been a bigger topic of conversation around the world than Game of Thrones and Donald Trump?Turns out, a lot.What's this movie about?Avengers: Endgame is following the devastating events of the Infinity War. The universe is in ruins. With the remaining allies, the Avengers assemble once more in order to undo Thanos' actions and restore order to the universe.
The culmination of 10 years and 22 films. The most comprehensive mythological ever presented on the screen, an incredible range of world-class talent, and all the rest. This is the "end of the road" Tony started us on.MY OPINION:Story:
We never see our heroes like this in any other Marvel film. They know they lost and they know that they can't do anything to reverse what happened in Infinity War. As an audience, you really feel the emotion of loss of hope.Everybody is in a different location, Iron Man is trapped in space with Nebula while Captain America, Hulk, Black Widow, and other fellow Avengers are in the Avenger tower.First of all, I love this movie, but at the same time, like all the other movies in the Marvel Universe, it has the same flaws.
This is a 3-hour long movie and they made a great job balancing all the character and action moments. Phasing sometimes is a little off, but that's okay because it doesn't distance you out from the movie.
In the beginning, Captain Marvel saves Tony Stark in the first 10 minutes of the movie and that to me is just lazy writing. It was too fast and it doesn't give you the time to acknowledge that these characters are in real danger. Another issue that I have with this movie is that Ant-Man is saved by a rat. I don't know whose idea that was, but we had some theories of how Ant-Man could return from the quantum realm and is this really what they gave us? We're supposed to believe that Ant-Man is saved by a rat. I just don't buy this stuff in movies.Characters:Let's talk about characters since this movie is heavily about the story and character ark. Characters are always brilliantly written and balanced throughout the whole film. They took some risks with two characters which could have turned out pretty bad, but somehow they managed to find the perfect way to do it. Of course, I'm talking about Thor and Hulk ( Bruce Banner ). I loved both of the characters. What they have changed felt quite ambitious and hilarious, although I sometimes miss the old Hulk smashing things like the good old days.
This film is heavily focused on Iron Man ( Tony Stark ) and Captain America ( Steve Rogers ). What they have done with these two characters is just wonderful and brilliant. In the beginning, you feel the tension between these two characters because of what happened in the Civil War. One of Tony's iconic line this movie proposed was " I love you 3000 " which added this film something special. Considering how Hawkeye's relationship with his daughter was described, this line emphasized it all perfectly. Tony's sacrifice at the end when he took all the infinity stones and snapped his finger killing Thanos and his army was very well done. And Tony's final line " I AM IRON MAN " added another layer of emotion to that moment. His final line is a reference to the very first Iron Man film that created this huge universe. Marvel finds the perfect way to end Tony's ark and it couldn't be any better. His monologue at the end was so meaningful and precious. In the end, as an audience, you understand and admit that this is the end of the Iron Man storyline.Captain America's story arc didn't fall behind Iron Man's in any manner. In this movie, Marvel finds a perfect way to end Captain America's ark. In the beginning, he is hopeless like all the fellow Avengers. He adds this film so much heart and emotion. At the final battle, we saw Captain America hold the Mjollnir which was an awesome moment. We saw Captain America move Mjholiner a little bit in Avengers: Age of Ultron and it was even better to see Captain America finally lift and hold Mjollnir which proves that he is finally worthy. After Hulk snapped and got every hero back in action Captain America says " AVENGERS ASSEMBLE ", this moment was something to be experienced. After the final battle, Captain America had to bring the stones back to fix different timelines. After that, we are seeing old Captain America which left us confused, but soon after that, we learn that after he puts the stones back to their original locations, he lived his full life with his only love Agent Carter. When he finally returns as an old man back to his timeline, he gives his shield to Falcon when everyone thought it was gonna be Bucky, but I thought it was a great moment between Captain America and Falcon. The movie ends with Captain America and Agent Carter dancing in the past which was a reference to the first Captain America film similar to the reference mentioned about Iron Man earlier. It was a great ending for Captain America's character ark. It couldn't end any better. It was a wonderful and bittersweet ending.Time Travel:Now it's the time for the main concept that everyone is talking about, which is time travel.
This is not an ordinary time travel film like Back to the Future. At the beginning of this film, we find out that Thanos used the stones again on another planet. Our heroes are once more going to try to get the stones from Thanos, but when they arrive they are learning that Thanos used the stones to destroy the stones. Then the film cuts to five years later...
Our heroes are desperate and try to move on some do, but not them. All of a sudden Ant-Man appears and talks about the possibilities of time travel. After Tony changes his decision and joins the team again for the possibilities of time travel. After they find out how time travel works they are going back in time and the movie turns into a time heist.Time travel is a risky thing to do in any movie because it has science behind it and if you change the rules of time travel people will judge every little thing, in the end, it could be a bad choice for your film. In this film, they change the rules and not everything makes sense, but after they explained how it works in this universe it started to makes more sense. This is a superhero movie after all not everything will going to make sense and that's okay. After they went back on time the movie shines and we as an audience are experiencing the old MCU films once again which was an awesome moment to experience in the theater. Our heroes are traveling different timelines through MCU the reason is they are trying to restore the stones before Thanos for the sake of the universe. Hawkeye and Natasha went to Vormir to get the soul stone, but they didn't know the requirements for the soul stone. Then we as audience witnessing the terrible event that happened to Natasha aka Black Widdow. She sacrifices herself for the soul stone which was a shocking moment that I didn't see coming. After all, this is a fun, ambitious, different and emotional time heist superhero film.CONCLUSION:In the end, this is a brilliantly written, well-directed and well-acted action-packed superhero film that fans were waiting for. Sometimes passing is little off and there are some lazy moments and not all the time travel stuff makes sense, but as a whole, it just works and creates a whole different superhero experience for the audience. I love this movie and every superhero fan will enjoy this movie. This is the end of the journey Tony had started us on and it ended beautifully.Rating: 9/10

Review Title: A superb movie if you exclude the complexities of Time Travel
Review:
Being a Marvel Fan, I am happy with the movie. The movie had some great moments a Fan could wish for. But the expectation from the movie especially after the performance of Infinity War (a mind blowing movie: 10/10) were not fulfilled. The movie literally had so many loop holes and lacked logic at many critical points that I couldn't really enjoy the positives as much as I did for Infinity War.I watched the Movie in IMAX 3D, so obviously the viewing experience was awesome as the movie was shot very well, the cinematography, the VFX, the action scenes, etc. were really great (10/10). But then came in time travel and they took a stand on the concept of time travel different from any other movie. Even that is fin as they have the freedom. But then repeatedly, at every crucial point they violated the rules that they set themselves. The concept of creating a parallel timeline, the concept of not effecting your present by travelling to the past was all lost when they started collecting the stones.
The same issue is with Captain Marvel altering the time line at the end of the movie.Another problem is the idea of how Thanos with such a huge army travelled through time to the present using just 1 vial of Pym particle and with no available technology of using the Pym Particle is beyond digestion. They need to explain that part as everything relies on that.There are many other loop holes and errors (I have counted more that 10 major-major issues). But the movie had many positive points. Professor Hulk finally appeared as expected. A base for Ronan has been set. Almost everyone is back for the Last Battle. And sadly, Iron man is dead (that another problem with the logic of the movie).No doubt that many movie have loop holes, but it wasn't expected at such a large scale of this Movie. It was a 10/10 because of the battles, because of the acting, etc. But it lost 2 crucial points because of the flawed storyline. The movie is an emotional sine curve, it has moment of anxiety, joy, horror, sadness, excitement, etc. But surely it's not a 'Movie of the Generation' or a 'Masterpiece'. I feel Infinity war deserves and keeps these titles.But worth a watch, and do watch it in IMAX, you would love the battles.

Review Title: A WORTHY END TO THE MCU INFINITY SAGA - BUT NOW WITHOUT IT'S FLAWS
Review: The film begins straight 3 weeks after the events of Infinity War with Captain Marvel rescuing Iron Man and Nebula and bringing them to Earth. IM doesn't want anything to do with the Avengers anymore so doesn't go with the rest of the team to hunt down Thanos who's now living on some distant planet. The Avengers along with CM get to the planet to find out that the Gauntlet with the stones has been destroyed along with the stones so that no one can undo what Thanos has done. At this moment Thor chops off Thanos' head and you then realise that the rest of the film isn't going to be about how to get back at Thanos. Remember this is in the very first 20 minutes.Fast forward 5 years and the Avengers have all moved on to other priorities in their lives and only BW and CA are running the Avengers. As luck would have it, a rat walks over the controls of the quantum machine thing and out pops Ant Man from the end of the last Ant Man film. He then teams up with BW and CA to reassemble the Avengers and go back in time to get the stones and undo what Thanos has snapped. The rest of the film is how the stones are recovered and how everything is resolved. This is my main gripe with this film, time travel...I always feel that films that feature time travel or alternate universes use this as an easy way to get around problems and issues with the story. They ended the previous film with killing off half the characters and then thought how can we bring them back? I know we'll just go back in time and sort everything out. Don't get me wrong, I love time travel films, one of my all-time favourites is back to the future, as long as time travel is what the theme of the story is, but to use time travel as an easy excuse to give the Heroes an advantage is the lazy option. Recently the re-booted Star Trek being an example of an alternate universe which just didn't have the same emotional connect as the original series as very easily everything that has been shown can just be erased/altered with time travel and introducing an alternate universe. If you want to watch a good series that uses alternate universes then I would highly recommend searching out Fringe which was shown around 10 years ago.So now we've established time travel is what the major portion of this film is going to be could we please stop referencing older time travel films just so the makers can poke fun at their own stupid idea before the audience does. The amount of times Back to the future is called upon is sometimes a bit shameful. This film gives you so much de ja vu that you know that you've seen this before, BKF2 anyone. There's even a scene reminding you of Doc's explanation to Marty about scewing the timeline. It's a shame Marvel couldn't think of any other way to get back at Thanos other than resorting to time travel. Also, why not just time travel back with CM to when Thanos was about to snap and add her into the fight as well? Would be a lot easier than trying to get the stones back one by one! Also, this time machine they devise not only lets you travel through time but also lets you change your geographical location, amazing! But I will say this, on the flip side using time travel to revisit the past films is the best way to tie everything in and a chance for some serious fan service!So once the stones are recovered Iron Man does the snap again and the entire Avengers characters return for one last bad ass battle with Thanos. Here there are some great action set pieces and the majority of the characters get their own small part to play, especially during the whole 'rugby' sequence with the new gauntlet. But the flaw here is that Iron Man uses the gauntlet to do the snap and not Thor or Hulk who are more powerful. But obviously Marvel wanted to end this infinity stone saga with the death of Iron Man as it started with Iron Man back in 2008. So a well justified send off for the character and also now not having to pay Robert Downey Jr so much either. I'd like to say the following, a more emotional ending during Iron Man's death scene would have been having Thor, CA, Hulk, and Hawkeye kneeling around Iron Man and at this point CA and IM shake hands to put aside their differences and then Gwyneth's character saying her line. Currently you see CA and Thor crying at IM's death but you don't really get a sense of where they're stood. Where's BW you ask? She died trying to get the soul stone and doesn't even get a funeral scene!So to summarise, even though there are so many flaws with the story and screenplay, being over 3 hours long, because you're 11 years and 22 films deep into this saga you easily brush over the minus points and only leave the cinema with plus points. The film is a cinematic gem and the final hour or so more than makes up for the short comings mentioned earlier.As an afterthought, the ending of the film shows CA not coming back to his reality after returning the stones to the respective points in time and instead living his life through to an old man with Agent Carter. Could this mean then that what we are now seeing is not the same universe but an alternate universe where things are now changed? How else would an easier solution be to include the X-Men into the MCU now that Disney has bought 20th Century Fox?

I walked out of the cinema and rode home on my bike. It was raining outside - oh how poetic - and I had a smile on my face. In the next moment I had tears in my eyes. Then I was smiling again.
Funny, what a movie can do to you.
In that moment I felt infinitely grateful to be born in this time. I mean, I could have been born around 1600. I would have had the chance to watch Shakespeare plays live. But I'm pretty happy to watch what must be todays equivalent of a Shakespeare play. I just witnessed a cinematic masterpiece. But not just that. I had the feeling I just experienced a final step and the end of an era.If you think Infinity War was overwhelming in it's quantity of superheroes in one place, then, oh boy, you've no idea what's coming for you. You think you're prepared for this movie? Think again, you're not.
Endgame is a new level.
In some regards it's more of an Avengers movie than the previous one. We're very limited in our assembly of heroes. It really focuses on our beloved six.Clint got a rogue makeover. The scene where he lost his family was really heartbreaking. You can understand his motives. He's clearly in distress. He needs to be woken up by Natasha to get onto the right path, again. But when he's awake Hawkeye is the hero that we once met.Natashas development from deadly assassin who works for scrupulous leaders to a leader who holds her new found family together and sacrifices herself to protect this family is one of the most incredible character arches to watch. Truth be told I never expected her to be the sacrificing one.
The MCU lost its greatest badass. Black Widow, I'm going to miss you.Thor! Please, get back into shape. I mean think of all the fun Loki would be making of you if he could see you! Brother, have you swallowed a planet? (Well, Loki is still dead, but he still managed to steel some moments in the true God of Mischief fashion. Wherever you are I hope the sun is shining on you and could you please not be dead? That would be great, thank you! I mean really, you have to be alive - somehow. Are you sure you checked that you really don't have a heartbeat?) Thor is the one who takes the finger snap the hardest and drowns his sorrows in alcohol which shows in his not so fit form than what we're used to. It's one of the funniest aspects of the whole movie. In general this movie is not just epic, it's funny in moments that are totally serious. With a little bit of mummys help you got yourself together again.
You couldn't resist, could you? You just had to get Mjölnir back.
The decision to join the Guardians of the Galaxy... oh how much potential I see.No Hulk in the last movie, therefore more Hulk in this one. A very different Hulk. I think Bruce Banner did something, that nobody expected. He accepted the Hulk as something that is a part of himself. Not as the green rage monster, but as something that isn't a mistake but a gift. A great massage: accept your faults and turn them into something beautiful. Embrace them and be proud.Captain America, you fought Red Skull, you fought Iron Man, you fought Thanos and now you fought yourself. Now you're worthy enough to wield Mjölnir. Truth be told it was the most beautiful and epic moment of my fangirl life to watch you pick up that hammer. It's a moment that I'll never forget. You're worthy of another big part of a heroes life. After years of fighting and suffering you're finally worthy enough to get your happy end. Steve, I'm so unbelievably happy for you and Peggy. You gave your shield to Sam. America, you have a new Captain.
Sam, be sure, we will follow you to the end of the line.Iron Man, to be honest I didn't like you when I first watched Iron Man. With time you grew on me. Now I can't imagine the MCU without you. But sadly it's a thought that we all have to live with. You're the beginning and the end of the whole infinity saga. You're the heart of the Avengers. Now more than ever.
And you invented time travel. Which definitely makes you the coolest Avenger.
Tony Stark, who gained the most after Thanos finger snap and lost the most while attempting to undo it. We should all pay our respect to the genius, billionaire, playboy (now married and the father of one daughter) and philanthropist that was Tony Stark.
Tony, I assure you, we will remember you.One in particular will do that.
Guess who's back? Spider Man!
And everybody else!
But most importantly Spider Man! You had like what? Three minutes of screen time? It's an accomplishment that you managed to leave tears in my eyes nearly every time I saw you. Especially your reunion with Tony was a moment of genuin happiness. The moment of your goodbye was a moment of genuine sadness.
Seeing you again... that was nice. Thank you for coming back, I guess. You can make all the tears up to me with a hell of a movie in July this year.Ladies and gentleman, it seems the superhero business finally understood that women can kick ass just as well as man. The symbolic act of gathering every female character together in one scene and let them kick Thanos in his purple behind, should be an eyeopener. Beware, everybody who lives under a rock and thinks a woman belongs in a kitchen, there are woman out there with brains and skills you could never imagine and together we will come for you.Often small people aren't taken seriously. I should know that, because I'm not that tall of a person myself. So it took me great satisfaction to see that small, underrated Ant-Man brings us the solution to this whole mess. Remember: especially small people can have the biggest impact.It's quite poetic, ironically tragic, how Thanos finds his end. Well, both times are. Thor took his advise and aimed for the head. The rest is dust in the wind.People might say it's an overly long attempt of making money with a storyline that took ten years to set up, an overwhelming amount of characters and too many references to all the other MCU movies. Well, my response to those people is: I don't care. Because I look at what this movie does with those who watch it. And what I see amazes me. I'm a strong believer that the fictional world is in some regards real because the fans let it become a realistic thing.
There are people who join you because you're your annoying self, sit through this three hour long epos and laugh with you even though you had to explain to them what was going on during the movie.
There are men sitting behind you in the cinema who don't even try to hide their tears when their favorite superhero dies.
When the whole theater gasps, cries out and is nearly getting a heart attack every time someone throws a punch at one of our heroes, because they can't stand watching them get hurt, you know you're sitting in a brillant and mind blowing MARVEL movie.
Give me one other movie franchise that has accomplished that. I dare you.I think superhero movies have this prejudice that they are supposed to be simple. There is a good and a bad guy. They fight and in the end the good guy wins. It's not like that anymore. MARVEL changed that. The whole MCU connects so many dynamics, storylines and characters that you really are lost if you don't watch all movies. It's quite clever. You have to watch every MARVEL movie to get the full experience in the end. So yes, some people will watch this movie and be completely confused in some scenes, because we're taking a trip down memory lane through a lot of MARVEL movies. But that's not what this movie stands for. It's not for falling asleep halfway through the movie or leaving the cinema before the credits roll down.
This movie is a gift, a treasure and a reward for all the love and passion and tears, for all those who stuck with MARVEL for the last ten years.
The ones who watched every minute and sat through every end credit scene just to get a few more seconds out of the movie.
It's for those who where in awe when Captain America was turned into a super soldier; who had goose-pimples when the Avengers first assembled, who fell a little bit more in love with Loki than with Thor, who where torn during the Civil War and wanted to protect Spider Man in his fight against the Vulture.
It's for everybody who felt like their heart was just ripped out of their chest after Infinity War.
We get a thank you, a band aid and a promise for much more to come.The end is not pleasing, there are things that could've been better, people that could've survived and people that could've come back.
But I think it's the best possible and most perfect end that we could've gotten out of all options. And there were fourteen million six hundred five other options. If this is what it takes to win, I take it. Where Infinity War was a brutal crushing of all our hearts, Endgame was the difficult task to put all of us back together, to reunite what was torn apart, to mend what was broken. It was as challenging as the collection of all the infinity stones for the avengers.
But it worked.
It's not undone. All the chaos not just disappeared, Infinity War wasn't simply erased. There are still broken parts and pieces, the events are going to leave scars.
But our family is back together again.
To quote Iron Man: »Part of the journey is the end.«
But an end doesn't have to be sad. Look at the Avengers:
One gets his peace.
One gets his time back.
One accepts himself for what he is.
One gets the chance to recover from his loses.
One protects her family.
One gets his family back for good.
If you look at it like that, I think everybody got their happy end.
An end can also be the start of a new beginning.There was an idea to bring together a group of remarkable people, see if they could become something more. See if they could work together when we needed them to to fight the battles we never could.
They could.
Earth mightiest heroes avenged us.
All is well.
The sun is shining again - on all of us.There is just one more thing to say:
Thank you, Avengers!

I have to say that I am a big fan of the Marvel Universe created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby since the 70s. Review Title: Not Infinity War level, but still a pretty good "ending" to the Avengers movies
Review:
It is not easy to end a series after a movie like Infinity War, even more having in account all the pressure the fans put on the ending. Endgame definitely dealt quite well with it. It is not as good as Infinity War, but then again, I doubt there will be a superheroes movie as good as that one for quite a long time, but overall it as a very good movie. A well written script, just as long as it needed to be to make it good (having in account all the goodbyes that needed to be given) with a masterly handling of the spectators emotions: you'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll suffer, you'll be anxious, all of it, several times, during the whole movie. On the downside, there a few crappier dialogues, mostly when they are trying to get the team together to travel in time (the one between Tony and Pepper, the one between Black Widow and Captain America, and a few more).
Still on the downside, there are a few actors to point out: Scarlett Johansson has a specially poor performance, with her two major scenes being quite horrible (her talk with Captain America, and her death), always overdramatic, always fake... Chris Evans wasn't much better, almost never making any kind of expression in a movie that asked a big lot out of him. On the plus side, Robert Downey Jr was great, as usual, and Chris Hemsworth surprised me big time, with a worthy performance. About the directing, I think it was just as good as any superheroe movie.
The visual effects were closing in on perfect, as one would expect.
The appearances of Captain Marvel gave too much the idea of convenience, with her saying that they probably won't see much of her, which basically leaves them with total freedom to bring her in when it is most convenient.
To finish, Infinity War left no choice but for them to mess with time travel (or dimension travel, whatever you wanna call it). As happens with every movie who does it, and even though they did seem to think a bit more about it than most movies, they still got themselves into a huge mess, and there a couple of errors in their theory.
All in all, 3 hours well spent, well paced by the writers and well put on screen to entertain the fans. And a finale that I think will please most fans.

Part of this down feeling is that now I'm not looking forward to anything. Stan Lee is gone, that's part of it too. Even after Infinity War, the dramatic irony was that we all knew the dead characters were coming back, no doubt (With Spiderman Far from Home, and other characters having more movie deals). But now what?So fans, prior to the movie, we knew many things:
The dead were coming back.There would probably be time travel involved, as well as the Quantum Realm.RDJ and Chris Evans where at the end of their contract.So the bar was high in terms of surprises, we already suspected the big "revelations" of the film. And, for me, when I expected the big clever satisfactory endind twist, instead, all I got was a fist fight.And a fist fight that violated the laws of the previous movie. In Infinity War, Ironman held his ground against Thanos for a bit, Cap could grabb the Gaunlet and surprised Thanos, Thor almost cut him in half. All of that against a Thanos that had all or most of the stones. Now those three together, with 2 godly weapons, are easily defeated by a "lesser" Thanos. As a fan, I expected Thanos to put up a fight with his wit, not his fists (or his army).But I'd be willing to overlook that if I had something in exchange. And this is the main downside of this movie. What I got was depressing, depressing, a bit of hope, depressing...Then 20 minutes of fight, and then more depressing stuff (death, getting old, characters that don't know each other...). The joyful "resurrection" happened off camera, and we didn't have time to celebrate or enjoy it. We have enough depressing things in real life, thanks.On another note, even as a man I felt insulted by the forced attempt at feminism, right before a guy with "man" in his name wins the fight. It felt like a half-hearted throw of a bone, very disrespectful to the female fandom. Sorry, embarrasing.I'd like to talk about the good things too. And the respect I have for the collective effort the cast and crew made. But I left the movie theatre very sad, and that's still how I feel.Sad movies can be good too, but that's not what I expected from this. That's what I would have loved to experience in the film.I give it a 7, because it's worth watching. Review Title: With Great Power, Comes No Responsibility
Review:
I watched Endgame twice. And both times, something just wasn't sitting right with me. The jokes generally landed, the fan service was everywhere, and it seemed like everything generally was wrapped up, even if Thanos was strangely overpowered without the Gauntlet and Captain Marvel's Deus Ex Machina appearance was cheap. It was, while no 10/10 amazing art piece (and of course it wasn't, it was never supposed to be), a seemingly solid blockbuster, with a huge, unstoppable marketing machine and legions of ravenous fans, hungry for more.All movies, irregardless of whether they set out to do so or not, have something to say. It's the same of all art. As human beings, we absorb messages given to us by these art pieces, even if they were designed 'merely' as simple entertainment.
In the world we live in, we're eager to forfeit choice, and in doing so, we forfeit responsibility. I liked Infinity War because it taught the Avengers something. It taught not only the Avengers, but should have taught the audience as well - heroes can't win every time. It's impossible. The Avengers, irregardless of their status, have lost, and we as a world, and they too, had to live with that.
Endgame's message is cheap and rather disheartening. The Avengers, instead of trying to live with their mistakes, are portrayed as people who'd rather cling on to the past and to their past failures. Tony Stark is the only character in the film who has accepted what has happened and moved on. In real life, there's no opportunity to go back and correct one's mistakes - we have to live with them. There's no 'save, reload' function, no time travel button.
The Avengers, rather than showing their strengths as admirable heroes who'd press on despite their losses, try to reverse their mistake, and despite their best efforts, doom several other realities to chaos or even destruction. They are confident at the beginning of the movie, eager to win against Thanos, but when they find that their loss cannot be reversed, they can't accept it. For five years, they grieve - as does the world.
Where is the human spirit of endeavor? During history, people have always stood back up from tragedy and done their best to rebuild. That's what we do as human beings.
Avengers: Endgame presents a flawed philosophy - it's the mistakes in the past that matter, not the choices in the future. In choosing the past, we absolve our responsibility for the future, and damn... that's dangerous.

Review Title: Solid, fun but ultimately inconstant (and incoherent) entry.
Review:
This movie has a half-dozen amazing scenes, a dozen great lines and two dozen great moments. But, it left me unfulfilled. First, the great. The elevator scene is one of the best in all the Marvel movies. Captain America using his cleverness to outwit Hydra. The fight against his younger self is great too. As is the hammer moment. Peter getting knocked out by Nebula and War Machine was hilarious. The opening scene with Hawkeye was a punch to the gut. The moment where all the heroes return near the end is overwhelming. There are other moments that really shine. I found myself Involuntarily clapping many times.But, the movie fails to deliver satisfying conclusions to most of its characters. Turns out Cap never sacrificed anything at all in the end. He lived 70 years with the woman he loved. All while leaving Bucky to be tortured (not to mention sitting idly by while numerous other atrocities occurred).
Kids, it's also cool to play video games all day and leave your responsibilities. Even if you have god like powers and people rely on you and hope for better days. You do you, and put someone else in charge so that you can do the hard work of threatening little kids on Fortnite. You know, the real important things in life.
Speaking of life, the soul stone requires an "everlasting" sacrifice of what you love. Except it doesn't. No one dies in the MCU. Not for long anyway. Why morn the loss of Loki for the third time. He's alive, duh. Why give vision and Black Widow a funeral, or wake or at least a eulogy? They didn't. The film does not care about these two characters deaths. Why should the audience.
And are they really dead? Just go back in time with the Pym particles anytime you want and, poof, they're alive. You could visit anytime you want to. Iron Man saw his dad. Hawkeye heard his daughter's voice. And that half of the Universe thing. No worries, they are all alive. In the end, all the bad guys dies and three Avengers.But, those three Avengers will stay dead for how long?
Does anyone seriously think they are really dead? As in forever? Or course not. In five years, all three of them will be in a Marvel movie again. So don't cry too hard, no one dies forever (in the MCU that is).

Review Title: Let me fill your plot holes
Review: Many Spoilers relating to perceived Plot Holes.Firstly, I loved this film. A fitting end to a fantastic series. Strong characters with stronger powers, and finally some emotional depth to get on board with.What is troubling me with many of the attention grabbing negative reviews here is the plot hole mantra being served up as fact, when a little further thought would have helped on many reviewer's offerings.1) "Why can CA suddenly pick up the hammer?" Answer, because he's worthy, not God Like strong. Same reason perhaps why Thanos can also wield it, but that's a moral discussion for another time.2) "Nebula should have warned them about the Soul Stone..." Answer, if she did then it would never have been released. She knew this and held the info back to aid the quest. BW had to be the one to fall as she truly loved HE, whereas he already had/has a family.3) "Time Travel makes no sense". Answer, well you just didn't pay attention to the exposition in the film did you? End Game's TT timeline altering conceit is not the same as Back to the Future etc. Go and watch it again. It makes perfect sense to me.4) "They all appeared out of nowhere, ready to fight, at the end." Answer, they were ready, just waiting to come back. In fact they'd only been gone a short while in their minds, as Peter Parker explains to Tony on the battlefield during their reunion/hug. Most of the surviving army from IW pre-snap (or the 'getting all dusty', as Peter put it) would still be in battle gear and ready for a fight. Dr Strange of course knew this 1 in 14.6 million timeline and was rallying the troops whilst they languished in limbo, clearly but secretly awaiting Hulk's re-snap. Then they all reappeared in Wakanda, where they dusted, and Dr Strange then ported them to the final battle, after a quick pep talk along with all the other heroes not present for the African battle in IW.... Wong will have helped here too as many were in other countries and not fighting in Wakanda.For me, these four supposed plot holes are well and truly filled up with asphalt, rolled flat, and have had fresh lines painted on them. Solid ground on the route needed to travel through this final Avengers film.As a film it's still not perfect in my eyes, a little baggy and disjointed in the middle. I particularly didn't like the Ocean's Eleven caper soundtrack during the heist sequences. I didn't like the depiction of Shr-ulk, Flab-Thor or the fancy new Audi e-trons (that absolutely would not have been developed after half the company staff disappears, along with the global economy etc....).But..... What a film nonetheless. I loved it for the most part, laughed and cried, and pushed my dropped jaw back into place a couple of times near the end. The Russo brothers did a great job holding the story together when it could have been so different otherwise (pun intended).Looking forward to seeing what Marvel Studios comes up with over the next decade.

Review Title: End to awesome era with some Pandering to the audience.
Review:
The thing that the writers and editors did so well in Infinity War was splicing all the mini subplots together. It was written and directed so well that it didn't feel disjointed or clunky. Endgame tried to do the same and failed. There were some plot holes and clucky awkward scenes with strange pacing. There were too many pop-culture references which is lazy writing and the jokes came off half-assed.
The plot itself wasn't about beating Thanos and restoring peace, it was more concerned with tieing up all the little plot ends for each character. Which became tiresome by the 3rd act. When the war broke in the 3rd act it felt like it had already been done in Infinity War. Apart from the restored characters (which was nice) it felt like they were showing that scene for the sake of it. Oh here's another battle, let's go kick some ass! rolls eyes... The message was clear; war, bad... We're all stronger together, if we put aside our differences and stand together we're better than the sum of our parts. Which is why it was confusing at the height of the battle the men and women were shown succeeding separately instead of teams working together. Which is quite relevant in today's political climate.
The ending was nice even if it was an easy way to finish it. What's better than a hero? A dead hero... As cynical as that may sound, the ending with Tony Starck narrating through the ending was a nice touch to the end of an epic era.
Now I'll have to rewatch them all from the first one, where it all began, inside of a cave...

Review Title: A brilliant finale to the longest movie series ever made
Review: Endgame is everything you would want in a grand finale to the MCU as we all grew up knowing it. However i preferred the Infinity Wars movie before it frankly, but only in the sense that i liked SW: The Empire Strikes Back, more than SW: Return of the Jedi, both some of my all time fave scifi films. I picked this is a non spoiler review simply because i dont discuss aspects of the plot or actions of the heroes, otherwise this is sort of a spoiler review, but it isn't, go see it before you read this stuff regardless you'd be an idiot to risk spoilers in these reviews.Infinity War had much better pacing throughout the film than Endgame did, the first half suffers from partly nonsensical pacing and a slowness to it that i haven't seen in any previous films, but i guess they were catering to the fans that want to savor their favorite actors and heroes before anything might happen to them, which it does well in that regard.My main and only gripe is that Captain Marvel is in the film, she was clearly a forced entry, likely forced upon the Russo Brothers behind the scenes by corporate, and her presence doesn't fit the plot, causes alot of 4th wall breaking as a result, reducing the immersive aspects of the film for me at least. And not to mention she is frankly unlikable, uncharismatic in the extreme (easily the least interesting and charismatic hero or main character in the entire MCU at this point, Nebula being put into a big role in this film did her wonders as a character and actress, she is no longer an also-ran in the MCU), unattractive (ScarJo has been looking over the hill in recent efforts but she hit the gym again for this film and i had no problems admiring her acting and physique), and has the acting skills of a dead fish frankly. Her character is also written like an emotionally dead Mary Sue and it seriously detracts from the story as a result, the Russo's did a good job of keeping her status consistent with her solo film aswell as keeping her out of the film as much as possible, the rewrites they must have had to do to the script to put her in would have given them stomach ulcers from the distaste I'm sure.Amen to the fact that she only appeared at the beginning and the end of the film, otherwise i would have seriously scaled down my rating, every scene she was in automatically reduced my enjoyment of the film as a whole.Otherwise the acting is great for everyone, the minor characters we've seen only in bit parts throughout the MCU, many of them have gotten much bigger roles and for the better, they were all stellar in their performances. The finale is definitely the highlight of it, and the reason you should see this film in cinema, as soo much goes on, it would be quite hard to follow on anything smaller than a 50+ inch 4k tv in the dark.The actors stepping out and/or dying have served their time and all had many great moments for you to observe and appreciate them in just this film alone before their exit from the screen, their character currency, was very well spent.Frankly i can see myself only occasionally watching any marvel movies in the future, and none in the cinema, and i'm not mad about it, i hold no resentments, i'm just satisfied 100% by this films outcome and my time has passed for what i enjoy in these films, i've outgrown it, and you see some ugly seeds being planted for future degradation of the MCU, with clear forced moments of girl power (i'm not against female superheroes or strong female roles, i have known such women all my life, the problem is far too many writers don't know how to craft such women, they don't need to PROVE anything, if they are strong women, it is largely self-evident in their voice, mannerisms and actions, you don't need to state it, or give them a ridiculous advantage over everyone else, and you simply don't need to fake it, and faking confidence and inner strength is what insecure, weak-willed women influenced by society and gurl power propaganda do, which causes their actions to become two-faced, obnoxious and repulsive, writers failing at writing strong women tend to create these monsters on a regular basis in tv and cinema now, and it's a serious plague. Captain Marvel is merely the latest, and most painfully obvious version of this problem.) that break the 4th wall and caused some serious cringing in the cinema on my part, something i haven't had trouble with watching MCU movies in the past.I'm very happy about how this film managed to dodge most of the bullets being fired at it by corporate Disney and i can stop watching MCU movies as a whole without any burning questions, i couldn't thank the Russo's enough for making Infinity Wars and Endgame, 2 of my favourite MCU films, right at the end of them all.

It harkens back to a time where going to the movies was an EVENT. I do have a few issues with the story structure and pacing of the movie which i will explain later, but those doubts completely vanished in the third act. This movie will shatter your expectations within the first ten minutes, and will leave you in complete disbelief and curiosity. The final battle sequence vs Thanos is by far the most well rounded battle sequence of all time. It has been said that it is a mess, but that is overshadowed by what are the best conclusions to characters in film history. Both Iron Man and Captain America were given what i would say are perfect story arcs (throughout the MCU).
Now, this movie does have a few things i would fix. First off, the part i was most excited for (the time heist) was the part that disapointed me the most. While the footage was amazing, they butchered the pace in the editing room and made what couldve been the best mix of nostalgia, risk, and cinematic genius into an action-packed but ultimately scattered sequence. However, other than that, there is no better way I could have imagined the Marvel Cinematic Universe ending.
While Infinity War may be the better movie because of its storytelling and stucture, Avengers Endgame is more than a movie, it is the culmination of a decade-long theatrical experience. For those reasons, this EXPERIENCE deserves a
10/10 (MASTERPIECE)

In the 70's, I grew up watching Spider Man and reading X-Men. They were groovy. Fast forward to 2008, and I saw Ironman, a character I couldn't care less about. I met my soon-to-be-wife, and she got me more involved with the MCU, and over the next several years, I backfilled my knowledge and interest into this wondrous fantasyland, eventually even caring about Captain America, who I cared even less about than Ironman.RDJ and Evans breathed humanity into their characters, as well as the rest of the tangential family I grew to appreciate and applaud. Marvel certainly had the right formula to rope me in, and care about the characters, which is the most important element of any story. The audience has to care about the characters. Even Thanos, complicated, merciless, driven and yet, somewhat understandable. Marvel did a brilliant job at sucking me into their Universe.And this all led up to Endgame. The title itself should have been a red flag. The very name of the movie signified...well...it's over. I mean, there wasn't a person on Earth who didn't know Ironman's fate. It was not a surprise or even a faint twist. He and Cap had run their course, and we were all well aware they had fulfilled their contractual obligations. We all knew it was death or retirement for most of the original Heroes.So, then. Marvel delivered exactly what had to be delivered, and nothing more. We got highs and lows. We got humor. We got drama. But we got no suspense. Everything played out exactly as it was supposed to, except it was egregiously padded with about an hour of slow, plodding, forced sentimentality.Do you know know what Ironman dying means? That's right, another 35 minutes of dull, agonizingly slow dolly shots heaped on top of the other hour of desperately boring scenes we already endured. Don't worry, though, we'll have a lifetime of Tony Stark's holographic lectures to listen to. Even in death, he wouldn't shut up.Aside from that, the deus ex machina provided by Capt'n Marvel, for whom an entire movie had to be filmed for the purpose of shoehorning her into the final battle, was an unnecessary message that "Women are just as tough as men." Thanks. We already knew that. Disney has a perpetual hard-on for lecturing us on things we already believe. I never doubted women are just as strong, if not stronger than men, as evidenced by my mom and step-mom.In fact, she should have ended the battle with her cavalcade of girls right then. She demonstrated she was more powerful than anyone else...but the Russo brothers didn't have the resolution we have, and were compelled to let her bungle it, and allow each Hero have a shot at haplessly reclaiming the bouncing glove, ricocheting nimbly out of each person's hand, extending an already painfully long battle even longer.All this, and Dr. Strange was just a second-tier afterthought, when it would have been much more compelling had he been hiding in the mirror dimension ready to unleash the Forces of the resurrected, to crush Thanos. That would have been too clever, the Russo brothers concluded, for the viewing audience.Finally, the last act Ironman performs, while struggling to complete a snap with the gauntlet, has his hand in A PERFECT POSITION TO GIVE THANOS THE FINGER, but instead declares with meek determination: "i am ironman."Other than that, great, mindless fun. The people who thought this was the greatest 11/10 movie of all time, full of awesomeness, wild feels and major sadface, are obviously children.

Review Title: Dissatisfied with the endgame of MCU
Review: Good things about the movie- 1. Screentime given to characters like Nebula, Scott Lang, Rhodey and Clint. 2. Tony's time with his daughter 3. Scenes from the previous films 4. Pepper Potts' suit 5. Tribute to Tony Stark/RDJ 6. Captain America meets Captain America 7. Fan service - Captain America is finally able to lift mjonir, Iron Man wears the infinity gauntlet and erases Thanos. Problems- 1. Ruined fan favourite characters : Thanos, Thor and Hulk 2. Can't feel the tension or emotion when a dramatic scene is instantly followed by a joke. Gamora's death in infinity war was a heart breaking moment and I could feel the loss/emotions that Thanos felt at that time. Didn't feel the same way about Natasha's death. For me "Mr. Stark, I don't feel so good" is probably one of the most emotional scenes ever. 3. Pace of the 1st half is slow and too much time has been taken to establish that the world has lost all its heroes and hopes and there is nothing that could be done 4. Replacing action with drama and comedy - All the action has been crammed in the last act of the movie instead of using it evenly throughout the movie. IW was an action packed movie from beginning till end - Hulk vs Thanos, New York battle, battle on Titan, final war in Wakanda. 5. Messy final act - It is very difficult to understand that who is fighting whom in the final war. I feared that infinity war won't be able to handle so many characters and storylines, but it was done perfectly. In Infinity war every character had atleast one scene in the film where they could use their superpowers and make their contributions. 5. Thanos is underpowered, less menacing, less focused/determined, and a completely different villain compared to the IW Thanos. This Thanos puts too much trust in Nebula and Gamora despite knowing about the future events. He is more interested in fighting the Avengers than collecting the infinity stones. IW Thanos(even without infinity stones) is so powerful that he is able to crush the tesseract cube with one hand, bodyslams Hulk and finishes the fight within few seconds, takes 6 superheroes to stop him from using the stones, sheds only a drop of blood on Titan, uses the 6 infinity stones after being hit with the full force of Thor's stormbreaker! 6. Destroyed Thor - Why? This guy has always been the one of the most powerful characters throughout the MCU and fans expected a lot from him after IW. Odin said that Thor is more powerful than him and Thor proves his worth in Ragnarok while fighting hela and in infinity war(when he takes the full force of a neutron star). His arrival in Wakanda and the attack on the minions/ships marked a turn of the tide in the war. 7. Professor Hulk - there was supposed to be a one-on-one fight between Thanos and Hulk. I like the nerdy Bruce Banner but I also know that no-one else can smash better than hulk. 8. Captain Marvel - the Future of MCU😠 The almighty Captain Marvel doesn't deserve this! She is just one film old and so she can't be the most powerful superhero so easily. Other superheroes like Thor and Iron Man took all these years to establish themselves and reach their full potential. We don't know who else she fought between Captain Marvel and Endgame and how did she become so much powerful to overpower Thanos! She can't lead the remaining Avengers like Captain America did and she definitely can't replace Iron Man!

Review Title: This movie is a true tribute to all Marvel fans.
Review:
This movie is a true tribute to all Marvel fans. This movie hits you with a triple dose of nostalgia and you will get more enjoyment out of this movie if you keep up to date with Marvel movies. The subtle references to past movies were amazing and you can tell the fans loved it by the cheering and applause these scenes would get. I have only been in a movie theater like this once before (Avengers: Infinity War), which shows how special this movie is.
I could go on and on about all the good things they did in this movie and all the amazing scenes they added, but I want to address the two big issues I have with this movie. The first one is that all the tension they build up in scenes are ruined by corny jokes. I feel like "thicc" Thor does not fit well in this movie because he just doesn't fit the mood they are trying to set. He would make jokes at inappropriate times which would ruin those scenes. This movie is supposed to have a serious tone at the beginning. People all around the world have lost their love ones, yet scenes like Hulk dabbing did not reflect the hardship they were going through. The second issue is the fact that the movie can feel slow at the beginning and you can see some clear scenes in the movie that they could've cut to make the film shorter. I can understand that they had to explain the results of the Thanos snap and how it affected everyone differently, but some scenes felt too dragged on. I can look past the problems such as their lack of consistency with their time traveling rules, but the other two issues can ruin the enjoyment you get out of the movie.
One character I want to point out in this movie that I thought shined compared to their past movies was Scott Lang (Ant Man). Seeing him interact with the rest of the Avengers was a treat to watch and I believe he will only get better from here. I would also like to mention that War Machine had some of his best lines in this movie and I believe this is his best movie yet.
One character that I could not stand is Captain Marvel. I think they wrote her poorly in this movie by making her feisty and cocky. She didn't want to work as a team and she thought she could do everything by herself, which made her a hateable character. I never cheered for a villain in a super hero movie before, but when Thanos used the power stone to punch Captain Marvel, I started to cheer for Thanos.

Really good overall for a superhero movie, I just wish they learn how to use their power and even the infinity stones, to bring healing to the world and make it a better place to live, not just defeat evil. But to actively DO GOOD.The problem that Thanos was trying to solve is a lack of resources for the inhabitants of the universe. His solution is just very messed up and stupid, to kill half the population.Instead, let him have a spiritual awakening, and the Avengers to use the stones to actually solve this to create more resources and/or increase the Abundance circulating in the universe while inspiring altruism and compassion.We need heroes to become ambassadors of Peace and altruism, not just defenders against threats (using violence). Review Title: A perfect ending to the most ambitious film saga ever created
Review:
This film's name itself gives a glimpse at the enormous weight this film carries on its shoulders. After ten years of Marvel, this film had to top it all. It had to be the best it possibly could be, and the results speak for themselves.
Most of this film's perceived greatness is derived from the hype behind it. Its much beloved twenty-one feature-length predecessors provide this movie with a huge fan base and their equivalently massive expectations. Those devoted fans were very obviously served very well. In the theater, there were cheers every time Captain America used Mjolnir and every time a new hero was brought back from the dead. However, this fan service deterred heavily from the movie. It broke the flow of the story and the action. It took the classic Marvel third act fight scene trope a little too far, to the point where it was just cliché. There was no reason to have all of the Avengers in the last scene other than fan service. The scene would have been much better if only Cap, Tony, and Thor fought Thanos. The Russos attempted to recreate a Lord of the Rings style final battle and only half succeeded. It was less fighting and more posing.
The hype was also a major detractor from the film. There were honestly no real "spoilers" to be spilled. Aside from Black Widow's death and the temporary ownership of Mjolnir by Cap, nothing was really surprising. This film was expected to end the story started by the first Iron Man and Captain America films, and that's exactly what it did. There is nobody that didn't see Tony's death and Cap's retirement coming (the latter was unexpected for sure, but we knew that Cap would be leaving one way or another). While the hype created an expectation of a completely unexpected ending, the film did not deliver.
Aside from those complaints, the film was very well made. It was incredibly structured, with each act clearly defined, even more so than other Marvel movies. The action was mostly well-done, with the crowning jewel of Hawkeye's fight with the Japanese gangsters. The shot of Captain America standing down Thanos's entire garrison was absolutely glorious, a perfect representation of the battle between good and evil. However, the best part of the movie was all the other movies. It was a perfect capstone to the most extravagant, complex storytelling venture ever taken.

Review Title: Out of 14 000 605 conclusions, this was the right one.
Review: I'm a big Marvel fan, not going to lie. I've grown up with this franchise and come to love it more and more each year. I thought this movie was a really well executed conclusion to the last 11 years of the MCU. I commend the Russo Brothers and Kevin Feige as well as all the actors and crew who have made this movie what it is.I'm not going to get into all the tiny little details and few plot holes in this movie because there are plenty of people who will tell you about it with a 1 star review if you scroll a bit. I can admit that there are a few plot holes but, I believe that can be overlooked. If we look at how well Marvel used it's characters and tied up storylines and characters arcs up really well. Not to mention, the comedy and fan service throughout the film and the emotionally charged fight scenes and death scenes. People in my cinema were laughing, crying and cheering. It was an experience, something I'll probably never experience again. It was a once in a generation event.This movie was probably the most emotional movie Marvel has ever done, taking it beyond just another superhero movie. Natasha and Tony's death scenes were beautifully done and were exactly how the characters deserved to be said goodbye to. Steve passing on the mantle of Captain America to Sam Wilson was sad yet made me so happy to see that Steve's legacy and values will not be forgotten in the MCU any time soon. Steve and Peggy's dance made me cry happy tears because Steve got all he ever wanted.There were plenty of other moments such as Steve saying "Avengers Assemble", Steve wielding Mjolnir, Peter and Tony reuniting and Morgan and Tony's "I love you three thousand" that will stay with fans for a long time to come.Avengers Endgame really did the original six Avengers justice, wrapped up storylines and began paving the way for the next phase of the MCU. This was not a perfect movie, there is no such thing, but Endgame really was something special. For those of you rating this movie a 1, you clearly didn't experience Endgame the way the Russo brothers intended you to and I find that very unfortunate.All in all, Avengers Endgame was a movie made for the fans that gave all the characters that we know and love a memorable moment. So thank you Joe and Anthony Russo, Kevin Feige, Robert Downey Jr, Chris Evans, Scarlett Johansson, Mark Ruffalo, Chris Hemsworth and Jeremy Renner and all other cast and crew members for a memorable film. And thank you Stan Lee for creating the characters we love so much.

Review Title: Good movie but nowhere near Infinity War
Review:
Even if it concludes many stories and movies of the MCU,the hype for this movie especially after the phenomenal Infinity War made me feel disappointed after I watched it.Let's start about the good elements of the film.
1)Black widow's death was very emotianal and was executed right as the character closed his arc in high fashion.
2)Captain america picks Thor's hammer was truly epic moment and the fight between Captain,Thor and Ironman Vs Thanos was very nicely done.
3)The time travel in different places in the movies of the MCU was I think the best thing about this movie,especially the scene with Starlord.
4)The addition of the Ancient One was great because she is such a great character.
5)The humour in this movie doesn't always succeed but it has some great laughs.
6)Tony Stark has a daughter.I thought that was very good idea.
7)Captain Marvel limited amount of screentime and the focus on the main Avengers.Also Antman and Hawkeye were great in this movie.
8)Great visual effects.
The negative ones.
1)The death of Tony Stark.Even if in some context I understand this decision,(Ironman was the one started it and ended it all) I believe that it was a wrong one and I was pretty angry about this.The death of Captain America wpuld be the great conclusion of the heroic character because his arc would be perfectly closed.In contrast the death of Ironman is wrong one not only because I love this character obviously but because he had a family now and his arc was pretty closed in the beggining of the movie.
2)The passing of the torch to Falcon.Falcon is a good character but Winter Soldier is propably the right choice to continue as Captain America not only because he was in the comics but it would be a great redemption story for the character.
3)Thanos was sidelined.Thanos was one of the most menacing and well made villains in the Infinity war.You can't just make him in this movie a simple villain with shallow reactions and character development.
4)The final battle was iconic yes.To see all the Avengers attack was pretty sweet but the execution wasn't.Obviously it was overstuffed and the action scenes and the reunion of the characters were very quick and sloppy.
5)Not enough time to the consequenses of the Infinity war.The amount of time given to the consequences was very limited especially in the scenes of Tony Stark on space.Also there were not even news or reactions of humans about this catastrophy.At least one scene to show television news.
6)Some unecessary slow scenes that could have been cut.
7)Professor Hulk would been better to become in the end of the movie so we could have some time with the original Hulk .
8)Fat Thor was funny at the beginning but you can't just take this awesome character that was created especially after Thor Ragnarok and was exceptional in Infinity war and used him just for laughs.
9)Some humour didn't hit well and made somes serious scenes useless.
10)But the biggest problem is the plot.The plot was overblowned and overstuffed.The pace was off and wasn't as good edited as Infinity war.Possibly
Russos were tired after the first movie and didn't pay much attention on details that make the plot works.
Avengers was without a doubt a good movie.It had some great action scenes and moments but in the end I feel disappointed because it could have been a lot better.Infinity War was a masterpiece and the hype for the Endgame was so massive that maybe it couldn't match the expectations.Russos made three almost perfect films(Captain America The Winter Soldier.Captain America Civil War and Avengers Infinity War)but Endgame is just a good one.I think that in second viewing I will like more Endgame and enjoy it more.I am still grateful for the work of the Russos and the course of the MCU all these years and I hope we will have some great movies along the way.RIP Tony Stark you will be always be Ironman.

The producers and directors made a bold move to present a whole new concept of how time traveling works, differing from classics of this genre, like the "back to the future" and "terminator" franchises.
In my opinion this whole decision becomes an issue when they're explaining their plan is going to work, since they take a really limited time of the movie doing that. I think they should've invested more time in that aspect, considering they had a three hour film and barely used fifteen minutes of that actively exposing their plan, basically saying that they were using time traveling as a solution and it wasn't the same thing as in "back to the future", not making the audiences understand them just so they can make a silly joke.
I later understood what they meant, but that required further research on the subject after the movie, and the audiences should leave the theaters understanding the whole movie plot, something that didn't happen to me and others.
