Review Title: A satisfying conclusion to the MCU.
Review: On it's own, Endgame is a great film. The story has many unexpected twists such as the death of Thanos and the entirety of the time heist sequence. The film, while great, still has it's issues. Thor and Hulk's character arcs from the previous movies have been thrown away in this. While I can see what the writers were going for with Thor, the same cannot be said for Hulk. Hulk's character arc was literally finished off screen, making his arc feel incomplete. The stakes also felt quite low. There isn't an immediate threat at the start, but then the movie decides to make up it's own threat at the middle of the movie, which felt kinda awkward. There was also lots of potential with showing the world after the decimation, but there's very little of that in the movie. We kept being told that people are miserable but we never see it, it's like nothing ever happened. But that's it in terms of issues, the rest of the film is still great. Every actor delivers a compelling performance, which is great considering that this movie's much more character driven rather than plot driven like Infinity War. Each act of this film felt like a different film. The first act felt like a drama about the aftermath of a universal scale event, the second act felt like a 'best of' compilation of the MCU, and the third act felt like the payoff of 11 years and 22 movies. Many moments felt extremely emotional such as Natasha's sacrifice and Tony's death. My favorite scene in the film by far is the scene where Steve finally gets his dance with Peggy. This film is a great conclusion to the MCU and that's all I have to say.

Review Title: Absolutely amazing way to end the Infinity Saga. Seriously, go watch this if you havn't already!
Review:
After nearly 11 years and 22 films, Marvels Infinity Saga has finally ended with Avengers: Endgame. And boy, what an ending it was! It nearly wrapped up almost everything you wanted to see wrapped up, and from the opening scene where Hawkeye's family gets turned to dust to Tony Stark's death it is a constant emotional rollercoaster. The cinematography here has drastically improved from the other Avengers movies, as this might be the best looking MCU movie yet. Even the score in this movie is really great, and that is one of my biggest problems with MCU in general. Alvin Silvestri crafts on of his best scores yet, and it absolutely works in the extremely emotional places where it's supposed to make you feel sad, happy, etc. The performances are great as well, as Robert Downey Jr and Chris Evans make the most out of their last performances as Tony Stark and Steve Rodgers respectively. Karen Gillan also gives a great performance as Nebula as well, and so does Jeremy Renner as Hawkeye, which was surprising since I didn't really care much about him until this movie.
Unfortunately, this isn't really a perfect movie though, as no movie is. I still think Infinity War is the way better movie though, since that felt way more streamlined and had a more clearer and cleaner plot. Here, the plot is sort of all over the place and messy, which I guess it kind of had to be, but it doesn't feel quite as smooth as Infinity War. The movie also takes a really long time to really get going, and i'd argue that it isn't until the climatic third act that the movie truly becomes a great movie. But overall, this is still a fantastic conclusion to a (mostly) great series of films, and it has to be one of the most fun experiences I have had in a theater.

Review Title: Secrecy and avoiding spoilers did no good to the Russos
Review:
Did I enjoy it? Yes. Did I feel content and as of a meaningful chapter of my life is properly closed? No.I'll tell you the issues I have with this movie as a fan from the beginning.
It does not close character arcs. No where in this movie does Thanos realise his mistake or the flaws of his plans. It does not seem redeeming or feel satisfying as a fan when villains show no remorse or guilt. They just die. It's anticlimactic.
Hawkeye kills a bunch of people yet it is Natasha that sacrifices herself. A death which was rushed by the directors, to a point where she didn't get a Funeral. The Russo's decides post production that she should die instead of Clint. Were we supposed to empathise with his family that has little emotional value to long running fans? Was she a more worthy character to be killed because the actress no longer wishes to return to the role after her solo Black Widow movie?
That's the issue, the writers and directors have always made open ended films. They are used to designing entertainment that sparks curiousity to what happens next (even though they barely follow up). That is why they did a poor job of finishing story arcs. Steve Rogers travelling back in time should have created an alternative timeline, as they had previously mentioned killing baby thanks would. Steve Rogers clearly suffering from PTSD once again, shows intentions of destructive behaviour if their plan to bring back the fallen doesn't work. Then he accomplished that, then left his entire life behind for a woman he barely knew. Because the writers didn't know how to come to an end. Tony's death was impactful, I'd say his storyline was the heart of the film.There are alot more issues I have, Thor's storyline was fun but at times I suspected that his body shape was a running joke that I couldn't understand because to me fat people are not funny simply by existing, yet the audience in the theatre took a look at him and laughed, the fat jokes did him no favour. It really showed that the Russo's could not keep up with taika Waititi's humour.
Okoye and Captain Marvel, two strong leads, were completely ignored at times.. Nebula had a good arc but she scarified herself. As her sister, Gamorra was willing to do I'm iW. These sisters are erased from a timeline now, and what this does to the guardians in that timeline unsettles me.I feel like the story was incredibly rushed. This is a Disney movie. They kept it very disney. I wanted a bit more angst. A bit more intellect. And I do believe if the Russo's weren't so committed to secrecy then they would have communicated better with writers and the actors that know these characters.The movie in its entirety was not impressive. I don't understand how the same directors and writers who made one of the best superhero movies in 2014, where characters had depth and reasoning, could end up making something that is incomparable to the older movies.The directors are also adding concepts after the release that make no sense, such as Bucky being less than human (a tortured war veteran), then saying things as Natasha will not get a Funeral because she has no family, etc etc. They have almost 0 understanding of certain characters.

Review Title: AVENGERS: ENDGAME NULLIFIED AVENGERS: INFINITY WAR!!!! PLOT-WISE, ONLY CAPTAIN MARVEL WAS WORSE!!!

I just saw Avengers: Endgame this morning. I'm a huge MCU fan as well as DCU fan. I was super excited to see Endgame as the continuation to Infinity War (which in my humble opinion, Infinity War is the greatest of the MCU). Please bear with me because I may go into tangents because I'm disappointed and emotions are kicking in. I know, I know, I know lol...it's only a movie, but if you're a big MCU fan...you'll understand where I'm coming from. I may be slightly biased as well(but aren't we all? So, if you just like a good CGI and emotional action movie...where the good guy ALWAYS WINS...I suppose you'll love this movie. I mean really...many liked Captain Marvel as well hahaha!Let me begin with Pros and Cons:Pros:
Good special effects like all MCU movies
Began with nice emotional substance from the beginning (somewhat like we've grown to know from DCU movies of the past. Dark Knight for example). So, it built up a lot of anticipation in which the storyline could have gone in any direction.
Thor finally killing Present Day Thanos with Stormbreaker(which is what Thanos said in Infinity War, "You should have gone for the head".
Iron Man with the Infinity Gauntlet to reverse the snap
All of the Avengers returning from the snap
Thanos' intelligence of figuring out the plan of the Avengers of obtaining the infinity stones
Thanos pretty much whipping all the Avengers until the very end even after Iron Man's snap(yeah, no one can lie. Thanos was still whipping butts until the very end...even without the Infinity Gauntlet lol)
(idk...that's pretty much it!)Cons:
Plot! Plot! Plot!
The entire narrative that changing anything in the past will not affect the future (and yes...that's stated very clearly. They even make references to Back to the Future and many other movies that those theories don't truly exist! Come on man!!! You don't have to be an Einstein to understand that anything that could get altered in your past will affect your future. Who hasn't daydreamed about changing the past...and then realized that you may not be whom you are today???)
Future Nebula killing the past Nebula had no affect on future Nebula...hmmmm
Black Widow sacrificing herself via suicide is ambiguous at most. If Hawkeye received the soul stone...what exactly did he sacrifice? Black widow is the one who sacrificed herself...so doesn't she deserve the soul stone(I know...she's dead...just saying)
Captain America wielding Thor's hammer....and controlling lightening. (I know...in Age of Ulton Captain America moves the hammer a little..very very little I might add)
Giving a counter personality to Thanos from what we've seen in Infinity War. Moral Ambiguity in my opinion. In Endgame....his personality is just plain evil?
Iron Man pulling the switcharoo on Thanos with the infinity gauntlet
The Ancient One giving Hulk the time stone....so how does Dr. Strange become Dr. Strange if she knows she's made a bad choice (I know...Captain America went back in time and returned the stones...sooooo....Dr. Strange was still able to protect the time stone?)
Very very very small part with Loki..smh!!! Loki is the "truth"!!! hahaha
The "turning to ash" of Thanos and his crew
Captain Marvel is pretty much a non factor. She got whipped by Thanos. What was the point of the solo movie of Captain Marvel??? hmmmmTo sum this up....I could go on and on and on, but I'll stop here. I just seriously believe that the Captain Marvel movie was totally unnecessary in connection with the MCU. I believe the quality of script writing of Infinity War was outstanding. Thanos became the fan favorite villain in MCU like the JOKER is in DCU. To me, Endgame took the heart out of character Thanos. Like i said at the beginning of my comment....I may be biased to a degree. When Thanos was whipping all the Avengers and finally wielded Iron Man's gauntlet....I was like, "hell yeah"!!! lol I got robbed hahaha. Anyways, those are my final two-cents!

The slower pace of the movie may leave young fans bored and uninterested but i found it engrossing and a nice change of pace from the previous movie Infinity War. In conclusion Endgame is a fun and surprisingly emotional end to the first 3 phases of the MCU.

Review Title: I Went To The Hall And Watched This Film Four Times
Review: I want to start out saying I love all the Marvel movies leading up to Endgame. I loved Infinity War because it seemed to be setting up a terrific conclusion to the original 6 Avengers story arc's. I was very wrong. Let's start with Tony's Arc. In Ironman 1 Tony is told you are a man who has everything and nothing. In Ironman 2 we find out his dad was distant and cold to him, and in ironman 3 he is getting panic attacks because he thinks it's up to him to save the world from all threats. So in Endgame he finally gets everything that's important. He becomes a Dad and husband and... was proven right by having to die saving the universe himself? Why? Because we are supposed to believe Tony can't retire? Of course he can. Didn't he say to Steve in AoU "isn't that why we fight so we can end the fight? So we can go home?" Tony wanted to retire. Tony's arc should have been about being a good dad like his father never was and finally becoming the man who has everything important. He should have learned that he doesn't have to do it all on his own. Team work should have won the final battle. What's the point of finally getting all the Avengers together if it's left to one man to sacrifice himself to save everyone? Tony's ending was not satisfying and it was not the end they have been building towards from the beginning. Now let's talk about the real tragedy in this movie. Steve Rogers character. We know he is a good man who always does what he believes is right. He calls Home the Avengers facility and says he can't ignore a situation that's headed south. He loved Peggy but found out she had gotten married and had a happy life and he tried moving on with her niece. This storyline was ignored which was ok because most of Steves storyline in the MCU has been about saving Bucky. You remember him right? Steve didn't seem to for the entire movie. Instead of thinking about Sam and Bucky and all the people they are going to save if their plan works when they find Thanos in the beginning of Endgame Steve's just looking at the Peggy compass that he hasn't looked at in at least 3 movies. Why? So we can all forget about his actual character development and think it's a great ending when he goes back in time to be with Peggy. I'm just going to ignore all the plot holes associated with Steve going back in time and just focus on the character assasination this commits. This means the same guy who says he can't ignore a situation headed south, who never ran away from a fight, who said I'm with you till the end of the line" to Bucky is just going to live out his life in the past never saving his friend from being a brain washed assassin, never saving his other friends parents from being killed by his best friend, never stopping any of the thousands of bad things he would know are going to happen? That's not Steve. The writers never let Steve get a personal life. He never found someone after Peggy and he never had anything except the Avengers. He was the one that was set up to die. The final battle starts with what is probably the most epic scene in comic book movie history but fizzles our soon after. Doctor Stranges plan makes no sense. How was this the only way they could win? Why couldn't Captain Marvel snap? Why couldn't captain Marvel just fly the gauntlet to another galaxy? Why couldn't Doctor Strange open a portal and drop the gauntlet on some random planet? In Infinity War why didn't Doctor Strange use his portal to go to Wakanda and tell Thor to aim for the head. The characters powers were very inconsistent for the first time in the MCU. Why was Thanos with no infinity stones able to fight Mjolnir and Storm Breaker but Thanos with all 6 stones would have lost to Storm Breaker if Thor would have just aimed for the head? Why can Captain Marvel fly through a huge spaceship 10 times but she gets knocked out after one punch from Thanos? Why does no one attack Thanos at the same time as someone else? Where's the big team up? You would think getting everyone together for the first time would have been the only way to defeat Thanos, but you'd be wrong because it's all about Tony stark. Even Steve picking up Mjolnir means nothing really because it has no affect on the end of the battle. Thor and Steve could be taken out of this movie and nothing would change. They do nothing of importance. This movie seems so disconnected from Infinity War that it's boggles my mind how this movie has the same writers and directors as Infinity War and it was filmed at the same time as Infinity War. How can you get one so wrong and the other so right? It seems clear to me that the writers and directors decided that Tony was dying and Steve was going back to the past no matter how much their story suffered from doing it. It's like they had a check list of things to put in the movie without actually making a good story that fit in with the rest of their movies. This is by far the most dissapointing ending to anything I've ever looked forward to.

Review Title: It's virtually impossible not to enjoy this film
Review: Impossible to be underwhelmed while watching this. You're going to love every minute.I've followed the MCU since Iron Man came out when I was 12 years old. For the most part, Marvel Studios always seems to one-up itself. Avengers: Endgame is absolutely no exception. It was much more than a love letter to the fans. The final battle between every single Avenger in the past 21 movies and Thanos' army rivals other battle scenes from other famous franchises like LOTR's helms deep. Every character we met up to this point gets at least one moment to shine in the fight. The entire third act, I had a huge grin on my face aside for Tony's death. His funeral scene was very touching and beautiful and a great tribute to RDJ's portrayal of the character.Going off that, the music Alan Silvestri provides for Endgame uses the same "Avengers Theme" and builds on it even more. I specifically loved the music during Tony's funeral and the end credits sequence. Personally, I think that it'll become iconic.If anyone complains about the time travel plot holes in this film, they need to take a chill pill. There is no time travel film that doesn't have its flaws. That should not be the takeaway from this movie. Most of them are actually explained pretty well if you really listen to the dialogue.The ONLY thing I will criticize is that it wouldn't really be able to stand on its own. In order for every moment and scene to carry weight, you need to have seen the other 21 films. But this kinda goes without saying. If you haven't been watching these flicks you're either stubborn or living under a rock.Would rate 15/10 if I could. Definitely a must-see.

Review Title: A Solid Ending for 10 Years Worth of Stories
Review:
I've been following the Marvel Cinematic Universe since Iron Man released in 2008, and this film right here, it feels like a good epilogue for all the characters that Marvel Studios has released in the 11 years it has been making movies. Endgame has more emotion, more drama when compared to the more action-packed and thrilling story that Infinity War has, but as a sequel to that movie Endgame certainly delivers.I'm not going to lie that this movie is perfect, it certainly has a few scenes which I thought could have done without. To mention the ones I dislike the most (and spoilers, for those who don't want to read them):1. Nerd Hulk
Sure, he proved important when he volunteered to wield Tony's gauntlet, but I thought that the "The Hulk was a part of me, he wasn't a disease but more like a cure" explanation Bruce did was sort of a copout. It doesn't explain also why he couldn't Hulk-out in Infinity War and if they really wanted to go and bring Nerd Hulk to the screen, why not show how Banner becomes this kind of Hulk instead of him explaining how he did it?2. Thanos' Ship Being Destroyed
Yeah, being one-shotted by Captain Marvel pissed me off. The entire MCU roster of heroes are down on the field, weathering the firestorm Thanos' ship is unleashing and then suddenly Carol Danvers flies right through it, destroying the ship in one blow. If I thought Nerd Hulk was a copout, then this scene was just cheap. Couldn't they sacrifice a few other heroes to actually heroically destroy the ship? Couldn't say Valkyrie or Star-Lord and the Guardians fly up there and show some struggle as they try to disable the ship? Couldn't the Wakandans use some kind of advanced tech they had to disable the ship's systems and then have a small group of heroes go in and destroy it?I suppose having Carol just tear through the ship is cheaper (budget-wise) and allows for the focus of the film to stay on the fight on the ground, but still. It was anti-climactic, and it also felt like it undermines the diminishes the power the main villain has.Spoilers stop there, and to conclude my review, I'm going to say Avengers Endgame was great. I felt my heart stir as I saw scenes depicting how the surviving members of the Avengers dealt with the events of Infinity War, and I smiled as I saw scenes that showed characters from previous movies make an appearance and actually contribute to the story. The ending was what really got to me, from the final fight between Thanos and the three-man team of Cap, Tony, and Thor, to the final lines of dialog between Thanos and Stark, that was just epic.Go see this movie, you won't regret it.

First off, If you rated this movie 10 out of 10, you are just a mindless movie drone and you have the intelligence of a plastic cup.This movie tragically suffers from the following: Predictable ending, needlessly long runtime, butchered character development, too slow pacing, inconsistent mood/tone, unexplained story/character elements, abuse of comedy, generic music score, overall lack of intensity, and it made the confusing concept of time-travelling in movies EVEN MORE CONFUSING.It's tragic...Infinity War had alot more balance and coherency, and in my opinion: This movie really needed to be better than the previous film, and It failed to do so. It often either lost my attention, or had me sitting there waiting for what WE KNEW was going to happen.That being said, some scenes and characters are handled a lot better than others, and when all those characters return from the dead to fight Thanos: THAT WAS EPIC! Mr. Stark had a nice departure from the MCU, and so did the Cap (ugh but that time-travel theory...)So yeah, painfully disappointing in what could have been the crowning achievement in the MCU.

I will approach the movie from a systemic approach: break it down to its very components, analyze it, and then put it back together and analyze it again; so that we can both see tree and the forest.To begin with, I must start this review with a line from Infinity War which summarizes pretty much what happened on this movie: "Where is Gamora, [...] Who is Gamora?, [...] Why is Gamora?" which literally translates into: "Where are the Russo Bros.?, [...] Who are the Russo Bros.?, [...] Why are the Russo Bros.?" From then on, we can all see what happens here. But let me state some fundamental facts before I go even deeper and analyze this movie. Fact is: The Russo Bros. did not watch Inception, they did not watch Interstellar, they did not watch Back to the Future, a single X-Men movie, and for Christ's sake they did not even watch any of the Avengers, Thor, or the Ant-man... but oh boy, did they watch a lot of Transformers movies, this one feels like the Dark Side of the Moon.I do not know if most people agree, but the movie was going to be already too long to have another army clash and now this time with all the heroes and now Thanos with all his big army! So, why this time not skip all that and just have a softer, not so loaded final battle where so much happens we movie viewers cannot appreciate a single moment? This is just an example not of "this is not broken, why fix it? But this is a rather: "They tried so hard this time, they failed catastrophically at it." Too much of the same... AGAIN? Come on... this is the Endgame, not a ---- WAR... P2 (Strike one).The theoretical background. Pretty much in cinema, there are two accepted theories when it comes to time travel - let us set aside Interstellar for a moment because no student, master or doctor in physics no matter how smart or how experienced would ever figure that one out! The two say pretty much that either "You cannot alter the past because whatever alterations were done, they have already occurred" or the other "If you go back in time, be careful not to alter it much or else you can create an alternate reality; but by just traveling you just changed the events thereof." I pretty much expected the second option because it simply follows the logic of the X-men movies. Thus, I expected the same from this one and wow, it does try the first alternative knowing that it pretty much causes the second to occur! (Strike two).Now, let us recap what happens on this movie relating to time travel. First mistake: Ant-man travelling back in time with Dr. Hulk's time machine. Dr. Hulk brings the Ant-man when he is an elderly, but as a child and as a teenager? I beg your pardon! How is that even possible? When did Dr. Hulk suit up the young Ant-man? Sorry, I did not catch that one! Second mistake: On the Ant-man and the Wasp, the old Wasp (Michelle Pfeiffer) stays in the quantum realm who looks like she stayed like 30 years or something and lived off from... eating a few electrons? That one aside, how come her time was so different than Ant-man's on this movie? Now, five years are five hours? I beg your pardon. Third mistake: Can anyone explain to me how Pim's particle works? Coz either Thanos synthetized like a billion tons of that thing in a few minutes, a few hours, or a few days and no one told us about, or he moved a gigantic machine that burns Gigawatts just to be turned on through time and space with just a tiny flask containing 10 ml of that thing!Now, let us recap what happens on this movie relating to alternate realities. First mistake: Capt. America vs. Capt. America. How come Captain America does not remember fighting against himself? The Capt. America from the past thinks he is battling Loki. But the Capt. America from the future does not seem a bit surprised to realize that he indeed fought against himself. Second mistake: Now, we have a Loki, a few minutes after being defeated on Avengers one taking control once again of the Tesseract, flying away to God knows where in front of many security guards. Since the Tesseract is the space stone, how did the Avengers recapture him again and bring him back to Earth a few hours, probably minutes later after he escaped with the Tesseract? How? Did Dr. Strange bring him back nice and softly and fixed that time line with nobody noticing it?- This one clearly alters the past in a HUGE WAY, but apparently with no side-effects. Third mistake: Thanos from the past is now defeated in the future. Am I sorry, what? If the Thanos from the past is defeated in the future, so which Thanos from the past actually triggers the Infinity Stones?; and in the subconscious mind of a few and in the conscious mind of the very few like myself, this is where the plot completely falls apart (SPOILER ON Interstellar: I mean, we could justify for a moment from Interstellar that a few photons escaped the event horizon of Gargantua, which in theory DOES NOT EVER HAPPEN, and that the probe actually manages to send the data on the edge of the event horizon back to the ship and the ship back to Earth. So, how is the probe retrieved again? How doesn't Cooper get sucked into the black hole too?). So Fourth mistake: Capt. America now travels back in time to return the stones, he does, and successfully to our understanding; and also now manages to live with the love of his life happily ever after? Yet, the past was not changed... the past where he mourns her loss, where he hits on the Black Widow, the past where he is all alone, and at some point makes out with his beloved's niece should therefore be now all gone. Fifth mistake: Now Thor from the future has deprived now and forever the Thor from the past of the Mjölnir. Wow... that blew my mind away beyond the fact that Capt. America held it and Thanos did too!! I mean, the sacred hammer can be held by anyone who deserves it, those were the words of Odin. Capt. America may use it, OK, maybe he deserves it... but Thanos? The Mjölnir should have at least refused to act on his will. Now, is Thor Ragnarok a fantasy of Thor since he does not have the Mjölnir anymore? When did Odin order make a new hammer in time for the battle against Malekith? Why didn't Captain America return the Mjölnir back to the Thor in the past?Now, let us recap what happens on this movie relating to the favorable outcome to the Avengers. The time line Dr. Strange predicts the Avengers' victory now does not make much sense, in particular remembering that he witnessed 14,000,605 possible outcomes and that he HAD THE TIME STONE in his possession. On Titan, the Avengers were about to defeat and indeed remove the gauntlet from Thanos' left arm, and why not, Dr. Strange or Ironman use it to vanish Thanos if either was going to die anyways, according to Dr. Strange. Yet, we see Star Lord loses it, Thanos breaks free, defeats them, and takes control of the time stone. Why did not Dr. Strange then warn Star Lord about Gamora's death? Why did he let that intentionally happen just to save an Iron man who was going to die anyways? (Strike three). Did he ever talk to Nick Fury about these events? Why are the time stone and the space vortex created by the sling rings so alike? Now, why does the time stone have that particular halo that no other stone has? Did he not curse the time stone as many people have assumed as the time stone possesses the halos of the sling rings? It now seems that even though Dr. Strange predicted that it was the only the way, to me it seemed the easy way, beyond the aforementioned inconsistencies.The movie as a hole suffers from inconsistencies, and plot holes way too noticeable. First, how did Thanos destroy the infinity stones? How did the Avengers defeat him now so easily? Well, he did not have the infinity stones. But later on that movie see Thanos even much more powerful WITHOUT the infinity stones. I would have predicted a sure defeat of Thanos on the hands of Iron Man, Captain America and Thor, no need for the cavalry or Captain Marvel for that matter. Yet, not even a drop of blood, getting blows from the Iron Man who spilled his blood with a single kick, now facing Thor with an axe and Captain America with a hammer... Thanos should have been the one who needed rescue. Why was not Captain Marvel able to defeat him single handedly? She could have. Thanos was about to do the snap again, yet the infinity stones suddenly disappear from Iron man's gauntlet into another gauntlet, he uses them and dies! (Strike four, OUT). Why did not Dr. Strange take the time stone and save Iron Man at that moment? Why did he not take the gauntlet and activate it away from Iron Man?... Oh yeah, I GOT IT, OK?... IT WAS THE ONLY WAY!A couple of questions we will never know the answer to. How did the Skull reach Vormir? How did he become the guardian of the soul stone? And why does the soul stone claim a soul in exchange?Many reviews have talked about the slow pace of the movie. Yes, at the beginning it is very slow-paced, you get the feeling too much time is wasted in pointless. We then see the knot untie pretty fast. Then once the lost ones are brought back, it rushes into one final huge battle worthy of a transformers movie where you cannot see much less appreciate what is happening.This is just poor plot writing because we see a very long introduction, which is not needed because we already know most of the characters. The knot of the movie feels very short. And since time is running short, we rush into a huge battle with 100,000 men on one side and probably the same on the other! There are plenty of movie reviews that cover this poor time management.Where are the Russo Bros.? They are here to make the Avengers movies! Hurrah!Who are the Russo Bros.? The ones who made Infinity War a blockbuster hit! Hurrah!Why are the Russo Bros... the ones who ruined the Avengers franchise? Because in their effort to make Endgame the best, they flipped it and failed blatantly at it!

This part was my only complaint, as we had to watch the failed experiments and bizarre explanations. The acting was great, as expected, as were the revenge scenes. Very satisfying. There was plenty of humor (noted the "Big Lebowski" reference to Thor, walking around in his bathrobe and slippers, gut hanging out) plenty of tragedy. The very end was a surprise, perhaps even the most satisfying part. The Captain got to have it all, in the end. Suspend disbelief and judgment about his possible changes to the "timeline", because most of what occurs once they enter the quantum realm, it could be argued, is one grand experiment, and journey, through time.

Stay for the visuals and fan service, not for the plot.I can't even begin to describe how disappointing Endgame was.The Good (Great moments and Fan service):1) The action sequences were epic and memorable.
2) Thanos was still powerful without the gauntlet.
3) Captain America finally wields Mjolnir.
4) Iron Man, Thor, and Captain America team up to fight Thanos.
5) Iconic lines such as "Avengers Assemble," "Hail Hydra," and "I am Iron Man".
6) Cap passes the torch to Falcon as opposed to Bucky. Considering his traumatic past, who knows if Bucky will ever go rogue in the future.
7) Solid performance by Robert Downey Jr.The Bad (Plot and Poor character motivations):1) Aside from Natasha and Tony Stark's deaths (which we knew was coming due to the numerous reports regarding RDJ's ending contract,) there were absolutely no stakes whatsoever.
2) Tony Stark figures out the ins and outs of time travel OVERNIGHT!
3)The time travel thing was so convenient, in that everything goes according to plan for all the characters involved. As shown with Gamora in Infinity War, Natasha's death was no exception since we already knew that a sacrifice had to be made.
4) Fat Thor and this sad excuse for Professor Hulk annoyed the crap out of me. Both characters barely served any purpose.
5) The Russo's truly have a soft spot for Captain America. How a vulnerable cap was able to block Thanos's massive blows with whatever was left of his shield still baffles me to this day. Vibranium or not.
6) That female regrouping shot made no sense at all. It was so out of place since all the characters were scattered and mixed up in the war zone. How they had the time to assemble is beyond me.
7) The movie is a huge diss to Infinity War (Best MCU film in my opinion). Literally all the dead characters come back to life. Thanos's plan gets reversed in its entirety. Again no consequences or risks taken whatsoever.
8) Prior to Infinity War's release, Kevin Feige and the writers were on the fence about whether or not they should kill off Spider-man, which they ended up doing. Such a bold temporary move only to be reversed in Endgame. Why they were on the fence about doing it in the first place makes no sense at all.
9) Apart from Tony Stark and Natasha's deaths, the dramatic and emotional scenes were watered down by too many misplaced jokes.
10) Similar to most MCU films, there were way too many jokes throughout the entire movie.
11) Thanos was a mustache-twirling villain.
12) The unlimited amount of PYM particles.
13) Scott Lang is brought back from the quantum realm by a rat.
14) Without any logical explanation, Captain Marvel just seemed to know where and how to find Tony Stark and Nebula.Overall, Endgame was both messy and frustrating to watch from a storytelling point of view. The end result is nothing more than mediocre. The saga should've ended with Infinity War.

He's supposed to feel like a broken man conflicted with the monster himself that he has to deal with. They should've used that more with Proffesor Hulk in this movie or at least his struggle of being known as a monster. I also think the cinematography and the soundtrack to the film really set the theme and made the movie 5x more exciting in my opinion. Overall I think this will go down as one of the biggest movies in all of cinema history. Never has there been a cinema project of a cinematic universe with superheroes where they can collide countless characters but also have an exciting story that has a huge climax.

After Avengers Infinity War, we waited for the Avengers Endgame. We wondered how the story would go on, how our heroes would turn back, what would be the end of Thanos. Many theories related to this have been put forward. Avengers Endgame was undoubtedly the most anticipated film of recent years. Normally, the higher the expectation, the higher the probability of disappointment. But this is not the case for Endgame. Whatever you're expecting, you find much more in the film. This means that the biggest concern about the film has disappeared.On the other hand, another comparison comes up. Is Endgame more successful than Infinity War? We can comfortably say it Avengers Infinity War is just the beginning of the story. Endgame was the finale of the story. So we shouldn't think of these two films as two separate stories. There is only one story divided into two parts.Avengers Endgame is, above all, a great homage to the ten-year history of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The story highlights the original Avengers team. Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow and Hawkeye are at the center of events. No character comes in front of them. Of course there are many characters that play an important role in the story outside the original Avengers team. Everyone's concern was that Captain Marvel, who was included in the Marvel world, overshadowed other heroes. We can say that this certainly did not happen. What is important in this struggle is not how strong you are, but how good you are. This comes to the fore in all areas. It gives good message about being a hero and a family.Of course, Avengers Endgame has some critical aspects. For example, is the three-hour period necessary in terms of the story? It can be discussed. The head of the story moves much slower than the rest. It also drags the heroes into an emotional predicament. Then the tempo is rising and the heavy scenes we are watching are getting more meaningful. The last 45 minutes of the movie is fully action packed. But the last 45 minutes goes so fast that you don't even realize it. Action and battle scenes are really successful. There is not even a slight distress about visual effects. There are also slight logic errors in the film, but in general the story is so successful that these details become meaningless and insignificant after a certain point.Lastly, Avengers Endgame doesn't have a movie end scene. Because after the film's final, there is no need for another scene. The Marvel legend Stan Lee appears with a small stage. But this is the last surprise scene in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Moreover, there is no clue about Marvel's future. This makes us wonder more about Spider-Man: Far from Home. 10/10

Review Title: Whole year of waiting, and that's all you've got?
Review:
This one time chance to do something even more epic than Infinity Wars, which would be a legendary feat, was wasted, as Endgame is nowhere near.Let me start with saying, that as a fan of superhero movies, I'm underwhelmed and disappointed with this new production, because it was supposed to be great, not just average. Fans hoped that it could top the Infinity Wars, but it failed miserably instead. Infinity Wars is still an ultimate superhero movie after all, and will stay that way for a long time...Same thing happen to Matrix, if you remember, ultimate sci-fi cyberpunk. They just couldn't make anything even remotely alike, let alone better (while plenty of fans had such a great ideas). Back to the topic...1. What did they do to Thor? What did they do to Hulk? Ant man becomes a town clown? All the Avengers couldn't be more miserable in that movie. What happened with unbroken superhero power of will? All of them are depressed, soaked in regrets and self pity. That's not how superheroes function! There's nothing uplifting and epic about this movie. Politically correct propaganda that crying over fallen heroes are more important than the survival of the individual, with the message that primary motivation should be to sacrifice yourself for others. Superheroes thrive regardless of anything and that to me should be a message, not crying over what already happened. "It has to work, if it doesn't than I don't know what I will do", or something like that, really? There are plenty of cheesy and meaningless lines like that, in this movie.2. Why every single sentence spoken is followed with a long pause, like there's some revelation that viewers need to think upon. That's seriously annoying. You remove all the pauses and movie becomes 2 hours instead. It's like with mechanical precision they inserted those pauses to add to a dramatic effect. It did its work to make people bored though.3. Time travel, seriously? They had to refer to "Back to the future" twice to justify that this time, time travel will be done right. Not creative at all, copy of something we've seen before. Again, so many ideas that could be mind blowing, rather than this "time heist", and yet they made their bet on time heist.
How about that: Thanos didn't erase 50% of population, but created a split into two parallel universes, where each half of population (and superheroes) lives their own lives, not knowing that the other part survived, and tries to revert what happened, and to unite with it's twin universe, so to speak. Then we could watch what happens in parallel universes, two timelines at the same time. If they really wanted time travel, why not make it more interesting, puzzling and... with less holes in the plot. Yes, I understand, that if you change something in past, you change someone else future by spinning new parallel universe, without changing your own past. But even with this simplification they couldn't make it right.
How did they manage to stuff the whole spaceship, full of warriors through the "quantum machine" with a limited whatever particles they had? Wouldn't it be lot easier for Avengers to get on the pod together to save some precious "pym particles" if that was possible. The list of technical flaws regarding this highly hypothetical time travel can go on and on. Nothing there makes sense.4. So snapping fingers is a new thing now? Full command of Infinity stones comes down to snapping fingers, like that's some kind of cool stuff that kids record on social media or maybe some secret trick that works with Infinity stones only? By the way, the gauntlet was forged in outer space with an energy from the star. Can this be replicated with microchips?5. Lots of repeats and repeats. Infinity Wars had so many original and creative ideas packed into it, including visuals and action scenes. In Endgame we witness again struggle for the gauntlet, revisiting same locations, chaotic clash of two armies, emerging of women only battalion (political correctness again intended, if only for a couple of seconds, which makes it even more out of context). That's another thing, some stuff repeat or drags on, like interaction between particular characters, the others are only shown for few seconds. Captain Marvel for example.6. Jokes were plenty, too many and tried so hard to be funny but were quite lame in most cases. Sadly the most funny joke was about open wifi in Thor's lair gaming zone, the other being "I can do that all day" by Cap fighting himself, "I know", and finally when Starlord and Thor get together in the spaceship at the end of the movie. Do you recall any other jokes? No, and that's because they were third class maybe, focused on making fun of Antman.7. Fornite, seriously? Why don't you mention AI home assistants and Instagram profiles, to be more aligned with current times.Then why so many 10/10? Well, probably because they're all sponsored reviews / sponsored likes, which becomes a norm in every industry.
That has to stop as well!!! IMDB has to become again a community of people who recommend and share their genuine opinions with others. Movie industry has to stop being driven by shareholders, drive for profit only and computer algorithms.
People crying in the cinema, as some articles report, clapping? I've seen people yawning and everyone left before the final credits. That's how bad it was, compared to Infinity Wars.

Usually, the main villain of the film is taken through a series of events, leading to their demise, and although Thanos was taken through this journey in Infinity War, Endgame is a new film, with somewhat new beginnings.The assassination of Thanos was carried out swiftly, and without any sort of struggle, which surprised me up until the point where we were told Thanos no longer had the stones. Not only did this bring panic and desperation to the table, but it showed how truly powerful the stones are, how Thanos can be such an unstoppable force with the stones, and merely a bump in the road without.How the killing of Thanos was depicted played a large part in how Thanos was no longer the problem. In other films, the killing of the villain comes with a large sense of relief and triumph, however when Thanos died it felt almost as though nothing had changed, it showed that The Avengers had still failed, and there was no going back.

2. Limited action scenes

Instead I just couldn't take him serious which is a shame because he's such a cool character.The action scenes just seemed to be resolved so quick. Review Title: As perfect a culmination to this ten year ride we could've hoped for. It wasn't the movie we thought we were going to get but the one we deserved, flaws and all.
Review: To me endgame was just about perfect, the story arch has some great twist and turns the keep you entertained the whole three hours. But some elements of endgame have caused massive controversy and criticism. The number one issue being the use of time travel. Now I've had some time to digest the use of time travel in the movie I have to agree that it was not done perfectly and has left some glaring oversights and inconsistencies. This has lead many people to even question why the writers would even take on the challenge of using time travel as a plot device, since it usually ends up a mess in movies.I believe that although the time travel as a plot device ended up being messy, it was a mess worth while for the final act of this era, which saw some of the pillars of the marvel franchise pass the torch to new comers entering phase four. The use of time travel allowed for us as an audience to watch some beautiful scenes that wouldn't need have been possible otherwise and yielded some much needed closure to die hard and casual marvel fans alike. Time travel allowed us to watch Tony Stark look at his father as a new father himself and share the insecurities they both have about raising a child. We were able to watch Thor talk to his late mother one more time and share a touching moment. Gomorra comes back from 2014 to kick Starlord square in the gonads. Thanos is killed twice. Nebula redeems all past transgressions. Having it capped off by Steve Rogers going back into time for good and living out his life with his one true love and growing old in peace.In the end the time travel made little to no sense, going against the rules of time travel the movie set itself. And seeming Steve Rogers has created an endless time loop with his actions. Now this may have been done so intentionally by the writers to allow for possible explanations for the upcoming Loki series or to open up new opportunities in phase four to play with the idea of alternative realties or dimensions. Regardless of intent, I'm willing to overlook these oversights for the gems time travel as a plot device produced on the big screen. Watching endgame is like watching a best of mix of all marvel movies for the past decade. The time travel pros outweigh the cons for me and gave the best possible final act for Tony Stark and Captain America. 9/10 for me, taking 1 star away for the inconsistencies in the time traveling which wasn't really a deal breaker for me. I loved just about everything in this conclusion to infinity war. If you're letting the time travel ruin this movie for you, all I can say is lighten up, after all super hero's rarely make 100% logical sense.

People complain about the plot, run time, overall story and conclusion... I myself am an iron man fan through and through so the ending for me was not only tearjerkingly sad, but triumphant for the hero that started the MCU storyline. So please keep negative comments about this masterpiece of a superhero epic to yourself and let everyone enjoy this thrilling and wonderful conclusion!

Review Title: Enjoyable but Passable. Missed the mark!
Review:
*SPOILER ALERT IF YOU HAVEN'T SEEN AVENGERS ENDGAME YET AND WANT TO, THEN SKIP THIS* Otherwise, please proceed reading.After watching the masterpieces of The Winter Soldier and Infinity War, I expected Endgame to trump them both in one massive all-out bow out performance for the main Avengers roster, a final hurrah. But I was disappointed with this film. I had such high expectations and I was severely frustrated. This is not the Russo Brothers best work.There are 11 main points why:
1) The whole story pivoted on a coincidental plot point weaker than the Martha moment in BvS. It was the rat walking over Antman's machine controls turning the machine on that started this movie. This is convoluted. This is a very weak plot point they could have done without. Antman could have found a way back through a time vortex which Janet warned him about. Or, the Avengers could have found his van, and took it back to Avengers HQ, and then turned it on and brought him back. The mysteries of the quantum realm and time travel would have still driven the first part of the film.2) Captain Marvel was unnecessary. After introducing Captain Marvel as Nick Fury's trump card,she was absent from the film. She was not the pivotal character that made any difference. She did not do anything that the avengers could not have done themselves. Her Deux Ex Machina moment in the final battle was not essential. Thor or Rocket could have rescued Tony in space and Hulk could have destroyed Thanos' ship. She did not add anything new or unique to the story.3) No Rematch between Hulk and Thanos. There should have been a rematch between them even if Hulk loses again. Captain America had a rematch and nearly won, the Hulk should have had too. Alternatively the Hulk could have destroyed Thanos ship. Natasha's death could have set up the ultimate Hulk rampage. Hulk has a healing power in the comics so his arm could have recovered quickly for this rampage. This was a missed opportunity that the audience would have loved to witness.4) Ironman and Captain America's reconciliation was completely unsatisfying and unearned. We know their conflict stem from moral, emotional and personal clash. They very nearly killed each other in Civil War and they made up as if nothing happened. It would have been better if they went back in time, Tony meets his dad, they have a heart to heart then they go back to the present and Tony forgives Steve. This would have given their reconciliation substance and made it a cathartic moment. After all, it was Tony's parent death that was the main issue of why they clashed in Civil War. This would also have tied in nicely with Steve being worthy of Thor's power later.5) Sudden change of pace. There was no build up of tension coming to the final conflict. One half of it is a lecture in quantum physics, and the other is them fighting Thanos. It felt like watching two movies with no transition in between.6) No in memoriam for Stan Lee. They should have had an in memoriam message for Stan Lee. This is after all, his life's work culminating in one film. He made such a huge contribution to the comic industry that not giving him proper honours was just poor manners. He passed away during the filming of this film. It would have been very fitting to have a remembrance message in his honour at the end of the time, just like anyone would if any one of the creators passed away during the duration of the MCU.7) Ironman is the only one that gets a story arc in this film. This felt like an ironman film and not an Avengers film because he was the only one that got a complete story arc and no one else.Too much focus on him, and not enough given to other characters. It might was well be called Ironman 4.8 ) Bucky Barnes should have been given the shield first just like in the comics. Who wouldn't have liked to see Captain's America fellow super soldier and best friend with a metal arm become the new Captain America? This would have been more faithful to the comics.9) What have they done to Thor? Really? They made him to be a fat drunk for comic relief and product placement. Seriously? Why bastardised a character who is widely beloved?10) So many questions unanswered. Where did Valkarie get the flying horse? Did Dr strange knew about Ant man and the rat? What happens if Natasha and Clint both jumped in the cliff? Who gets the soul stone then? Where is Loki now? Did Dr strange know about these events? Did he know about Captain Marvel? How comes Thanos did not notice the stones were not firing on his arms in the end? How comes Stark's suit held the stones? For a film that was supposed to make the Avengers story come full circle, it left a lot of questions unanswered.11) Thanos is the MCU's best villain, and his ending was so flat. They could have given Thanos' story a new detail or a different aspect of his personality or mission . But this film treated him as a disposable villain and not the Thanos the audience feared and admired in Infinity War. Also, they killed him in an anti-climatic way at the end.These 11 points are the biggest reasons why Avengers Endgame was a letdown. It could have been the MCU's masterpiece, but it was not. It's an enjoyable but passable movie with a few great moments. It was DISAPPOINTING

Directed by Anthony and Joe RussoEnding the 22 movie-long "Infinity Saga", comes AVENGERS: ENDGAME. It is really surprising that something remotely close to the first movie actually happened; crossing over all the heroes from the previous films and then Marvel Studios creates this feature, which is unbelievable. Endgame, following Infinity War, has the remaining Avengers go back in a "time heist" where they collect the Infinity Stones themselves to return the other heroes. The movie perfectly balances action and some other scenes (mostly), also giving us an emotional sendoff to Avengers leaders Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.) and Captain America (Chris Evans).The other characters seem to also have changed into new directions. Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner) has now become a ninja-style warrior; Dr. Banner (Mark Ruffalo) has now united with his split green personality into Professor Hulk. All of this has happened because of the snap and it doesn't end without a cost. Just like Stark himself states, Part of the Journey is The End as our heroes (also including Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson) are forced to face the true consequences that truly lead to victory; which is truly a powerful message to send. Endgame is truly a masterpiece.During the more emotional moments, we're supposed to feel something yet they throw some jokes into it which prevents those scenes from being what they should be.As wished, all the heroes who fallen victim to the finger-snap are brought back when Hulk decides to test out the new Iron Gauntlet when he snaps his own fingers to bring everyone back, and then it goes into the finale where almost everyone (with the considerable exceptions of Vision and Loki) fights against the old version of Thanos (Josh Brolin) to save humanity with, Thor fighting a little better, Captain America has been revealed to have been worthy of lifting war hammer MjÖlnir all along. and... surprise, surprise... Iron Man making the sacrifice!As well, some jokes did land greatly at times and as explained above it is worth watching AVENGERS: ENDGAME... if you saw the other 21 movies :)

In this scenario Tony would send back the stones to their timelines at the same time as snapping his fingers. Review Title: it's a comic movie, things are meant to be over the top and unrealistic, so why not just sit back and enjoy what we're being given?
Review: Leaving the cinema quite weirded out the first time round I went to see it a second time few days ago and now I can say that as a huge Marvel fan, I am more or less satisfied with how things ended. Of course it's a superhero movie containing a lot of CGI, a lot of things that don't make sense at all and it's not flawless at all but for me, it was great fun, and the way they managed to create this universe and have all these films connected is just amazing. I loved the journey and I loved most parts of this film.I'd like to address some points (open questions to me, things I loved, things I'm not that fond of etc.) in particular (huge SPOILERS for those who haven't seen it yet!):The very end of that movie was way too cheesy for my taste. Of course, with Tony a major character died and with Steve another major character arch came to a conclusion, and yes we're all sad that Nat is gone and yes we're all happy that Clint was reunited with his family, but all in all it was way too long and too hollywood-esque played on one's heart strings. For me, this could've been solved in a more classy way.I'm a bit confused as of why the entire time travel theme seems to cause so many misunderstandings and so much anger. It's been etablished in this movie that when you travel back in time you're not changing your former present but create another timeline. So therefore it's very clear to me that if Nebula from the future kills Nebula from the past she doesn't vanish.I often read that people wondered as of how Thanos was able to travel to the future, which also was perfectly well explained in the movie: Nebula from the past was seen opening a portal to let him in, using the time machine the Avengers have built.How on earth did Valkyrie manage to bring a pegasus?! She's been living in Sakaar all those years after the Valkyries had been defeated by Hela and then went on a space ship, travelled to Asgard, fought there against Hela again and then travelled towards earth where she helped building New Asgard, so how could she have had a flying horse?Sometimes there was a bit too much fan service. F.e. the entire scene with Korg and Miek was simply just to let us see these two again, but having them around didn't lead to anything.I loved the entire Thor story arch. That guy has been through so much and felt so guilty and useless because he didn't go for the head in the first place so him having this depression was only natural. And I felt that Chris Hemsworth was having a blast shooting this film, which always brings out the best of him.I loved the humour. Especially seeing so much of Scott Lang in this movie was very cool.I'm going with the opinion of Valkyrie that she liked Hulk and Banner better before they merged into one but then again, some development in that story is also nice to see.The most epic scene for me was when in preparation of the big battle all that were snapped away and been brought back turned up.Why on earth was Thanos so strong, even without the stones?In the beginning, Cap states they had been looking for Thanos but were unable to find him. Only when Nebula mentions 'The Garden', Rocket out of nowhere suddenly knows what planet Thanos is on. Why didn't he mention that earlier?I often read people were disappointed that there was only one real battle in this movie as they expected it to be more of a fight but I found this very cool. Infinity War was very much of a fighting movie so I was glad this one wasn't that much. Even superheroes don't have to fight all the time to make an impression.I could go on and on with that but after watching it a second time I figured out why exactly I wasn't that happy with that movie after seeing it the first time round: For me it all was too simple and I was puzzled as of how much I had been able to get right by watching the trailers etc. Many of my theories were just proven right and normally, this doesn't happen. And many things were too easy in my opinion, f.e. that everyone wondered how Ant-Man would be able to leave the Quantum Realm without the help of the others and then a rat pushed all the right buttons by accident?But then - it's a comic movie, things are meant to be over the top and unrealistic, so why not just sit back and enjoy what we're being given?

Review Title: I think I liked the movie, but...
Review: By the click of the glove of infinity, I happened to attend the night show of the premiere, and here I am, having arrived home early in the morning, I am writing these lines. The whole movie epic from the studio "Marvel" has come to an end. Many films, characters and plot twists intertwined in order for the viewer to appreciate the three-hour denouement of superhero adventures. But, in my humble opinion, the new part of the Avengers has both pluses and minuses.First of all, it is worth noting that Avengers: Endgame is a masterpiece. With one huge amendment - a marketing masterpiece. Frankly, I can't remember a more anticipated tape. By the amount of discussion, rumors and, sorry for the boring slang, hype, this film is an obvious record holder. The bar of expectations from the final part of the saga was quite high, and, as practice shows (and the colors of the reviews on Kinopoisk), this fact may not play into the hands of the creators of the picture.But still, my review is positive with a solid and well-founded assessment. The plot may be a little lame, but you simply don't want to pay attention to some inconsistencies between the tapes, as you are completely immersed in what is happening on the screen. Of course, you can blame the creators for the solid length of the dialogues (and, as a result, the length of the film), but, as for me, this is pure subjectivity. The final tape is obliged to reveal all the characters (of which there are many) and it is problematic to do this using standard timing.Is it worth talking about the visual component of the picture? I think everything is obvious, like the plans of Thanos. Magnificent special effects and cinematography are simply pleasing to the eye. Still, the picture is the trump ace of Marvel. The soundtrack is of course also top notch. Thanks to these two components, dynamic scenes simply do not let you tear yourself away from the screen (especially the final battle).And everything seems to be done according to the canons of the best movie sagas, but the film simply does not give itself ten points. In the presence of a long way of becoming heroes, and a hopeless situation, and a complex alternative way to solve the problem, and a villain who is not inferior in strength to the heroes. But, as a spectator, I did not feel the scope and possible catastrophic consequences of the coming great battle. Alas, the film does not look with bated breath and constant surprise from what is happening. Avengers: Endgame is trying to hit the viewer with an element of drama, but in my opinion, it turned out very poorly. The emotional techniques used by the creators are extremely obvious and do not affect the sophisticated viewer.Also to the minuses of the film, I would attribute the abundance of corporate humor from Marvel. Very strangely, it is combined with an atmosphere of grief and hopelessness from the loss of half the world's population.Of course, Avengers: Endgame is a great entertaining movie. But, alas, it will not be difficult to predict the plot (and denouement) of the film, since what is happening on the screen is too banal and stereotyped.Will the heart skip a beat from dramatic moments, like when watching "Logan" or "The Dark Knight Rises"? I think no. But it was precisely on the dramatic component that the main bet was made, which, in the case of me, did not work.

There is so much to love about this movie. I chuckled, I cried (more than once) and I gripped my seat. I cheered.
While I am completely satisfied in some respects, there are a few things so "off" that I can't for the life of me understand what they were thinking, in the decisions.the main reasons I took off two points- and it was almost three:
Thor. They completely ruined him, for NO reason. It is not accurate to his history in the comics or even their own movies. Nothing about the "God of Thunder" should or could have led to the hot mess they portrayed him as for the bulk of the film. The comic relief I suppose they were trying for was both grossly unfair and unnecessary- to the character and the movie and the fans. Marvel, do better.
Captain America. While the ending got him was sweet I suppose and satisfying in some respects, are we conveniently supposed to dismiss and forget the family Peggy Carter has before he changed that timeline? People that his decision would have erased? They showed him as very aged. According to all that's been said of his powers, he ages so incredibly slowly that he would still be young, watching people around him get old. We are led to believe he "got a life" one, not many- with Peggy Carter. And he's now old? How?
Nebula- she killed the past version of her. How does that possibly work? Wouldn't that delete HER, forever?
I could go into Black Widow and Tony (why?? Again not accurate to the comics and not who could and should have done it- ok yes, dramatic story ending and all but...)- but the other points were the more bothersome to me.
All of this said- the movie is beautifully shot, cinematically fabulous, wonderfully acted. It wore me out in a good way, and any Marvel fan of any of these beloved heroes needs to see it. Just be prepared for some parts that keep it from being the absolute masterpiece it could have been.

Review Title: Excellent ending to a 10 years saga
Review:
Right at the beginning, we are struck with Thanos' death which surprises everybody, contradicts all the theories and builds expectation and curiosity. The first hour is a bit slow paced but it is important to explain exactly what is going on with the universe. But then with the goal of going back in time set, thanks to the rat, the film gets a faster pace full of easter eggs and well-tailored plot.
Every hero has an important role in everything except for Captain Marvel, who I personally found to be underused in this movie. Maybe because of her immense power and the difficulty in using the character and ending the movie too soon.
The comeback with Thanos and character from the alternate timeline coming to the main one gave the movie that epic battle and amazing use of all characters. One of the few things that bothered me, was Captain America casting lightning while wielding Mjolnir because it's known that the lightning power comes from Thor himself and there is no reference in any books or saga inside or outside the MCU that would suggest that could be possible. Even though it was a little bit off, it added that epic feeling to the battle and everyone that I asked liked it. Did not see any complaints. The last hour was full of emotions, excitement, sadness, joy, and completely full of tears. Personally, I liked the ending very much. It differed from all theories I heard and read but one, the very first actually, that talked about going back in time. The movie is unpredictable, exciting, well-tailored and brought an amazing conclusion.
I completely recommend it.

Review Title: Touching last chapter to the Marvel Saga
Review: So, Endgame. This is the last chapter to the Marvel series of movies that began in 2008 with Iron Man.11 years later, it's right that the series showcasing the journeys of characters such as Iron Man, Captain America, Spiderman and Thor should have a grand send-off. This film didn't disappoint. There is a general fear that sequels can't live up to the first film, and that final movies can't meet audience expectations. The writers and actors had a large task ahead of them as this is a movie featuring multiple characters and various threads need to be tied together.Not being a Marvel fan myself, I had to read up on the previous installments, as I was told that this film would make no sense unless one had watched the previous film as it was a direct continuation. That's true. Even so, I enjoyed the character studies and the crossovers of different worlds. What was particularly thrilling was to see lead characters from different films come together and interact. For example, short scenes with Chris Pratt and Chris Hemsworth as Star Lord and Thor respectively, and Benedict Cumberbatch as Doctor Strange engaging with Robert Downey Jr's Iron Man were very exciting and satisfying to watch, mainly just out of curiosity regarding how the actors would respond to one another and what the dynamic between the characters would be. As a viewer I have a vision of how the characters would engage with one another and it was curious to see various relationships brought to life in a slightly different manner than initially imagined. The interactions were naturalistic though and believable, because the actors were top of the game.There was drama, and there was also plenty of humour to go around. Paul Rudd was very endearing and likeable as the awkward and slightly lost Ant-Man, Chris Hemsworth was hilarious as a drunk and depressed Thor, and Robert Downey Jr whose Tony Stark I usually find too irritating for his attention seeking and smart-ass manner was touching and sensitive, especially in regard to his relationship with Tom Holland's Peter Parker. I do wish they could have fit in Natalie Portman and Tom Hiddleston more, but that's the danger with 'team-movies'- the focus invariably has to lie with a few select characters. It is a shame that Thor and Jane never received the closure they deserved on screen, however.Knowing that this was the last time that some of the characters would ever interact added poignancy and sadness to some of the scenes. What needed closure was generally given closure, and the last scene is very beautiful- a perfect ending to the Marvel film universe.

Review Title: One of the Best Movies I've Ever Seen
Review: First off, I know people may consider me overrating this movie, but we have opinions, so if you didn't like Endgame that much/it's not one of your favorite movies, you can skip this review.Before even seeing the movie, I went to Wikipedia to see how it was doing in its box office, and when I scrolled down (I forgot why), I tried to not look at the plot, but I accidentally spotted the last paragraph which had "Tony Stark's funeral", and I just felt like slapping my forehead over and over. However, even with this spoiler, this movie is one of my favorites ever.While this movie was far from perfect (plot holes, not as intense action as IW) it was nonetheless incredible and perfectly contained lots of emotion and still had enough action for it to be considered an action movie, but come on: it was meant to be the culmination of 22 films and 11 years of work, so I can see why there was lots of emotion and satisfaction displayed. It delivered a very proper sendoff for the main 6 in my opinion: Iron Man's family, coming to terms with Cap, and of course his snap; Captain America fighting Thanos, lifting Mjolnir, and declaring "Avengers... assemble"; Thor wielding both Stormbreaker and Mjolnir, growing in his character through depression (yet still having the opportunity to grow since Endgame isn't his last film); Hulk merged himself and became both smart and strong (people complain he's weak since he can't increase strength with anger, but I believe MCU Hulk never had that ability and he literally lifted the entire Avengers compound with ONE hand), reversed the snap for half of life while only losing an arm (though I would've loved a rematch with him against Thanos); Black Widow sacrificed herself to allow Hawkeye to see his family and we can get an origin film on her; Hawkeye sees his family and goes through character arcs of becoming Ronin and eventually recovering. All in all, there is no way that this film did not greatly change the MCU, and I thought it did for the better.I've only been an MCU fan since 2018 (though I saw GOTG and Black Panther earlier than 2018 but I didn't know about the MCU) before Infinity War came out, but I have seen most of the films to be able to rank them, and this film goes on the top of my list. In Endgame, I understood most of if not all of the references made to earlier movies, such as "on your left", "I am Iron Man", "I can do this all day", and more, but obviously the character arcs impacted me the most despite me being a fan for merely a year, and I quickly developed a liking and understanding of the MCU. To feel such a connection with characters I knew for less than a year was very surprising to me, yet I always come back to this movie for satisfaction to indulge a bit on everything it provides.An MCU movie isn't an MCU movie without action; the Big 3 vs Thanos was great (though I wish it lasted twice as long), and Thor showed prowess despite being out-of-shape (disarming Thanos and nearly beheading him with Cap), yet Cap easily took the best 1v1 fight. Then, the Battle of Earth (I like that name), while only 15-20 minutes, was great with all the dead heroes revived, and the Portals theme is among my favorite music to listen to, along with Iron Man's funeral music, The Real Hero. The action, while limited, was spectacular nonetheless, as well as epic.Overall, this movie was great for me in terms of emotion, character arcs, and action, and it is still one of my most loved films ever.

Review Title: Just Because it "Had to Happen" Doesn't Mean I Have to Like Ot
Review:
*** SEVERE SPOILER ALERT ***
*** Seriously, don't read if you haven't seen *** *** the movie. It will definitely ruin it for ***
*** you. ***As an MCU fan, "Avengers Endgame" was simply not an option - it was an absolute must. And something that had to be seen... especially before all the plot points started leaking. I think this is true for many of us. So, it's no surprise that it's breaking all kinds of box office records. However, what IS surprising to me is the number of exhorbitantly high reviews. No doubt the movie is pretty entertaining to watch. But... it was also excruciatingly painful. Painful to watch them effectively destroy all of my favorite characters. I don't see how anyone could enjoy the film that much with this going on. And... I have SO many questions.First of all, the movie is fairly slow in several parts. This isn't too bad overall (not nearly as bad as Captain Marvel), but given that we were forced to watch it late at night (only time we could get tickets), there were definitely a couple of head bobs involved. But, now, for the questions.... and concerns...So... how did Captain Marvel know that Tony Stark and Nebula were stranded and where? I saw no explanation of this anywhere. All we know is that Fury only had time to simply trigger the "pager" before he vaporized. So where did Marvel get the information about what to do and where to look? Feels to me like there's a missing scene or two there. Or I was half asleep. Captain Marvel is powerful... but she's not God or clairvoyant.Speaking of Captain Marvel, why does she have to be so conceited? She basically tells the Avengers that they lost to Thanos because they didn't have her there. That may be true, but she doesn't have to be a complete jerk about it. Granted, Thor can be an arrogant arse too at times, which is one of the things I dislike most about his character. Trying to imagine Superman, a similarly all powerful character, saying something like that. I can't.While Tony Stark is clearly brilliant minded, it was simply too much to accept that he miraculously stumbled on the solution to time travel, especially in such a short period of time.I can't for the life of me understand how Hawkeye/Black Widow managed to acquire the Soul stone. The requirement is for one person to sacrifice that which they love to get the stone. But there was no such sacrifice. Each of them did their best to sacrifice themselves all the way to the end, which defeats the purpose. Should never have worked.In "Infinity War", they made such a big deal about how the Infinity Gauntlet was forged on Nidavellir and the only thing strong enough to house all the stones at once. Yet, Tony is able to whip up not one but TWO gauntlet-like devices that can wield the stones. Just doesn't flow to me.While I know that Captain America has proven himself worthy enough to lift Mjolnir, I think it's silly for us to believe that he would also immediately have Thor's power to command lightening. Yes, I know that the comics say this is possible. I just don't know how he would have known how to convincingly without having done it before.I'm sorry, but the gratuitous and pandering "all woman" attack scene was beyond rediculous and so unnecessary. There have always been so many incredibly powerful women in the MCU, and they were already contributing to probably more than half of the final battle scene. Having them assemble together like that to try to prove something or make some kind of political statement was completely over the top. Way too obvious and damaged the movie IMHO. I don't care what the MCU thinks their future is. This didn't help.These are the biggest questions/concerns that negatively impacted the movie, but there are many others. And again, the biggest problem I have is in how they just destroyed all of the main Avengers. And the worst destructions are with characters that aren't even dead (Thor, The Hulk, Captain America). Yes, I know this is Marvel's plan... to make room for other characters. Doesn't mean I have to like it. Again, the movie was good but not great. Honestly, I enjoyed "Infinity War" (and many others) so much more. Losing half the universe wasn't nearly as bad.
