The great late Roger Ebert once said "It's not what a movie is about, it's how it is about it."
Applying this very sensible yardstick to Endgame makes it inevitable to call it a movie as near cinematic perfection as a blockbuster can possibly be. This film has delivered on every count. It has emotion, action, humour, you name it.
The Russo brothers have achieved s.th. I would not have expected in a movie which includes time travel in order to restore half the Universe, of all the preposterous notions! And what they have achieved is finding those moments in the story which have allowed the invested fan to feel emotional and moved, as well as entertained. These moments have also allowed the main cast to showcase their acting chops and, by doing so, have given the actors their due respect. They are not only meant to kick, smash things and stand in front of a green screen. And it's this particular facet of Endgame which I appreciated most. Not every movie in the MCU has been able to strike that note. That said, I love every one of the 22 movies that have brought us to this magnificent Endgame.
Many quibble over some aspects of the story, most mystifyingly about the death of Black Widow, which was as unexpected as it was emotional. Saying she was killed off to drive the plot by motivating her male team-mates to achieve success in their fight against Thanos is absurd. The character of Natasha Romanoff is as tough and courageous as all the other Avengers and she sacrifices herself willingly for the greater good; it could just as well have been Clint Barton. This sacrifice should be taken at face value, because trying to apply political correctness to superhero blockbusters simply spoils the fun. There is a time and a place to harp on about political correctness, feminism, etc. - but movies like this one are not it.

Thank you Marvel. Thank you Russos. Thank you Avengers. That was what every fan wanted and needed at the same time.
Rarely does a film give an audience what it truly wants. I always fear that most movie studios hold back from giving it their "best movie" due to pressure for sequel sales, outdoing themselves, cost etc. But Endgame gives you everything. It's a Marvel fans dream.
The storyline was brilliant. The audience truly feels the tragic effects of the snap at the end of Infinity war at the beginning of the movie and then continues on a rollercoaster with our favourite characters, ones that we've spent years and years cheering, undoing all of the damage Thanos caused.
The final battle is everything. Fight choreography, CGI, suspense, everything. "Avengers.... Assemble"
"I knew it!"
"I am Iron Man"
Wow. Just wow. I was gripping my seat throughout the whole film at the sheer intensity of what we were seeing and what we have been waiting to see for all of these years.

Review Title: ALL fan service, and abandonment of potential. No ending plot hole
Review:
I have a different perspective to share from all the other theories and reviews I've seen. I will focus on just 2 to try and keep it short. The movie was straight fan service, and being a big fan of Marvel, of course I enjoyed the film. Over 200 well placed Easter eggs that added consistency made this film a marvel in itself. However, because of the amount of fan service, I felt like Endgame as a movie suffered a great deal. The shift in rhetoric left me unsatisfied and, in more disarray, than Infinity war!
Rhetoric : If you examine the sociological factors portrayed recently, it tells a slightly different story than the usual formula of good guy fights bad guy with the same powers/back ground/family. It becomes a bit more ambiguous rather than black vs white. Examples being
Winter solder who is a good person just following orders
CIVIL WAR
ghost being forgiven (antman wasp),
vulture being relatable and like Tony (homecoming),
not assuming who the real enemy is, and not earning a victory against the villain (captain marvel).
Lastly is Thanos who talks about real problems we face today like population, not being grateful, mass extinction, and global warming. He essentially made others like himself after the snap. Why not double resources some say; because it leaves people with a worse mentality. Halving the populous made survivors activists. They undone his character development by replacing him with his 2012 version who is more arrogant and a tyrant. This is capitalized on with nebula who refuses to believe she would change in the future and is willing to die. When the black/white vision of society views a complex character, it will not be received well equating a hurt box office. Magneto is a perfect example of ambiguity because he is a holocaust survivor who is witnessing a near genocide of a race AGAIN and refuses to watch. What really kills me is the line "saw whales in the river... yeah, no pollution".
Timeline disarray. There are 6 realities (of the many) introduced in endgame. 3 where Thanos likely wins, and 1 where he and Nebula are gone with ALL the avengers alive including Vision and Widow. This is the only reality were everyone wins. Infinite time loops will likely occur in some of these too. Steve in the original reality should NOT have come back if he chose to stay in the past. The catch to the MCU is that we never followed the original reality; we followed the last one where there are 2 Steve rogers. Consider his decelerated aging. In Civil war, Peggy said she married before 1953 and she had Alzheimer's when Steve visited. The picture she on her nightstand had her, a boy, and a girl (w no husband) just like an alternate universe Steve rogers does. During endgame when Steve first sees her through the window, the only picture she has on her desk is Steve's picture. This is well after she was married. Agents of shield never disclosed her husband's identity. And no, Steve is not a person to generally sit by, but another Steve is out there anyway, and the original Steve is getting much older when the action starts.Last note: Endgame featured my favorite versions of the surviving characters by far. Dynamic and realistic likable hero's.

Review Title: Not what I expected but still a good movie
Review: It is important to note I am a huge MCU a fan. I firmly believe that that each film is as unique as its lead characters, but importantly plays a part in the journey leading up to Avengers: Endgame.Avengers: Infinity War was a great film. The plot was smooth, the multiple storylines merging was seamless, and the tone of the film was dark and heartbreaking with light nods of humour. If you look at this film as part one and Avengers: Endgame as part two, they are very different.Infinity War's ending of Thanos' success and the Avengers' defeat should have been the tone that carried throughout the beginning of Endgame. I did not feel this sorrow (other than the first scene with Hawkeye).There was more humour than necessary, and I am still torn about the transformations of Thor and the Hulk. I enjoyed Thor: Ragnarok very much and Thor's comedic moments are truly a delight. In Infinity War, The Hulk "wouldn't come out." This led audiences to believe he would make an epic appearance in Endgame, which he did not. He barely smashed anything and was transformed into the best of both Bruce and the big guy; however, I enjoyed The Hulk and Thor's interactions in Ragnarok, when the Hulk began speaking in full conversations. When I watch the film again I might have a greater appreciation for their character transformations.Because the feel of the film was more light and playful than Infinity War, I knew that the Avengers would ultimately win. I just didn't know how. I definitely did not predict the end of Infinity War, as I did not believe Thanos would find all six stones. I wish we had a bit more time with Captain Marvel at the beginning of the film and got to see more of her interacting with the surviving Avengers.I very much enjoyed reliving parts of other MCU films as the Avengers traveled through time. There were some great tear jerker moments (both happy and sad, and the ending of the film was quite satisfying. Cap got the girl and lived a full life, Tony met his fate (as many predicted), and Thor left with the Guardians of the Galaxy, which opens up an opportunity for another film.The reunions were heart wrenching, and I was so overjoyed to see the dusted characters return to Cap's aid in his most dire moment. The interaction between Tony and Peter Parker was long overdue but worth the wait!Overall it was satisfying and a fantastic movie. I cannot wait to see it again!

Firstly, I want to state it here now I rarely EVER use such a term as perfection but in my opinion the word has its exceptions and in the case of Avengers Endgame it rightly deserves such a claim or at least that the view could be held for debate, the sheer work put into it alone suggests the admiration the whole crew has for the project and for the MCU itself and credit to them because in my eyes its a work of art, a true masterpiece. I remember distinctly making sure to have tickets booked WAY in advance to be able to see this within the first day of its release (this is in the U.K) the same goes to its DVD release and having the break between the two viewings its allowed me to evaluate the film and all its twists and turns with a much deeper insight. Therefore here is my personal critique of it and warning there will be spoilers regarding major plot points.Right from the beginning I got the feeling the film although obviously the second part to Avengers Infinity War was going to be different than its predecessor and I realised that from the start comparing the differences, AIW began with Thanos retrieving the Infinity Stones whereas AE began with the aftermath of the disintegration of half of the Universes' lifeforms, i.e Clints' family being wiped from existence which to add was a brilliant choice into a visualisation of how far the snap had reached across the Universe and how many people's lives were going to be seemingly changed forever. The instant pain you felt for Clint is heart breaking and to make it worse you understand that although you connect with the character that's just one family throughout the cosmos. The follow up between Tony and Nebula being stranded in space was also a great choice as both characters surprisingly gel well together with both clutching onto the last bit of hope they have left after their defeat and trying desperately to hold on as along as possible.
Captain Marvels appearance was shocking as well as you didn't expect them to be saved so soon which you could argue being a nudge into plot development yet it works as you get to see them reunite with those they didn't see in AIW (Tony with Steve & Natasha/Nebula with Rocket) etc. It was also a correct decision to show Tony's anger towards the Avengers (Steve in particular) for letting him down not being there and for not listening to him when suggesting a armour around the world, you can see in RDJ's performance just how devastated Tony is and how defeatist he has become from the battle with Thanos which is truly convincing and seeing Steve trying to console him to no avail is also saddening, this is where things start to pick up as Tony has gave up entirely and unable to fight the rest of the Avengers and others go on to track down Thanos which was clearly a decision you didn't see coming this early on in the film, they manage to track down Thanos and with the added help from Captain Marvel they manage to control Thanos's power and surround him (too easily in my opinion but I guess they knew what to expect this time and he didn't have the Infinity Stones anymore so...) after Thanos tells them he destroyed the stones Thor's swish kill from nowhere beheading him with Stormbreaker completely threw me off and utterly was shocking and still satisfying with his "I went for the head" remark, I remember seeing that moment for the first time and I truly had no idea where they were going to go from there as we obviously all had our own preconceived theories by then, to then see the five years later go across the screen, well...
From then, you see the true devastation Thanos has left in his wake with the support group held by Steve, the missing posters printed everywhere and large memorials to those lost in the disintegration and the remaining Avengers trying to move on years after, you sense they're all still too broken and just trying to deal with things the best they can Steve and Natasha are the worst of and its not until the re-emergence of Scott with the help of a little furry friend do they begin to realise there may still be a chance to redeem themselves and save those lost.
The 'time heist' was extremely satisfying and was well thought out and crafted, I don't understand why so many people as I've seen had problems with it? It wasn't that hard to work out... Your present self can't change your past selves actions to change your future selves outcome, it doesn't work like that that's why instead of changing the actions that were already cemented they changed those actions from ever happening in the first place by retrieving the stones before Thanos.
Anyway, it was well executed and seeing a few familiar faces and a couple surprise ones was that more satisfying.
Now, what really pleased me with this film although the wait for it was lengthy it was well worthwhile was the final showdown between all of the MCU characters we've grown to love through the years and Thanos and his army, I just thought it was spectacular, truly stunning, one of the best final showdowns I've EVER seen and I don't say that with ease, believe me.
I apologise for going into too much detail here about the plot movements and everything there's a reason to it, basically from the start up to this point you get the old testament of which is featured in many films past and present, the face off between the believably un-defeatable foe, the minor loss or in this case huge loss, the aftermath (this phase) the realisation that there is a way back from the defeat and a shot at redemption and the courage to fulfil that destiny, now of course with all movies the chances are that the protangonists are going to win but what Marvel does so well and this film the proof of that is always maintain the disbelief in that theory, maybe not completely but always have a curveball or two to surprise even the most hard pleasing of viewer, who would've honestly called Thanos being killed within the first act? Let's be honest.
The writing, the screenplay, direction, acting, set pieces, set designs, visual effects and everything else make this a thrill to watch from start to finish, yes you can pick it apart and find faults with it but if we're being honest with ourselves that's just down to our own opinions on how it should've been and not giving enough credit to the monumental task the Marvel team had to face with this film, especially with the success of AIW and all the other films in the franchise for that matter, let alone the die hard fans they had to contend with, you can't please everyone but I truly believe if you re-watch this film with an open mind no matter how you felt about it beforehand and just take a moment to notice how much creativity, detail and effort must of went into it all you'll see it differently and hopefully with the same appreciation that I do, I understand we all wish certain things turned out differently, don't get me wrong I do as well, I believe they shouldn't have killed off Natasha (I know she's getting her own feature film set in the past but still) I understood Tony's, of course sad but you could see he was passing on the mantle in a way? Same as Steve but yeah, Nat's death hit me harder because I thought it could've been left out really? Maybe replacd by Nebula? To redeem herself for all the times she tried to kill Gamora? I don't know I guess the writers have their own reasons.
Overall I see the potential the Marvel team saw with such a daring and risk taking project and they pulled off the impossible, to make a highly suspenseful, hugely enjoyable, showstopper of a film with a HUGE ensemble cast and MANY moments the fans will NEVER be able to forget, the culmination of 22 films all worth their own spot in the list.

Review Title: Did I see the same movie that everyone else did?
Review: I know I'm risking my own life here by not giving it a 9 or a 10 and praising the movie, but here's my opinion.First of all I didn't think this was a bad movie. It was fun and fulfilling, but I had much higher expectations after infinity war. There were some good action scenes, there was a lot more story, and the ending battle scene was very fun to watch. However it may just be me, but my expectations were a lot higher. When I saw that the movie was 3 hours long I was excited and was hoping that it would give us a ton of fighting and destruction and emotional scenes with tons of reveals and great pacing and all that. I did not find that. Instead I got a confusing, emotionless drama where no one seemed to care anymore. None of the characters seemed to care that this was their last chance, no matter what. Hulk and Thor didn't take it seriously (Thor is now fat, for comedic effect), and Tony Stark didn't want to try for a second time but everyone else took it a little more seriously, but not to the point where it should be. The directors tried to make it more light-hearted, but in my opinion I would have liked to see a more serious Marvel movie where everyone has a sense of urgency and everyone knows the stakes. Another problem I had was the pacing. It is very slow at the beginning, since it tries to set the scene and establish the tone of the movie. All of the characters are assembled, and they all chill at the Avengers HQ for a while, and Captain Marvel is so cocky. It made me pretty mad that a character with that much power is so unwise and not respectable. Then Ant-Man comes in, and he proposes the idea of the Quantum Realm to the Avengers. This is another problem I have with the movie. The movie does a very poor job of explaining how the Quantum Realm works and how time works regarding the Quantum Realm. It would have been a lot better if they found an easier way to explain it, if there is an easier way, or just not used the concept at all. The entirety of the second act consists of all of the Avengers trying to obtain the Infinity Stones in the past, with some minor action scenes and a good amount of comedic relief. The third act is by far the best part, with all of the fighting that I was expecting to be more strewn out throughout the movie. I am fine with this scene though, since I liked that they had all of the Avengers come together at once. I did think it was kind of ridiculous that Captain America picked up Thor's hammer though, but I thought it was a good addition to the fight scene. Also, why did Captain Marvel come in so late? She could have destroyed Thanos's whole army before it caused so much chaos, but instead she comes in much later.Like I said, I did not think this was a bad movie. However I do not think Avengers: Endgame deserves a 9.1 on IMDb. There were many inconsistencies with this movie and Infinity War, but I thought this was an OK end to the Avengers Franchise. I expected more, but that's OK, I will take what I got.

Review Title: A weak 8 but even that is WAY TOO generous

Why? Because it is just too easy to get lots of attention with it thanks to all the hype & marketing around the movie. It is emotional I don't deny that & I know some people might cry but this many people uploading their cried out eyes, ruined make-up, etc & say how it is the best 10/10 thing ever even though it's their first Marvel movie? It's obviously not genuine.Some of the flaws because even a couple of those make this review long.The first 2 hours felt rushed, as if they want to include way too many things. They tried to emphasize how important this is yet it was full of joking around. Made an odd vibe.Based on the movie's logic, literally NO ONE has to die. No one. If Gamora can survive, anyone can. Your daddy died? No prob, let's get you a new Tony. They could do it! Also, if you think about the stones, you can find out they could have numerous infinity gauntlets at their disposal. Not one, not too, literally infinite amount of infinity gauntlets to become absolute gods. They didn't care about other realm's future anyways by doing those things, so why not? Loki went away with one? No prob, let's improvise & go back to another one. So if Loki doesn't go away with the stone, then they have one & can go back to another one the same way. Easy.How can cap bring back the stones to the exact same place? Just think how they got them. Also, how can he become old in the same universe when they said it is not the same? It is the same world, then 2 Steve existed & the traveler knew everything when the previous movies happened yet didn't care about all the disasters?Captain Marvel? They hyped up the character, acted as if her movie was important before Endgame to fool people & rake in money because after Endgame it would be a flop. Importance in the movie? Close to 0. She was barely in it, almost 0 talk(thank god though).New Captain America? The whole franchise went as if it will be Bucky. The one who is the most important for Steve, has similar powers too. All of a sudden, not him but Falcon. I've heard something like it's Falcon in the comics too, alright whatever but the way they made this happen, it felt off. Like it has to be him even though nothing indicated it. Felt like when someone gives a big reward to a kid just because his parents are really influential and demand it.Thor? Laughed about it a couple of times but they pushed it too far & also this character change makes the previous movies 100% pointless. It was a gradual personality buildup through numerous movies, especially Ragnarok & Infinity War. Just to create an overweight emotionally fragile God(like really??) who was not so long ago an overpowered God, a pure alpha man who almost killed Thanos with all the infinity stones but now so fragile he is afraid to talk to women. Doesn't make sense.Hulk? Hulk???The "girl power" walking together scene also felt really forced just to get some polcorrect points. Illogical. In a colossal war on a big field, this thing just won't happen. How? Also why would it happen?As a closure, Russos jumped ship. Their last Marvel movie. They understand what is coming & want to leave when things go well. Good decision from them. Just check the characters who retire & those who come in their places. Check the lingering polcorrect & forced vibe this movie had while the older ones did not. They chose pandering instead of quality for many scenes. Review Title: Overall a good movie, but some overlooked issues
Review: This movie was by no means a bad movie. Obviously, considering the complex and lengthy build up to its eventual release, it was never going to be bad, however I can't help but feel that all this hype led to it being somewhat lackluster and a little underwhelming. The story was great and the intricacy of the plot was impressive, after all they managed to pull off time travel and alternate realities almost perfectly, which deserves recognition, however after the first hour of this, it started getting boring. The movie opens with 30 minutes that I can't help but feel weren't really needed. Most of what happens in the first hour to be honest could probably have been cut down and condensed into maybe 25 minutes of amazing film, but instead felt like a bit of a drag. The climax of the movie is where I really felt like it shone. The action is superb, the way in which the characters play off each other's strengths and use their brains just as much as their brawn is always refreshing to see in this type of movie, and the eventual ending to the whole thing, while feeling like a slight cop-out, does take you by surprise and leaves you wishing there was another hour or two of that sort of thing, rather than the first part. All in all though, a very enjoyable movie, and a brilliant conclusion to what has been over 20 movies in the making. Despite a few issues that left me with a bit of a sour taste in my mouth, I did thoroughly enjoy and will be watching again.

Review Title: Fan-service, tear-jerker plus long awaited "surprises" = good but not as good as it should be
Review:
I'm sorry, if the title sounds a little bit harsh but having invested so much emotional energy in those characters over the last decade, the movie really felt like a big letdown for me. And although I would never tell someone who loves a movie, whichever it may be, that he shouldn't, the 10 rating simply cannot be real.
Yes, everyone has his own opinion, so here is mine - most of the screenplay felt like taken from the comments under the HISHE and SinemaSins or similar channels videos. Like they have put in lines, scenes and characteristics solely to try to please fans, regardless whether it fits the inner logic of the narrative.
Couple of scenes, although I liked them, felt like taken point by point from Pixar - we know that you care about our characters, we know how to make you cry for them. Sometimes it comes of as a great conclusion, or most of the time as a beautiful scene, but in the end it is just a filler scene for a farewell for a character. Of course not all of them.
The whole time travelling thing - it has two flaws. Firstly, time travelling stories are always full of plotholes. They simply cannot not have them. Even if they put rules by which they would go, it still will leave a lot of continuity and logical errors. And because they are so many, I really am trying to skip over them. But I find the second flaw even worse - what will be their excuse now to not use this tactic every time there is a big bad that does damage? Will it be as lame as the explanation for the absence of Capitan Marvel? Or why couldn't Strange at least try to reverse time on Tony's damaged hand/body? At least to show it is not an option.
And talking of Strange, when he announced the extremely low positive outcomes in Infinity War, it already put the expectations quite high. So the way it all played out felt quite disappointing to me. I am sorry but it really made no sense in the context they created. Say if it was necessary for Tony to have a daughter, who will somehow inspire the idea of time-travelling then maybe, maybe I could understand the whole let-him-win-is-the-way-to-defeat-Thanos. Now it somehow feels pointless, it just gave Tony some years of happiness before the end.
Also I am sorry but there was absolutely no point in exactly Him, not Hulk or Thor, who hypothetically have a better chance of survival, to be the one to snap in the end. It felt just like a cheap way to kill him. If he had programmed somehow the new "gauntlet" to not be able to be used by anyone else... which by the way leads me to an ever bigger question - I get that Tony is the universe genius, but if it was so easy to make a gauntlet, why was it so hard for Thanos to get one? They could have still sacrificed Tony but in a better and more logical way.
And I don't even want to start with Cap - I like that he wielded Thor's hammer because not only was it cool, but it was the way he wouldn't be dead after the first slap on the head from Thanos. But before that... c'mon he is a super hero, but not that powerful.
I didn't like the choreography of the last battle. Heroes seemed to be missing from a certain fight without a reason to. It was really stupid that once all the vanished heroes returned, none of them tried to disarm the spaceship. There is no excuse for not having Gamora and Nebula (who I don't know how is still alive) fight their father. Same goes for Hulk, who was totally wasted second movie in a row. BUT I SIMPLY LOVED SCARLET WHICH!! Her scene was everything the last battle should have been. It was perfect and I was wishing for a similar with Hulk and Thor, and the two daughters, and maybe Strange. Because I am sorry, I love the rest of the heroes, but none of them should stand that big chance against Thanos (Lightning Cap excluded, and Captain Marvel, because she is basically missing).
Wow... I actually am surprised by how long my rant went, and the worst is - there is so much more of it. I know, in reality it doesn't really matter, and I am fully aware that no movie can please anyone. But this franchise was one I really cared for, and that is why I was disappointed.
It is not a bad movie, but it wasn't a very good one either. And it is a bad conclusion of a saga that I really liked. And it is about whether they killed off or didn't kill off someone, it's the way they did it. (Btw, if it is soul-for-a-soul with the soul stone, when Cap returns it, no matter how, which soul does he get back? Just wondering...)
It could have, should have and deserved to have been better.

That battle was awesome, with every character coming back to fight Thanos and his army, and then Captain America freakin lifts Mjolnir to fight Thanos one on one it was incredible. I know this is a long review but I loved this movie and if I had the time and money I'd go see it again. Definitely worth the wait, go see it!

Review Title: Cap and Iron man save this one from poor writing.

I would normally not write reviews on imdb but I had to for this one after reading comments like this movie is at "times as good as the return of the king and at times better" "this is the best superhero movie ever" etc etc is in my opinion first of all not even close to the Lord of the rings and not even the best mcu movie let alone best super hero movie ever. The hulk is actually good in this and surprisingly I kind of liked Thor's humour in this with his chemistry with rocket racoon has dome genuinely funny moments. The characters are well done and genuinely have good chemistry.
Bad points now .....The ppl who wrote the script are being praised but it's just really poor writing ...it's like this movie was made with the thought of ppl don't have an iq of more than 5 so really dumb it down. The idea of time travel would take years to crack ...these guys get it right within minutes if it was this easy everyone would be doing it. There would be soo many variables that could affect the future but it's all sidelined for a very linear story ...go back get the stones and that's about it ...nothing about the parameters the consequences of time travel. Brie larson is genuinely awful and I think marvel need to dump this character or else it's gonna end badly for marvel ...she's acting all tough ..no fear ..cocky ...yet it all feels soo farfetched she literally looks like a fish out of water you don't believe for a second she's all that. She literally recons a whole planet in seconds lol talk about being a Mary sue ...there's one bs line in the movie where I was just rolling my eyes ...as a hologram she says she needs to go and keep order on thousands of planets lol they could have just said other planets ...when they said thousands I just thought there you are Mary sue. She couldn't have looked worse but they even accomplished that with an even goofier hair cut she genuinely has zero charisma on screen and even the russo brothers can't save captain marvel. Her power levels might be extreme but she doesn't feel that way it all just seems a bit of a yeah just go with it.
Next bad point Thanos turned out to be a complete loser ..when they introduced him in infinity war you feel this guy means business ....they tried to turn him in to some anti hero and got it soo wrong ...if you look at Zod in mos he is not afraid of dying but he would never become a hermit ....him constantly sitting down makes him seem like a dejected loser and it takes away a lot of the intimidation factor ...he just seems like a recluse rather than a leader.
The points above can be forgiven but the biggest problem this movie has that hurts it a lot is where's the human loss factor ....almost 4 billion disappeared ....there's no chaos ..where's the authority there would be martial law where's the remaining leaders ??? The human cost ??? All you see is a lame group therapy session. Who elected the Avengers as leaders?? Who do they answer to?? Is there law??? All these glaring questions have been left unanswered and that's what breaks this movie ....someone wrote in a review that the return of the king won best picture Oscar...yes it did cause it was that good ....they also said this movie at least deserves a nomination?? For what ?? Cause fanboy's said so cause it got more fan votes lol ridiculous it's like saying Justin Bieber should win all the grammys just cause he's more popular even the the quality is seriously lacking.
The cap scene at the end is a good farewell and emotional but he definitely screws up the time line ...where is the cap stuck in the ice?? Etc it's just again a big problem with this movie...time travel is child's play.
The battle scene at the end seems like it just happened by accident rather than a build up towards a big battle. Thanos in the past finds out and he goes through in to present time ...it's a good fight but it just doesn't build up just happens ...the end finale in the return of the king builds towards that which is why the payoff is soon much more epic.
The first hour is not good thats where there should have shown the actual impact where theres chaos and the authority ask the avengers to intervene ..who died and made these guys incharge ...were they elected to represent the humans ..they operating under what juristiction...so for the person saying deserves an oscar ...that itself is one reason why it doesnt ecen get close to a nomination let alone win. The second hour is the heist where it gets interesting ...the big fight is about 20/30 minutes max and the ending farewell is about 20 min's. Cap and iron man are the most interesting with Thor kind of becoming the comic relief this time. All in all a good movie and yes probably satisfying ending but I think the movie could have been soo much better. Ppl like grace Randolph should be fired how the he'll is she a critic ??? Very poor quality critics nowadays. P.'s I'm not a dc or marvel fan I just want to see good deep thought out movies that stand out the test of time ...for me the dark knight is still the best written and executed comic book genre movie in my opinion.

Review Title: Heartbreaking, just like you'd expect. But unexpected in so many different ways
Review:
I've been a fan of the MCU since 2010, when the first Captain America movie was released and to be honest, knowing that the cast's contracts will be ending in this movie I couldn't ask for a better culmination for the 21-film journey. Even the characters I used to hate, I began to see the light in them after watching Avengers: Endgame. Although previous Avengers franchises have barely shown a great deal towards Natasha Romanoff, I'm glad that in this movie they were able to showcase the attributes and personality she was able to unfold throughout all the films and morph them into one scene. I've grown appreciation towards her in this movie and I'd like to commend Scarlett Johansson for her infamous portrayal of the character. I've been a fan of Iron Man since his first movie although I've barely shown avid interest due to its release being in my younger years. But he has always been my all-time favorite Avenger and his departure scene in the film has made me feel several things: bravery, appreciation, and love despite him being a fictional comic character. I've grown attachment towards Tony, Pepper, Rhodey, Happy, the Iron Man family and even Peter Parker that's been close to Tony in the recent events of the Marvel Cinematic Universe timeline. Although upset about his death because of the fact that he started it all, I would gladly appreciate the efforts Robert Downey Jr. has put on the character for the past 11 years. We were able to see the growth and transformation of a narcissistic, playboy, and goody two shoes Tony Stark and at the same time love the surprisingly warm-hearted, intelligent and creative inventor of the Avengers superhero team.
Chris Evans has always openly shown his love for Captain America since day 1. He is his biggest fan and to see his final farewell in this movie; with it being so obviously expressed in the film in several moments brought tears to my eyes. Despite it being beautifully produced and perfectly directed, the family, friendship and lessons learned all throughout the MCU journey will always remain intact. And me being emotionally attached to the characters and the community will miss the theories and element of surprise and excitement when waiting for the next film. Other than that, Avengers: Endgame; fan or not has shown an exquisite portrayal of what it is to say goodbye to a lifelong worth of friendship and memories; and that a part of the journey is the end.

Review Title: Does not live up to the hype by any stretch of the imagination
Review: I went into this movie with very high expectations after being told "it's the best movie of all time" and was left disappointed by how forgettable it actually was. I was beyond excited to see it but it just struck me how much weaker it was than it's first half, if you really stop and think about it for just a second not one of the characters in endgame are as impactful as they were in infinity war, barring possibly Tony Stark and black widow (and of course Hawkeye and Ant-Man as they weren't there in infinity war). Infinity war did a great job of giving characters screen time to showcase what they brought to the movie and to the team, it brought out their emotions, their feelings, it brought each and every character to life. Endgame on the other hand fell flat in this regard the characters of Thor and Hulk for example had physical changes which detracted from their overall performance and feel of the characters. My main concern with this movie however is the portrayal of Thanos, Thanos is the ultimate villain he is the only strong villain in the MCU and after being ultimately the central character of Infinity War he seemed so tame this time round, he wasn't a menace overarching everything that you had constant fear of he was not "inevitable" but merely another punch and explosion villain, there was no grand scheme no plan no character to the mad Titan just a little more of the same. The pacing of the story was also slightly off for me as it felt like we get off to an emotional start with Tony almost dying in space then we got this break then the next thing that happens is we kill Thanos and go back in time, it just felt a bit all over the place and a bit sloppy. Do not take from all my criticisms that this is a bad movie. It is a wonderful conclusion to a great story told by marvel, but it is by no means the best movie of all time, its not even the best avengers movie or superhero movie for that matter. I do think for a concluding movie it hits the right notes in terms of its emotion, it's grandness and it's story, and I do think it may have benefitted from being further broken up into more movies to fix the pacing issue. Well worth a watch but don't believe the hype.

Going into this movie, I knew that I was about to witness the ending to a storyline that we've been following since 2008, with the first Iron Man movie kicking off an unprecedented entry in cinematic history. It does not matter if you are a comic book fan or not, but these movies brought something entirely new to the audiences. This movie was the culmination of 11 years of storytelling where the superheroes appearing in the final battle are all fully fleshed characters with their own arcs and backstories. Being a movie fan in general, after all these years reading on trivia boards about the things that could have happened like Sam Raimi's 4th Spider-Man movie, or any other project where somebody dropped off and then it stuck in development hell, it becomes very impressive to think how much passionate work went into making those movies. And Disney sure helped a lot in this, but still even the House of Mouse had its own hardships over some projects.As for the movie itself, it was a truly moving love letter to the fans, Marvel's history, the superheroes, everyone. I am so happy to have been in the first showing here in my country, where everyone in the roomwas fully invested with the vrowds cheering, crying and being so united into being fans and enjoying the movie. It felt like i was in a concert where everyone was having an amazing time.Despite the criticism, I found all the characters arcs ending in a fitting way. Yes I am sad to see Iron Man go, but still there was no way of keeping him around in a recurring capacity. He was the one that started the story and finished it by getting the ultimate form of power in his world and saving the universe. He died a hero saying by his iconic phrase (I am Iron Man) reminding us how far he came as a character. Cap was the "man out of time". He was not being selfish for going back rather than returning to where he always longed to be. It was a big part of his arc all these years to have the desire to go back, but as it was not possible he stayed to fight as a fully realised hero. I could go on to discuss all th character arcs but superfans already know all the stories to understand that the movie was a perfect ending for everyone. Of course business comes into play and many possible spinoffs could be setup from this ending. But still, there were no visible teases, no lingering questions about this universe and the main storyline and no-post credits scene, something that while I was waiting for it, it felt right that there was nothing included. Finally, I would like to mention how much I enjoyed the fanservice like every single MCU character appearing in the final battle and Cap lifting the Mjolnir, which were both images seen in the comics but no superhero movie had ever such a vast universe that things like this would be possible.If you have not seen the movie, or even the whole series, I suggest that you do. I dare to say that it was the Star Wars of our generation. I am very happy to have experienced this saga.

Review Title: Probably the best of the series but the ending is wrong.
Review: I loved all MCU movies and I really enjoyed Endgame. Everything seems well balanced, the interactions, the comedy, the action with a spectacular ending fight. But they made a huge a mistake.The whole concept of time travel in this movie is based on what professor Hulk said. Forget all movies that have time travel. If you travel to the past, your past is now your new future and your former present is the past, so you can't change your past with something you do in your future. Something that Nebula also agrees on, and even the Ancient One confirms later in the movie.All movie works great with this concept so when they travel to the past our heroes just enter different realities. In the end though Captain America goes back in time and stays there, IN THAT REALITY, but miraculously appears as an old man in our present. That shouldn't happen. We didn't see instant consequences when removing the stones from the past (even if they returned them afterwards), but we show instantly an old Captain America sitting on a bench in 2024. That is completely wrong. That creates a problem with Nebula killing her past self, removing Thor's Hammer from the past in Thor 2, Loki stealing the Tesseract in 2012 and ofcourse Thanos being dead since 2014.If you ignore this mistake, then Endgame is the perfect marvel comics superhero movie.

Review Title: 3000/10 no question. A perfect culmination to the 11 year journey Marvel has taken us through.
Review: A bitter sweet ending but also the perfect way to end things. The pace may be called "slow" compared to Infinity War but there wasn't a scene that you could miss. You can't look at time travel the way Back to the Future explains it. Everyone who is mad about the "plot holes" doesn't understand the concept of time that Professor Hulk explained in the movie. Marvel got it exactly right with Endgame. Just when you think it can't get any better, it does. I had very high expectations for this movie & Marvel (as they always do) exceeded them. It's hard for me to understand how they could make a movie like this when there are such high expectations for it. The movie is a perfect way to end the 11 year journey they took us on. I don't know what they have in store for us in phase 4 but I'm sure it will still be good. Review Title: Maybe it will be better a second time around! Maybe...
Review: I thought the entire premise of the movie was really good. The writing, the acting, the visual effects. However it was all too long-drawn for a very short ending finale that didn't leave me, personally, feeling like THANOS got what he deserved, especially since this is not the same THANOS that annihilated half of living creatures across the universe at the end of Infinity War.I also thought I'd see THE HULK have a big showdown with Thanos this time around, which would have really got the crowds cheering, as he got his butt kicked by Thanos at the start of Infinity War. Thought, since he used the Infinity Gauntlet and the Infinity Stones, that power surge through him would allow him to become angrier than ever before, and that anger would be converted to real POWER. That's a fight I would have liked to have seen, and I think a lot of others too. It would have brought the house down...especially just when the first half of the last fight where Captain America, Thor and Iron Man are getting their butt kicked by Thanos.The build-up to the finale was great. But it was too much for a very short-fall ending. And the Soul Stone death of Black Widow made no sense, since Nebula could have easily have told them that's how to get the Soul Stone. Also the entire score, look and feel of the SOUL STONE piece was a COPY-PASTE from Infinity War. So if you cried then, you're probably NOT going to be as emotive this time around. I did like the play off of Hawkeye and Black Widow. They are great actors.Captain Marvel? I wanted to see her wield the Infinity Stones to her own advantage. After all, she is pure energy, she can absorb them in theory. Got nothing. She was shown as powerful as any other Avenger in the movie apart from bringing down Thanos' ship. Come on!It would have been awesome to see THOR convert back to the fit soldier he is when he summons the lightning just before fighting Thanos in the end. That would have made the crowd go crazy again. Instead we got a lazy Thor whose storm breaker couldn't even dent Thanos one it, but it was made as the most powerful weapon! WHAT?Also, how does Nebula kill her younger self and still stay alive in the same timeline? There are so many weird things that don't make sense. If she shares the same memory lapse and hard drive, surely when the younger one dies the older one vanishes instantly?The movie works, and on many levels, but on many levels it just doesn't. It's very funny at times and trots along. What I miss is the sheer WOW factor I got in Infinity War, the plot twists, the "I didn't expect that at all" moments. One of the greatest moments of Infinity War, I remember, that was unexpected, was when Thanos reverses back time to get the Mind Stone from Vision after Scarlett destroys it. It was sheer genius. And of course the end when everyone dies. Those moments were just not there in Avengers: Endgame. And the end dragged on too long. Like a bad Lord of The Rings: Return Of The King ending. At least in Return of the King, the shot when all of them bow to Frodo, it is an historic moment in cinema. I wept like a baby. In this, it is sad, but not that sad...Infinity War's ending was way sadder and left us all on shock!The fan-service was really well done taking you through all the different Marvel movies of the last few years, the subtle easter eggs, the guest casting etc. Really well done and seamless. As stated, visually, it has all the elements, but someone like Christopher Nolan or Steve Spielberg, would have done more justice to the Endgame" script and storyline than The Russo Brothers I fear. In Civil War the Russo Brothers shot it out of the park, like with Infinity War, giving us that ending no one saw when we come to know Bucky killed Stark's parents. Amazing! In Endgame that just didn't happen.Maybe it will be better a second time around! Maybe...I'll wait a week and watch it.Is it worth seeing? Of course it is. This is just fan theorisations post a screening. Like it, Love it or Hate it, the movie is what it is.

Review Title: EndGame - An exciting conclusion (with a few shortcomings)
Review:
EndGame is probably going to be the most watched movie of this decade and rightly so. It has taken a buildup of over 20 movies to set this up and it is nothing short of exceptional. Marvel has really pulled out all stops in the making of this movie.
However the movie is not without some shortcomings, I am going to list out all the WOW factors and things that were sorely lacking.
Note - Spoilers ahead **********************************
WOW Factors:
Marvel has catered to the comic fanbase and included some far awaited moments in this movie.
Some of these include:
-A throwback scene to the winter soldier when Captain America gets in the lift full of Hydra agents, here marvel has also alluded a reference to the controversial comic book where Captain America was revealed to be Hydra Agent.
-We finally see Captain America wield Mjolnir a feat long awaited by Marvel fans who had lost all hope when Mjolnir was destroyed in Ragnarok.
-We also have the Professor Hulk (does this lead to Maestro?)
-And we finally hear the words "Avengers Assemble" awaited for so long by the fans.
Things missed out:
-Timeline -This was handled a bit loosely with 3 simple rules (what time travel is not), this leads to a lot of questions. This could be a big detrimental factor as more marvel movies and series and planned from after EndGame. If this point is not explained clearly, the further movies and TV series based on MCU are definitely going to contradict this point.
-The other factor that I can think of is that editing could have been a bit better, I thought that the first half was a bit stretched and the war could and should have been a bit longer.
-Captain Marvel vs Thanos is a fight that just did not happen ( I don't count the first part or when she is trying to pull the gauntlet).
-The Children of Thanos who were a handful in the Infinity War weren't given any screen time during the war, would have definitely liked to see Avengers kick their ass.
-And finally the most sorely missed scene was a round 2 between Hulk and Thanos, that would have really been the star WOW moment.Overall still the EndGame has been an exciting and an emotionally satisfying end to the Infinity Saga.

Review Title: When a film is this good, you can forgive a lot.
Review:
This film did some very amazing things. The acting was flawless; the dialogue was entertaining; the action was great; the music was perfect. They made a movie that concluded a 20+ series in a satisfying way, which anyone whose read the final book of a long series is INCREDIBLY easy to mess up. This is definitely a good movie.It's nowhere near the best film ever though. Remember when Return of the Jedi came out and a whole bunch of people were upset because the Ewoks were "dumb"? To this day, some people still think that one "dumb thing" ruined the movie. Well, Endgame has about a dozen "dumb things" and a handful of plot holes too. That's not to say that they ruin the movie, just... tarnish it a bit.I'm going to sum up a few of the "dumb things" and plots holes at the end, but before that I have to say this: Endgame is definitely a film worth watching and even with all it's flaws, you won't be able to deny that it's a great movie.
And here we go.Thor Lebowski. This is the old "let's take something bad-ass and make it lame for a laugh" trope. Thor is absolutely the favorite Avenger for many Marvel fans. I saw this film with my younger brother and he was frustrated every single time Thor was on screen. I stunk that they didn't do the character justice.Caption Marvel needs our help! No she doesn't. It could have been so bad-ass to see all of the female heroes teaming up to take on some giant monster alien or something. Instead they "help" Captain Marvel bring the Infinity Gauntlet 600 yards through squishy minions. Danvers is essentially Marvel's answer to Superman. She is invulnerable, faster then light, has super strength, she can fly, and she can shoot energy from her body. She could be at that van faster than Quicksilver if he was still alive. What a waste of an awesome team-up scene.Speaking of the power house that is Captain Marvel. Why didn't they call her back when they were planning to time-travel? Having Sudo-Superwoman there would make getting the Stones a whole lot easier and less risky. And you can't say it wasn't important enough for her to come. Half of the universe depended on them succeeding.Can't bring Black Widow. Except they can. Gamora's back and she died the same way. Captain America's heading there anyway to return the Soul Stone. Just travel to 5 minutes before she dies and then bring her back home. Easy as pie. This also works with Tony and Vision and Peter Parker's parents and anyone who died at some point. That and the whole age reversal thing that Professor Hulk did to Scott pretty much cures death.Speaking of Gamora being back. 2014 Thanos and company somehow travel through time without Pym Particles or time machine suit and bracelets. The platform Nebula that fingered wasn't a time machine, the suits/bracelets are. That's why Tony and Steve could travel to 1970 from 2014 sans platform.Speaking of messing up time-travel. Old Mr. Rogers doesn't make much sense. the scene seemed to imply that Steve had traveled back to when he was frozen, married Ms. Carter and waited until that day to go meet them on that bench. But it's clearly stated by at least 3 characters that that's not how time-travel works. Nothing done in the past effects the original timeline. That's why killing 2014 Thanos doesn't make it so he never attacked in Infinity War. It's why killing 2014 Nebula didn't make present Nebula vanish. And why Loki escaping with the Tesseract didn't change anything either. Because it's in an alternate timeline. And if Steve used his time machine suit to return to the original timeline wouldn't he have had to return to the platform when Banner tried bringing him back? I thought that's what the platform did, lock onto them so that they can come back.

Review Title: It's not right, but it's okay.
Review: Being a big Marvel fan I was really excited about watching Endgame. The CGI was amazing, the end fight scene was brilliant and I was happy to see Pepper Potts get some screen time! I loved Tony Stark being able to have that treasured time with his dad Howard and the same with Thor and his mother. But there was too many unanswered questions and unnecessary decisions and scenes! First of all I think it was a big mistake to kill off Black Widow, she's an amazing member of the avengers and I think she is literally the skeleton of the group! I don't understand why they gave her more screen time with Hawkeye and not the hulk? It seems a bit strange! I don't understand why she sacrificed her life for a GOTG character as well? It makes no sense. I don't think I can forgive Marvel for killing off Iron Man, why would they make a decision like that? Unless this happens in the comics? (I haven't read them) I feel sorry for The Hulk, I didn't know if he was coming or going to be honest and poor Thor! He was portrayed as a joke, it wasn't fair to let a character like him become a drunk? And Captain Marvel, she didn't get hardly any screen time, it's so odd because she was built up to be the one who saves the Avengers. I felt it was dragged out a bit more than what it should have been to be honest, 3 hours was a bit long but it did go fast! But my biggest disappointment was there being NO end credit scene! (I felt like an idiot in the cinema waiting for it) I just felt like there was something missing... or maybe a lot of things missing! A good try from Marvel but to be honest I think it was a bit of a stab in the back to their fans and they let us down a bit. I did love the credit scene though, the signatures with the actors was a lovely touch, but I think more should have been done, there was a lot more room for potential.

You know when you watch something and you just keep waiting for those "YES!!!" moments? I felt this movie was sorely lacking in those, which is unfortunate with it being the final movie. I get that it can't be a five hour movie (not that I or any Marvel fan wouldn't have watched), but with 3 hours to tie together a huge franchise of films, this was a little lackluster.I will try to keep it as simple as possible with a pro/con list:Pros:
-Captain America had an amazing character developing. Made him much more lovable since he was something of a "prude" in previous films.
-Bruce Banner as a perfect 50/50 mix with Hulk is hysterical
-Nebula also had a pretty decent character development/role to play
-Loved Stark's new family and interaction w/ his dad. His role throughout the movies made his death bittersweet.Cons:
-Like most, I laughed at seeing Thor turn into the Dude basically. However....he is such a beast of a character in other movies and has such amazing potential as a god that it's sad to see him turned into comic relief.

Review Title: Avengers Comes Through with Solid, Not Spectacular Movie
Review:
Avengers: Endgame has been a huge hit already making $2.7 billion making it the second highest grossing movie of all time worldwide. The final Avengers movie, Avengers: Endgame, was good but not quite as good as some of the movies that had come before it. Directors Anthony Russo and Joe Russo did a good job of trying to make the storyline unpredictable and different than all the other movies but they made too many changes.
The movie begins 23 days after Avengers: Infinity War (2018) ended, which was a disappointment because we don't get to see what happened after Thanos (Josh Brolin) wiped out half of the world's population. Instead it begins with Thor (Chris Hemsworth) killing Thanos who was weaken after destroying the stones to prevent further use.
The movie jumps 5 years into the future after this when Steve Lang (Paul Rudd) escapes from the quantum realm and heads to the Avengers building where he finds Natasha Romanoff (Scarlett Johansson) and Steve Rogers (Chris Evans). He explains to them that the last 5 years have felt like 5 hours to him and tells them about his theory of time travel that they could use to go back in time, get the Infinity Stones and stop Thanos. They decide to try this plan and recruit the rest of the Avengers team to travel back and stop Thanos.
Some of the changes in movie did not work well. The directors tried to add some comedy to the movie by making Thor fat, but it was just weird and did not work real well with the story. They also have made the Avengers to big by trying to include too many characters like, Peter Parker (Tom Holland), Brie Larson (Carol Danvers), the Guardians of the Galaxy, and other characters that just do not fit in well with the rest of the original characters.
As they did in all the other Avengers movies all of the main actors did a great job with their characters. Tony Stark (Robert Downey Jr.), Steve Rogers, Bruce Banner (Mark Ruffalo), Thor, Natasha Romanoff, Clint Barton (Jeremy Renner) were all played very well. Robert Downey Jr. was especially good in portraying Tony Stark. The plot was good but could have been more interesting, just because the movie was pretty slow in the beginning and middle. Still the plot was far pretty than the previous Marvel movie Captain Marvel (2019) which had a extremely boring and predictable plot.
All of the editing, photography, and setting was extremely well put together everything looked very realistic throughout the whole movie, similar to the previous 3 The Avengers (2012), Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015), and Avengers: Infinity War. They did a great job in the final battle scene of making a very realistic setting they really fit the mood of the battle.
Overall Avengers: Endgame is a very well put together movie that is a strong finish to the Avengers series. Avengers: Endgame will not disappoint fans and is very much worth seeing as it will close one of the best movie series of all time.

Review Title: A movie that hits right in the feels
Review: After the events of Infinity war everyone was at the edge of their seat wating for the next installment in the infinity saga, what would happen to our heroes, how would they reverse the snap, and most of all, where was Thanos? As the title says Avengers Endgame was a movie that hit right in the feels and was not just a movie, but an experience. Bits such as fat Thor and Professor Hulk were a fresh theme for the movie. Some thought that fat Thor was a body shaming skit when in reality it showed what depression can be like, he had lost everything, his family, his friend, half of his people were gone, and when he finally had his shot at redemption he failed to stop the snap, even fulfilling his duty to kill Thanos could not stop the inevitable, Thor became an image of what happens when yuou could lose everything. Like the man said, reality is often dissapointing.Professor Hulk was also a fresh and fun addition to the movie, the result of 18 months in a gamma radiation like hibernation transformed our small and intelligent Doctor Banner and our big and strong Hulk into one being, uniting the two halfs, and it also opened up a door of opportunity for the MCU's future, when Hulk put on the new gauntlet and snapped, he took probably an ungodly amount of gamma radiation even he could not handle. burning and scarring his arm, but also maybe allowing for the introduction to Maestro, a combination of Dr. Banners intelligence and the Hulks brute force and anger, turning him into a supervillain, plus it would not make sense to include Professor Hulk if they aren't even going to experiment with Maestro.Not all of Endgame was comedy and action though, sadly we lost 3 of the most important members of the MCU, I think why Natasha gave her life for the soul stone instead of letting Clint do it is because she had no one, she was alone for most of her life, apart from Banner, but that part of the MCU was like a weird limbo relationship, something that did and didn't happen, but regardless she knew the price for the stone and did it because Clint still has a chance to see his family, a chance to finally hear his wifes voice and feel his children in his arms, which of course happened. And oh god Robert Downey Jr. definitely made people cry, for 11 years hes taken on the roll he was born for and executed so perfectly, from a cave in the middle east to a civil war with his best friends to finally giving his life for the future of his daughter, his wife Pepper (I don't think they married but why not) and his friends, he gave them a future to keep on being heroes. We love you 3000 Robert. And Chris Evans, he too gave the best performance of any Captain American, him lifting the hammer and those two words were what we had been waiting for since the first avengers movie, and spending his life with his Peggy after returning the stones is the most selfless thing he could do.Endgame isn't just a movie, it's an end of an era, we con't get a movie quite like Endgame in the MCU, but that's okay. We'll always cherish this movie and memory.

Review Title: A tribute to the fandom and an undoubtedly epic conclusion to this franchise.
Review: Avengers: Endgame may have just become my favorite installment in the Marvel Cinematic Universe and will also be remembered for decades to come in cinema history for most of the same reasons. I'd like to point the various shortcomings of the film first, the fallout of The Decimation from Infinity War is ultimately heartfelt but at times slow and the same can be said for around the middle of the second act as the time traveling shenanigans drag just a little bit. For the former I feel like because most of the trailer footage was from the beginning of the film the beginning felt like just watching the same thing again and the latter because of how convoluted it got with the time travel logic. It makes no sense, the plot is solid but these films are character driven stories and that's what Endgame greatly succeeds at throughout the 3 hour run-time which personally didn't bother me at all. There were a couple of character decisions I didn't like such as Thor's portrayal being well done but a bit forced (Fortnite). It's the same thing with Professor Hulk, I didn't like how he just became the way he was off screen. That's all I didn't like, now get ready for overwhelming praise. Avengers: Endgame is structured so well and in a completely different way from the previous Avengers flick but the two compliment each other in the best ways and they feel like one story that's of a colossal length but the films handle it so differently while still making it feel cohesive. Like I previously mentioned, the movie is character driven and it seems like the team behind the film really understand the ins and outs of these characters and their purpose in making the narrative more compelling. The arcs and storylines come full circle while still setting up Phase 4 enough to not need a Post-Credit scene which doesn't hold the movie back at all as it's clearly the culmination of the stories from the past 11 years. Tony has been defending the world for years and he's never truly gotten to rest until now since he finally could save the world he'd been defending. Cap finally gets to some good for himself and gets to live a life after willingly sacrificing his chance to live one in fighting for the good of people. Thor finally is able to be who is instead of having to attempt to live up to what destiny says what he's supposed to be. Bruce finally comes to piece with his supposed enemy the Hulk and finds a way to ease the conflict between the two. Nat finally clears the red in her ledger after sacrificing herself and ending the turmoil within herself that was caused by her past. Clint finally reunites with his fallen family after being so consumed by his guilt and dread that he resorted to violence to cope with his emotions. I said finally a lot there and for good reason because the thematic elements are from the depth found within the characters. Avengers: Endgame progressively gets more intriguing as it continues, the third act is by far the strongest with the resurrection of the fallen heroes and what is most likely the largest scale battle we have ever seen in a movie. The fan service in the third act greatly benefits the story in my eyes, I love how it was all built up. Cap wielding Mjolnir, the exchanges of meaningful dialogue and by far my favorite, the moment in which all the characters stand together on the same battlefield and charge toward's Thanos and his massive army after Cap says some of my favorite words a character has ever said: Avengers, assemble. The cgi wasn't even a flaw here, it didn't matter to me. The whole thing was amazing, people often throw around the word epic and don't use it in the right context. This is how you use it correctly, this epic. I walked away from the theater stunned by the conclusion to the film, the arcs of these memorable characters end in the most satisfying way possible and the final battle was indescribable. Despite the issues I mentioned earlier, I loved Avengers: Endgame as it provided a remarkably satisfying ending to the previous 21 MCU films in a beyond epic conclusion which balances comedy and an entire range of powerful emotions ambitiously and successfully.

One of the most popular, most hyped, and biggest franchises of all time finally comes to end. The movie was very enjoyable and entertaining, especially for Marvel fans. The movie will make you cheer, laugh, and cry. Seeing all these beloved characters on screen for possibly the last time really does something. Endgame serves as a good conclusion to a well-known franchise. But how does it stand as a film?The plot was pretty standard, the heroes use time travel to collect all the infinity stones to resurrect everyone who died. They do so, but past Thanos finds out and attacks the present-day Marvel HQ building in an attempt to get the stones. The heroes fight his army to defend the stones and end up winning. The use of time travel leads to some complications and plotholes that force you to suspend disbelief a bit too much.The first act was supposed to be sad because of all the losses we were met with after Infinity War. The color palette is dark and everyone is brooding. But, its an MCU movie so there has to be unnecessary quips that completely ruin the dreadful tone that was previously established. Instead of a persisting feeling of melancholy and grief, the first act feels empty and boring. The first act of Endgame is a prime example of how not to use comedy.The second act was basically intertextuality mixed with some light fan service, a few unwanted jokes, and some truly emotional, character-driven moments. There was an initial feeling of tension because these guys only had one shot. They end up screwing the whole thing up, and someone gets the brilliant idea to go back in time and get more Pym particles. But, that ends up completely ruining the high stakes and tension. But, it does give us one of the best scenes in the movie, which is when Tony meets his dad. That scene gave us a great understanding of Tony's relationship with his father. The moment was personal, character-driven, and touching. everything was pretty standard.The third act was a tribute to the entire MCU. It had a bunch of references and heavy fan service. If you are an MCU fan you will cheer during the final battle. Cap picking up Thor's hammer and Tony sacrificing himself were both important moments in their character arcs. If you aren't that big of a fan, you probably won't care about the final battle, because there is 0 tension or high stakes. Fan service isn't a bad thing, but you have to build tension and fear if you want a good climax. Throwing around references may feel amazing during the first viewing, but you will soon see that there are barely any stakes and it will take a lot out of the movie.The movie did justice to Cap and Tony, and I honestly couldn't have asked for a better ending to their character arcs. But, it wasted Thor and Hulk and used them for nothing but quips. I honestly didn't care about the other characters all that much. This is one of those extremely entertaining, "don't think about it too much" movies. There a few plotholes and the ending kinda drags, but it certainly is enjoyable. I'm not a Marvel fan, but I will admit this movie is pretty good. There are better MCU movies and far better comic-book movies. Not as good as Infinity War, but still entertaining.

Review Title: A great conclusion to a long journey -Very minor Spoilers - Honestly just watch this movie being even glancing at any of these
Review: The only way that I can best describe the entire run of the Marvel Cinematic Universe up until this point is this - There was once a day where it was very nice out, and on a whim, you invited some of your buddies to go and have a picnic. Well that day ended up being a blast, so much so that you decided that on this day, every year, you and your friends will have a picnic, where you all catch up with each other and have some fun. Each year the amount of people that attend this picnic increases, as your friends start to bring members of their family as well as new found loves. Some years the weather doesn't cooperate and your picnic isn't as great as it had been in the past, yet you and everyone else are still very much in love with the idea of having this great big get-together every year. You are now at your 11th picnic - That's 11 years of tradition that you started - You're looking around at all the people who are attending and this year, has the largest attendance. Your buddies aren't just bringing in their siblings and parents, they now have kids of their own - Kid's that were born into this tradition and think it's only natural to have it. Today the sun is warm, and the nature is stunning - this picnic is the greatest out of them all. You're thinking back to 11 years ago and think "wow, how could something so small, so simple, turn into something this big and special?"We were truly best to be a part of the ride the that started off with Robert Downey Jr's Tony Stark, which snowballed after he proclaimed to the world, "I am Iron Man". To think that those words carried so much weight, that when you heard them for the final time, you were hit with flashbacks from all that had transpired over these 11 years and left in tears.Thank you to all that worked on these fantastic pictures - Thank you for giving our beloved characters the endings we as fans could only dream of.Excelsior!

SPOILERS!Before you say it - Yes, I know it's just a movie. Now... There were several inconsistencies that kept me from being completely satisfied. The biggest was - WTH happened to Thor?? Watiti and Hemsworth have destroyed the Thor character just because they wanted to make jokes. This was a god. The future King of Asgard. The future ALL-FATHER! Sure, he'd lost his mother, his father, and his best friend, and maybe his brother (several times). But he took the brunt of a star to craft a weapon - the Thanos killing kind - and needed to find a home for, and take of, his people. So he has a set back and what does he do?? He gives up. They turned him into a Volgstagg! There is no way this "new" Thor is worthy to wield Mjolnir. The new Thor is lazy and self centered, hardly the sort of warrior and leader that Odin imagined. This Thor abandoned his people, abandoned his friends, and abandoned his duty. Not worthy at all.If Thor had been in shape and not coming off an Asgardian sized bender he might have given a better showing against Thanos and not been tossed around like a rag doll. Heck, Captain America gave a better effort with Mjolnir than Thor did with "a King's weapon". And what of Thor's magic belt? It was in the inventory log of the new Avengers HQ (see Spiderman - Homecoming). That belt allegedly doubles Thor's strength. Did he forget about it? Think about it for a second because if Cap is worthy to wield Mjolnir then he "shall posses the power of Thor". That means Thanos should have been facing the power of TWO THORS! With the belt that would have been the power of THREE THORS. So Thor bears the weight of Stark having to die to wield the stones because he wasn't ready to face Thanos. In Infinity War, an in-shape Thor, single-handedly defeated the Outriders and decimated their ships. Then he and Stormbreaker overcame the power of a full strength Gauntlet to come within about 24 inches of killing Thanos. But this Thor is easily bested by Thanos. It's like the directors dumbed him down to make it more even, maybe so Captain Marvel can steal the show.-------------
Captain America - his change in timeline begs the question: What happened to the plane with the bombs he was flying? Did he even go to Hydra HQ to get Bucky? If he didn't ditch the plane then he didn't go into the ice and so where is the plane? Also, he took Mjolnir into his alternate timeline - where is it now? Can Thor summon it? Did Cap have children? Since his genetics were altered, are his children any stronger, faster, or smarter? Did he ever tell Peggy that he made out with her great niece?And handing the role of Captain America off to Bucky makes more sense than Sam. Sam has no super strength or healing ability, and we've seen how much of a beating CA takes all the time. I'd guess that without Stark tech he's not long for the CA role.-------------
The Gauntlet was made by Eitri. He was the only one who could have made Thanos a "device capable of harnessing the power of the stones." Thanos killed the Dwarves and shut down the forge just to make sure that Eitri couldn't make another one. But it turns out that all you need is a glove. Stark just grabbed them and without knowing how they needed to be "harnessed" just popped them into his glove. I'd say Eitri is a hoax.-------------
Lastly, the snap. If we remember back, Gamora used the phrase "a snap of his fingers" as a way of describing how easy it would be for Thanos to kill half the universe when he finally got all the stones. There was no instruction manual that said it had to be a finger snap. And even if that actually WAS the method to kill half of the universe - HOW DID GAMORA KNOW??? And why would Eitri make that a requirement? Some sort of twisted sense of humor?
Loved the movie, but there were all sorts of issues with the flow. And don't even get me started on the timeline of the creation of the gauntlet. THAT is seriously messed up.
